LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Aram, Son of Shem
Summary: Aram was a son of Shem and the father of Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
KeyStory: Aram's sons became the Aramean peoples, neighbors of Israel for centuries to come.
RelatedPeople: Shem; Uz, Son of Aram; Hul; Gether; Mash
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Aran
Summary: Aran was a son of Dishan and a grandson of Seir the Horite.
KeyStory: Aran is named with his brother Uz among Dishan's children.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Ard
Summary: Ard was a son of Benjamin, named among the children of Israel who went down into Egypt.
KeyStory: Ard appears in the list of Jacob's family that came into Egypt.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Areli
Summary: Areli was a son of Gad, named among the children of Israel who went down into Egypt.
KeyStory: Areli appears in the list of Jacob's family that came into Egypt.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Arioch
Summary: Arioch was the king of Ellasar who joined Chedorlaomer's alliance against the cities of the plain.
KeyStory: Arioch marched with the eastern kings and was defeated when Abram pursued them to rescue Lot.
LifeLesson: Empires rise and fall, but God's promise to Abram outlasted every king of his day.

Name: Arodi
Summary: Arodi was a son of Gad, named among the children of Israel who went down into Egypt.
KeyStory: Arodi appears in the list of Jacob's family that came into Egypt.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Arphaxad
Summary: Arphaxad was the son of Shem, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Arphaxad appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Asenath
Summary: Asenath was the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, whom Pharaoh gave to Joseph as his wife. She bore him Manasseh and Ephraim.
KeyStory: Asenath became the mother of two tribes of Israel, born in Egypt before the famine's worst years.
RelatedPeople: Joseph, Son of Jacob; Poti-pherah; Manasseh; Ephraim
LifeLesson: God can plant His people in the unlikeliest places — even Pharaoh's court.

Name: Ashbel
Summary: Ashbel was a son of Benjamin, named among the children of Israel who went down into Egypt.
KeyStory: Ashbel appears in the list of Jacob's family that came into Egypt.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Asher
Summary: Asher was the eighth son of Jacob, the second by Zilpah, and the father of Jimnah, Ishuah, Isui, Beriah, and Serah.
KeyStory: Asher's tribe later enjoyed rich food and royal delicacies, just as Jacob had blessed him.
RelatedPeople: Jacob; Zilpah; Jimnah; Ishuah; Isui; Beriah; Serah
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Ashkenaz
Summary: Ashkenaz was the son of Gomer, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Ashkenaz appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Asshur
Summary: Asshur was a son of Shem, and the ancestor linked with the building of Nineveh, Rehoboth, Calah, and Resen.
KeyStory: Asshur went out from the land of Shinar and built great cities, including Nineveh, which would later loom large in Israel's story.
LifeLesson: God's story stretches across empires — even Nineveh's founder has a place in it.

Name: Baal-hanan
Summary: Baal-hanan, the son of Achbor, reigned in Edom after Saul died.
KeyStory: Baal-hanan is the seventh king named in Edom's king list.
RelatedPeople: Achbor; Saul, King of Edom; Hadar, King of Edom
LifeLesson: Kingdoms rise and fall, but God's promise to Israel outlasted every throne of Edom.

Name: Bashemath, Daughter of Elon
Summary: Bashemath was the daughter of Elon the Hittite and a wife of Esau — a different Bashemath from Ishmael's daughter named in Genesis 36.
KeyStory: Esau married Bashemath when he was forty, and she and Judith were a grief of mind to Isaac and Rebekah.
RelatedPeople: Esau; Judith, Wife of Esau; Elon, Father of Adah
LifeLesson: Two women can share a name and walk very different paths; God knows each one.

Name: Bashemath, Daughter of Ishmael
Summary: Bashemath was a wife of Esau, the daughter of Ishmael and the sister of Nebajoth, and the mother of Reuel. She is also called Mahalath in Genesis 28.
KeyStory: Bashemath tied Esau's house to Ishmael's line, and her son Reuel fathered four dukes of Edom.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Becher
Summary: Becher was a son of Benjamin, named among the children of Israel who went down into Egypt.
KeyStory: Becher appears in the list of Jacob's family that came into Egypt.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Bedad
Summary: Bedad was the father of Hadad, who reigned as king in Edom.
KeyStory: Bedad is named only as Hadad's father, in the list of Edom's kings.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Beeri
Summary: Beeri was a Hittite, the father of Judith, one of Esau's wives.
KeyStory: Beeri is named only as Judith's father, in the record of Esau's marriages at forty years old.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Bela
Summary: Bela, the son of Beor, was the first king named as reigning in Edom before any king reigned over Israel.
KeyStory: Bela reigned from Dinhabah, opening the list of Edom's kings.
LifeLesson: Kingdoms rise and fall, but God's promise to Israel outlasted every throne of Edom.

Name: Belah
Summary: Belah was a son of Benjamin, named among the children of Israel who went down into Egypt.
KeyStory: Belah appears in the list of Jacob's family that came into Egypt.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Ben-ammi, Son of Lot
Summary: Ben-ammi was the son of Lot by his younger daughter, born in the cave after Sodom's destruction, and the ancestor of the Ammonites.
KeyStory: Lot's younger daughter bore Ben-ammi, whose name means 'son of my people,' and whose descendants became the nation of Ammon.
RelatedPeople: Lot; Lot's Wife; Moab, Son of Lot
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Beor
Summary: Beor was the father of Bela, the first king of Edom named in Genesis.
KeyStory: Beor is named only as Bela's father, in the list of Edom's kings.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Bera
Summary: Bera was the king of Sodom who rebelled against Chedorlaomer and lost the battle in the Valley of Siddim.
KeyStory: Bera's defeat left Sodom plundered and Lot captured — until Abram rescued them and Bera offered Abram the recovered goods, which Abram refused.
LifeLesson: Empires rise and fall, but God's promise to Abram outlasted every king of his day.

Name: Beriah
Summary: Beriah was a son of Asher, named among the children of Israel who went down into Egypt.
KeyStory: Beriah appears in the list of Jacob's family that came into Egypt.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Bethuel
Summary: Bethuel was the youngest son of Nahor and Milcah, and the father of Rebekah and Laban.
KeyStory: Bethuel's daughter Rebekah became Isaac's wife, tying Nahor's family to the promise line.
RelatedPeople: Nahor, Brother of Abraham; Milcah; Rebekah; Laban
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Bilhah
Summary: Bilhah was Rachel's handmaid, given to Jacob as a wife, and the mother of Dan and Naphtali.
KeyStory: When Rachel could not bear children, she gave Bilhah to Jacob, and Bilhah bore Dan and then Naphtali.
LifeLesson: God hears the unheard: Bilhah's sons became two tribes of Israel.

Name: Bilhan
Summary: Bilhan was a son of Ezer and a grandson of Seir the Horite.
KeyStory: Bilhan is named first among Ezer's three children.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Birsha
Summary: Birsha was the king of Gomorrah who joined Sodom's rebellion against Chedorlaomer and was defeated with him.
KeyStory: Birsha's city fell with Sodom's in the Valley of Siddim, and its people were carried off until Abram's rescue.
LifeLesson: Empires rise and fall, but God's promise to Abram outlasted every king of his day.

Name: Buz
Summary: Buz was a son of Nahor and Milcah, and the brother of Uz.
KeyStory: Buz is named among the eight children Milcah bore to Nahor in the family record after the binding of Isaac.
RelatedPeople: Nahor, Brother of Abraham; Milcah; Uz, Son of Nahor
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Cainan
Summary: Cainan was the son of Enos and the father of Mahalaleel. He lived 910 years.
KeyStory: Cainan stands in the godly line from Seth toward Noah, a link in the chain of generations.
LifeLesson: Faithfulness is often quiet: one generation passing the truth to the next.

Name: Canaan, Son of Ham
Summary: Canaan was the youngest son of Ham and the father of the Canaanite peoples.
KeyStory: After the flood, Noah's words about Canaan set the course for the land that would later bear his name.
LifeLesson: Sin has consequences that reach beyond one person — which is why grace matters so much.

Name: Carmi
Summary: Carmi was a son of Reuben, named among the children of Israel who went down into Egypt.
KeyStory: Carmi appears in the list of Jacob's family that came into Egypt.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Chedorlaomer
Summary: Chedorlaomer was the king of Elam who led the alliance of eastern kings against Sodom and Gomorrah.
KeyStory: After twelve years of rule, Chedorlaomer crushed a rebellion of the plain's cities, took Lot captive, and was himself routed by Abram's night attack.
LifeLesson: Empires rise and fall, but God's promise to Abram outlasted every king of his day.

Name: Cheran
Summary: Cheran was a son of Dishon, the son of Anah, and a descendant of Seir the Horite.
KeyStory: Cheran is named last among Dishon's four children.
RelatedPeople: Dishon, Son of Anah; Hemdan; Eshban; Ithran
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Chesed
Summary: Chesed was a son of Nahor and Milcah, named among the eight children Milcah bore him.
KeyStory: Chesed appears in the family record of Nahor, the branch of Abraham's family that stayed behind.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Cush
Summary: Cush was the son of Ham, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Cush appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Dan
Summary: Dan was the fifth son of Jacob, the first by Bilhah, and the father of Hushim.
KeyStory: Dan's tribe later became known for judging his people, just as Jacob had blessed him.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Deborah, Rebekah's Nurse
Summary: Deborah was the nurse who came with Rebekah from her homeland and stayed with her household until her death.
KeyStory: Deborah died near Bethel on Jacob's journey home and was buried under an oak called Allon-bachuth, the oak of weeping.
LifeLesson: A lifetime of quiet, faithful service is mourned deeply — Deborah's oak was named for weeping.

Name: Dedan, Son of Jokshan
Summary: Dedan was a son of Jokshan and a grandson of Abraham and Keturah.
KeyStory: Dedan is named with his brother Sheba among Jokshan's sons.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Dedan, Son of Raamah
Summary: Dedan was a son of Raamah and a grandson of Cush, in the line of Ham.
KeyStory: Dedan is named with his brother Sheba among Raamah's sons in the Table of Nations.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Diklah
Summary: Diklah was the son of Joktan, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Diklah appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Dinah
Summary: Dinah was the daughter of Jacob and Leah, and the sister of Jacob's twelve sons.
KeyStory: Dinah's story in Shechem led her brothers Simeon and Levi to take revenge on the whole city — a dark chapter of vengeance.
RelatedPeople: Jacob; Leah; Simeon, Son of Jacob; Levi; Shechem, Son of Hamor; Hamor
LifeLesson: Dinah's story warns us: one wrong answered with a greater wrong only multiplies the harm.

Name: Dishan
Summary: Dishan was a son of Seir the Horite, and the father of Uz and Aran.
KeyStory: Dishan is named among Seir's sons and among the dukes of the Horites.
RelatedPeople: Seir; Uz, Son of Dishan; Aran
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Dishon, Son of Anah
Summary: Dishon was a son of Anah and a grandson of Zibeon, and the father of Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
KeyStory: Dishon is named among Anah's children, a different Dishon from the son of Seir.
LifeLesson: Two men can share a name and walk very different paths; God knows each one.

Name: Sheba, Son of Raamah
Summary: Sheba was a son of Raamah and a grandson of Cush, in the line of Ham.
KeyStory: Sheba is named with his brother Dedan among Raamah's sons in the Table of Nations.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Shelah, Son of Judah
Summary: Shelah was the third son of Judah by the daughter of Shuah, kept back from marrying Tamar after his brothers died.
KeyStory: Shelah survived his brothers and fathered a line of his own, though Judah's promise to give him to Tamar was never kept.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Sheleph
Summary: Sheleph was the son of Joktan, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Sheleph appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Shemeber
Summary: Shemeber was the king of Zeboiim, one of the cities of the plain that rebelled against Chedorlaomer.
KeyStory: Shemeber's city fell with the other cities of the plain in the battle of the Valley of Siddim.
LifeLesson: Empires rise and fall, but God's promise to Abram outlasted every king of his day.

Name: Shepho
Summary: Shepho was a son of Shobal and a grandson of Seir the Horite.
KeyStory: Shepho is named among Shobal's five children.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Shillem
Summary: Shillem was a son of Naphtali, named among the children of Israel who went down into Egypt.
KeyStory: Shillem appears in the list of Jacob's family that came into Egypt.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Shimron
Summary: Shimron was a son of Issachar, named among the children of Israel who went down into Egypt.
KeyStory: Shimron appears in the list of Jacob's family that came into Egypt.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Shinab
Summary: Shinab was the king of Admah, one of the cities of the plain that rebelled against Chedorlaomer.
KeyStory: Shinab's city shared Sodom's defeat in the Valley of Siddim, where the kings fell into tar pits.
LifeLesson: Empires rise and fall, but God's promise to Abram outlasted every king of his day.

Name: Shobal
Summary: Shobal was a son of Seir the Horite, and the father of Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
KeyStory: Shobal is named among Seir's sons and among the dukes of the Horites.
RelatedPeople: Seir; Alvan; Manahath; Ebal; Shepho; Onam
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Shuah, Son of Keturah
Summary: Shuah was a son of Abraham and Keturah, named among the six children of Abraham's later marriage.
KeyStory: Shuah appears in the genealogy of Abraham's later children, who were sent eastward with gifts.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Shuah the Canaanite
Summary: Shuah was a Canaanite whose daughter married Judah, and whose grandsons were Er, Onan, and Shelah.
KeyStory: Judah married Shuah's daughter in Canaan, and her sons' story became part of the line leading to David.
RelatedPeople: Judah; Er; Onan; Shelah, Son of Judah
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Shuni
Summary: Shuni was a son of Gad, named among the children of Israel who went down into Egypt.
KeyStory: Shuni appears in the list of Jacob's family that came into Egypt.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Sidon
Summary: Sidon was the son of Canaan, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Sidon appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Simeon, Son of Jacob
Summary: Simeon was the second son of Jacob by Leah, and the father of Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul.
KeyStory: Simeon joined Levi in avenging Dinah at Shechem, and his tribe later scattered within Israel, just as Jacob had foretold.
RelatedPeople: Jacob; Leah; Levi; Dinah; Jemuel; Jamin; Ohad; Jachin; Zohar, Son of Simeon; Shaul
LifeLesson: Anger acted on without God leaves a legacy of scattering — Simeon's story is a warning.

Name: Tarshish
Summary: Tarshish was the son of Javan, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Tarshish appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Tebah
Summary: Tebah was a son of Nahor by his concubine Reumah.
KeyStory: Tebah is named among Reumah's four sons in the record of Nahor's family.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Tema
Summary: Tema was a son of Ishmael, named among the children born after Abraham's first family.
KeyStory: Tema appears in the genealogy of Abraham's later children and their descendants.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Teman
Summary: Teman was a son of Eliphaz, named among the dukes of Edom.
KeyStory: Teman appears in the record of Edom's dukes, the chiefs descended from Esau.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Terah
Summary: Terah was the son of Nahor and the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. He lived 205 years.
KeyStory: Terah led his family out of Ur toward Canaan, but they settled in Haran, where he died — and Abram's journey continued from there.
RelatedPeople: Nahor, Father of Terah; Abraham; Nahor, Brother of Abraham; Haran; Lot
LifeLesson: A journey can stall with one generation and resume with the next; God is patient with families.

Name: Thahash
Summary: Thahash was a son of Nahor by his concubine Reumah.
KeyStory: Thahash is named among Reumah's four sons in the record of Nahor's family.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Tidal
Summary: Tidal was the king of Goiim, called 'king of nations,' who joined Chedorlaomer's alliance.
KeyStory: Tidal marched with the eastern kings against the cities of the plain and was driven back by Abram.
LifeLesson: Empires rise and fall, but God's promise to Abram outlasted every king of his day.

Name: Timna
Role: Sister of Lotan; Concubine of Eliphaz
Summary: Timna was the sister of Lotan, daughter of Seir, and the concubine of Eliphaz, to whom she bore Amalek.
KeyStory: Timna links two houses of Edom: Seir's Horite family by birth, and Esau's line by her son Amalek.
RelatedPeople: Lotan; Seir; Eliphaz, Son of Esau; Amalek
LifeLesson: God names women in genealogies where the world might forget them.

Name: Timnah
Summary: Timnah was a duke of Edom, named among the chiefs who ruled by their families and dwelling places.
KeyStory: Timnah appears in the closing list of Edom's dukes, the chiefs descended from Esau.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Tiras
Summary: Tiras was the son of Japheth, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Tiras appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Togarmah
Summary: Togarmah was the son of Gomer, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Togarmah appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Tola
Summary: Tola was a son of Issachar, named among the children of Israel who went down into Egypt.
KeyStory: Tola appears in the list of Jacob's family that came into Egypt.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Tubal-cain
Summary: Tubal-cain was the son of Lamech and Zillah, an instructor of everyone who works in bronze and iron.
KeyStory: Tubal-cain forged tools and weapons from metal, opening the age of craftsmanship.
RelatedPeople: Lamech, Son of Methusael; Zillah; Naamah
LifeLesson: Skill and craftsmanship are God-given — and like every gift, they can serve good or harm.

Name: Tubal
Summary: Tubal was the son of Japheth, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Tubal appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Uz, Son of Aram
Summary: Uz was a son of Aram and a grandson of Shem, named in the Table of Nations.
KeyStory: Uz appears among Aram's sons, one of the branches of Shem's line after the flood.
RelatedPeople: Aram, Son of Shem; Hul; Gether; Mash
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Uz, Son of Dishan
Summary: Uz was a son of Dishan and a grandson of Seir the Horite.
KeyStory: Uz is named with his brother Aran among Dishan's children.
LifeLesson: Three men named Uz appear in Genesis, and God knows each one apart.

Name: Uz, Son of Nahor
Summary: Uz, also called Huz, was the firstborn son of Nahor and Milcah, and the brother of Buz.
KeyStory: Uz heads the list of the eight children Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother.
RelatedPeople: Nahor, Brother of Abraham; Milcah; Buz
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Uzal
Summary: Uzal was the son of Joktan, named among the nations that spread across the earth after the flood.
KeyStory: Uzal appears in the Table of Nations, tracing the peoples of the earth back to Noah's family.
LifeLesson: God's promise to fill the earth moved forward through families like this one.

Name: Zaavan
Summary: Zaavan was a son of Ezer and a grandson of Seir the Horite.
KeyStory: Zaavan is named among Ezer's three children.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Zebulun
Summary: Zebulun was the tenth son of Jacob, the sixth by Leah, and the father of Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
KeyStory: Zebulun's tribe later dwelt by the seashore, just as Jacob had blessed him.
RelatedPeople: Jacob; Leah; Sered; Elon, Son of Zebulun; Jahleel
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Zepho
Summary: Zepho was a son of Eliphaz, named among the dukes of Edom.
KeyStory: Zepho appears in the record of Edom's dukes, the chiefs descended from Esau.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Zerah of Bozrah
Summary: Zerah of Bozrah was the father of Jobab, who reigned as king in Edom.
KeyStory: Zerah is named only as Jobab's father, in the list of Edom's kings — a different Zerah from Judah's and Reuel's sons.
LifeLesson: Three men named Zerah appear in Genesis, and God knows each one apart.

Name: Zerah, Son of Judah
Summary: Zerah was the twin son of Judah and Tamar, whose hand came out first at birth, marked with a scarlet thread.
KeyStory: Zerah's scarlet thread marked him first, but his brother Pharez was born before him and carried the line forward.
LifeLesson: Being first out of the gate is not the same as carrying the promise.

Name: Zerah, Son of Reuel
Summary: Zerah was a son of Reuel and a grandson of Esau by Bashemath, Ishmael's daughter, and one of the dukes of Edom.
KeyStory: Zerah is named among Reuel's four sons and among the dukes that came of Reuel in Edom.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Zibeon
Summary: Zibeon was a son of Seir the Horite, and the father of Ajah and Anah.
KeyStory: Zibeon is named among Seir's sons and among the dukes of the Horites.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Zillah
Summary: Zillah was Lamech's other wife and the mother of Tubal-cain and Naamah.
KeyStory: Zillah listened as Lamech boasted of his revenge, a dark moment in the early story of humanity.
RelatedPeople: Lamech, Son of Methusael; Tubal-cain; Naamah
LifeLesson: Even in a household marked by violence, God still knew Zillah by name.

Name: Zilpah
Summary: Zilpah was Leah's handmaid, given to Jacob as a wife, and the mother of Gad and Asher.
KeyStory: When Leah stopped bearing children, she gave Zilpah to Jacob, and Zilpah bore Gad and then Asher.
LifeLesson: God hears the unheard: Zilpah's sons became two tribes of Israel.

Name: Zimran
Summary: Zimran was a son of Abraham and Keturah, named among the children born after Abraham's first family.
KeyStory: Zimran appears in the genealogy of Abraham's later children and their descendants.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Ziphion
Summary: Ziphion was a son of Gad, named among the children of Israel who went down into Egypt.
KeyStory: Ziphion appears in the list of Jacob's family that came into Egypt.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Zohar, Father of Ephron
Summary: Zohar was the father of Ephron the Hittite, from whom Abraham bought the cave of Machpelah.
KeyStory: Zohar is named only as Ephron's father, in the transaction that gave Abraham his first owned land in Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Zohar, Son of Simeon
Summary: Zohar was a son of Simeon and a grandson of Jacob, named among the family that went into Egypt.
KeyStory: Zohar is named among Simeon's six sons — a different Zohar from the father of Ephron.
RelatedPeople: Simeon, Son of Jacob; Jemuel; Jamin; Ohad; Jachin; Shaul
LifeLesson: Two men can share a name and walk very different paths; God knows each one.

Name: Abiasaph, Son of Korah
Summary: Abiasaph was a son of Korah, the Levite, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Abiasaph is named with his brothers Assir and Elkanah among Korah's sons.
RelatedPeople: Korah, Son of Izhar; Assir, Son of Korah; Elkanah, Son of Korah
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Abihu
Summary: Abihu was a son of Aaron and Elisheba, and one of the priests of Israel.
KeyStory: Abihu went up Mount Sinai with Moses and saw God, but later offered strange fire with his brother Nadab and died.
LifeLesson: Closeness to God is no substitute for obedience: Abihu saw God and still offered strange fire.

Name: Ahisamach
Summary: Ahisamach was of the tribe of Dan, and the father of Aholiab, the craftsman of the tabernacle.
KeyStory: Ahisamach is named only as Aholiab's father, in the record of the tabernacle's builders.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Aholiab
Summary: Aholiab, also spelled Oholiab, was the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, and Bezaleel's fellow craftsman on the tabernacle.
KeyStory: God gave Aholiab skill alongside Bezaleel, and together they made the tabernacle, the ark, and the priestly garments.
LifeLesson: Art and craftsmanship are Spirit-given gifts, made for God's house.

Name: Amminadab
Summary: Amminadab was the father of Elisheba, Aaron's wife, and of Naashon, the prince of Judah.
KeyStory: Amminadab's children tied the priestly line to Judah's royal line: his daughter married Aaron, his son led Judah.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Amram
Role: Father of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
Summary: Amram was a son of Kohath, of the tribe of Levi, and the husband of Jochebed. His children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
KeyStory: Amram married Jochebed, and their son Moses, hidden at birth from Pharaoh's decree, became the deliverer of Israel.
LifeLesson: Faithful parents in dark times can raise the very person God will use.

Name: Assir, Son of Korah
Summary: Assir was a son of Korah, the Levite, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Assir is named with his brothers Elkanah and Abiasaph among Korah's sons.
RelatedPeople: Korah, Son of Izhar; Elkanah, Son of Korah; Abiasaph, Son of Korah
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Bezaleel
Summary: Bezaleel, also spelled Bezalel, was the son of Uri, of the tribe of Judah, and the chief craftsman of the tabernacle.
KeyStory: God filled Bezaleel with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, understanding, and knowledge, to design and build the tabernacle and all its furnishings.
LifeLesson: Art and craftsmanship are Spirit-given gifts, made for God's house.

Name: Eleazar
Summary: Eleazar was a son of Aaron and Elisheba, and the priest who succeeded Aaron after his death.
KeyStory: Eleazar served through the wilderness years, stood with Joshua at the division of the land, and carried the priesthood after Aaron.
RelatedPeople: Aaron; Elisheba; Nadab; Abihu; Ithamar; Phinehas
LifeLesson: Faithfulness over a long life is its own kind of greatness.

Name: Eliezer, Son of Moses
Summary: Eliezer was the second son of Moses and Zipporah, born in Midian — a different Eliezer from Abraham's steward.
KeyStory: Moses named him Eliezer, saying, 'The God of my father was my help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.'
LifeLesson: Two men can share a name and walk very different paths; God knows each one.

Name: Elisheba
Summary: Elisheba was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Naashon, and the wife of Aaron. She bore him Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
KeyStory: Elisheba became the mother of Israel's priestly line, standing at the head of the family that would serve in the tabernacle.
RelatedPeople: Aaron; Amminadab; Naashon; Nadab; Abihu; Eleazar; Ithamar
LifeLesson: God names women in genealogies where the world might forget them.

Name: Elkanah, Son of Korah
Summary: Elkanah was a son of Korah, the Levite, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe — a different Elkanah from Samuel's father.
KeyStory: Elkanah is named with his brothers Assir and Abiasaph among Korah's sons.
RelatedPeople: Korah, Son of Izhar; Assir, Son of Korah; Abiasaph, Son of Korah
LifeLesson: Two men can share a name and walk very different paths; God knows each one.

Name: Elzaphan
Summary: Elzaphan was a son of Uzziel and a grandson of Kohath, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Elzaphan and his brother Mishael were called by Moses to carry the bodies of Nadab and Abihu out of the camp.
LifeLesson: Obedience sometimes means hard, holy work no one else wants to do.

Name: Gershom
Summary: Gershom was the firstborn son of Moses and Zipporah, born in Midian during Moses' exile.
KeyStory: Moses named him Gershom, saying, 'I have been a stranger in a strange land.'
RelatedPeople: Moses; Zipporah; Eliezer, Son of Moses; Jethro
LifeLesson: Even in exile, God was building Moses' family for the journey ahead.

Name: Hebron, Son of Kohath
Summary: Hebron was a son of Kohath and a grandson of Levi, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Hebron is named among Kohath's four sons — Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel — in the record of Levi's house.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Hur
Summary: Hur was a companion of Moses who held up his hands during the battle with Amalek, and who was left in charge of the people with Aaron while Moses was on the mountain.
KeyStory: When Moses' hands grew heavy, Aaron and Hur held them up until sunset, and Israel prevailed over Amalek.
LifeLesson: Victory often comes through the friends who hold your arms up when you cannot.

Name: Ithamar
Summary: Ithamar was the youngest son of Aaron and Elisheba, and one of the priests of Israel.
KeyStory: Ithamar oversaw the Levites' work on the tabernacle, keeping account of the gold, silver, and bronze used in its making.
LifeLesson: Faithful stewardship of holy things is holy work itself.

Name: Izhar
Summary: Izhar was a son of Kohath and a grandson of Levi, and the father of Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
KeyStory: Izhar's son Korah would later lead a rebellion against Moses and Aaron — a warning from within Levi's own house.
RelatedPeople: Kohath; Korah, Son of Izhar; Nepheg; Zichri
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Jethro
Role: Priest of Midian; Father-in-Law of Moses
Summary: Jethro was the priest of Midian, the father of Zipporah, and Moses' father-in-law. He is also called Reuel.
KeyStory: Jethro sheltered Moses in Midian, gave him Zipporah as wife, and later advised him to share the burden of judging Israel — counsel Moses followed.
RelatedPeople: Moses; Zipporah; Gershom; Eliezer, Son of Moses
LifeLesson: Wise counsel from outside the family can be God's gift: Jethro taught Moses to share the load.

Name: Jochebed
Role: Mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
Summary: Jochebed was a daughter of Levi, the wife of Amram, and the mother of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
KeyStory: When Pharaoh ordered Hebrew boys drowned, Jochebed hid baby Moses three months, then set him in a basket among the reeds — and later nursed him in Pharaoh's own house.
RelatedPeople: Amram; Moses; Aaron; Miriam; Pharaoh's Daughter
LifeLesson: A mother's courage can carry a child from a basket of reeds to the palace — and to a calling.

Name: Korah, Son of Izhar
Summary: Korah was a son of Izhar, a Levite, and the father of Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph — a different Korah from Esau's son.
KeyStory: Korah is named in Exodus among Levi's house; his later rebellion against Moses is told in Numbers, where the earth swallowed him and his followers.
RelatedPeople: Izhar; Assir, Son of Korah; Elkanah, Son of Korah; Abiasaph, Son of Korah; Moses; Aaron
LifeLesson: Gifts and position do not equal God's calling: Korah wanted Aaron's place and lost everything.

Name: Libni
Summary: Libni was a son of Gershon and a grandson of Levi, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Libni is named with his brother Shimi among Gershon's sons in the record of Levi's house.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Mahali
Summary: Mahali was a son of Merari and a grandson of Levi, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Mahali is named with his brother Mushi among Merari's sons in the record of Levi's house.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Mishael
Summary: Mishael was a son of Uzziel and a grandson of Kohath, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Mishael and his brother Elzaphan were called by Moses to carry the bodies of Nadab and Abihu out of the camp.
LifeLesson: Obedience sometimes means hard, holy work no one else wants to do.

Name: Mushi
Summary: Mushi was a son of Merari and a grandson of Levi, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Mushi is named with his brother Mahali among Merari's sons in the record of Levi's house.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Naashon
Summary: Naashon was the son of Amminadab and the brother of Elisheba, and the prince of the tribe of Judah. In Numbers his name is spelled Nahshon.
KeyStory: Naashon led Judah's offerings for the tabernacle and marched at the head of Israel's tribes through the wilderness.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Nadab
Summary: Nadab was the firstborn son of Aaron and Elisheba, and one of the priests of Israel.
KeyStory: Nadab went up Mount Sinai with Moses and saw God, but later offered strange fire before the LORD and died — a warning about worship on God's terms, not ours.
LifeLesson: Closeness to God is no substitute for obedience: Nadab saw God and still offered strange fire.

Name: Nepheg
Summary: Nepheg was a son of Izhar and a grandson of Kohath, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Nepheg is named with his brothers Korah and Zichri among Izhar's sons.
RelatedPeople: Izhar; Korah, Son of Izhar; Zichri
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Nun, Father of Joshua
Summary: Nun was of the tribe of Ephraim, and the father of Joshua, Moses' successor.
KeyStory: Nun is named only as Joshua's father — yet his son led Israel into the land Moses could only see.
LifeLesson: A parent's legacy can be a child who finishes what you only began.

Name: Pharaoh's Daughter
Summary: Pharaoh's daughter found the baby Moses in a basket among the reeds and raised him as her own son in Pharaoh's house.
KeyStory: Though her father had ordered Hebrew boys drowned, she had compassion on the crying child, hired his own mother as his nurse, and named him Moses.
LifeLesson: Compassion can defy even a king's decree — and change the course of a nation.

Name: Phinehas
Summary: Phinehas was the son of Eleazar and the grandson of Aaron, and a priest known for his zeal for God's honor.
KeyStory: Phinehas turned away God's wrath in the wilderness by acting against open sin, and God gave him a covenant of an everlasting priesthood.
LifeLesson: Zeal for God's honor, rightly aimed, can turn away wrath and save a people.

Name: Puah
Summary: Puah was one of the two Hebrew midwives who feared God and refused Pharaoh's order to kill newborn Hebrew boys.
KeyStory: When Pharaoh commanded the midwives to kill every Hebrew son at birth, Puah and Shiphrah let the boys live — and God gave them families of their own.
LifeLesson: Fearing God matters more than fearing a king — even when disobedience is dangerous.

Name: Putiel
Summary: Putiel was the father of the wife of Eleazar, and the grandfather of Phinehas.
KeyStory: Putiel is named only in the genealogy of Aaron's house, as the father of Eleazar's wife.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Shimi
Summary: Shimi was a son of Gershon and a grandson of Levi, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Shimi is named with his brother Libni among Gershon's sons in the record of Levi's house.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Shiphrah
Summary: Shiphrah was one of the two Hebrew midwives who feared God and refused Pharaoh's order to kill newborn Hebrew boys.
KeyStory: When Pharaoh commanded the midwives to kill every Hebrew son at birth, Shiphrah and Puah let the boys live — and God dealt well with them.
LifeLesson: Fearing God matters more than fearing a king — even when disobedience is dangerous.

Name: Uri
Summary: Uri was the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and the father of Bezaleel, the craftsman of the tabernacle.
KeyStory: Uri is named only as Bezaleel's father, in the line that gave Israel its master craftsman.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Uzziel
Summary: Uzziel was a son of Kohath and a grandson of Levi, and the father of Mishael, Elzaphan, and Zithri.
KeyStory: Uzziel's sons Mishael and Elzaphan were the ones called to carry Nadab and Abihu out of the sanctuary after their deaths.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Zichri
Summary: Zichri was a son of Izhar and a grandson of Kohath, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Zichri is named with his brothers Korah and Nepheg among Izhar's sons.
RelatedPeople: Izhar; Korah, Son of Izhar; Nepheg
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Zipporah
Summary: Zipporah was a daughter of Jethro, priest of Midian, and the wife of Moses. She bore him Gershom and Eliezer.
KeyStory: Zipporah married Moses during his years in Midian, and on the journey back to Egypt she acted swiftly to spare Moses' life.
RelatedPeople: Moses; Jethro; Gershom; Eliezer, Son of Moses
LifeLesson: A spouse's quick, brave action can save the very mission God gave.

Name: Zithri
Summary: Zithri was a son of Uzziel and a grandson of Kohath, named in the genealogy of Moses' tribe.
KeyStory: Zithri is named with his brothers Mishael and Elzaphan among Uzziel's sons.
LifeLesson: God's story keeps moving through families we know almost nothing about — and He knows them all.

Name: Dibri
Summary: Dibri was of the tribe of Dan, and the father of Shelomith.
KeyStory: Dibri is named only as Shelomith's father, in the account of his grandson's blasphemy and stoning.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Shelomith
Summary: Shelomith was the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan, and the mother of the man who blasphemed the Name and was stoned.
KeyStory: Shelomith's son fought with an Israelite in the camp, blasphemed the Name, and was put in custody until Moses inquired of the LORD — and her name is preserved in the law that followed.
LifeLesson: A mother's name can be remembered even in her family's hardest chapter — God does not look away.

Name: Son of Shelomith
Summary: The son of Shelomith — Scripture gives him no name — was a man of mixed parentage, his father an Egyptian, who blasphemed the Name during a fight in the camp.
KeyStory: After he cursed the Name, Moses put him in custody, inquired of the LORD, and the whole congregation stoned him outside the camp — establishing the law that whoever blasphemes the Name shall be put to death.
LifeLesson: Words against God's holy Name are no small thing: what we say about Him reveals what we believe about Him.

Name: Abidan, Son of Gideoni
Summary: Abidan, son of Gideoni, was the prince of the tribe of Benjamin at the census in the wilderness.
KeyStory: Abidan led Benjamin's 35,400 men and brought the tribe's offering for the dedication of the altar.
LifeLesson: Small tribes are still fully counted in God's camp.

Name: Abiezer
Summary: Abiezer, son of Gilead — called Jeezer in the census list — founded a clan of Manasseh whose families later settled west of the Jordan.
KeyStory: Abiezer's clan is named in the second census and again when the daughters of Zelophehad's kinsmen received their inheritance.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Abihail, Father of Zuriel
Summary: Abihail is named in Numbers as the father of Zuriel, chief of the Merarites.
KeyStory: Abihail's son Zuriel oversaw the Levites who carried the tabernacle's frames.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Abiram
Summary: Abiram, son of Eliab, joined Korah's rebellion against Moses and Aaron and refused to come up when Moses summoned him.
KeyStory: Abiram stood at the door of his tent with his family as the ground opened and swallowed the rebels alive.
RelatedPeople: Dathan; Eliab, Son of Pallu; Korah, Son of Izhar; Moses; Aaron
LifeLesson: Pride that will not listen ends where the ground gives way.

Name: Achan
Summary: Achan, son of Carmi, took devoted plunder at Jericho and brought defeat on Israel at Ai, and he and his household were stoned in the Valley of Achor.
KeyStory: When Israel fled before Ai, Joshua found that Achan had hidden a Babylonian garment, silver, and gold in his tent, and Israel stoned him and burned what was his.
RelatedPeople: Carmi, Son of Zabdi; Zabdi, Father of Carmi; Joshua
LifeLesson: One man's hidden sin can defeat a whole people — and confession is the only way back.

Name: Achsah, Daughter of Caleb
Summary: Achsah, daughter of Caleb, married Othniel who captured Kirjath-sepher, and she asked her father for springs of water to go with her dry field.
KeyStory: Achsah boldly asked Caleb for the upper and lower springs, and he gave her both.
LifeLesson: Ask for the springs, not just the field.

Name: Adoni-zedek, King of Jerusalem
Summary: Adoni-zedek was king of Jerusalem when he heard that Gibeon had made peace with Israel, and he led five kings against Gibeon.
KeyStory: Adoni-zedek's alliance was shattered by hailstones and a lengthened day at Beth-horon, and he was hanged with the four other kings at Makkedah.
RelatedPeople: Hoham, King of Hebron; Piram, King of Jarmuth; Japhia, King of Lachish; Debir, King of Eglon; Joshua
LifeLesson: Five kings against one God is still no contest.

Name: Ahiezer, Son of Ammishaddai
Summary: Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai, was the prince of the tribe of Dan at the census in the wilderness.
KeyStory: Ahiezer led Dan's 62,700 men and brought the tribe's offering for the dedication of the altar.
LifeLesson: Strength is a trust to be offered back to God.

Name: Ahihud, Son of Shelomi
Summary: Ahihud, Son of Shelomi was the prince of Asher appointed to divide the land of Canaan by inheritance among the tribes.
KeyStory: Ahihud was named by the LORD, with Eleazar and Joshua, to apportion the promised land to the nine and a half tribes.
LifeLesson: Dividing what God gives takes honest hands.

Name: Ahiman, Son of Anak
Summary: Ahiman, son of Anak, was one of the Anakim the spies saw dwelling in Hebron.
KeyStory: The spies found Ahiman in Hebron and carried home a report of giants that melted Israel's courage.
RelatedPeople: Anak; Sheshai, Son of Anak; Talmai, Son of Anak; Caleb
LifeLesson: A fearful report can undo a whole people; a faithful one can steady them.

Name: Ahira, Son of Enan
Summary: Ahira, son of Enan, was the prince of the tribe of Naphtali at the census in the wilderness.
KeyStory: Ahira led Naphtali's 53,400 men and brought the tribe's offering for the dedication of the altar.
LifeLesson: The last tribe in line is still named, counted, and given its offering.

Name: Ammiel, Son of Gemalli
Summary: Ammiel, Son of Gemalli was one of the twelve spies Moses sent from the tribe of Dan to search out the land of Canaan.
KeyStory: Ammiel spent forty days spying out Canaan, then joined the ten who brought back a fearful report that turned Israel back into the wilderness.
LifeLesson: Seeing the same land as Caleb, he saw only giants — faith is a choice about what you trust.

Name: Ammihud
Summary: Ammihud is named in Numbers as the father of Elishama the prince of Ephraim, and of Shemuel and Pedahel among the men who divided the land.
KeyStory: Ammihud's sons served Israel in the wilderness and in the dividing of Canaan.
RelatedPeople: Elishama, Son of Ammihud; Shemuel, Son of Ammihud; Pedahel, Son of Ammihud; Moses
LifeLesson: A father's legacy is measured in the service of his children.

Name: Ammishaddai
Summary: Ammishaddai is named in Numbers as the father of Ahiezer.
KeyStory: Ammishaddai is named only as the father of Ahiezer, in the census and camp order of Israel.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Anak
Summary: Anak was the forefather of the Anakim, the tall people of Canaan whose size frightened the ten spies.
KeyStory: The spies reported the sons of Anak in Hebron, and Israel felt like grasshoppers beside them — but Caleb still urged them to go up at once.
RelatedPeople: Ahiman, Son of Anak; Sheshai, Son of Anak; Talmai, Son of Anak; Caleb; Joshua
LifeLesson: Giants look smaller to those who remember who promised the land.

Name: Arad
Summary: Arad was the Canaanite king of the south who attacked Israel on the march and took some of them prisoner.
KeyStory: Israel vowed to destroy the cities of Arad's king, and the LORD delivered the Canaanites into their hand at Hormah.
LifeLesson: A vow made to God in defeat can become a victory in His time.

Name: Arba, Father of Anak
Summary: Arba, father of Anak, was the greatest man among the Anakim, and Kirjath-arba — that is, Hebron — was named for him.
KeyStory: Arba's name lived on in the city of the Anakim until Caleb drove them out and took Hebron for his inheritance.
LifeLesson: Even giants have fathers, and even their cities change hands.

Name: Asriel, Son of Gilead
Summary: Asriel, son of Gilead, founded a clan of Manasseh east of the Jordan.
KeyStory: Asriel is named among the sons of Gilead in the second census of Israel.
RelatedPeople: Gilead, Son of Machir; Machir, Son of Manasseh
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Azzan
Summary: Azzan is named in Numbers as the father of Paltiel, one of the princes who divided the land.
KeyStory: Azzan is named only as the father of Paltiel, appointed to apportion Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Balaam
Summary: Balaam, son of Beor, was a prophet from Pethor whom Balak king of Moab hired to curse Israel — but God put blessings in his mouth instead.
KeyStory: On the road to Moab, Balaam's donkey spoke to him and turned from the angel of the LORD; from the heights he blessed Israel four times and foretold a star out of Jacob.
RelatedPeople: Balak; Beor, Father of Balaam; Moses
LifeLesson: No payment can buy a curse on those God has blessed.

Name: Balak
Summary: Balak, son of Zippor, was king of Moab when Israel approached his land, and he hired Balaam to curse them.
KeyStory: Balak watched Israel camp on his border and sent for Balaam again and again, but every oracle came back a blessing.
LifeLesson: Fear of God's people only grows when you fight the God who keeps them.

Name: Beor, Father of Balaam
Summary: Beor is named in Numbers as the father of Balaam the prophet from Pethor.
KeyStory: Beor's son Balaam was hired to curse Israel and instead blessed them four times.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Bohan, Son of Reuben
Summary: Bohan, son of Reuben, is named in the stone that marked the border of Judah's inheritance.
KeyStory: The stone of Bohan stood on the boundary line between Judah and Benjamin, a landmark named for a man.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Bukki, Son of Jogli
Summary: Bukki, Son of Jogli was the prince of Dan appointed to divide the land of Canaan by inheritance among the tribes.
KeyStory: Bukki was named by the LORD, with Eleazar and Joshua, to apportion the promised land to the nine and a half tribes.
LifeLesson: Dividing what God gives takes honest hands.

Name: Carmi, Son of Zabdi
Summary: Carmi, son of Zabdi, was the father of Achan, whose taking of devoted plunder at Jericho cost Israel the battle of Ai.
KeyStory: Carmi's son Achan confessed to hiding a garment, silver, and gold, and the whole household paid for the sin.
RelatedPeople: Zabdi, Father of Carmi; Achan; Joshua
LifeLesson: A father's name can be remembered through a son's worst day — and still be worth redeeming.

Name: Chislon
Summary: Chislon is named in Numbers as the father of Elidad, one of the princes who divided the land.
KeyStory: Chislon is named only as the father of Elidad, appointed to apportion Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Cozbi
Summary: Cozbi, daughter of Zur, a prince of Midian, was brought into the camp by Zimri at the height of Israel's idolatry at Peor.
KeyStory: Cozbi was slain with Zimri by Phinehas, and her death marked the end of the plague on Israel.
RelatedPeople: Zimri, Son of Salu; Zur; Phinehas
LifeLesson: The pleasures of idolatry end where God's holiness begins.

Name: Dathan
Summary: Dathan, son of Eliab, joined Korah's rebellion against Moses and Aaron and refused to come up when Moses summoned him.
KeyStory: Dathan stood at the door of his tent with his family as the ground opened and swallowed the rebels alive.
RelatedPeople: Abiram; Eliab, Son of Pallu; Korah, Son of Izhar; Moses; Aaron
LifeLesson: Refusing God's appointed leadership is refusing God Himself.

Name: Debir, King of Eglon
Summary: Debir was king of Eglon and one of the five kings who allied against Gibeon and were defeated by Joshua.
KeyStory: Debir joined Adoni-zedek against Gibeon, fled to the cave at Makkedah, and was hanged with the other four kings.
LifeLesson: Alliances against God end in the same cave.

Name: Deuel
Summary: Deuel is named in Numbers as the father of Eliasaph the prince of Gad; in the camp order he is also called Reuel.
KeyStory: Deuel's son Eliasaph led the tribe of Gad through the wilderness.
LifeLesson: God knows His people under every name they are called.

Name: Eldad
Summary: Eldad was one of the seventy elders on whom the Spirit rested in the wilderness; though he stayed in the camp, he prophesied there.
KeyStory: When the Spirit fell on the elders, Eldad prophesied in the camp, and Moses refused to stop him, wishing all the LORD's people were prophets.
LifeLesson: God's Spirit is not confined to the place where we expect Him.

Name: Eliab, Son of Helon
Summary: Eliab, son of Helon, was the prince of the tribe of Zebulun at the census in the wilderness.
KeyStory: Eliab led Zebulun's 57,400 men and brought the tribe's offering for the dedication of the altar.
LifeLesson: A name shared with others still belongs to one man's own calling.

Name: Eliab, Son of Pallu
Summary: Eliab, son of Pallu, was the father of Dathan and Abiram, the Reubenites who joined Korah's rebellion.
KeyStory: Eliab's sons Dathan and Abiram rose against Moses and were swallowed by the earth with their households.
LifeLesson: A father's grief can be the warning a whole people needs to hear.

Name: Eliasaph, Son of Deuel
Summary: Eliasaph, son of Deuel, was the prince of the tribe of Gad at the census in the wilderness; in the camp order he is also called the son of Reuel.
KeyStory: Eliasaph led Gad's 45,650 men and brought the tribe's offering for the dedication of the altar.
LifeLesson: Two names for one man remind us that Scripture is a family record, not a list of strangers.

Name: Eliasaph, Son of Lael
Summary: Eliasaph, son of Lael, was the chief of the Gershonites, the Levites who carried the tabernacle's curtains and coverings.
KeyStory: Eliasaph oversaw the Gershonite families in their service of carrying the dwelling place of God.
LifeLesson: Not all service is seen — some of it is carrying the very walls of worship.

Name: Elidad, Son of Chislon
Summary: Elidad, Son of Chislon was the prince of Benjamin appointed to divide the land of Canaan by inheritance among the tribes.
KeyStory: Elidad was named by the LORD, with Eleazar and Joshua, to apportion the promised land to the nine and a half tribes.
LifeLesson: Dividing what God gives takes honest hands.

Name: Elishama, Son of Ammihud
Summary: Elishama, son of Ammihud, was the prince of the tribe of Ephraim at the census in the wilderness, and the grandfather of Joshua.
KeyStory: Elishama led Ephraim's 40,500 men and brought the tribe's offering for the dedication of the altar.
LifeLesson: The faith of one generation can put the next in sight of the promised land.

Name: Elizaphan, Son of Parnach
Summary: Elizaphan, Son of Parnach was the prince of Zebulun appointed to divide the land of Canaan by inheritance among the tribes.
KeyStory: Elizaphan was named by the LORD, with Eleazar and Joshua, to apportion the promised land to the nine and a half tribes.
LifeLesson: Dividing what God gives takes honest hands.

Name: Elizur, Son of Shedeur
Summary: Elizur, son of Shedeur, was the prince of the tribe of Reuben at the census in the wilderness.
KeyStory: Elizur led Reuben's 46,500 men and brought the tribe's offering for the dedication of the altar.
LifeLesson: God counts His people tribe by tribe — no one is lost in the crowd.

Name: Enan
Summary: Enan is named in Numbers as the father of Ahira.
KeyStory: Enan is named only as the father of Ahira, in the census and camp order of Israel.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Ephod
Summary: Ephod is named in Numbers as the father of Hanniel, one of the princes who divided the land.
KeyStory: Ephod is named only as the father of Hanniel, appointed to apportion Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Eran
Summary: Eran, son of Ephraim, founded a clan of Ephraim named in the second census.
KeyStory: Eran is named among the sons of Ephraim when Israel was counted a second time in the plains of Moab.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Evi
Summary: Evi was one of the five kings of Midian slain by Israel in the war that followed the idolatry at Peor.
KeyStory: Evi fell to Israel's sword when Moses sent a thousand men of every tribe against Midian.
RelatedPeople: Rekem; Zur; Hur, King of Midian; Reba; Moses; Phinehas
LifeLesson: The gods of Midian could not protect their own kings.

Name: Gaddi, Son of Susi
Summary: Gaddi, Son of Susi was one of the twelve spies Moses sent from the tribe of Manasseh to search out the land of Canaan.
KeyStory: Gaddi spent forty days spying out Canaan, then joined the ten who brought back a fearful report that turned Israel back into the wilderness.
LifeLesson: Seeing the same land as Caleb, he saw only giants — faith is a choice about what you trust.

Name: Gaddiel, Son of Sodi
Summary: Gaddiel, Son of Sodi was one of the twelve spies Moses sent from the tribe of Zebulun to search out the land of Canaan.
KeyStory: Gaddiel spent forty days spying out Canaan, then joined the ten who brought back a fearful report that turned Israel back into the wilderness.
LifeLesson: Seeing the same land as Caleb, he saw only giants — faith is a choice about what you trust.

Name: Gamaliel, Son of Pedahzur
Summary: Gamaliel, son of Pedahzur, was the prince of the tribe of Manasseh at the census in the wilderness.
KeyStory: Gamaliel led Manasseh's 32,200 men and brought the tribe's offering for the dedication of the altar.
LifeLesson: God gives every tribe its own leader and its own part to play.

Name: Gemalli
Summary: Gemalli is named in Numbers as the father of Ammiel, one of the twelve spies.
KeyStory: Gemalli is named only as the father of Ammiel, whom Moses sent to search out Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Geuel, Son of Machi
Summary: Geuel, Son of Machi was one of the twelve spies Moses sent from the tribe of Gad to search out the land of Canaan.
KeyStory: Geuel spent forty days spying out Canaan, then joined the ten who brought back a fearful report that turned Israel back into the wilderness.
LifeLesson: Seeing the same land as Caleb, he saw only giants — faith is a choice about what you trust.

Name: Gideoni
Summary: Gideoni is named in Numbers as the father of Abidan.
KeyStory: Gideoni is named only as the father of Abidan, in the census and camp order of Israel.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Gilead, Son of Machir
Summary: Gilead, son of Machir son of Manasseh, gave his name to the land of Gilead east of the Jordan.
KeyStory: Gilead's descendants, including Zelophehad and his daughters, inherited the hills that still bear his name.
RelatedPeople: Machir, Son of Manasseh; Hepher, Son of Gilead; Zelophehad; Manasseh
LifeLesson: A name can become a place where generations live.

Name: Hanniel, Son of Ephod
Summary: Hanniel, Son of Ephod was the prince of Manasseh appointed to divide the land of Canaan by inheritance among the tribes.
KeyStory: Hanniel was named by the LORD, with Eleazar and Joshua, to apportion the promised land to the nine and a half tribes.
LifeLesson: Dividing what God gives takes honest hands.

Name: Helek
Summary: Helek, son of Gilead, founded a clan of Manasseh east of the Jordan.
KeyStory: Helek is named among the sons of Gilead in the second census of Israel.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Helon
Summary: Helon is named in Numbers as the father of Eliab.
KeyStory: Helon is named only as the father of Eliab, in the census and camp order of Israel.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Hepher, Son of Gilead
Summary: Hepher, son of Gilead, was the father of Zelophehad, whose five daughters won the right of daughters to inherit.
KeyStory: Hepher's line ran through Zelophehad to five daughters who stood before Moses and asked for their father's inheritance.
LifeLesson: A father's inheritance can pass through daughters who dare to ask.

Name: Hobab
Summary: Hobab, son of Raguel the Midianite, was the brother-in-law of Moses, who asked him to guide Israel through the wilderness he knew.
KeyStory: Moses begged Hobab not to leave them, saying he would be as eyes to Israel in the desert.
LifeLesson: Knowledge of the road is a gift worth offering to God's people.

Name: Hoglah
Summary: Hoglah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who asked Moses for their father's inheritance.
KeyStory: Hoglah stood with her sisters before Moses and the congregation, and God granted daughters the right to inherit when there is no son.
RelatedPeople: Zelophehad; Mahlah; Noah, Daughter of Zelophehad; Milcah, Daughter of Zelophehad; Tirzah; Moses
LifeLesson: Five sisters standing together changed the law of inheritance.

Name: Hoham, King of Hebron
Summary: Hoham was king of Hebron and one of the five kings who allied against Gibeon and were defeated by Joshua.
KeyStory: Hoham joined Adoni-zedek against Gibeon, fled to the cave at Makkedah, and was hanged with the other four kings.
LifeLesson: Alliances against God end in the same cave.

Name: Horam, King of Gezer
Summary: Horam was king of Gezer when he came up to help Lachish, and Joshua struck him and his people down until none remained.
KeyStory: Horam marched to Lachish's aid too late, and Joshua destroyed him and his army on the spot.
LifeLesson: Coming to the aid of a lost cause does not make it won.

Name: Hori, Father of Shaphat
Summary: Hori, Father of Shaphat is named in Numbers as the father of Shaphat, one of the twelve spies.
KeyStory: Hori, Father of Shaphat is named only as the father of Shaphat, whom Moses sent to search out Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Hur, King of Midian
Summary: Hur was one of the five kings of Midian slain by Israel in the war that followed the idolatry at Peor.
KeyStory: Hur fell to Israel's sword when Moses sent a thousand men of every tribe against Midian.
RelatedPeople: Evi; Rekem; Zur; Reba; Moses; Phinehas
LifeLesson: The gods of Midian could not protect their own kings.

Name: Igal, Son of Joseph
Summary: Igal, Son of Joseph was one of the twelve spies Moses sent from the tribe of Issachar to search out the land of Canaan.
KeyStory: Igal spent forty days spying out Canaan, then joined the ten who brought back a fearful report that turned Israel back into the wilderness.
RelatedPeople: Joseph, Father of Igal; Moses; Caleb; Joshua
LifeLesson: Seeing the same land as Caleb, he saw only giants — faith is a choice about what you trust.

Name: Jabin, King of Hazor
Summary: Jabin was king of Hazor when he gathered the kings of the north against Israel at the waters of Merom.
KeyStory: Jabin's great host, with horses and chariots, was defeated by Joshua at Merom, and Hazor itself was burned with fire.
LifeLesson: Chariots and numbers are no answer to the LORD of hosts.

Name: Jair, Son of Manasseh
Summary: Jair, son of Manasseh, captured the towns of Argob east of the Jordan and called them Havoth-jair, the towns of Jair.
KeyStory: Jair took the small towns of Argob and gave them his own name, which they kept for generations.
LifeLesson: What God gives, a faithful man puts his name to and keeps.

Name: Japhia, King of Lachish
Summary: Japhia was king of Lachish and one of the five kings who allied against Gibeon and were defeated by Joshua.
KeyStory: Japhia joined Adoni-zedek against Gibeon, fled to the cave at Makkedah, and was hanged with the other four kings.
LifeLesson: Alliances against God end in the same cave.

Name: Jephunneh, Father of Caleb
Summary: Jephunneh is named in Scripture as the father of Caleb, the faithful spy who followed the LORD fully.
KeyStory: Jephunneh's son Caleb was one of only two spies who urged Israel to trust God and enter the land.
LifeLesson: A father's name can live on in a child's courage.

Name: Jobab, King of Madon
Summary: Jobab was king of Madon when he joined Jabin of Hazor against Israel at the waters of Merom.
KeyStory: Jobab marched with the northern kings and fell with them when Joshua struck the host at Merom.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Jogli
Summary: Jogli is named in Numbers as the father of Bukki, one of the princes who divided the land.
KeyStory: Jogli is named only as the father of Bukki, appointed to apportion Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Joseph, Father of Igal
Summary: Joseph, Father of Igal is named in Numbers as the father of Igal, one of the twelve spies.
KeyStory: Joseph, Father of Igal is named only as the father of Igal, whom Moses sent to search out Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Kemuel, Son of Shiphtan
Summary: Kemuel, Son of Shiphtan was the prince of Ephraim appointed to divide the land of Canaan by inheritance among the tribes.
KeyStory: Kemuel was named by the LORD, with Eleazar and Joshua, to apportion the promised land to the nine and a half tribes.
LifeLesson: Dividing what God gives takes honest hands.

Name: Lael
Summary: Lael is named in Numbers as the father of Eliasaph.
KeyStory: Lael is named only as the father of Eliasaph, in the census and camp order of Israel.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Machi
Summary: Machi is named in Numbers as the father of Geuel, one of the twelve spies.
KeyStory: Machi is named only as the father of Geuel, whom Moses sent to search out Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Mahlah
Summary: Mahlah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who asked Moses for their father's inheritance.
KeyStory: Mahlah stood with her sisters before Moses and the congregation, and God granted daughters the right to inherit when there is no son.
RelatedPeople: Zelophehad; Noah, Daughter of Zelophehad; Hoglah; Milcah, Daughter of Zelophehad; Tirzah; Moses
LifeLesson: Five sisters standing together changed the law of inheritance.

Name: Medad
Summary: Medad was one of the seventy elders on whom the Spirit rested in the wilderness; though he stayed in the camp, he prophesied there.
KeyStory: When the Spirit fell on the elders, Medad prophesied in the camp, and Moses refused to stop him, wishing all the LORD's people were prophets.
LifeLesson: The gift is God's to give, not ours to gatekeep.

Name: Michael, Father of Sethur
Summary: Michael, Father of Sethur is named in Numbers as the father of Sethur, one of the twelve spies.
KeyStory: Michael, Father of Sethur is named only as the father of Sethur, whom Moses sent to search out Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Milcah, Daughter of Zelophehad
Summary: Milcah, daughter of Zelophehad, was one of the five sisters who asked Moses for their father's inheritance.
KeyStory: Milcah stood with her sisters before Moses and the congregation, and God granted daughters the right to inherit when there is no son.
RelatedPeople: Zelophehad; Mahlah; Noah, Daughter of Zelophehad; Hoglah; Tirzah; Moses
LifeLesson: Five sisters standing together changed the law of inheritance.

Name: Nahbi, Son of Vophsi
Summary: Nahbi, Son of Vophsi was one of the twelve spies Moses sent from the tribe of Naphtali to search out the land of Canaan.
KeyStory: Nahbi spent forty days spying out Canaan, then joined the ten who brought back a fearful report that turned Israel back into the wilderness.
LifeLesson: Seeing the same land as Caleb, he saw only giants — faith is a choice about what you trust.

Name: Nethaneel, Son of Zuar
Summary: Nethaneel, son of Zuar, was the prince of the tribe of Issachar at the census in the wilderness.
KeyStory: Nethaneel led Issachar's 54,400 men and brought the tribe's offering for the dedication of the altar.
LifeLesson: Faithful men lead best when they simply show up where God counts them.

Name: Noah, Daughter of Zelophehad
Summary: Noah, daughter of Zelophehad, was one of the five sisters who asked Moses for their father's inheritance.
KeyStory: Noah stood with her sisters before Moses and the congregation, and God granted daughters the right to inherit when there is no son.
RelatedPeople: Zelophehad; Mahlah; Hoglah; Milcah, Daughter of Zelophehad; Tirzah; Moses
LifeLesson: Five sisters standing together changed the law of inheritance.

Name: Nobah
Summary: Nobah captured Kenath and its villages east of the Jordan and called them Nobah, after his own name.
KeyStory: Nobah went and took Kenath with its towns and named the whole district after himself.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Ocran
Summary: Ocran is named in Numbers as the father of Pagiel.
KeyStory: Ocran is named only as the father of Pagiel, in the census and camp order of Israel.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Og
Summary: Og was king of Bashan, a giant of the remnant of the Rephaim, who was defeated by Israel at Edrei.
KeyStory: Og came out against Israel with all his people, and Israel struck him down until none remained, taking sixty walled cities of Bashan.
LifeLesson: No giant is too big for the God who has already promised the land.

Name: On, Son of Peleth
Summary: On, son of Peleth, was a Reubenite who joined Korah's rebellion against Moses and Aaron.
KeyStory: On rose up with Korah, Dathan, and Abiram against Moses in the wilderness, and is named no more after the rebellion.
RelatedPeople: Dathan; Abiram; Peleth; Korah, Son of Izhar; Moses
LifeLesson: Joining a rebellion is a choice with a name attached to it.

Name: Othniel, Son of Kenaz
Summary: Othniel, son of Kenaz and Caleb's younger brother, captured Kirjath-sepher and married Achsah, and later became Israel's first judge.
KeyStory: Othniel took Kirjath-sepher and won Achsah as his wife; years later the Spirit of the LORD came on him and he delivered Israel from Cushan-rishathaim.
RelatedPeople: Caleb; Achsah, Daughter of Caleb; Kenaz
LifeLesson: The courage that takes one city can grow into the courage that delivers a nation.

Name: Pagiel, Son of Ocran
Summary: Pagiel, son of Ocran, was the prince of the tribe of Asher at the census in the wilderness.
KeyStory: Pagiel led Asher's 41,500 men and brought the tribe's offering for the dedication of the altar.
LifeLesson: Every offering given in obedience is remembered by name.

Name: Palti, Son of Raphu
Summary: Palti, Son of Raphu was one of the twelve spies Moses sent from the tribe of Benjamin to search out the land of Canaan.
KeyStory: Palti spent forty days spying out Canaan, then joined the ten who brought back a fearful report that turned Israel back into the wilderness.
LifeLesson: Seeing the same land as Caleb, he saw only giants — faith is a choice about what you trust.

Name: Paltiel, Son of Azzan
Summary: Paltiel, Son of Azzan was the prince of Issachar appointed to divide the land of Canaan by inheritance among the tribes.
KeyStory: Paltiel was named by the LORD, with Eleazar and Joshua, to apportion the promised land to the nine and a half tribes.
LifeLesson: Dividing what God gives takes honest hands.

Name: Parnach
Summary: Parnach is named in Numbers as the father of Elizaphan, one of the princes who divided the land.
KeyStory: Parnach is named only as the father of Elizaphan, appointed to apportion Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Pedahel, Son of Ammihud
Summary: Pedahel, Son of Ammihud was the prince of Naphtali appointed to divide the land of Canaan by inheritance among the tribes.
KeyStory: Pedahel was named by the LORD, with Eleazar and Joshua, to apportion the promised land to the nine and a half tribes.
LifeLesson: Dividing what God gives takes honest hands.

Name: Pedahzur
Summary: Pedahzur is named in Numbers as the father of Gamaliel.
KeyStory: Pedahzur is named only as the father of Gamaliel, in the census and camp order of Israel.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Peleth
Summary: Peleth is named in Numbers as the father of On, who joined Korah's rebellion.
KeyStory: Peleth is named only as the father of On, the Reubenite who rose up against Moses.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Piram, King of Jarmuth
Summary: Piram was king of Jarmuth and one of the five kings who allied against Gibeon and were defeated by Joshua.
KeyStory: Piram joined Adoni-zedek against Gibeon, fled to the cave at Makkedah, and was hanged with the other four kings.
LifeLesson: Alliances against God end in the same cave.

Name: Raphu
Summary: Raphu is named in Numbers as the father of Palti, one of the twelve spies.
KeyStory: Raphu is named only as the father of Palti, whom Moses sent to search out Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Reba
Summary: Reba was one of the five kings of Midian slain by Israel in the war that followed the idolatry at Peor.
KeyStory: Reba fell to Israel's sword when Moses sent a thousand men of every tribe against Midian.
RelatedPeople: Evi; Rekem; Zur; Hur, King of Midian; Moses; Phinehas
LifeLesson: The gods of Midian could not protect their own kings.

Name: Rekem
Summary: Rekem was one of the five kings of Midian slain by Israel in the war that followed the idolatry at Peor.
KeyStory: Rekem fell to Israel's sword when Moses sent a thousand men of every tribe against Midian.
RelatedPeople: Evi; Zur; Hur, King of Midian; Reba; Moses; Phinehas
LifeLesson: The gods of Midian could not protect their own kings.

Name: Salu
Summary: Salu is named in Numbers as the father of Zimri, the Simeonite prince slain at Peor.
KeyStory: Salu's son Zimri was killed by Phinehas for openly defying God in the sight of all Israel.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Sethur, Son of Michael
Summary: Sethur, Son of Michael was one of the twelve spies Moses sent from the tribe of Asher to search out the land of Canaan.
KeyStory: Sethur spent forty days spying out Canaan, then joined the ten who brought back a fearful report that turned Israel back into the wilderness.
RelatedPeople: Michael, Father of Sethur; Moses; Caleb; Joshua
LifeLesson: Seeing the same land as Caleb, he saw only giants — faith is a choice about what you trust.

Name: Shammua, Son of Zaccur
Summary: Shammua, Son of Zaccur was one of the twelve spies Moses sent from the tribe of Reuben to search out the land of Canaan.
KeyStory: Shammua spent forty days spying out Canaan, then joined the ten who brought back a fearful report that turned Israel back into the wilderness.
LifeLesson: Seeing the same land as Caleb, he saw only giants — faith is a choice about what you trust.

Name: Shaphat, Son of Hori
Summary: Shaphat, Son of Hori was one of the twelve spies Moses sent from the tribe of Simeon to search out the land of Canaan.
KeyStory: Shaphat spent forty days spying out Canaan, then joined the ten who brought back a fearful report that turned Israel back into the wilderness.
RelatedPeople: Hori, Father of Shaphat; Moses; Caleb; Joshua
LifeLesson: Seeing the same land as Caleb, he saw only giants — faith is a choice about what you trust.

Name: Shechem, Son of Gilead
Summary: Shechem, son of Gilead, founded a clan of Manasseh east of the Jordan.
KeyStory: Shechem is named among the sons of Gilead in the second census of Israel.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Shedeur
Summary: Shedeur is named in Numbers as the father of Elizur.
KeyStory: Shedeur is named only as the father of Elizur, in the census and camp order of Israel.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Shelomi
Summary: Shelomi is named in Numbers as the father of Ahihud, one of the princes who divided the land.
KeyStory: Shelomi is named only as the father of Ahihud, appointed to apportion Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Shelumiel, Son of Zurishaddai
Summary: Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai, was the prince of the tribe of Simeon at the census in the wilderness.
