KeyStory: Shelumiel led Simeon's 59,300 men and brought the tribe's offering for the dedication of the altar.
LifeLesson: Leadership is counted in service, not in size.

Name: Shemida
Summary: Shemida, son of Gilead, founded a clan of Manasseh east of the Jordan.
KeyStory: Shemida is named among the sons of Gilead in the second census of Israel.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Shemuel, Son of Ammihud
Summary: Shemuel, Son of Ammihud was the prince of Simeon appointed to divide the land of Canaan by inheritance among the tribes.
KeyStory: Shemuel was named by the LORD, with Eleazar and Joshua, to apportion the promised land to the nine and a half tribes.
LifeLesson: Dividing what God gives takes honest hands.

Name: Sheshai, Son of Anak
Summary: Sheshai, son of Anak, was one of the Anakim the spies saw dwelling in Hebron.
KeyStory: The spies found Sheshai in Hebron and carried home a report of giants that melted Israel's courage.
RelatedPeople: Anak; Ahiman, Son of Anak; Talmai, Son of Anak; Caleb
LifeLesson: A fearful report can undo a whole people; a faithful one can steady them.

Name: Shiphtan
Summary: Shiphtan is named in Numbers as the father of Kemuel, one of the princes who divided the land.
KeyStory: Shiphtan is named only as the father of Kemuel, appointed to apportion Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Shuthelah
Summary: Shuthelah, son of Ephraim, founded a clan of Ephraim named in the second census.
KeyStory: Shuthelah is named among the sons of Ephraim when Israel was counted a second time in the plains of Moab.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Sihon
Summary: Sihon was king of the Amorites at Heshbon; he refused Israel passage and was defeated, and his land became Israel's first possession east of the Jordan.
KeyStory: Sihon gathered his people and fought Israel at Jahaz, and Israel took all his cities from the Arnon to the Jabbok.
LifeLesson: The door God opens is often the one a king tries to shut.

Name: Sodi
Summary: Sodi is named in Numbers as the father of Gaddiel, one of the twelve spies.
KeyStory: Sodi is named only as the father of Gaddiel, whom Moses sent to search out Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Susi
Summary: Susi is named in Numbers as the father of Gaddi, one of the twelve spies.
KeyStory: Susi is named only as the father of Gaddi, whom Moses sent to search out Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Tahan
Summary: Tahan, son of Ephraim, founded a clan of Ephraim named in the second census.
KeyStory: Tahan is named among the sons of Ephraim when Israel was counted a second time in the plains of Moab.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Talmai, Son of Anak
Summary: Talmai, son of Anak, was one of the Anakim the spies saw dwelling in Hebron.
KeyStory: The spies found Talmai in Hebron and carried home a report of giants that melted Israel's courage.
RelatedPeople: Anak; Ahiman, Son of Anak; Sheshai, Son of Anak; Caleb
LifeLesson: A fearful report can undo a whole people; a faithful one can steady them.

Name: Tirzah
Summary: Tirzah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who asked Moses for their father's inheritance.
KeyStory: Tirzah stood with her sisters before Moses and the congregation, and God granted daughters the right to inherit when there is no son.
RelatedPeople: Zelophehad; Mahlah; Noah, Daughter of Zelophehad; Hoglah; Milcah, Daughter of Zelophehad; Moses
LifeLesson: Five sisters standing together changed the law of inheritance.

Name: Vophsi
Summary: Vophsi is named in Numbers as the father of Nahbi, one of the twelve spies.
KeyStory: Vophsi is named only as the father of Nahbi, whom Moses sent to search out Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Zabdi, Father of Carmi
Summary: Zabdi, son of Zerah son of Judah, was the father of Carmi and the grandfather of Achan, whose sin troubled Israel.
KeyStory: Zabdi's household was taken by tribe, family, and man until Achan was found and his hidden plunder exposed.
RelatedPeople: Carmi, Son of Zabdi; Achan; Zerah, Son of Judah; Joshua
LifeLesson: What is buried in a tent cannot stay buried from God.

Name: Zaccur
Summary: Zaccur is named in Numbers as the father of Shammua, one of the twelve spies.
KeyStory: Zaccur is named only as the father of Shammua, whom Moses sent to search out Canaan.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Zelophehad
Summary: Zelophehad, son of Hepher, died in the wilderness leaving no sons, and his five daughters appealed to Moses for their father's inheritance.
KeyStory: The daughters of Zelophehad stood before Moses, Eleazar, and the whole congregation, and God ruled that daughters inherit when there is no son.
RelatedPeople: Mahlah; Noah, Daughter of Zelophehad; Hoglah; Milcah, Daughter of Zelophehad; Tirzah; Hepher, Son of Gilead; Moses
LifeLesson: Asking God for justice, in the open, is itself an act of faith.

Name: Zimri, Son of Salu
Summary: Zimri, son of Salu, was a prince of Simeon who openly brought the Midianite woman Cozbi into the camp at Peor.
KeyStory: Zimri's open defiance was stopped by Phinehas, whose zeal turned away God's wrath from Israel.
LifeLesson: Sin flaunted in the open is still sin — and it still costs.

Name: Zippor
Summary: Zippor is named in Numbers as the father of Balak, king of Moab.
KeyStory: Zippor's son Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel and heard only blessings instead.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Zuar
Summary: Zuar is named in Numbers as the father of Nethaneel.
KeyStory: Zuar is named only as the father of Nethaneel, in the census and camp order of Israel.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

Name: Zur
Summary: Zur was a prince of Midian and the father of Cozbi, and one of the five Midianite kings slain by Israel.
KeyStory: Zur's daughter was slain with Zimri at Peor, and Zur himself fell to Israel's sword in the war against Midian.
LifeLesson: The gods of Midian could not protect their own princes.

Name: Zuriel, Son of Abihail
Summary: Zuriel, son of Abihail, was the chief of the Merarites, the Levites who carried the tabernacle's frames, bars, and pillars.
KeyStory: Zuriel oversaw the Merarite families in their heavy, unseen service of the tabernacle.
RelatedPeople: Abihail, Father of Zuriel; Moses; Merari
LifeLesson: The heaviest work of worship is often done by hands nobody applauds.

Name: Zurishaddai
Summary: Zurishaddai is named in Numbers as the father of Shelumiel.
KeyStory: Zurishaddai is named only as the father of Shelumiel, in the census and camp order of Israel.
LifeLesson: Even a single mention means God did not overlook him.

KeyStory: He declared to Jehoshaphat and all Judah, Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God's — and told them they would not need to fight, but only stand and see the salvation of the LORD.
LifeLesson: God's word through one faithful voice steadied a whole nation. When the battle is bigger than you, stand still and watch what God does.
Name: Jahaziel, Son of Zechariah
RelatedPeople: Zechariah, Father of Jahaziel; King Jehoshaphat
Role: Levite of the Sons of Asaph
Summary: Jahaziel was a Levite of the sons of Asaph upon whom the Spirit of the LORD came in the midst of the congregation as Judah faced a vast invading army.

KeyStory: He appears in Jahaziel's genealogy: Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph.
LifeLesson: Zechariah is named in Scripture only as Jahaziel's father, yet his name stands in the line God used at Judah's crisis. A quiet place in the story is still a place in the story.
Name: Zechariah, Father of Jahaziel
Role: Levite of the Sons of Asaph
Summary: Zechariah was a Levite of the sons of Asaph, named in Scripture as the father of Jahaziel, in the line given when the Spirit came upon his son.

Name: Shechem, Son of Hamor
Summary: Shechem was the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince whose assault on Dinah brought destruction on his city.
KeyStory: Shechem took Dinah by force, then asked to marry her — and while his men were weakened by circumcision, Simeon and Levi killed them all.
RelatedPeople: Hamor; Dinah; Jacob; Simeon, Son of Jacob; Levi
LifeLesson: Desire without restraint destroys both the one who takes and everyone around him.

Name: Abagtha
Summary: One of the seven chamberlains who served Ahasuerus at his feast.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: Even attendants at a feast are part of the story.

Name: Abda, Father of Adoniram
Summary: Abda was the father of Adoniram, overseer of Solomon's tribute labour.
KeyStory: Abda, father of Adoniram.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Abda, Son of Shammua
Summary: Abda son of Shammua, named in Nehemiah 11:17.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Abdi, Father of Kish
Summary: Abdi was the father of Kish, a Merarite Levite who cleansed the temple under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Abdi is named only as the father of Kish the son of Abdi.
LifeLesson: A Merarite father's name is kept in the temple roster.

Name: Abdi, Son of Elam
Summary: Son of Elam named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Abdi, Son of Malluch
Summary: Son of Malluch and father of Kishi in Ethan's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:44: Son of Malluch and father of Kishi in Ethan's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Abdi stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Abdiel
Summary: Father of Ahi son of Guni in Gad's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:15: Father of Ahi son of Guni in Gad's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Abdiel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Abdon, Son of Hillel
Summary: Abdon, son of Hillel, a Pirathonite, judged Israel eight years; he had forty sons and thirty nephews who rode on seventy ass colts.
KeyStory: Abdon judged Israel eight years, and his forty sons and thirty nephews rode on seventy ass colts; he died and was buried in Pirathon in Mount Ephraim.
LifeLesson: A judge's household rode like a parade — seventy ass colts for one family.

Name: Abdon, Son of Jehiel
Summary: Firstborn son of Jehiel the father of Gibeon.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:30; 1 Chronicles 9:36: Firstborn son of Jehiel the father of Gibeon.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Abdon stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Abdon, Son of Micah
Summary: Abdon, son of Micah, was one of the men Josiah commanded to enquire of the LORD concerning the found book, and he went to Huldah the prophetess.
KeyStory: The king commanded Hilkiah, Ahikam, Abdon the son of Micah, Shaphan and Asaiah to enquire of the LORD.
RelatedPeople: Micah, Father of Abdon; King Josiah
LifeLesson: A king who hears God's word sends men to ask what it means.

Name: Abdon, Son of Shashak
Summary: Named among the sons of Shashak in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:23: Named among the sons of Shashak in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Abdon stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Abednego
Summary: Abednego (KJV: Abed-nego) was the Babylonian name given to Azariah, one of Daniel's three companions; he was set over the affairs of the province of Babylon and, with Shadrach and Meshach, refused the golden image and walked out of the fiery furnace unharmed. ONE profile covers both names; he is a different man from Azariah son of Hoshaiah.
KeyStory: Abednego was bound and cast into the midst of the burning fiery furnace with his two friends, and the king saw four men walking loose in the fire, unhurt.
LifeLesson: God is present in the fire, not only after it — the fourth man walks in the midst of it.
RelatedEvents: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the Fiery Furnace

Name: Abi-albon the Arbathite
Summary: Abi-albon the Arbathite was among David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Abi-albon the Arbathite stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: Arbath gave David a warrior for the thirty.

Name: Abi, Mother of Hezekiah
Summary: Abi, daughter of Zachariah, was the mother of Hezekiah, the king who trusted the LORD above all Judah's kings.
KeyStory: Abi, mother of Hezekiah.
RelatedPeople: King Hezekiah; Zachariah, Father of Abi
LifeLesson: The mother of Judah's most trusting king is named in a single verse.

Name: Abia, Son of Rehoboam
Summary: Son of Rehoboam and king in the line of Judah after him.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:10: Son of Rehoboam and king in the line of Judah after him.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Abia stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Abiah, Son of Becher
Summary: Son of Becher, named among the sons of Becher.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:8: Son of Becher, named among the sons of Becher.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Abiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Abiah, Son of Samuel
Summary: Abiah, Samuel's second son, was made a judge at Beersheba with his brother Joel. Both took bribes and perverted judgment, and Israel cited their failure when demanding a king.
KeyStory: Abiah's corrupt judgeship helped push Israel to ask for a king like the nations.
LifeLesson: Leadership passed down without character becomes the very reason people stop trusting it.

Name: Abiah, Wife of Hezron
Summary: Wife of Hezron after his death, named as the mother of Ashur.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:24: Wife of Hezron after his death, named as the mother of Ashur.
LifeLesson: The mention of Abiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Abiathar, Priest
Summary: Abiathar, who had carried the ephod for David, sided with Adonijah against Solomon, and Solomon thrust him out of the priesthood, fulfilling the word against Eli's house, though he spared his life because he had borne the ark.
KeyStory: Abiathar sides with Adonijah and is deposed.
RelatedPeople: King David; King Solomon; Zadok, High Priest; Jonathan, Son of Abiathar
LifeLesson: A lifetime of service does not excuse one disloyal choice at the decisive hour.

Name: Abiathar, Son of Ahimelech
Summary: Abiathar, son of Ahimelech, alone escaped the massacre at Nob, fleeing to David with the ephod. He served as David's priest through his fugitive years and his reign, bringing the ephod whenever David inquired of God.
KeyStory: Abiathar escaped Nob with the ephod and carried God's guidance to David for forty years.
RelatedPeople: Ahimelech, Son of Ahitub; King David; Zadok, Son of Ahitub; Ahimelech, Son of Abiathar
LifeLesson: Surviving a massacre is not the end of a calling; Abiathar served a lifetime after his worst day.

Name: Abiel the Arbathite
Summary: Mighty man of David, called the Arbathite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:32: Mighty man of David, called the Arbathite.
LifeLesson: The mention of Abiel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Abiel
Summary: Abiel was the father of Kish and of Ner, making him the grandfather of Saul and of Abner, Saul's commander.
KeyStory: Abiel's two sons fathered both Israel's first king and his army's captain.
RelatedPeople: Kish, Son of Abiel; Ner, Son of Abiel
LifeLesson: One household can shape a nation's whole first generation of leadership.

Name: Abiezer, Son of Hammoleketh
Summary: Son of Hammoleketh, named in Manasseh's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:18: Son of Hammoleketh, named in Manasseh's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Abiezer stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Abiezer the Anethothite
Summary: Abiezer the Anethothite was among David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Abiezer the Anethothite stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: Anathoth, a priests' town, also gave David a warrior.

Name: Abiezer the Anetothite
Summary: Captain over the ninth month's course, of the Benjamites.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:12: Captain over the ninth month's course, of the Benjamites.
LifeLesson: The mention of Abiezer in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Abiezer the Antothite
Summary: Valient man of David's armies and captain of the ninth month's course.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:28; 1 Chronicles 27:12: Valient man of David's armies and captain of the ninth month's course.
LifeLesson: The mention of Abiezer in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Abigail, Daughter of Nahash
Role: Sister of Zeruiah; Mother of Amasa
Summary: Abigail, daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah, was the mother of Amasa by Ithra. She is distinct from Abigail, Nabal's widow, who became David's wife.
KeyStory: Abigail daughter of Nahash mothered Amasa, the commander Joab murdered.
RelatedPeople: Zeruiah; Amasa, Son of Ithra; Ithra
LifeLesson: Two Abigails, two houses — the record keeps each woman's story straight.

Name: Abihail, Daughter of Eliab
Summary: Abihail, daughter of Eliab son of Jesse, was a wife of Rehoboam named alongside Mahalath.
KeyStory: Rehoboam took Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse to wife.
LifeLesson: Even a single named line can anchor a person in a real family.

Name: Abihail, Son of Huri
Summary: Son of Huri son of Jaroah son of Gilead, father of the Gadite brethren listed after him.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:14: Son of Huri son of Jaroah son of Gilead, father of the Gadite brethren listed after him.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Abihail stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Abihail, Wife of Abishur
Summary: Wife of Abishur and mother of Ahban and Molid.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:29: Wife of Abishur and mother of Ahban and Molid.
LifeLesson: The mention of Abihail in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Abihail
Summary: Father of Esther (Hadassah), named when Esther is introduced and when the Purim letters are written.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: A father's name can open a daughter's story.

Name: Abihud
Summary: Son of Bela, named among the sons of Bela.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:3: Son of Bela, named among the sons of Bela.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Abihud stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Abijah, Course Head
Summary: Eighth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:10: Eighth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
LifeLesson: The mention of Abijah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Abijah, Daughter of Zechariah
Summary: Abijah, daughter of Zechariah, was the mother of Hezekiah, who was twenty-five when he began to reign twenty-nine years in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Hezekiah's mother's name was Abijah, the daughter of Zechariah.
RelatedPeople: King Hezekiah; Zechariah, Father of Abijah
LifeLesson: A reforming king's mother is named at the start of his reign.

Name: Abijah, King of Judah
Summary: Abijah, son of Rehoboam and Maachah, reigned three years in Jerusalem; he trusted the LORD against Jeroboam's far larger army and won a great victory, though he married fourteen wives.
KeyStory: Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim, appealed to the covenant with David, and Judah prevailed because they relied on the LORD God of their fathers.
RelatedPeople: Rehoboam; Maachah, Daughter of Absalom; Jeroboam; King Asa
LifeLesson: Victory belongs to those who rely on the LORD, not to the larger army.

Name: Abijah
Summary: Priest who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10).
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: A signature on a covenant is a public stand.

Name: Abijam, King of Judah
Summary: Abijam, son of Rehoboam, reigned three years in Jerusalem and walked in the sins of his father, though God preserved David's line in Jerusalem for David's sake.
KeyStory: Abijam's short reign and war with Jeroboam.
LifeLesson: A short reign still matters: God judges kings by whether their hearts are wholly His.

Name: Abimelech, Son of Abiathar
Summary: Son of Abiathar and priest under David, with Zadok.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 18:16: Son of Abiathar and priest under David, with Zadok.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Abimelech stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Abimelech, Son of Gideon
Summary: Abimelech, son of Gideon by his Shechemite concubine, murdered his seventy brothers, was made king by the men of Shechem, and died at Thebez when a woman dropped a millstone on his head. He is distinct from Abimelech, king of Gerar, in Genesis.
KeyStory: Abimelech hired vain men with temple silver, slew his brothers on one stone, was crowned at Shechem, burned the tower of Shechem, and was mortally wounded at Thebez by a piece of a millstone, asking his armourbearer to finish him lest men say a woman slew him.
RelatedPeople: Gideon; Jotham, Son of Gideon; Zebul; Gaal, Son of Ebed
LifeLesson: A crown bought with brothers' blood ends under a millstone.

Name: Abinadab of Kirjath-jearim
Summary: Abinadab of Kirjath-jearim kept the ark of the Lord in his house for twenty years after it was returned from the Philistines, and his son Eleazar was set apart to guard it.
KeyStory: Abinadab's house sheltered the ark through two decades when Israel had no king.
RelatedPeople: Eleazar, Son of Abinadab; Uzzah, Son of Abinadab; Ahio, Son of Abinadab
LifeLesson: Quiet, unseen keeping of holy things matters as much as public ministry.

Name: Abinadab, Son of Jesse
Summary: Abinadab, Jesse's second son, was passed over by Samuel at the anointing and later served in Saul's army against the Philistines at Elah.
KeyStory: Abinadab was presented before Samuel and passed over, then fought at Elah beside his brothers.
RelatedPeople: Jesse; King David; Eliab, Son of Jesse; Shammah, Son of Jesse
LifeLesson: Being passed over is not the same as being rejected; every brother had his place in the battle.

Name: Abinadab, Son of Saul
Summary: Abinadab, son of Saul, died with his father and brothers on Mount Gilboa when the Philistines defeated Israel.
KeyStory: Abinadab fell on Gilboa with Saul, Jonathan, and Malchi-shua.
RelatedPeople: King Saul; Jonathan; Malchi-shua, Son of Saul
LifeLesson: Loyalty to a failing father can still cost a son everything.

Name: Abinoam, Father of Barak
Summary: Abinoam is named only as the father of Barak, from Kedesh-naphtali, whom Deborah summoned to lead Israel against Sisera.
KeyStory: Abinoam appears in Judges only as Barak's father.
LifeLesson: A father's name carried into a battle he never fought.

Name: Abiram, Son of Hiel
Summary: Abiram was Hiel's firstborn, in whom Hiel laid Jericho's foundation, according to the word of Joshua.
KeyStory: Abiram, in whom Jericho's foundation was laid.
RelatedPeople: Hiel the Bethelite; Segub, Son of Hiel
LifeLesson: A child's life spent on a father's ambition is a sober warning.

Name: Abishag, Shunammite
Summary: Abishag, a fair young Shunammite, was brought to cherish the aged David in his last days, and after his death Adonijah's request for her as wife exposed his renewed claim to the throne.
KeyStory: Abishag cherishes David and becomes Adonijah's pretext.
RelatedPeople: King David; King Solomon; Adonijah, Son of Haggith
LifeLesson: Even a quiet servant can become the occasion that exposes a hidden ambition.

Name: Abishai, Son of Zeruiah
Summary: Son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, and one of David's mighty men.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:16; 1 Chronicles 11:20: Son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, and one of David's mighty men.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Abishai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Abishai
Summary: Abishai, son of Zeruiah and brother of Joab, was one of David's chief warriors. He went with David into Saul's camp, rescued David from the giant Ishbi-benob, and twice asked to kill Shimei for cursing David. He commanded a third of the army against Absalom.
KeyStory: Abishai stood beside David in Saul's camp, against giants, and against Absalom.
LifeLesson: A brother's loyalty in battle is proven again and again, not once.

Name: Abishua, Ancestor of Ezra
Summary: Ancestor of Ezra named in his genealogy, son of Phinehas.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: A long line of priests ends in a scribe.

Name: Abishua, Son of Bela
Summary: Son of Bela, named among the sons of Bela.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:4: Son of Bela, named among the sons of Bela.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Abishua stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Abishua, Son of Phinehas
Summary: Son of Phinehas and priest in Aaron's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:4; 1 Chronicles 6:50: Son of Phinehas and priest in Aaron's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Abishua stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Abishur
Summary: Son of Shammai, whose wife was Abihail.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:28: Son of Shammai, whose wife was Abihail.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Abishur stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Abital, Wife of David
Summary: Wife of David and mother of Shephatiah, born in Hebron.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:3: Wife of David and mother of Shephatiah, born in Hebron.
LifeLesson: The mention of Abital in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Abital
Summary: Abital was one of David's wives at Hebron and the mother of Shephatiah, his fifth son.
KeyStory: Abital is named once, as the mother of David's fifth son at Hebron.
RelatedPeople: King David; Shephatiah, Son of David
LifeLesson: Some mothers are remembered by one line — and that line is enough.

Name: Abitub
Summary: Son of Shaharaim by Hushim.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:11: Son of Shaharaim by Hushim.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Abitub stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Abner, Son of Ner
Summary: Abner, son of Ner, commanded Saul's army, made Ish-bosheth king after Saul's death, and then defected to David, bringing the northern tribes with him. Joab murdered him at Hebron in revenge for his brother Asahel, and David publicly mourned him.
KeyStory: Abner held Saul's kingdom together, then handed it to David — and was murdered for an old battlefield debt.
KeyVerses: 1 Samuel 14:50; 1 Samuel 17:55; 1 Samuel 26:5; 2 Samuel 2:8; 2 Samuel 3:27; 1 Kings 2:5; 1 Kings 2:32; 1 Chronicles 26:28
RelatedPeople: King Saul; Ner, Son of Abiel; Ish-bosheth, Son of Saul; Joab; King David; Joab, Son of Zeruiah; Amasa, Son of Jether; Ner, Father of Abner; Ner, Son of Jehiel
LifeLesson: Revenge dressed as justice still murders; David's mourning shows what a kingdom should grieve.

Name: Absalom, Son of David
Summary: Third son of David, born in Hebron to Maachah daughter of Talmai.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:2: Third son of David, born in Hebron to Maachah daughter of Talmai.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Absalom stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Achaicus
Summary: Achaicus was one of the Corinthian brethren who came to Paul and supplied what was lacking from the church, refreshing Paul's spirit.
KeyStory: Achaicus was one of the Corinthian brethren who came to Paul and supplied what was lacking from the church, refreshing Paul's spirit.
LifeLesson: Coming in person can supply what letters cannot.

Name: Achbor, Son of Michaiah
Summary: Achbor, son of Michaiah, was one of Josiah's messengers sent to inquire of Huldah concerning the found book.
KeyStory: Achbor sent to inquire of Huldah.
RelatedPeople: King Josiah; Hilkiah, High Priest; Michaiah, Father of Achbor; Huldah, Prophetess
LifeLesson: Inquiry is the right response to a word that condemns us.

Name: Achish, Son of Maoch
Summary: Achish, son of Maoch and king of Gath, twice sheltered David. David feigned madness before him to escape, and later lived under his protection at Ziklag, raiding Israel's enemies while Achish believed he fought for Philistia.
KeyStory: Achish sheltered the very man destined to defeat his people, fooled twice by David's acting.
LifeLesson: God can hide his anointed in the enemy's own city when the time is not yet ripe.

Name: Achsa, Daughter of Caleb
Summary: Daughter of Caleb, named in the Caleb line of Judah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:49: Daughter of Caleb, named in the Caleb line of Judah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Achsa stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Adaiah, Father of Jedidah
Summary: Adaiah of Boscath was the father of Jedidah, mother of Josiah.
KeyStory: Adaiah, father of Jedidah.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Adaiah, Father of Maaseiah
Summary: Adaiah was the father of Maaseiah, a captain of hundreds in Jehoiada's covenant.
KeyStory: Adaiah is named only as the father of Maaseiah the son of Adaiah.
LifeLesson: A father's name endures in his son's faithful act.

Name: Adaiah, Son of Ethan
Summary: Son of Ethan and father of Zerah in Asaph's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:41: Son of Ethan and father of Zerah in Asaph's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Adaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Adaiah, Son of Jeroham, Priest
Summary: Son of Jeroham son of Pashur son of Malchijah, priest dwelling in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:12: Son of Jeroham son of Pashur son of Malchijah, priest dwelling in Jerusalem.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Adaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Adaiah, Son of Jeroham
Summary: Adaiah son of Jeroham, named in Nehemiah 11:12.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Adaiah, Son of Joiarib
Summary: Adaiah son of Joiarib, named in Nehemiah 11:5.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Adaiah, Son of Shimhi
Summary: Named among the sons of Shimhi in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:21: Named among the sons of Shimhi in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Adaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Adalia
Summary: One of the ten sons of Haman, slain by the Jews in Shushan and afterwards hanged on the gallows.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: A house built on hatred falls with its builder.

Name: Addar
Summary: Son of Bela, named among the sons of Bela.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:3: Son of Bela, named among the sons of Bela.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Addar stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ader
Summary: Named among the sons of Beriah in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:15: Named among the sons of Beriah in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ader stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Adiel, Father of Azmaveth
Summary: Father of Azmaveth, over the king's treasures.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:25: Father of Azmaveth, over the king's treasures.
LifeLesson: The mention of Adiel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Adiel, Father of Maasiai
Summary: Father of Maasiai the priest, son of Jahzerah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:12: Father of Maasiai the priest, son of Jahzerah.
LifeLesson: The mention of Adiel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Adiel, Prince of Simeon
Summary: Prince of Simeon named among those whose families increased greatly.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:36: Prince of Simeon named among those whose families increased greatly.
LifeLesson: The mention of Adiel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Adin
Summary: Head of a family listed among those who returned from exile.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: A family's return is recorded household by household.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Adina, Son of Shiza
Summary: Son of Shiza the Reubenite, a captain of the Reubenites, with thirty with him.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:42: Son of Shiza the Reubenite, a captain of the Reubenites, with thirty with him.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Adina stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Adino the Eznite
Summary: Adino the Eznite, the Tachmonite that sat in the seat, was chief among David's captains. He lifted his spear against eight hundred men at one time and slew them. Some modern renderings call him Josheb-basshebeth.
KeyStory: Adino slew eight hundred men in a single encounter.
LifeLesson: One man's spear, in God's hand, can stand where an army cannot.

Name: Adlai, Father of Shaphat
Summary: Father of Shaphat, over the herds in the valleys.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:29: Father of Shaphat, over the herds in the valleys.
LifeLesson: The mention of Adlai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Admatha
Summary: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media who saw the king's face.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: Counsel near the throne carries weight for a kingdom.

Name: Adna, of Harim's Course
Summary: Head of Harim's priestly course in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:15).
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Courses of service keep worship ordered across generations.

Name: Adna, Son of Pahath-moab
Summary: Son of Pahath-moab named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Adnah, Captain of Judah
Summary: Adnah was chief of the captains of thousands of Judah under Jehoshaphat, with three hundred thousand mighty men of valour.
KeyStory: Of Judah, the captains of thousands: Adnah the chief, and with him three hundred thousand mighty men of valour.
LifeLesson: God's law taught throughout the land, and willing service under a faithful king, strengthened Judah.

Name: Adnah, Captain of Manasseh
Summary: Captain of the thousands of Manasseh who fell to David at Ziklag.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:20: Captain of the thousands of Manasseh who fell to David at Ziklag.
LifeLesson: The mention of Adnah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Adoni-bezek
Summary: Adoni-bezek was a Canaanite king captured at Bezek by Judah and Simeon; after his thumbs and great toes were cut off, he acknowledged that God had repaid him as he had done to seventy kings, and he died at Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Judah and Simeon found Adoni-bezek at Bezek, cut off his thumbs and great toes, and brought him to Jerusalem, where he died.
LifeLesson: A king who once mutilated others met the same measure himself — and owned it as God's repayment.

Name: Adonijah, Son of David
Summary: Fourth son of David, born in Hebron to Haggith.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:2: Fourth son of David, born in Hebron to Haggith.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Adonijah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Adonijah, Son of Haggith
Summary: Adonijah, David's son by Haggith, exalted himself to be king while David was old, gathered Joab and Abiathar, and after Solomon's anointing asked for Abishag as wife, for which Solomon had him executed.
KeyStory: Adonijah's bid for the throne and his execution.
RelatedPeople: King David; King Solomon; Haggith, Mother of Adonijah; Joab, Son of Zeruiah; Abiathar, Priest; Abishag, Shunammite
LifeLesson: Seizing a crown God has given to another is rebellion, not ambition.

Name: Adonijah, the Levite
Summary: Adonijah was one of the Levites sent with Jehoshaphat's princes to teach the book of the law throughout Judah.
KeyStory: With the princes went Levites, including Adonijah, and they taught in Judah with the book of the law.
LifeLesson: God's law taught throughout the land, and willing service under a faithful king, strengthened Judah.

Name: Adonijah
Summary: Adonijah, David's fourth son by Haggith, was born at Hebron. In 2 Samuel he appears only in the list of David's sons born there; his later attempt to seize the throne belongs to the story of Kings.
KeyStory: Adonijah, son of Haggith, was David's fourth son, born at Hebron.
LifeLesson: Birth order is not destiny; the fourth son's story would wait for another book.

Name: Adonikam
Summary: Head of a family listed among those who returned from exile.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: A family's return is recorded household by household.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Adoniram, Officer of Solomon
Summary: Adoniram, son of Abda, was over Solomon's tribute labour, and was later stoned by Israel when Rehoboam sent him to collect it; he is also called Adoram.
KeyStory: Adoniram oversees the tribute and is stoned under Rehoboam.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Rehoboam; Abda, Father of Adoniram
LifeLesson: The face of an unpopular policy is often the first to fall.

Name: Adoram
Summary: Adoram was over the tribute, the officer who gathered forced labour and revenue, in David's administration at the time of Sheba's revolt.
KeyStory: Adoram held the unpopular office of tribute in David's settled kingdom.
LifeLesson: The tax collector's name survives beside the generals' — administration is also service.

Name: Adrammelech, Son of Sennacherib
Summary: Adrammelech, son of Sennacherib, with his brother Sharezer, slew his father as he worshipped in the house of Nisroch, and escaped to Armenia.
KeyStory: Adrammelech slays Sennacherib and flees.
RelatedPeople: Sennacherib, King of Assyria; Sharezer, Son of Sennacherib
LifeLesson: The king who mocked the living God was murdered by his own sons in his god's house.

Name: Adrammelech
Summary: Adrammelech was a son of Sennacherib who, with his brother Sharezer, murdered his father as he worshipped in the house of Nisroch and fled to Ararat.
KeyStory: After Sennacherib returned to Nineveh, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him down with the sword in the temple of his god.
LifeLesson: A king who mocked God found no safety even in his own god's house.

Name: Adriel the Meholathite
Summary: Adriel the Meholathite married Merab, Saul's elder daughter, after Saul broke his promise to give her to David. Years later five of Merab's sons by Adriel were handed to the Gibeonites in atonement for Saul's bloodguilt.
KeyStory: Adriel married the princess David was promised, and his sons later paid for Saul's sins.
LifeLesson: Promises broken by kings fall hardest on the families caught between them.

Name: Aeneas
Summary: Aeneas had been bedridden with palsy for eight years at Lydda when Peter found him and said, Aeneas, Jesus Christ makes you whole. He arose immediately, and all Lydda and Sharon turned to the Lord.
KeyStory: Aeneas lay eight years on a bed, and rose at a sentence, and two towns turned to the Lord.
LifeLesson: Eight years of paralysis ended in one command. Aeneas rose, and his neighbours saw and believed.

Name: Agabus
Summary: Agabus was a prophet who came from Jerusalem to Antioch and foretold a great dearth throughout the world, which came to pass in the days of Claudius. Years later at Caesarea he bound his own hands and feet with Paul's girdle, foretelling Paul's arrest at Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Agabus bound himself with Paul's girdle and said, So shall the Jews bind the man who owns this girdle.
LifeLesson: True prophecy costs the prophet his comfort. Agabus acted his message with his own hands bound.

Name: Agag, King of Amalek
Summary: Agag was king of the Amalekites when Saul defeated them. Saul spared him against God's command, and Samuel put him to death at Gilgal, declaring that as Agag's sword had bereaved mothers, so his mother would be childless.
KeyStory: Agag's spared life exposed Saul's disobedience, and Samuel finished the judgment Saul refused.
LifeLesson: Partial obedience is disobedience, and someone else often has to finish what we refuse.

Name: Agee, Father of Shammah
Summary: Agee the Hararite is named as the father of Shammah, one of David's three mighty men who defended the lentil field.
KeyStory: Agee's son held a field alone against the Philistines.
LifeLesson: A father's name is carried by a son who would not run.

Name: Agur
Summary: Agur, son of Jakeh, was the author of the sayings in Proverbs 30, a humble wisdom teacher who confessed his own ignorance before God.
KeyStory: Agur's words begin with weariness and confession — 'I am more brutish than any man' — then gather sharp observations about pride, greed, and the fear of the Lord.
LifeLesson: Agur teaches that wisdom begins with knowing how little we know and fearing the God who knows all.

Name: Ahab, Son of Kolaiah
Summary: Ahab, son of Kolaiah, was one of the false prophets among the Babylonian exiles whom Jeremiah denounced; he prophesied lies in God's name, and Jeremiah foretold that Nebuchadnezzar would roast him and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah in the fire.
KeyStory: Jeremiah named Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah as men who prophesied lies, and said the king of Babylon would slay them before the exiles' eyes.
RelatedPeople: Zedekiah, Son of Maaseiah; Jeremiah; King Nebuchadnezzar
LifeLesson: Using God's name to bless what God has not blessed ends in exposure.

Name: Aharah
Summary: Third son of Benjamin, named among the sons of Benjamin.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:1: Third son of Benjamin, named among the sons of Benjamin.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Aharah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Aharhel
Summary: Son of Harum, named among the families of Judah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:8: Son of Harum, named among the families of Judah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Aharhel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahasai, Son of Meshillemoth
Summary: Ahasai son of Meshillemoth, named in Nehemiah 11:13.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Ahasbai, Father of Eliphelet
Summary: Ahasbai the Maachathite is named as the father of Eliphelet, one of David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Ahasbai's son stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: Maachah gave David a warrior for the thirty.

Name: Ahasuerus
Summary: King of Persia in whose reign the events of Esther unfold; an accusation against Judah was also written to him in the days of the return.
KeyStory: Rebuilding of the Temple
KeyVerses: Ezra 4:6; Esther 1:1; Esther 1:2; Esther 1:9; Esther 1:10; Esther 1:15; Esther 1:16; Esther 1:17; Esther 1:19; Esther 2:1; Esther 2:12; Esther 2:16; Esther 2:21; Esther 3:1; Esther 3:6; Esther 3:7; Esther 3:8; Esther 3:12; Esther 6:2; Esther 7:5; Esther 8:1; Esther 8:7; Esther 8:10; Esther 8:12; Esther 9:2; Esther 9:20; Esther 9:30; Esther 10:1; Esther 10:3
LifeLesson: God rules over kings who do not know him.
RelatedEvents: Rebuilding of the Temple; Esther Saves Her People

Name: Ahaz, King of Judah
Summary: Ahaz walked in the ways of Israel's kings, sacrificed his son, copied a Damascus altar for the temple, and bought Assyria's help with temple treasure, inviting the very oppression he feared.
KeyStory: Ahaz copies the Damascus altar and appeals to Assyria.
KeyVerses: 2 Kings 16:1; 2 Kings 16:10; 2 Chronicles 28:1; 2 Chronicles 28:22; 2 Chronicles 28:24; Isaiah 7:1; Isaiah 7:10-14; Isaiah 8:1; Hosea 1:1; Micah 1:1
RelatedPeople: Tiglath-Pileser, King of Assyria; Rezin, King of Syria; Urijah, Priest; Jotham, King of Judah; King Hezekiah; Pekah, King of Israel; Isaiah
LifeLesson: Fear that copies the world instead of trusting God ends by serving what it feared.

Name: Ahaz, Son of Jotham
Summary: Son of Jotham in the kingly line of Judah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:13: Son of Jotham in the kingly line of Judah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahaz stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahaz, Son of Micah
Summary: Son of Micah and father of Jehoadah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:35; 1 Chronicles 9:41: Son of Micah and father of Jehoadah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahaz stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahaziah, King of Israel
Summary: Ahaziah, son of Ahab, reigned two years, walked in his father's ways and served Baal, and after falling through a lattice in Samaria he sent to inquire of Baal-zebub and died by Elijah's word.
KeyStory: Ahaziah falls, inquires of Baal-zebub, and dies.
RelatedPeople: King Ahab; Jezebel; Elijah; Jehoram, King of Israel
LifeLesson: When trouble comes, the god a man inquires of reveals the god he serves.

Name: Ahaziah, King of Judah
Summary: Ahaziah, son of Jehoram and Athaliah, reigned one year, walked in the ways of Ahab's house, and was slain by Jehu while visiting the wounded Jehoram of Israel at Jezreel.
KeyStory: Ahaziah visits Jehoram and is slain by Jehu.
RelatedPeople: Jehoram, King of Judah; Athaliah; Jehu, King of Israel; Jehoram, King of Israel; Jehosheba, Daughter of Jehoram; Jehu, Son of Nimshi
LifeLesson: A one-year reign can still reveal a heart: Ahaziah followed his mother's house rather than the LORD.

Name: Ahaziah, Son of Joram
Summary: Son of Joram in the kingly line of Judah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:11: Son of Joram in the kingly line of Judah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahaziah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahban
Summary: Son of Abishur by Abihail.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:29: Son of Abishur by Abihail.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahban stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Aher
Summary: Father of Hushim in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:12: Father of Hushim in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Aher in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ahi, Son of Abdiel
Summary: Son of Abdiel son of Guni, chief of the house of Gad's fathers.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:15: Son of Abdiel son of Guni, chief of the house of Gad's fathers.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahi stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahi, Son of Shamer
Summary: Son of Shamer in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:34: Son of Shamer in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahi stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahiah, Scribe of Solomon
Summary: Ahiah, son of Shisha, served with his brother Elihoreph as one of Solomon's scribes.
KeyStory: Ahiah, scribe of Solomon.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Elihoreph, Scribe of Solomon; Shisha, Father of Elihoreph and Ahiah
LifeLesson: Quiet offices, faithfully held, keep a kingdom honest.

Name: Ahiah, Son of Ehud
Summary: Son of Ehud who removed the inhabitants of Geba.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:7: Son of Ehud who removed the inhabitants of Geba.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahiam, Son of Sacar
Summary: Son of Sacar the Hararite, one of David's mighty men.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:35: Son of Sacar the Hararite, one of David's mighty men.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahiam stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahiam, Son of Sharar
Summary: Ahiam, son of Sharar the Hararite, was among David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite stood among David's thirty.
RelatedPeople: King David; Sharar, Father of Ahiam
LifeLesson: A Hararite father raised one of the thirty.

Name: Ahian
Summary: Son of Shemidah, named among the sons of Shemidah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:19: Son of Shemidah, named among the sons of Shemidah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahian stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahiezer, Son of Shemaah
Summary: Chief of those who came to David at Ziklag, son of Shemaah the Gibeathite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:3: Chief of those who came to David at Ziklag, son of Shemaah the Gibeathite.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ahiezer in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ahihud, Son of Gera
Summary: Son of Gera, begotten after the removal to Manahath.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:7: Son of Gera, begotten after the removal to Manahath.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahihud stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahijah, Son of Jerahmeel
Summary: Son of Jerahmeel, named among the sons of Jerahmeel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:25: Son of Jerahmeel, named among the sons of Jerahmeel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahijah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahijah the Pelonite
Summary: Mighty man of David, called the Pelonite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:36: Mighty man of David, called the Pelonite.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ahijah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ahijah the Shilonite
Summary: Ahijah of Shiloh met Jeroboam in a field, tore his new garment into twelve pieces, and gave ten to Jeroboam, declaring that God would tear the kingdom from Solomon for his idolatry.
KeyStory: Ahijah tears his garment and promises Jeroboam ten tribes.
LifeLesson: God's judgment is announced before it falls, and His promises outlive the kings who break them.

Name: Ahijah, Treasurer
Summary: Levite over the treasures of the house of God and the treasures of the dedicated things.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:20: Levite over the treasures of the house of God and the treasures of the dedicated things.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ahijah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ahijah
Summary: Chief who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10).
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: A signature on a covenant is a public stand.

Name: Ahikam, Son of Shaphan
Summary: Ahikam, son of Shaphan, was one of Josiah's messengers to Huldah, and later protected Jeremiah; he was the father of Gedaliah, governor after the fall.
KeyStory: Ahikam sent to Huldah and father of Gedaliah.
RelatedPeople: King Josiah; Shaphan, Scribe; Huldah, Prophetess; Gedaliah, Son of Ahikam; Shaphan, Son of Azaliah; Huldah, the Prophetess
LifeLesson: A faithful official's son governed the remnant his father's king had lost.

Name: Ahikam
Summary: Ahikam, son of Shaphan, was a court official whose hand protected Jeremiah when the priests and prophets demanded his death, arguing that Hezekiah had spared Micah for like words. His son Gedaliah later became governor, and Ahikam's protection extended to Jeremiah's release to Gedaliah's care.
KeyStory: When the priests demanded Jeremiah's death, the hand of Ahikam son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah, so that he was not given into the people's hand to be put to death.
LifeLesson: One official's hand can be the difference between a prophet's death and his deliverance.

Name: Ahilud, Father of Jehoshaphat the Recorder
Summary: Ahilud was the father of Jehoshaphat, Solomon's recorder.
KeyStory: Ahilud, father of the recorder.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Ahilud, Father of Jehoshaphat
Summary: Ahilud is named as the father of Jehoshaphat, David's recorder.
KeyStory: Ahilud's son kept the official record of David's whole reign.
LifeLesson: A recorder's father is remembered by his son's faithful pen.

Name: Ahimaaz, Father of Ahinoam
Summary: Ahimaaz is named as the father of Ahinoam, Saul's wife, and so the grandfather of Saul's children.
KeyStory: Ahimaaz's daughter married into the first royal house of Israel.
RelatedPeople: Ahinoam, Daughter of Ahimaaz; King Saul
LifeLesson: Family ties bind us into stories far larger than our own.

Name: Ahimaaz, Officer of Solomon
Summary: Ahimaaz was one of Solomon's twelve officers, over Naphtali, and had Solomon's daughter Basmath as wife; he is distinct from Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.
KeyStory: Ahimaaz, officer over Naphtali.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Basmath, Daughter of Solomon
LifeLesson: A name shared with a famous man does not make two men one.

Name: Ahimaaz, Son of Zadok
Summary: Ahimaaz, son of Zadok, ran messages for David during Absalom's revolt, hiding with Jonathan son of Abiathar at En-rogel, and later outran the Cushite to bring David news of Absalom's death.
KeyStory: Ahimaaz outran every messenger to bring David the news he dreaded.
KeyVerses: 2 Samuel 15:27; 2 Samuel 17:17; 2 Samuel 18:19; 2 Samuel 18:23; 1 Chronicles 6:8; 1 Chronicles 6:53
RelatedPeople: Zadok, Son of Ahitub; Jonathan, Son of Abiathar; King David
LifeLesson: The fastest runner still has to deliver hard news.

Name: Ahiman, Porter
Summary: Porter in the companies of the children of Levi, brother of Shallum.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:17: Porter in the companies of the children of Levi, brother of Shallum.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ahiman in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ahimelech, Son of Abiathar
Summary: Ahimelech, son of Abiathar, is named among David's chief officers as priest alongside Zadok in the list of David's administration.
KeyStory: Ahimelech son of Abiathar served as priest in David's settled kingdom.
RelatedPeople: Abiathar, Son of Ahimelech; Zadok, Son of Ahitub; Abiathar, Priest
LifeLesson: A son can inherit his father's office and serve it quietly.

Name: Ahimelech, Son of Ahitub
Summary: Ahimelech, son of Ahitub, was priest at Nob. He gave David the showbread and Goliath's sword, believing David on the king's business, and Saul had him and eighty-five priests murdered for it on Doeg's report.
KeyStory: Ahimelech fed a fugitive in good faith and was murdered for it, with his whole priestly city.
RelatedPeople: King Saul; King David; Doeg the Edomite; Abiathar, Son of Ahimelech
LifeLesson: Kindness to a fugitive can cost everything — and still be right.

Name: Ahimelech the Hittite
Summary: Ahimelech the Hittite was with David in the wilderness when David crept into Saul's camp at night. David asked him who would go down with him, and Ahimelech is named beside Abishai in that daring night raid.
KeyStory: Ahimelech the Hittite stood with David on the night David stole Saul's spear and cruse.
LifeLesson: Loyalty is proved on night raids, not in daylight speeches.

Name: Ahimelech
Summary: Ahimelech was the priest whose house David came to while fleeing Saul, as the title of Psalm 52 records — an act of mercy that cost Ahimelech his life.
KeyStory: When David fled to Nob, Ahimelech gave him bread and a sword; Doeg reported it to Saul, and Ahimelech and the priests of Nob were put to death.
LifeLesson: Ahimelech shows costly kindness — he helped God's anointed without knowing the price, and paid it.

Name: Ahimoth
Summary: Son of Elkanah, named among the sons of Elkanah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:25: Son of Elkanah, named among the sons of Elkanah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahimoth stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahinadab, Son of Iddo
Summary: Ahinadab, son of Iddo, was one of Solomon's twelve officers, over Mahanaim.
KeyStory: Ahinadab, officer over Mahanaim.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Iddo, Father of Ahinadab
LifeLesson: Mahanaim, once a refuge, became a store-city: peace repurposes war's places.

Name: Ahinoam, Daughter of Ahimaaz
Summary: Ahinoam, daughter of Ahimaaz, was the wife of Saul and the mother of his sons and daughters.
KeyStory: Ahinoam was queen beside Israel's first king through his whole troubled reign.
RelatedPeople: King Saul; Ahimaaz, Father of Ahinoam
LifeLesson: Queenship beside a declining king is its own quiet endurance.

Name: Ahinoam the Jezreelitess
Summary: Ahinoam the Jezreelitess was one of David's wives, taken with him through his fugitive years and captured and rescued at Ziklag. She was the mother of Amnon, David's firstborn.
KeyStory: Ahinoam shared David's fugitive years, captivity at Ziklag, and the birth of his firstborn.
LifeLesson: The wives who shared the wilderness years are part of the king's story too.

Name: Ahinoam, Wife of David
Summary: Wife of David, the Jezreelitess, and mother of Amnon, born in Hebron.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:1: Wife of David, the Jezreelitess, and mother of Amnon, born in Hebron.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ahinoam in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ahio, Driver of the Cart
Summary: Drove the cart bearing the ark from the house of Abinadab.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 13:7: Drove the cart bearing the ark from the house of Abinadab.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ahio in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ahio, Son of Abinadab
Summary: Ahio, son of Abinadab, walked before the ark with his brother Uzzah as it was brought up from Kirjath-jearim toward Jerusalem on a new cart.
KeyStory: Ahio walked before the ark on the day his brother died beside it.
RelatedPeople: Abinadab of Kirjath-jearim; Uzzah, Son of Abinadab; King David
LifeLesson: Walking before the ark is honour — and the day can still end in grief.

Name: Ahio, Son of Beriah
Summary: Named among the sons of Beriah in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:14: Named among the sons of Beriah in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahio stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahio, Son of Jehiel
Summary: Son of Jehiel the father of Gibeon.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:31; 1 Chronicles 9:37: Son of Jehiel the father of Gibeon.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahio stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahishahar
Summary: Son of Bilhan, named among the sons of Bilhan.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:10: Son of Bilhan, named among the sons of Bilhan.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahishahar stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahishar, Steward of Solomon
Summary: Ahishar was steward of Solomon's household, over the king's house.
KeyStory: Ahishar, steward of Solomon's house.
LifeLesson: Running a great house well is itself a calling.

Name: Ahithophel, Counsellor
Summary: The king's counsellor under David.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:33: The king's counsellor under David.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ahithophel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ahithophel the Gilonite
Summary: Ahithophel the Gilonite was David's counsellor, whose counsel was prized as if it were the oracle of God. He defected to Absalom, advised the rebellion, and when his counsel was rejected for Hushai's, he went home, set his house in order, and hanged himself.
KeyStory: Ahithophel's counsel was treated as God's own oracle — until one rejection drove him to hang himself.
RelatedPeople: King David; Absalom; Hushai the Archite; Eliam
LifeLesson: Brilliance without loyalty ends in despair; counsel is only as good as the master it serves.

Name: Ahitub, Ancestor of Ezra
Summary: Ancestor of Ezra named in his genealogy.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: A long line of priests ends in a scribe.

Name: Ahitub, Father of Meraioth
Summary: Father of Meraioth, in the Jerusalem priestly line of Seraiah son of Hilkiah (Nehemiah 11:11).
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: A father's name anchors his son's line.

Name: Ahitub, Father of Zadok
Summary: Ahitub is named as the father of Zadok, the priest who served David and anointed Solomon. He belongs to the Eleazar line, distinct from Ahitub son of Phinehas of Eli's house.
KeyStory: Ahitub fathered the priest who would anoint Solomon and carry the priesthood forward.
LifeLesson: Two men can share a name and belong to entirely different stories.

Name: Ahitub, Son of Amariah
Summary: Son of Amariah and priest in Aaron's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:7; 1 Chronicles 6:52: Son of Amariah and priest in Aaron's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahitub stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahitub, Son of Azariah
Summary: Son of Amariah and priest in Aaron's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:11; 1 Chronicles 6:52: Son of Amariah and priest in Aaron's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahitub stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahitub, Son of Phinehas
Summary: Ahitub, son of Phinehas and grandson of Eli, is named as the father of Ahiah, who served as priest wearing the ephod in Saul's camp.
KeyStory: Ahitub links Eli's fallen house to the priest who served Saul after the ark was lost.
LifeLesson: Even a broken priestly line still carried the ephod and the duty of seeking God.

Name: Ahlai, Father of Zabad
Summary: Father of Zabad among David's mighty men.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:41: Father of Zabad among David's mighty men.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ahlai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ahlai
Summary: Child of Sheshan, named in the Jerahmeel genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:31: Child of Sheshan, named in the Jerahmeel genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahlai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahoah
Summary: Son of Bela, named among the sons of Bela.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:4: Son of Bela, named among the sons of Bela.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahoah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahumai
Summary: Son of Jahath, named among the families of the Zorathites.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:2: Son of Jahath, named among the families of the Zorathites.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahumai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ahuzam
Summary: Son of Ashur by Naarah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:6: Son of Ashur by Naarah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ahuzam stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Aiah, Son of Zibeon
Summary: Son of Zibeon, named among the sons of Zibeon.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 1:40: Son of Zibeon, named among the sons of Zibeon.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Aiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Aiah
Summary: Aiah is named as the father of Rizpah, Saul's concubine and mother of Armoni and Mephibosheth.
KeyStory: Aiah's daughter became the mother whose vigil shamed a king into justice.
LifeLesson: A father's name survives in a daughter's famous grief.

Name: Akkub, Porter
Summary: Porter in the companies of the children of Levi.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:17: Porter in the companies of the children of Levi.
LifeLesson: The mention of Akkub in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Akkub, Son of Elioenai
Summary: Son of Elioenai son of Neariah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:24: Son of Elioenai son of Neariah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Akkub stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Akkub
Summary: A porter who returned with Zerubbabel, later taught the Law when Ezra read it and kept the gates at the wall's dedication.
KeyStory: Return from exile
KeyVerses: Ezra 2:42; Ezra 2:45; Nehemiah 7:45; Nehemiah 8:7; Nehemiah 11:19; Nehemiah 12:25
LifeLesson: Gatekeepers can also be teachers.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile; Ezra Reads the Law; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Alameth, Son of Becher
Summary: Son of Becher, named among the sons of Becher.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:8: Son of Becher, named among the sons of Becher.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Alameth stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Alemeth, Son of Jehoadah
Summary: Son of Jehoadah, named among the sons of Jehoadah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:36; 1 Chronicles 9:42: Son of Jehoadah, named among the sons of Jehoadah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Alemeth stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Alexander (1 Timothy)
Summary: Alexander is named in 1 Timothy alongside Hymenaeus as one delivered unto Satan that they might learn not to blaspheme. He is listed separately from Alexander the coppersmith of 2 Timothy, since the letters do not identify them as the same man.
KeyStory: Alexander is named in 1 Timothy alongside Hymenaeus as one delivered unto Satan that they might learn not to blaspheme. He is listed separately from Alexander the coppersmith of 2 Timothy, since the letters do not identify them as the same man.
LifeLesson: Discipline in the church aims at learning, not merely punishment.

Name: Alexander of Ephesus
Summary: Alexander was a man put forward by the Jews during the Ephesian riot, who tried to address the theatre crowd in defence of his people, but was shouted down when the crowd recognised him as a Jew. He is distinct from Alexander son of Simon of Cyrene and from Alexander named in the later epistles.
KeyStory: Alexander was thrust forward to speak in the theatre and drowned out by two hours of shouting.
LifeLesson: A crowd in uproar hears no defence. Alexander's silence warns us against reasoning with a riot.

Name: Alexander, Son of Simon of Cyrene
Summary: Alexander was a son of Simon of Cyrene, named by Mark alongside his brother Rufus, which suggests both brothers were known to Mark's readers as members of the early church.
KeyStory: Mark names Alexander only as the son of the man who carried Jesus' cross.
RelatedPeople: Simon of Cyrene; Rufus, Son of Simon of Cyrene
LifeLesson: A father's one afternoon at the cross shaped a family's faith. Alexander is remembered because Simon carried it.

Name: Alexander the Coppersmith
Role: Opponent who did Paul much evil
Summary: Alexander the coppersmith did Paul much evil and greatly withstood his words, so that Paul warns Timothy to beware of him. He is listed separately from the Alexander of 1 Timothy, since the letters do not identify them as the same man.
KeyStory: Alexander the coppersmith did Paul much evil and greatly withstood his words, so that Paul warns Timothy to beware of him. He is listed separately from the Alexander of 1 Timothy, since the letters do not identify them as the same man.
LifeLesson: Opposition to the gospel is met with warning, not vengeance; the Lord will reward.

Name: Allon, Son of Jedaiah
Summary: Son of Jedaiah son of Shimri son of Shemaiah in Simeon's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:37: Son of Jedaiah son of Shimri son of Shemaiah in Simeon's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Allon stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Alphaeus
Summary: Alphaeus was the father of the apostle James son of Alphaeus, and, by Mark's account, of Levi the tax collector who became the apostle Matthew. He is named only through his sons.
KeyStory: Alphaeus is known only as the father of two apostles, James and Levi, called from very different lives.
LifeLesson: A father can be remembered for the sons God called. Alphaeus raised two men Jesus chose.

Name: Amal
Summary: Son of Helem in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:35: Son of Helem in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Amal stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Amariah, Ancestor of Ezra
Summary: Ancestor of Ezra named in his genealogy; a different Amariah from the men of Nehemiah's day.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: A long line of priests ends in a scribe.

Name: Amariah, Chief Priest
Summary: Amariah the chief priest was set by Jehoshaphat over all matters of the LORD in the Jerusalem court of judges.
KeyStory: Jehoshaphat charged that Amariah the chief priest is over you in all matters of the LORD, and Zebadiah for all the king's matters.
RelatedPeople: King Jehoshaphat; Zebadiah, Son of Ishmael
LifeLesson: Judgment belongs to the LORD, so judges must act in His fear, faithfully, with a perfect heart.

Name: Amariah, Priest Distributor
Summary: Amariah served with Kore in the cities of the priests, giving portions to his brethren by courses under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Amariah served with Kore in the cities of the priests, giving portions to his brethren by courses under Hezekiah.
RelatedPeople: Kore, Son of Imnah; King Hezekiah
LifeLesson: Fair portions for every priest, great and small, came through faithful distributors.

Name: Amariah, Son of Azariah
Summary: Son of Azariah and priest in Aaron's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:11; 1 Chronicles 6:52: Son of Azariah and priest in Aaron's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Amariah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Amariah, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:42).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: The list ends with ordinary names, because ordinary people were the point.

Name: Amariah, Son of Hebron
Summary: Second son of Hebron in David's divisions.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 23:19; 1 Chronicles 24:23: Second son of Hebron in David's divisions.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Amariah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Amariah, Son of Hezekiah
Summary: Amariah, son of Hezekiah, is named only in Zephaniah's genealogy (Zephaniah 1:1), as the prophet's great-grandfather. He is one of several Amariahs in Scripture; this one is identified by his place in Zephaniah's line.
KeyStory: Amariah appears only in Zephaniah's genealogy, as the prophet's great-grandfather between Gedaliah and Hezekiah.
RelatedPeople: Zephaniah; Gedaliah, Son of Amariah; Hezekiah, Son of Amariah
LifeLesson: Amariah's one verse holds a whole generation together. Most of God's people live their lives in a single line of a genealogy — and that is enough.

Name: Amariah, Son of Meraioth
Summary: Son of Meraioth and priest in Aaron's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:7; 1 Chronicles 6:52: Son of Meraioth and priest in Aaron's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Amariah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Amariah, Son of Shephatiah
Summary: Amariah son of Shephatiah, named in Nehemiah 11:4.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Amariah the Priest
Summary: Priest who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:3) and returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:2); the course of Amariah in Joiakim's days bears his name (Nehemiah 12:13).
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: Sealing, returning, and heading a course: one priest's career.

Name: Amasa, Son of Abigail
Summary: Son of Abigail, David's sister, by Jether the Ishmeelite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:17: Son of Abigail, David's sister, by Jether the Ishmeelite.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Amasa stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Amasa, Son of Hadlai
Summary: Amasa, son of Hadlai, was one of the heads of Ephraim who stood up against bringing Judah's captives into Samaria.
KeyStory: Amasa the son of Hadlai stood with the other heads against the returning host.
LifeLesson: Mercy to captives began with leaders willing to stand up.

Name: Amasa, Son of Ithra
Summary: Amasa, son of Ithra and of Abigail, David's sister, commanded Absalom's army in the revolt. David forgave him and made him commander in Joab's place, and Joab murdered him at Gibeon while greeting him as a brother.
KeyStory: Amasa led Absalom's revolt, was forgiven and promoted — then murdered by Joab with a greeting kiss.
RelatedPeople: Ithra; Abigail, Daughter of Nahash; King David; Joab
LifeLesson: Forgiveness from a king is no shield against a rival's dagger.

Name: Amasa, Son of Jether
Summary: Amasa, son of Jether, had been Absalom's captain and then David's; in Kings he is named with Abner as one of the two captains Joab slew in peacetime.
KeyStory: Amasa named among Joab's peacetime victims.
RelatedPeople: King David; Joab, Son of Zeruiah; Abner, Son of Ner; Jether, Father of Amasa
LifeLesson: Changing sides does not change the danger of trusting the wrong commander.

Name: Amasai, Chief of Captains
Summary: Chief of the captains upon whom the spirit came, who declared, Thine are we, David, and on thy side.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:18: Chief of the captains upon whom the spirit came, who declared, Thine are we, David, and on thy side.
LifeLesson: The mention of Amasai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Amasai, Father of Mahath
Summary: Amasai was the father of Mahath, a Kohathite Levite who cleansed the temple under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Amasai is named only as the father of Mahath the son of Amasai.
LifeLesson: A Levite's father is named in the cleansing roster.

Name: Amasai, Priest of the Ark
Summary: Priest who blew with the trumpet before the ark of God.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:24: Priest who blew with the trumpet before the ark of God.
LifeLesson: The mention of Amasai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Amasai, Son of Elkanah
Summary: Son of Elkanah, named among the sons of Elkanah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:25: Son of Elkanah, named among the sons of Elkanah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Amasai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Amashai, Son of Azareel
Summary: Amashai son of Azareel, named in Nehemiah 11:13.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Amasiah, Son of Zichri
Summary: Amasiah, son of Zichri, willingly offered himself unto the LORD and commanded two hundred thousand mighty men of valour under Jehoshaphat.
KeyStory: Next to Jehohanan was Amasiah the son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself unto the LORD, with two hundred thousand mighty men.
LifeLesson: God's law taught throughout the land, and willing service under a faithful king, strengthened Judah.

Name: Amaziah, Father of Hashabiah
Summary: Father of Hashabiah in Ethan's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:45: Father of Hashabiah in Ethan's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Amaziah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Amaziah, King of Judah
Summary: Amaziah defeated Edom but brought Edom's gods home and worshipped them, then challenged Jehoash of Israel and was captured, and was later slain in a conspiracy at Lachish.
KeyStory: Amaziah defeats Edom, worships its gods, and falls to Jehoash.
RelatedPeople: Jehoash, King of Israel; Jehoaddan, Mother of Amaziah; Joash, King of Judah; Jehoaddan, of Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Victory can become a snare when the victor bows to the gods he just defeated.

Name: Amaziah, Son of Joash
Summary: Son of Joash in the kingly line of Judah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:12: Son of Joash in the kingly line of Judah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Amaziah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Amaziah
Summary: Amaziah was the priest of Bethel under Jeroboam II who tried to silence Amos. He reported Amos to the king as a conspirator, ordered him to flee to Judah and stop prophesying at Bethel, the king's sanctuary — and Amos answered with a prophecy of Amaziah's own ruin.
KeyStory: Amaziah, priest of the king's chapel at Bethel, accused Amos of conspiracy and ordered him out of Israel — and heard his own downfall pronounced in reply.
RelatedPeople: Amos; Jeroboam II, King of Israel
