LifeLesson: Amaziah defended an institution against God's word and lost everything. Never let loyalty to a place or a post overrule loyalty to the truth.

Name: Ami
Summary: Descendant of Solomon's servants listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Service in God's house spans generations.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Amittai
Summary: Amittai is named as the father of the prophet Jonah (Jonah 1:1), and Jonah is called 'son of Amittai' again in the history of Jeroboam II's reign, where his prophecy of Israel's restored borders came true.
KeyStory: Amittai's son Jonah, called 'son of Amittai,' was sent to Nineveh — and his earlier prophecy of Israel's borders had already proved true under Jeroboam II.
LifeLesson: Amittai's son ran from God and was still used by Him. A parent's legacy is not cancelled by a child's detour.

Name: Ammiel, Father of Machir
Summary: Ammiel of Lo-debar is named as the father of Machir, who sheltered Mephibosheth and later supplied David at Mahanaim.
KeyStory: Ammiel's son sheltered a lame prince and fed a fleeing king.
LifeLesson: A father's house can become a refuge for princes.

Name: Ammiel, Son of Obed-edom
Summary: Sixth son of Obed-edom the porter.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:5: Sixth son of Obed-edom the porter.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ammiel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ammihud, Father of Uthai
Summary: Father of Uthai in the Jerusalem list, son of Omri son of Imri son of Bani.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:4: Father of Uthai in the Jerusalem list, son of Omri son of Imri son of Bani.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ammihud in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ammihud, Son of Laadan
Summary: Son of Laadan and father of Elishama in Ephraim's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:26: Son of Laadan and father of Elishama in Ephraim's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ammihud stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Amminadab, Chief of Uzziel
Summary: Chief of the sons of Uzziel who brought up the ark, with his brethren an hundred and twelve.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:10; 1 Chronicles 15:11: Chief of the sons of Uzziel who brought up the ark, with his brethren an hundred and twelve.
LifeLesson: The mention of Amminadab in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Amminadab, Son of Kohath
Summary: Son of Kohath and father of Korah in the Kohathite line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:22: Son of Kohath and father of Korah in the Kohathite line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Amminadab stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ammizabad, Son of Benaiah
Summary: Son of Benaiah, in his father's course of the third month.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:6: Son of Benaiah, in his father's course of the third month.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ammizabad stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Amnon, Son of David
Summary: Firstborn son of David, born in Hebron to Ahinoam.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:1: Firstborn son of David, born in Hebron to Ahinoam.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Amnon stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Amnon, Son of Shimon
Summary: Son of Shimon in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:20: Son of Shimon in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Amnon stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Amnon
Summary: Amnon, David's firstborn by Ahinoam, lusted after his half-sister Tamar, tricked her into his chamber, and assaulted her, then hated her and cast her out. Two years later Absalom had him murdered at a sheep-shearing feast.
KeyStory: Amnon's lust for Tamar destroyed his sister, his standing, and finally his life.
RelatedPeople: King David; Ahinoam the Jezreelitess; Tamar, Daughter of David; Absalom
LifeLesson: Lust that takes what it wants and then hates what it took destroys everyone it touches.

Name: Amok
Summary: Priest who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Priests restored worship before walls were rebuilt.

Name: Amon, Governor of the City
Summary: Amon, governor of the city, was ordered by Ahab to hold Micaiah in prison on bread and water of affliction until the king returned in peace.
KeyStory: Ahab commanded that Micaiah be carried back to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son, and put in prison.
RelatedPeople: King Ahab; Micaiah, Son of Imla
LifeLesson: Carrying out an unjust order is still a share in the injustice.

Name: Amon, King of Judah
Summary: Amon, son of Manasseh, walked in all his father's ways and served the idols his father served, and after two years his servants conspired and slew him.
KeyStory: Amon's two-year reign and assassination.
RelatedPeople: Manasseh, King of Judah; Meshullemeth, Mother of Amon; King Josiah
LifeLesson: Following a father's sins without his repentance is a short road to ruin.

Name: Amon, Son of Manasseh
Summary: Son of Manasseh king of Judah in the kingly line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:14: Son of Manasseh king of Judah in the kingly line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Amon stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Amoz, Father of Isaiah
Summary: Amoz was the father of Isaiah the prophet, who wrote the acts of Uzziah and prayed with Hezekiah against Sennacherib.
KeyStory: Amoz is named as the father of Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.
LifeLesson: A prophet's father is remembered because his son spoke for God.

Name: Amplias
Summary: Amplias was a Roman Christian whom Paul greets as his beloved in the Lord.
KeyStory: Amplias was a Roman Christian whom Paul greets as his beloved in the Lord.
LifeLesson: To be beloved in the Lord is a title worth more than any earthly honour.

Name: Amram, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives; a different Amram from the father of Moses.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Sin named honestly is the first step back to God.

Name: Amram, Son of Dishon
Summary: Son of Dishon, named among the sons of Dishon the Horite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 1:41: Son of Dishon, named among the sons of Dishon the Horite.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Amram stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Amzi, Son of Zechariah
Summary: Amzi son of Zechariah, named in Nehemiah 11:12.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Amzi
Summary: Son of Hashabiah and father of Bani in Ethan's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:46: Son of Hashabiah and father of Bani in Ethan's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Amzi stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Anaiah
Summary: Stood beside Ezra on the platform at the reading of the law.
KeyStory: Ezra reads the law
LifeLesson: Standing to hear God's word is an act of reverence.

Name: Anan
Summary: Chief who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10).
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: A signature on a covenant is a public stand.

Name: Anani
Summary: Son of Elioenai son of Neariah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:24: Son of Elioenai son of Neariah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Anani stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ananiah, Grandfather of Azariah
Summary: Grandfather of Azariah the wall builder (Nehemiah 3:23: Azariah son of Maaseiah son of Ananiah). Not the town of Ananiah (Nehemiah 11:32).
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: A grandfather's name survives in his grandson's work.

Name: Ananias, Husband of Sapphira
Summary: Ananias, with his wife Sapphira, sold land and secretly kept back part of the price while presenting the rest as the whole gift. Confronted by Peter for lying to the Holy Spirit, he fell dead, and fear came on the whole church.
KeyStory: Ananias laid part of the price at the apostles' feet as if it were all, and fell dead at Peter's question.
LifeLesson: God does not demand everything, but He will not be lied to about it. Ananias kept his money and lost his life.

Name: Ananias of Damascus
Summary: Ananias was a devout disciple at Damascus whom the Lord sent to the blinded Saul after the Damascus road. He laid hands on Saul, who regained his sight and was baptised, and later defended Ananias' character before the Jerusalem crowd.
KeyStory: Ananias, who feared Saul's reputation, obeyed and called the persecutor brother, and Saul rose baptised.
LifeLesson: Obedience to a frightening assignment can open a persecutor's eyes. Ananias went, and Paul began.

Name: Ananias, the High Priest
Summary: Ananias the high priest ordered Paul struck during his defence before the Sanhedrin, and later came down to Caesarea with Tertullus to accuse Paul before Felix. He is distinct from Ananias of Damascus and from Ananias the husband of Sapphira.
KeyStory: Ananias ordered Paul struck on the mouth for speaking, and Paul answered with a prophecy he did not know he spoke.
LifeLesson: Office does not make a man just. Ananias used the high priesthood to strike a prisoner mid-sentence.

Name: Anath, Father of Shamgar
Summary: Anath is named only as the father of Shamgar, the judge who slew six hundred Philistines with an ox goad.
KeyStory: Anath appears in Judges only as Shamgar's father.
LifeLesson: A name in a lineage can be all that remains — and it is still worth recording.

Name: Anathoth, Son of Becher
Summary: Son of Becher, named among the sons of Becher.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:8: Son of Becher, named among the sons of Becher.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Anathoth stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Andronicus
Summary: Andronicus was a kinsman of Paul and a fellowprisoner, described as of note among the apostles and in Christ before Paul himself.
KeyStory: Andronicus was a kinsman of Paul and a fellowprisoner, described as of note among the apostles and in Christ before Paul himself.
LifeLesson: Faithfulness before we ever meet the famous is still faithfulness; God notes those who were in Christ early and stood firm.

Name: Aniam
Summary: Son of Shemidah, named among the sons of Shemidah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:19: Son of Shemidah, named among the sons of Shemidah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Aniam stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Annas
Summary: Annas was the former high priest and father-in-law of Caiaphas, still powerful enough that Jesus was first taken to him on the night of the arrest, and he sat among those who examined Peter and John after Pentecost.
KeyStory: Jesus was led first to Annas, who questioned Him before sending Him bound to Caiaphas.
RelatedPeople: Caiaphas; Simon Peter; John the Apostle
LifeLesson: Power that has passed can still do harm. Annas shows how influence lingers long after office ends.

Name: Antipas
Summary: Antipas was Christ's faithful martyr, slain among the believers at Pergamos, where, the letter to that church says, Satan dwells.
KeyStory: Antipas was Christ's faithful martyr, slain among the believers at Pergamos, where, the letter to that church says, Satan dwells.
LifeLesson: Faithfulness unto death in a hostile city is remembered by Christ himself.

Name: Antothijah
Summary: Named among the sons of Shashak in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:24: Named among the sons of Shashak in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Antothijah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Anub
Summary: Son of Coz, named in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:8: Son of Coz, named in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Anub stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Apelles
Summary: Apelles was a Roman Christian described by Paul as approved in Christ.
KeyStory: Apelles was a Roman Christian described by Paul as approved in Christ.
LifeLesson: Approval in Christ is proved by standing firm through testing, not by reputation.

Name: Aphiah
Summary: Aphiah is named as a Benjamite ancestor in Saul's genealogy, a man of the family from which Israel's first king came.
KeyStory: Aphiah stands at the head of the line that runs through Bechorath and Zeror to Kish and Saul.
LifeLesson: God raises kings from families the world counts as nothing.

Name: Aphses
Summary: Eighteenth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:15: Eighteenth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
LifeLesson: The mention of Aphses in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Apollos
Summary: Apollos was an eloquent Jew from Alexandria, mighty in the Scriptures, who preached at Ephesus knowing only the baptism of John until Aquila and Priscilla expounded the way of God more perfectly to him. He then helped the churches in Achaia mightily, showing from the Scriptures that Jesus was Christ.
KeyStory: Apollos preached boldly what he knew, learned more perfectly from a tentmaking couple, and proved from Scripture that Jesus was Christ.
LifeLesson: Apollos knew half the story and preached it well, then humbly learned the rest. Teachability made his eloquence useful.

Name: Appaim
Summary: Son of Nadab and father of Ishi.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:30: Son of Nadab and father of Ishi.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Appaim stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Apphia
Summary: Apphia, called beloved, is addressed with Philemon and Archippus at the opening of Paul's letter to Philemon.
KeyStory: Apphia, called beloved, is addressed with Philemon and Archippus at the opening of Paul's letter to Philemon.
LifeLesson: A sister addressed by name in a letter shares fully in its appeal.

Name: Ara, Son of Jether
Summary: Son of Jether in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:38: Son of Jether in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ara stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Arad, Son of Beriah
Summary: Named among the sons of Beriah in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:15: Named among the sons of Beriah in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Arad stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Arah
Summary: Son of Ulla in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:39: Son of Ulla in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Arah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Aram, Son of Shamer
Summary: Son of Shamer in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:34: Son of Shamer in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Aram stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Araunah the Jebusite
Summary: Araunah the Jebusite owned the threshingfloor where the destroying angel stopped during the plague after David's census. David insisted on buying it at full price rather than accepting it as a gift, and built an altar there — the future site of the temple.
KeyStory: Araunah offered his threshingfloor free, but David bought it at full price for an altar.
LifeLesson: A sacrifice that costs nothing is no sacrifice — David would not offer one.

Name: Archelaus
Summary: Archelaus was a son of Herod the Great who ruled Judea, Samaria, and Idumea after his father's death. Joseph, returning from Egypt, turned aside to Galilee when he heard Archelaus reigned in Judea.
KeyStory: One sentence in Matthew explains why Jesus grew up in Nazareth: Joseph feared Archelaus and settled in Galilee instead.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Mary, Mother of Jesus; Joseph, Husband of Mary; Herod the Great
LifeLesson: God guides His people through ordinary prudence as well as dreams. Joseph's detour to Nazareth fulfilled prophecy.

Name: Archippus
Summary: Archippus was Paul's fellow-soldier, addressed in Philemon, and charged in Colossians to take heed to the ministry he had received in the Lord and fulfil it.
KeyStory: Archippus was Paul's fellow-soldier, addressed in Philemon, and charged in Colossians to take heed to the ministry he had received in the Lord and fulfil it.
LifeLesson: A ministry received in the Lord deserves to be fulfilled, not merely begun.

Name: Ardon
Summary: Son of Caleb son of Hezron by Azubah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:18: Son of Caleb son of Hezron by Azubah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ardon stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Argob, Officer of Pekahiah
Summary: Argob was with Pekahiah in the palace at Samaria when Pekah conspired and smote the king; he is named among those slain with him.
KeyStory: Argob slain with Pekahiah.
RelatedPeople: Pekahiah, King of Israel; Pekah, King of Israel; Arieh, Officer of Pekahiah
LifeLesson: Standing beside a doomed king is itself a danger.

Name: Aridai
Summary: One of the ten sons of Haman, slain by the Jews in Shushan and afterwards hanged on the gallows.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: A house built on hatred falls with its builder.

Name: Aridatha
Summary: One of the ten sons of Haman, slain by the Jews in Shushan and afterwards hanged on the gallows.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: A house built on hatred falls with its builder.

Name: Arieh, Officer of Pekahiah
Summary: Arieh was with Pekahiah in the palace at Samaria when Pekah conspired and smote the king; he is named among those slain with him.
KeyStory: Arieh slain with Pekahiah.
RelatedPeople: Pekahiah, King of Israel; Pekah, King of Israel; Argob, Officer of Pekahiah
LifeLesson: Courtiers fall with the courts they serve.

Name: Ariel
Summary: A chief man sent by Ezra to bring Levites for the temple service.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: God's house needs its workers gathered deliberately.

Name: Arioch, Captain of the Guard
Summary: Arioch was captain of Nebuchadnezzar's guard who was sent to slay the wise men of Babylon when none could tell the king's dream; Daniel asked him why the decree was so hasty, and Arioch brought Daniel before the king. He is a different man from Arioch, king of Ellasar, who already has a profile.
KeyStory: Arioch was commanded to destroy the wise men, but Daniel sought him with counsel and wisdom, and Arioch brought Daniel in haste before the king.
LifeLesson: Even an executioner's errand can be interrupted by a wise question.

Name: Arisai
Summary: One of the ten sons of Haman, slain by the Jews in Shushan and afterwards hanged on the gallows.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: A house built on hatred falls with its builder.

Name: Aristarchus
Summary: Aristarchus was a Macedonian of Thessalonica who travelled with Paul, was seized in the Ephesian riot, accompanied Paul to Jerusalem and later to Rome, and shared his imprisonment there.
KeyStory: Aristarchus was dragged into the Ephesian theatre, sailed with Paul to Rome, and shared his prison.
LifeLesson: Aristarchus stayed from riot to prison. Faithful companions do not leave when the journey turns hard.

Name: Aristobulus
Role: Head of a household in Rome
Summary: Aristobulus is named only as the head of a household in Rome whose members Paul greets; the letter does not say whether Aristobulus himself was a believer.
KeyStory: Aristobulus is named only as the head of a household in Rome whose members Paul greets; the letter does not say whether Aristobulus himself was a believer.
LifeLesson: God's greeting reaches into whole households, and faith often takes root house by house.

Name: Armoni, Son of Saul
Summary: Armoni, son of Saul by his concubine Rizpah, was handed over with his brother Mephibosheth to the Gibeonites in atonement for Saul's slaughter of Gibeon, and was hanged at the beginning of barley harvest.
KeyStory: Armoni, Rizpah's son, was hanged for a bloodguilt he did not commit.
RelatedPeople: King Saul; Rizpah, Daughter of Aiah; Mephibosheth, Son of Saul
LifeLesson: The sins of kings are sometimes paid by sons who never sat on a throne.

Name: Arnan, Son of Rephaiah
Summary: Named in the chain of sons after Hananiah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:21: Named in the chain of sons after Hananiah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Arnan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Artaxerxes
Summary: King of Persia who first stopped Jerusalem's rebuilding, then authorized Ezra's return and Nehemiah's wall-building, and whose twentieth year dates Nehemiah's commission.
KeyStory: Rebuilding of the Temple
KeyVerses: Ezra 4:7; Ezra 4:8; Ezra 4:11; Ezra 4:23; Ezra 6:14; Ezra 7:1; Ezra 7:7; Ezra 7:11; Ezra 7:12; Ezra 7:21; Ezra 8:1; Nehemiah 2:1; Nehemiah 5:14; Nehemiah 13:6
LifeLesson: The same throne that hindered can later help; God turns kings' hearts.
RelatedEvents: Rebuilding of the Temple; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Artemas
Role: Messenger to be sent to Titus
Summary: Artemas was one whom Paul planned to send to Titus in Crete, so that Titus could then come to Paul at Nicopolis.
KeyStory: Artemas was one whom Paul planned to send to Titus in Crete, so that Titus could then come to Paul at Nicopolis.
LifeLesson: Relief workers in the gospel allow others to move on to the next task.

Name: Arza, Steward of Elah
Summary: Arza was steward of Elah's house in Tirzah, in whose house the drunken king was slain by Zimri.
KeyStory: Arza's house, where Elah was slain.
RelatedPeople: Elah, King of Israel; Zimri, King of Israel
LifeLesson: A steward's house became a crime scene when his master drank on duty.

Name: Asa, Father of Berechiah
Summary: Father of Berechiah the Levite, son of Elkanah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:16: Father of Berechiah the Levite, son of Elkanah.
LifeLesson: The mention of Asa in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Asahel, Overseer
Summary: Asahel was one of the overseers under Cononiah and Shimei over the offerings and tithes under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Asahel was one of the overseers under Cononiah and Shimei over the offerings and tithes under Hezekiah.
RelatedPeople: Cononiah, the Levite; Shimei, Brother of Cononiah; King Hezekiah; Azariah, Chief Priest
LifeLesson: Many overseers together kept one storehouse honest.

Name: Asahel, Son of Zeruiah
Summary: Son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, and one of David's valiant men.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:16; 1 Chronicles 11:26: Son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, and one of David's valiant men.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Asahel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Asahel, the Levite
Summary: Asahel was one of the Levites sent with Jehoshaphat's princes to teach the book of the law throughout Judah.
KeyStory: With the princes went Levites, including Asahel, teaching from the book of the law of the LORD.
LifeLesson: God's law taught throughout the land, and willing service under a faithful king, strengthened Judah.

Name: Asahel
Summary: Asahel, son of Zeruiah and brother of Joab, was swift of foot as a wild roe. He chased Abner alone at Gibeon and would not turn aside, so Abner killed him with the hinder end of his spear, and Joab never forgave it.
KeyStory: Asahel's speed carried him alone after Abner — and Abner killed him for it.
RelatedPeople: Zeruiah; Joab; Abishai; Abner, Son of Ner; Jonathan, Son of Asahel
LifeLesson: Speed without wisdom runs alone into a spear.

KeyVerses: Psalm 50:1; Psalm 73:1; 1 Chronicles 6:39; 1 Chronicles 15:17; 1 Chronicles 16:5; Ezra 2:41; Nehemiah 7:44; Nehemiah 11:17; Nehemiah 12:35; 2 Chronicles 5:12; 2 Chronicles 29:30; 2 Chronicles 35:15

KeyStory: Ashpenaz was ordered to feed the Judean youths the king's meat and wine, but Daniel proved him with pulse and water for ten days, and the youths appeared fairer than all who ate the king's portion.
LifeLesson: God can give a captive favour with his captor — and a captor can choose to listen.

Summary: Chief who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10).
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: A signature on a covenant is a public stand.

Name: Baal-hanan the Gederite
Summary: Gederite over the olive trees and sycomore trees in the low plains.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:28: Gederite over the olive trees and sycomore trees in the low plains.
LifeLesson: The mention of Baal-hanan in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Baal, Son of Jehiel
Summary: Son of Jehiel the father of Gibeon.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:30; 1 Chronicles 9:36: Son of Jehiel the father of Gibeon.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Baal stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Baal, Son of Reaia
Summary: Son of Reaia and father of Beerah in Reuben's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:5: Son of Reaia and father of Beerah in Reuben's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Baal stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Baana, Father of Zadok
Summary: Father of Zadok the wall builder; a different name from Baanah the leader.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: A father's name can open a son's story.

Name: Baanah, Father of Heleb
Summary: Baanah the Netophathite is named as the father of Heleb, one of David's thirty mighty men. He is distinct from Baanah son of Rimmon, who murdered Ish-bosheth.
KeyStory: Baanah the Netophathite fathered one of David's thirty.
LifeLesson: A father's name can belong to a warrior's house, not a murderer's.

Name: Baanah, Father of Heled
Summary: Father of Heled the Netophathite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:30: Father of Heled the Netophathite.
LifeLesson: The mention of Baanah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Baanah, Son of Hushai
Summary: Baanah, son of Hushai, was one of Solomon's twelve officers, over Asher and Aloth.
KeyStory: Baanah, officer over Asher.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Hushai, Father of Baanah
LifeLesson: The north's provision passed through steady hands.

Name: Baanah, Son of Rimmon
Summary: Baanah, son of Rimmon the Beerothite and a captain of Ish-bosheth's bands, murdered Ish-bosheth in his bed at noon with his brother Rechab and carried his head to David, expecting reward. David had both brothers executed.
KeyStory: Baanah murdered his own king for a reward and was executed for it the same day.
RelatedPeople: Ish-bosheth, Son of Saul; Rechab, Son of Rimmon; King David
LifeLesson: A brother in murder is a brother in judgment.

Name: Baanah
Role: Leader of the Return; Covenant Sealer
Summary: A leader who returned with Zerubbabel and later sealed the covenant.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Returning well and sealing the covenant belong together.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Baara
Summary: Wife of Shaharaim, named beside Hushim.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:8: Wife of Shaharaim, named beside Hushim.
LifeLesson: The mention of Baara in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Baaseiah, Son of Malchiah
Summary: Son of Malchiah and father of Michael in Asaph's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:40: Son of Malchiah and father of Michael in Asaph's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Baaseiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Baasha, King of Israel
Summary: Baasha of Issachar conspired against Nadab, wiped out Jeroboam's house as prophesied, yet walked in Jeroboam's sins himself and warred with Asa of Judah.
KeyStory: Baasha wipes out Jeroboam's house and repeats his sin.
RelatedPeople: Nadab, King of Israel; Elah, King of Israel; King Asa; Jehu, Son of Hanani; Ben-hadad, King of Syria
LifeLesson: God may use a man to judge another's sin and still judge that man for his own.

Name: Bakbakkar
Summary: Levite dwelling in Jerusalem after the return.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:15: Levite dwelling in Jerusalem after the return.
LifeLesson: The mention of Bakbakkar in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Bakbuk
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Bakbukiah
Summary: Levite among the Jerusalem residents (Nehemiah 11:17), in the watches (Nehemiah 12:9), and porter at the dedication (Nehemiah 12:25).
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: One Levite watched, waited, and kept the gates.

Name: Baladan, Father of Berodach-Baladan
Summary: Baladan was the father of Berodach-Baladan, king of Babylon, who sent to Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Baladan, father of Berodach-Baladan.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Bani, Father of Imri
Summary: Father of Imri in the Jerusalem list, of the children of Pharez.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:4: Father of Imri in the Jerusalem list, of the children of Pharez.
LifeLesson: The mention of Bani in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Bani, Son of Amzi
Summary: Son of Amzi and father of Shamer in Ethan's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:46: Son of Amzi and father of Shamer in Ethan's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Bani stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Bani, Son of Hashabiah
Summary: Bani son of Hashabiah, named in Nehemiah 11:22.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Bani the Gadite
Summary: Bani the Gadite was among David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Bani the Gadite stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: Gad across the Jordan gave David a warrior for the thirty.

Name: Bani the Levite
Summary: Levite who taught the law at Ezra's reading, prayed at the covenant renewal, and sealed the covenant; father of Uzzi the overseer (Nehemiah 8:7, 9:4, 9:5, 10:13, 11:22).
KeyStory: Ezra reads the law
LifeLesson: Teaching, praying, and signing: one Levite did all three.

Name: Bani
Summary: Head of a large returning family (642 in Ezra 2:10); his sons sealed the covenant (Ezra 2:10; Nehemiah 7:15, 10:14).
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: A family's return is recorded household by household.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Barabbas
Summary: Barabbas was a notorious prisoner, held for insurrection and murder, whom Pilate released at the Passover feast while the crowd demanded Jesus be crucified in his place.
KeyStory: The crowd chose Barabbas and sent Jesus to the cross, and the guilty man walked free on the innocent man's sentence.
LifeLesson: Barabbas is every one of us: set free because another took his place. His freedom cost Jesus His life.

Name: Barachel
Summary: Barachel the Buzite was the father of Elihu, named in Job as Elihu is introduced before his speeches.
KeyStory: Barachel himself speaks no words in the book; he is known only as Elihu's father, of the kindred of Ram.
LifeLesson: Even a one-line mention in Scripture counts: Barachel's son spoke truth, and a father's name is preserved with it.

Name: Bariah
Summary: Son of Shemaiah son of Shechaniah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:22: Son of Shemaiah son of Shechaniah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Bariah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Barkos
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Bartimaeus
Summary: Bartimaeus was a blind beggar sitting by the roadside near Jericho. Hearing that Jesus of Nazareth passed by, he cried out for mercy, threw aside his garment, and received his sight, then followed Jesus on the way.
KeyStory: Bartimaeus shouted over the crowd, Son of David, have mercy on me, and left his cloak behind when Jesus called.
LifeLesson: The crowd told him to be quiet, and he shouted louder. Mercy belongs to those who will not stop asking.

Name: Baruch, Son of Col-hozeh
Summary: Baruch son of Col-hozeh, named in Nehemiah 11:5.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Baruch, Son of Zabbai
Summary: Baruch son of Zabbai, named in Nehemiah 3:20.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Baruch
Summary: Baruch, son of Neriah, was Jeremiah's scribe. He wrote Jeremiah's words in a roll, read them in the temple, rewrote the scroll after Jehoiakim burned it, bought the field at Anathoth as witness to the promise, and was carried to Egypt with Jeremiah. When he despaired of his own sorrows, God told him to seek not great things for himself.
KeyStory: Baruch wrote at Jeremiah's mouth all the words of the Lord in a roll, read it in the Lord's house, and wrote it again after the king burned it, with many like words added.
KeyVerses: Jeremiah 32:12-16; Jeremiah 36:4-32; Jeremiah 43:1-7; Jeremiah 45:1-5; Nehemiah 10:6; Nehemiah 11:5
RelatedPeople: Jeremiah; Seraiah, Son of Neriah; Johanan, Son of Kareah
LifeLesson: Faithful writing and reading of God's word is ministry, even when the king burns the book.

Name: Barzillai the Gileadite
Summary: Barzillai the Gileadite, a very aged and wealthy man of Rogelim, brought beds, basins, wheat, barley, and food to David and his exhausted people at Mahanaim during Absalom's revolt. He refused David's invitation to Jerusalem and asked only that Chimham go in his place.
KeyStory: Barzillai fed a fleeing king at Mahanaim and asked nothing for himself in return.
KeyVerses: 2 Samuel 17:27; 2 Samuel 19:32; 2 Samuel 19:34; 2 Samuel 19:37; 1 Kings 2:7; Ezra 2:61; Nehemiah 7:63
RelatedPeople: King David; Chimham; King Solomon; Barzillai
LifeLesson: Generosity in a king's darkest hour, asking nothing back, is remembered for generations.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Barzillai
Summary: A priest who returned but could not prove his genealogy; he had taken his name from Barzillai the Gileadite, whose daughter he married.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Even an unproven genealogy is still recorded.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Basmath, Daughter of Solomon
Summary: Basmath, a daughter of Solomon, was given as wife to Ahimaaz, one of Solomon's officers over Naphtali.
KeyStory: Basmath, wife of Ahimaaz.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Ahimaaz, Officer of Solomon
LifeLesson: A princess married to an officer still lived by the kingdom's provision.

Name: Bavai, Son of Henadad
Summary: Bavai son of Henadad, named in Nehemiah 3:18.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Bazluth
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Bealiah
Summary: One of those who came to David at Ziklag.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:5: One of those who came to David at Ziklag.
LifeLesson: The mention of Bealiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Bebai
Summary: Head of a family listed among those who returned from exile.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: A family's return is recorded household by household.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Becher, Son of Benjamin
Summary: Son of Benjamin, named among the sons of Benjamin.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:6: Son of Benjamin, named among the sons of Benjamin.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Becher stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Bechorath
Summary: Bechorath, son of Aphiah, is named in Saul's genealogy between Aphiah and Zeror.
KeyStory: Bechorath links Aphiah's line to Zeror, Abiel, Kish, and Saul.
LifeLesson: Every link in a family line matters to the story God is writing.

Name: Bedan, Son of Ulam
Summary: Son of Ulam, named among the sons of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:17: Son of Ulam, named among the sons of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Bedan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Bedeiah, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:35).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: The law applied to every household alike.

Name: Beeliada, Son of David
Summary: Son of David born in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 14:7: Son of David born in Jerusalem.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Beeliada stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Beera, Daughter of Zophah
Summary: Daughter of Zophah in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:37: Daughter of Zophah in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Beera stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Beerah, Son of Baal
Summary: Son of Baal and prince of the Reubenites, carried away captive by Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:6: Son of Baal and prince of the Reubenites, carried away captive by Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Beerah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Beeri, Father of Hosea
Summary: Beeri is named only as the father of the prophet Hosea (Hosea 1:1). Nothing else is told of him; his place in Scripture is as the father of a prophet whose own family became God's sermon to Israel.
KeyStory: Beeri's only mention is as Hosea's father, in the opening line of his son's prophecy.
LifeLesson: Beeri is a reminder that some saints are remembered for one thing only: raising a child God would use. That is no small legacy.

Name: Bela, Son of Azaz
Summary: Son of Azaz son of Shema son of Joel, who dwelt in Aroer.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:8: Son of Azaz son of Shema son of Joel, who dwelt in Aroer.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Bela stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Bela, Son of Benjamin
Summary: Son of Benjamin, named among the sons of Benjamin.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:6; 1 Chronicles 8:1: Son of Benjamin, named among the sons of Benjamin.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Bela stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Belshazzar
Summary: Belshazzar was king of Babylon who, at a great feast for a thousand lords, drank wine from the gold and silver vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple, praising gods of gold and silver; a hand wrote Mene, Mene, Tekel, Upharsin on the wall, Daniel interpreted it — God had numbered his kingdom and finished it — and that very night Belshazzar was slain and Darius the Mede took the kingdom.
KeyStory: At Belshazzar's feast the fingers of a man's hand wrote on the plaster of the wall, and Daniel read the writing: thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting.
RelatedPeople: King Nebuchadnezzar; Daniel; Darius the Mede
LifeLesson: Drinking from vessels taken from God's house while praising idols is the last feast before the writing on the wall.

Name: Ben-Abinadab, Officer of Solomon
Summary: Ben-Abinadab was one of Solomon's twelve officers, over Dor, and had Solomon's daughter Taphath as wife.
KeyStory: Ben-Abinadab, officer over Dor.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Taphath, Daughter of Solomon
LifeLesson: Marriage into the king's house did not exempt an officer from his month's duty.

Name: Ben-Dekar, Officer of Solomon
Summary: Ben-Dekar was one of Solomon's twelve officers, over Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh, and Elon-beth-hanan.
KeyStory: Ben-Dekar, officer over Makaz and Beth-shemesh.
LifeLesson: Small districts, faithfully governed, hold a kingdom together.

Name: Ben-Geber, Officer of Solomon
Summary: Ben-Geber was one of Solomon's twelve officers, over Ramoth-gilead and the towns of Jair and the region of Argob.
KeyStory: Ben-Geber, officer over Ramoth-gilead.
LifeLesson: Frontier districts need steady men, not only strong ones.

Name: Ben-Hadad I, King of Syria
Summary: Ben-Hadad, son of Tabrimon and grandson of Hezion, king of Syria, took Asa's silver and gold and attacked Baasha's cities, breaking his league with Israel.
KeyStory: Ben-Hadad I breaks with Baasha for Asa.
RelatedPeople: King Asa; Baasha, King of Israel; Tabrimon, Father of Ben-Hadad I
LifeLesson: Bought allies fight for the payer, not for the cause.

Name: Ben-Hadad II, King of Syria
Summary: Ben-Hadad, king of Syria in Ahab's days, besieged Samaria twice and was twice defeated, then was smothered by his servant Hazael, who took his throne.
KeyStory: Ben-Hadad II besieges Samaria and is murdered by Hazael.
RelatedPeople: King Ahab; Hazael, King of Syria
LifeLesson: A king who trusted his servant's blanket more than God's prophet died by it.

Name: Ben-Hadad III, King of Syria
Summary: Ben-Hadad, son of Hazael, reigned after his father and oppressed Israel until Jehoahaz prayed, and Jehoash recovered from him the cities his father had taken.
KeyStory: Ben-Hadad III oppresses Israel until Jehoash recovers the cities.
RelatedPeople: Hazael, King of Syria; Jehoahaz, King of Israel; Jehoash, King of Israel
LifeLesson: Oppression outlives the oppressor, but so does God's answer to prayer.

Name: Ben-hadad, King of Syria
Summary: Ben-hadad, king of Syria at Damascus, accepted Asa's silver and gold, broke his league with Baasha, and sent his captains against the cities of Israel.
KeyStory: Ben-hadad smote Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim and the store cities of Naphtali, and Baasha left off building Ramah.
RelatedPeople: King Asa; Baasha, King of Israel
LifeLesson: Relying on a foreign alliance instead of the LORD brought Asa a rebuke, even when it worked.

Name: Ben-hanan
Summary: Son of Shimon in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:20: Son of Shimon in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ben-hanan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ben-Hesed, Officer of Solomon
Summary: Ben-Hesed was one of Solomon's twelve officers, over Aruboth, Sochoh, and the land of Hepher.
KeyStory: Ben-Hesed, officer over Aruboth and Hepher.
LifeLesson: Faithful administration is rarely sung, but always needed.

Name: Ben-Hur, Officer of Solomon
Summary: Ben-Hur was one of Solomon's twelve officers, over the hill country of Ephraim, providing food for the king's household one month a year.
KeyStory: Ben-Hur, officer over Ephraim.
LifeLesson: A month's provision, given faithfully, fed a kingdom.

Name: Ben, Singer
Summary: Levite of the second degree appointed at the bringing up of the ark.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:18: Levite of the second degree appointed at the bringing up of the ark.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ben in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ben-zoheth
Summary: Son of Ishi in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:20: Son of Ishi in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ben-zoheth stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Benaiah, Ancestor of Jahaziel
Role: Levite of the Sons of Asaph
Summary: Benaiah, son of Jeiel, was an ancestor of Jahaziel, father of Zechariah in the line of Asaph's singers.
KeyStory: Benaiah stands in Jahaziel's line: son of Jeiel, father of Zechariah.
RelatedPeople: Jahaziel, Son of Zechariah; Zechariah, Father of Jahaziel
LifeLesson: A singer's family line carried the praise that met an invading army.

Name: Benaiah, Overseer
Summary: Benaiah was one of the overseers under Cononiah and Shimei over the offerings and tithes under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Benaiah was one of the overseers under Cononiah and Shimei over the offerings and tithes under Hezekiah.
RelatedPeople: Cononiah, the Levite; Shimei, Brother of Cononiah; King Hezekiah; Azariah, Chief Priest
LifeLesson: Many overseers together kept one storehouse honest.

Name: Benaiah, Priest of the Ark
Summary: Priest who blew with the trumpet before the ark of God.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:24: Priest who blew with the trumpet before the ark of God.
LifeLesson: The mention of Benaiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Benaiah, Prince of Simeon
Summary: Prince of Simeon named among those whose families increased greatly.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:36: Prince of Simeon named among those whose families increased greatly.
LifeLesson: The mention of Benaiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Benaiah, Singer of Second Degree
Summary: Levite of the second degree appointed to sing with psalteries on Alamoth at the bringing up of the ark.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:18; 1 Chronicles 15:20: Levite of the second degree appointed to sing with psalteries on Alamoth at the bringing up of the ark.
LifeLesson: The mention of Benaiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Benaiah, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Benaiah, Son of Jehoiada
Summary: Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, was a valiant man of Kabzeel who slew two lionlike men of Moab, killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day, and slew a great Egyptian with his own spear. David set him over his guard.
KeyStory: Benaiah killed lions in pits, giants with their own spears, and two lionlike men of Moab.
KeyVerses: 2 Samuel 8:18; 2 Samuel 23:20; 2 Samuel 23:21; 2 Samuel 23:22; 2 Samuel 23:23; 1 Kings 1:8; 1 Kings 2:34; 1 Chronicles 11:22; 1 Chronicles 18:17
RelatedPeople: King David; Jehoiada, Father of Benaiah; Joab; King Solomon; Joab, Son of Zeruiah
LifeLesson: Courage in pits and snow is the same courage that guards a throne.

Name: Benaiah, Son of Nebo
Summary: Son of Nebo named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Benaiah, Son of Pahath-moab
Summary: Son of Pahath-moab named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Benaiah, Son of Parosh
Summary: Son of Parosh named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Benaiah the Pirathonite
Summary: Benaiah the Pirathonite was among David's thirty mighty men. He is distinct from Benaiah son of Jehoiada, captain of the guard.
KeyStory: Benaiah the Pirathonite stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: Two Benaiahs served David — a captain and a thirty-man — and both were valiant.

Name: Benhail, Prince of Judah
Summary: Benhail was one of the princes Jehoshaphat sent in his third year to teach in the cities of Judah.
KeyStory: In Jehoshaphat's third year he sent his princes, including Benhail, to teach in the cities of Judah.
LifeLesson: God's law taught throughout the land, and willing service under a faithful king, strengthened Judah.

Name: Beninu
Summary: Levite who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10).
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: A signature on a covenant is a public stand.

Name: Benjamin, of Jerusalem
Summary: A Benjamin who repaired a section of the wall (Nehemiah 3:23) and a Benjamin who played at the dedication (Nehemiah 12:34); whether one man or two is not stated. Not Benjamin, Jacob's son.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: Jerusalem's builders and musicians are both named.

Name: Benjamin, Son of Bilhan
Summary: Son of Bilhan, named among the sons of Bilhan.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:10: Son of Bilhan, named among the sons of Bilhan.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Benjamin stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Benjamin, Son of Harim
Summary: Son of Harim named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10:31-32).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Beno, Son of Jaaziah
Summary: Son of Jaaziah, named among the sons of Merari by Jaaziah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:26: Son of Jaaziah, named among the sons of Merari by Jaaziah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Beno stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Berachah, Son of Ziklag Band
Summary: One of those who came to David at Ziklag, of Saul's brethren of Benjamin.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:3: One of those who came to David at Ziklag, of Saul's brethren of Benjamin.
LifeLesson: The mention of Berachah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Berachiah, Father of Asaph
Summary: Father of Asaph the singer, son of Shimea.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:39: Father of Asaph the singer, son of Shimea.
LifeLesson: The mention of Berachiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Beraiah
Summary: Named among the sons of Shimhi in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:21: Named among the sons of Shimhi in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Beraiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Berechiah, Doorkeeper
Summary: Doorkeeper for the ark at its bringing up.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:23: Doorkeeper for the ark at its bringing up.
LifeLesson: The mention of Berechiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Berechiah, Father of Meshullam
Summary: Father of Meshullam the wall builder (Nehemiah 3:4, 6:18).
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: A father's name stands behind his son's work.

Name: Berechiah, Son of Asa
Summary: Son of Asa son of Elkanah, Levite who dwelt in the villages of the Netophathites.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:16: Son of Asa son of Elkanah, Levite who dwelt in the villages of the Netophathites.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Berechiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Berechiah, Son of Meshezabeel
Summary: Grandfather of Meshullam the wall builder, named in his genealogy (Nehemiah 3:4).
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: A grandfather's name survives in his grandson's work.

Name: Berechiah, Son of Meshillemoth
Summary: Berechiah, son of Meshillemoth, was one of the heads of Ephraim who stood up against bringing Judah's captives into Samaria.
KeyStory: Berechiah the son of Meshillemoth stood with the other heads against the returning host.
LifeLesson: Four heads together stopped a city from adding sin to sin.

Name: Berechiah, Son of Zerubbabel
Summary: Named among the sons of Zerubbabel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:20: Named among the sons of Zerubbabel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Berechiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Berechiah
Summary: Berechiah is named as the father of the prophet Zechariah (Zechariah 1:1, 1:7). Nothing else is told of him.
KeyStory: Berechiah's mentions are as Zechariah's father, in the opening verses of his son's prophecy.
LifeLesson: Berechiah, like Beeri and Pethuel, is remembered for a son God used. The quiet work of a household echoes in prophecy.

Name: Bered, Son of Shuthelah
Summary: Son of Shuthelah and father of Tahath in Ephraim's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:20: Son of Shuthelah and father of Tahath in Ephraim's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Bered stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Beri, Son of Zophah
Summary: Son of Zophah in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:36: Son of Zophah in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Beri stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Beriah, Son of Elpaal
Summary: Son of Elpaal and head of the fathers of the inhabitants of Aijalon, who drove away the inhabitants of Gath.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:13: Son of Elpaal and head of the fathers of the inhabitants of Aijalon, who drove away the inhabitants of Gath.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Beriah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Beriah, Son of Ephraim
Summary: Son born to Ephraim after Ezer and Elead were slain, named Beriah because it went evil with his house.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:23: Son born to Ephraim after Ezer and Elead were slain, named Beriah because it went evil with his house.
LifeLesson: The mention of Beriah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Beriah, Son of Shimei
Summary: Son of Shimei, named among the sons of Shimei.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 23:10: Son of Shimei, named among the sons of Shimei.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Beriah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Bernice
Summary: Bernice was the sister of Herod Agrippa II and accompanied him to Caesarea, where she sat in state to hear Paul's defence before Festus and Agrippa.
KeyStory: Bernice entered with great pomp to hear a prisoner, and left having heard the gospel from his own lips.
LifeLesson: Pomp cannot protect a soul from the word it hears. Bernice heard Paul and is left, like Agrippa, at the edge of decision.

Name: Berodach-Baladan, King of Babylon
Summary: Berodach-Baladan, son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah when he heard he had been sick, and Hezekiah showed him all his treasures.
KeyStory: Berodach-Baladan's embassy to Hezekiah.
RelatedPeople: King Hezekiah; Baladan, Father of Berodach-Baladan
LifeLesson: Showing off treasure to a foreign embassy invites the embassy's army.

Name: Besai
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Besodeiah
Summary: Father of Meshullam the wall builder (Nehemiah 3:6).
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: A father's name stands behind his son's work.

Name: Beth-rapha
Summary: Son of Eshton, named in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:12: Son of Eshton, named in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Beth-rapha stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Bezai
Summary: Head of a family listed among those who returned from exile.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: A family's return is recorded household by household.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Bezaleel, Son of Pahath-moab
Summary: Son of Pahath-moab named among those who had taken foreign wives; a different Bezaleel from the tabernacle craftsman.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Sin named honestly is the first step back to God.

Name: Bezer, Son of Zophah
Summary: Son of Zophah in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:37: Son of Zophah in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Bezer stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Bichri
Summary: Bichri is named as the father of Sheba, the Benjamite who raised a revolt against David after Absalom's fall.
KeyStory: Bichri's son blew the trumpet that split Israel after Absalom.
LifeLesson: A father's name is carried into rebellion by his son.

Name: Bigtha
Summary: One of the seven chamberlains who served Ahasuerus at his feast.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: Even attendants at a feast are part of the story.

Name: Bigthan
Summary: Chamberlain and doorkeeper who with Teresh conspired against Ahasuerus; Mordecai exposed the plot and both were hanged. The name is spelled Bigthana in Esther 6.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: A plot exposed in time saves a king and a people.

Name: Bigvai
Role: Leader of the Return; Head of a Father's House
Summary: A leader who returned with Zerubbabel, head of a large family, whose sons also returned with Ezra.
KeyStory: Return from exile
KeyVerses: Ezra 2:2; Ezra 2:14; Ezra 8:14; Nehemiah 7:7; Nehemiah 7:19; Nehemiah 10:16
LifeLesson: Faithfulness in returning to rebuild is remembered by name.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Bilgah, Course Head
Summary: Fifteenth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:14: Fifteenth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
LifeLesson: The mention of Bilgah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Bilgah
Summary: Priest who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10).
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: A signature on a covenant is a public stand.

Name: Bilhan, Son of Jediael
Summary: Son of Jediael and father of Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tharshish, and Ahishahar.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:10: Son of Jediael and father of Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tharshish, and Ahishahar.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Bilhan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Bilshan
Summary: A leader who returned with Zerubbabel, named in both return lists.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Faithfulness in returning to rebuild is remembered by name.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Bimhal
Summary: Son of Japhlet, named among the children of Japhlet.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:33: Son of Japhlet, named among the children of Japhlet.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Bimhal stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Binea, Son of Moza
Summary: Son of Moza, father of Rapha in the chapter 8 list.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:37; 1 Chronicles 9:43: Son of Moza, father of Rapha in the chapter 8 list.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Binea stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Binnui
Summary: A Levite who sealed the covenant, repaired the wall, and is named as father of Noadiah.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
KeyVerses: Ezra 8:33; Ezra 10:30; Ezra 10:38; Nehemiah 3:24; Nehemiah 7:15; Nehemiah 10:9; Nehemiah 12:8
LifeLesson: One man's service can span treasure, wall, and covenant.
RelatedEvents: Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall; Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Bishlam
Summary: Named among those who wrote to Artaxerxes against Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Rebuilding of the Temple
LifeLesson: Opposition to rebuilding is an old story.

Name: Bithiah
Summary: Daughter of Pharaoh whom Mered took, named as mother of Mered's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:18: Daughter of Pharaoh whom Mered took, named as mother of Mered's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Bithiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Biztha
Summary: One of the seven chamberlains who served Ahasuerus at his feast.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: Even attendants at a feast are part of the story.

Name: Blastus
Summary: Blastus was the king's chamberlain through whom the people of Tyre and Sidon sought peace with Herod Agrippa I, having made him their friend, because their country was nourished by the king's country.
KeyStory: Tyre and Sidon made Blastus their friend to sue for peace with the king who fed them.
LifeLesson: Courtiers open doors that armies cannot. Blastus turned a trade quarrel into a peace embassy.

Name: Bocheru
Summary: Son of Azel, named among the six sons of Azel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:38; 1 Chronicles 9:44: Son of Azel, named among the six sons of Azel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Bocheru stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Bukki, Ancestor of Ezra
Summary: Ancestor of Ezra named in his genealogy, son of Abishua.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: A long line of priests ends in a scribe.

Name: Bukki, Son of Abishua
Summary: Son of Abishua and priest in Aaron's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:5; 1 Chronicles 6:51: Son of Abishua and priest in Aaron's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Bukki stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Bukkiah, Son of Heman
Summary: Son of Heman the king's seer, sixth lot for song.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 25:4; 1 Chronicles 25:13: Son of Heman the king's seer, sixth lot for song.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Bukkiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Bunah
Summary: Son of Jerahmeel, named among the sons of Jerahmeel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:25: Son of Jerahmeel, named among the sons of Jerahmeel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Bunah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Bunni
Summary: Levite who led prayer at the covenant renewal.
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: Prayer and confession renew a covenant people.

Name: Buz, Father of Jahdo
Summary: Father of Jahdo in Gad's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:14: Father of Jahdo in Gad's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Buz in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Caesar Augustus
Summary: Caesar Augustus was the first Roman emperor. His decree that all the world be taxed sent Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, where Jesus was born, fulfilling the prophecy of the Messiah's birthplace.
KeyStory: An emperor's census moved a carpenter's family to Bethlehem, and prophecy was fulfilled by a tax form.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Mary, Mother of Jesus; Joseph, Husband of Mary
LifeLesson: God uses the decrees of empires to keep His promises. Augustus thought he was counting subjects; he was staging a birth.

Name: Caiaphas
Summary: Caiaphas was high priest during Jesus' ministry and trial. He advised that one man should die for the people, presided over the night hearing that condemned Jesus, and later opposed the apostles.
KeyStory: Caiaphas tore his clothes at Jesus' claim and declared Him guilty of blasphemy before the council.
LifeLesson: Caiaphas was right that one man would die for the people, and wrong about everything it meant. God can speak truth through unwilling lips.

Name: Calcol
Summary: Son of Zerah, named among the five sons of Zerah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:6: Son of Zerah, named among the five sons of Zerah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Calcol stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Caleb, Son of Hezron
Summary: Son of Hezron, also called Chelubai, father of a large Judahite family.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:18; 1 Chronicles 2:42: Son of Hezron, also called Chelubai, father of a large Judahite family.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Caleb stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Caleb, Son of Hur
Summary: Son of Hur, firstborn of Ephratah, and father of Shobal, Salma, and Hareph.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:50: Son of Hur, firstborn of Ephratah, and father of Shobal, Salma, and Hareph.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Caleb stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Carcas
Summary: One of the seven chamberlains who served Ahasuerus at his feast.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: Even attendants at a feast are part of the story.

Name: Careah, Father of Johanan
Summary: Careah was the father of Johanan, captain under Gedaliah at Mizpah.
KeyStory: Careah, father of Johanan.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Carmi, Son of Reuben
Summary: Son of Reuben the firstborn of Israel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:3: Son of Reuben the firstborn of Israel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Carmi stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Carpus
Role: Host at Troas who kept Paul's belongings
Summary: Carpus was the believer at Troas with whom Paul left his cloke, books, and parchments, which he asks Timothy to bring.
KeyStory: Carpus was the believer at Troas with whom Paul left his cloke, books, and parchments, which he asks Timothy to bring.
LifeLesson: Keeping another's books safe is a small trust that serves a great work.

Name: Carshena
Summary: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media who saw the king's face and advised on Vashti's deposition.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: Counsel near the throne carries weight for a kingdom.

Name: Chalcol
Summary: Chalcol, son of Mahol, was named among the wise men with whom Solomon's wisdom was compared.
KeyStory: Chalcol named among the wise.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Ethan the Ezrahite; Darda; Mahol, Father of Chalcol and Darda
LifeLesson: A wise name on a list is still a life God noticed.

Name: Chelal, Son of Pahath-moab
Summary: Son of Pahath-moab named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Chelluh, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:35).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: God's people are called to holy distinctness.

Name: Chelub, Brother of Shuah
Summary: Brother of Shuah and father of Mehir.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:11: Brother of Shuah and father of Mehir.
LifeLesson: The mention of Chelub in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Chenaanah, Father of Zedekiah the Prophet
Summary: Chenaanah was the father of Zedekiah, the false prophet who promised Ahab victory.
KeyStory: Chenaanah, father of Zedekiah.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Chenaanah, Father of Zedekiah
Summary: Chenaanah was the father of Zedekiah, the prophet who made horns of iron before Ahab.
KeyStory: Chenaanah is named only as the father of Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah.
LifeLesson: A name in a prophet's patronymic is still part of the record.

Name: Chenaanah
Summary: Son of Bilhan, named among the sons of Bilhan.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:10: Son of Bilhan, named among the sons of Bilhan.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Chenaanah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Chenani
Summary: Levite who led prayer at the covenant renewal.
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: Prayer and confession renew a covenant people.

Name: Chenaniah, Master of Song
Summary: Chief of the Levites for song, who instructed about the song because he was skilful.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:22; 1 Chronicles 15:27: Chief of the Levites for song, who instructed about the song because he was skilful.
LifeLesson: The mention of Chenaniah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Chenaniah, Officer
Summary: Of the Izharites, with his sons, for the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:29: Of the Izharites, with his sons, for the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges.
LifeLesson: The mention of Chenaniah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Chileab
Summary: Chileab, David's second son by Abigail, was born at Hebron. He is named among David's six sons born there and then disappears from the record.
KeyStory: Chileab, son of Abigail, was David's second son, born at Hebron.
LifeLesson: Some sons of kings are named once — and the record still counts them.

Name: Chilion, Son of Elimelech
Summary: Chilion, son of Elimelech and Naomi, died in Moab after marrying Orpah.
KeyStory: Chilion went with his family to Moab, married Orpah, and died there with his brother, leaving Naomi widowed and childless.
RelatedPeople: Elimelech; Naomi; Orpah; Mahlon, Son of Elimelech
LifeLesson: Two brothers, two Moabite wives, two early graves — and Naomi left alone.

Name: Chimham
Summary: Chimham was associated with Barzillai the Gileadite, who asked David to let Chimham cross the Jordan and live at court in his place when Barzillai himself was too old to go to Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Chimham crossed over to David's court in the place of the aged Barzillai.
LifeLesson: Going in another's place is its own quiet honour.

Name: Chloe of Corinth
Role: Head of a household in Corinth
Summary: Chloe is named in 1 Corinthians 1:11 as head of a household whose members reported the contentions dividing the Corinthian church.
KeyStory: Chloe is named in 1 Corinthians 1:11 as head of a household whose members reported the contentions dividing the Corinthian church.
LifeLesson: Honest reports about division are the first step toward healing it.

Name: Chushan-rishathaim
Summary: Chushan-rishathaim, king of Mesopotamia, was the first oppressor of Israel in Judges; Israel served him eight years until Othniel delivered them.
KeyStory: After Israel did evil, God sold them into the hand of Chushan-rishathaim, whom they served eight years before Othniel's deliverance.
LifeLesson: Oppression in Judges always follows the same pattern: evil, bondage, crying out, and a deliverer.

Name: Chuza
Summary: Chuza was the steward of Herod Antipas' household and the husband of Joanna, who followed and supported Jesus. His household thus touched both Herod's court and Jesus' ministry.
KeyStory: Chuza managed Herod's house while his wife Joanna travelled with Jesus and supported Him.
LifeLesson: God works inside powerful households through ordinary stewards. Chuza's home became a bridge between court and kingdom.

Name: Claudia
Summary: Claudia was one of the believers with Paul in Rome who sends greetings in 2 Timothy, alongside Eubulus, Pudens, and Linus.
KeyStory: Claudia was one of the believers with Paul in Rome who sends greetings in 2 Timothy, alongside Eubulus, Pudens, and Linus.
LifeLesson: Women stood among the believers who stayed with Paul in Rome.

Name: Claudius Caesar
Summary: Claudius Caesar was emperor in the 40s and 50s AD. A famine in his reign sent relief from Antioch to Judea, and his expulsion of Jews from Rome sent Aquila and Priscilla to Corinth, where they met Paul.
KeyStory: Claudius expelled the Jews from Rome, and the exiles Aquila and Priscilla became Paul's fellow workers in Corinth.
LifeLesson: An emperor's edict scattered believers, and the scattering planted churches. God writes straight with crooked decrees.

Name: Claudius Lysias
Summary: Claudius Lysias was the chief captain of the Roman garrison at Jerusalem who rescued Paul from the temple mob, arrested him, and, learning he was a Roman citizen, sent him under guard to Felix at Caesarea with a letter stating the case.
KeyStory: Lysias pulled Paul from the mob, learned he was a Roman, and sent him by night to Caesarea with a letter.
RelatedPeople: Paul; Felix; Ananias, the High Priest
LifeLesson: A Roman's letter carried Paul to his next hearing. Lysias did justice without knowing the gospel he protected.

Name: Clement
Summary: Clement was a fellowlabourer with Paul at Philippi whose name, Paul says, is in the book of life. He is traditionally, but not certainly, identified with Clement of Rome.
KeyStory: Clement was a fellowlabourer with Paul at Philippi whose name, Paul says, is in the book of life. He is traditionally, but not certainly, identified with Clement of Rome.
LifeLesson: Labouring in the gospel is recorded where it matters most, in the book of life.

Name: Cleopas
Summary: Cleopas was one of the two disciples who met the risen Jesus on the road to Emmaus and recognised Him in the breaking of bread. He is traditionally identified with Cleophas, the husband of Mary named at the cross in John's Gospel.
KeyStory: Cleopas walked seven miles with a stranger who opened the Scriptures, and knew Him when He broke the bread.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Mary, Mother of James and Joses
LifeLesson: Jesus meets us on ordinary roads and opens the Scriptures before He opens our eyes. Walk with Him and listen.

Name: Col-hozeh
Summary: Father of Shallun the wall builder, and ancestor in Maaseiah's Jerusalem line (Nehemiah 3:15, 11:5).
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: A father's name lives on in his children's work.

Name: Cononiah, Chief of the Levites
Summary: Cononiah, chief of the Levites with Shemaiah, Nethaneel, Hashabiah, Jeiel and Jozabad, gave the Levites five thousand small cattle and five hundred oxen for Josiah's Passover.
KeyStory: Conaniah also, and Shemaiah and Nethaneel, his brethren, and Hashabiah and Jeiel and Jozabad, chief of the Levites, gave unto the Levites for passover offerings.
RelatedPeople: Shemaiah, Chief of the Levites; Nethaneel, Chief of the Levites; King Josiah
LifeLesson: Levite chiefs gave so their brethren could serve without lack.

Name: Cononiah, the Levite
Summary: Cononiah the Levite was ruler over the offerings, tithes and dedicated things brought faithfully into the house of the LORD under Hezekiah, with Shimei his brother next.
KeyStory: Cononiah the Levite was ruler over the offerings and tithes, and Shimei his brother was the next.
RelatedPeople: Shimei, Brother of Cononiah; King Hezekiah
LifeLesson: Faithful handling of gifts honours both giver and God.

Name: Cornelius
Summary: Cornelius was a devout centurion of the Italian band at Caesarea who feared God, gave alms, and prayed continually. An angel sent him to Peter, whose visit to his house opened the church to the Gentiles, as the Holy Spirit fell on his household before baptism.
KeyStory: Cornelius sent for Peter, and while Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit fell on his Gentile household.
LifeLesson: God hears the prayers of outsiders. Cornelius prayed in Caesarea, and the church's door opened to the world.

Name: Coz
Summary: Father of Anub and Zobebah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:8: Father of Anub and Zobebah.
LifeLesson: The mention of Coz in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Crescens
Summary: Crescens was a co-worker of Paul who had departed to Galatia by the time Paul wrote 2 Timothy.
KeyStory: Crescens was a co-worker of Paul who had departed to Galatia by the time Paul wrote 2 Timothy.
LifeLesson: Being sent is itself a trust; the gospel spreads by departures as well as arrivals.

Name: Crispus
Summary: Crispus was the chief ruler of the synagogue at Corinth who believed on the Lord with all his house after Paul's preaching, and was baptised by Paul himself.
KeyStory: Crispus, the synagogue ruler, believed with all his house and was baptised by Paul's own hand.
LifeLesson: The synagogue ruler became a church member. Crispus crossed the line his office had drawn.

Name: Cush, the Benjamite
Summary: Cush the Benjamite is named in the title of Psalm 7, a psalm David sang concerning Cush's words against him — a distinct man from Cush the son of Ham.
KeyStory: David answers slander with an appeal to the righteous Judge, asking God to vindicate him if he is innocent and to stop the violence of his accuser.
LifeLesson: When falsely accused, David's example is to take the case to God rather than take revenge into one's own hands.

Name: Cushi, Father of Zephaniah
Summary: Cushi is named only as the father of the prophet Zephaniah (Zephaniah 1:1), the first link in the four-generation genealogy that traces Zephaniah back to King Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Cushi's only mention is as Zephaniah's father, opening the prophet's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Cushi's single verse anchors a prophet in a family. God works through generations, not just individuals.

Name: Cushi, Messenger of Joab
Summary: Cushi is identified only by this name when Joab sent him to tell David of Absalom's death. He ran after Ahimaaz, delivered the news plainly, and answered David's question about Absalom with the words that broke the king's heart.
