KeyStory: Cushi, known only by his name, carried the news of Absalom's death to David.
RelatedPeople: King David; Ahimaaz, Son of Zadok; Joab
LifeLesson: The bearer of the hardest news deserves to be remembered for telling it straight.

Name: Dalaiah
Summary: Son of Elioenai son of Neariah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:24: Son of Elioenai son of Neariah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Dalaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Dalphon
Summary: One of the ten sons of Haman, slain by the Jews in Shushan and afterwards hanged on the gallows.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: A house built on hatred falls with its builder.

Name: Damaris
Summary: Damaris was a woman at Athens who believed after Paul's address on Mars' Hill, named alongside Dionysius the Areopagite. Acts records nothing further of her.
KeyStory: Damaris is named once, among those who clave unto Paul and believed at Athens.
LifeLesson: One verse holds a whole conversion. Damaris believed at Athens and is remembered for it.

Name: Daniel, of the House of Ithamar
Summary: A priest of the house of Ithamar who returned with Ezra; a different Daniel from the prophet.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: Returning to God's house is a family decision.

Name: Daniel, Son of David
Summary: Second son of David, born in Hebron to Abigail.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:1: Second son of David, born in Hebron to Abigail.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Daniel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Dara
Summary: Son of Zerah, named among the five sons of Zerah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:6: Son of Zerah, named among the five sons of Zerah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Dara stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Darda
Summary: Darda, son of Mahol, was named among the wise men with whom Solomon's wisdom was compared.
KeyStory: Darda named among the wise.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Ethan the Ezrahite; Chalcol; Mahol, Father of Chalcol and Darda
LifeLesson: Wisdom in others is a mirror, not a rival.

Name: Darius the Mede
Summary: Darius the Mede, son of Ahasuerus, took the kingdom of Babylon at about sixty-two years of age after Belshazzar's death; he set Daniel over the whole realm, was tricked by his satraps into the lions' den decree, and found Daniel unharmed at dawn, then decreed that men should tremble before Daniel's God. Scholars debate whether Darius the Mede is a throne name, a governor, or another figure of the period; the entry follows the text's own account.
KeyStory: Darius sealed the lions' den with his own signet, spent the night fasting, and at dawn cried to Daniel whether his God had delivered him — and Daniel answered that God had shut the lions' mouths.
LifeLesson: A law signed in haste cannot be undone by regret — but God can still deliver the man it condemns.

Name: Darius the Persian
Summary: A later Persian king named as the chronological marker for the records of priests and Levites in Nehemiah's day.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: God's people keep their records across reigns and generations.

Name: Darius
Summary: Darius I, king of Persia, is the Darius of Haggai and Zechariah: the Temple rebuilding resumed and was completed in his reign, in the second year of which both prophets began to preach. He is distinct from Darius the Mede of Daniel's time.
KeyStory: In the second year of Darius, Haggai and Zechariah called the returned exiles back to the unfinished Temple, and the work resumed under his rule.
KeyVerses: Haggai 1:1; Zechariah 1:1; Ezra 4:5; Ezra 4:24; Ezra 5:5; Ezra 5:6; Ezra 5:7; Ezra 6:1; Ezra 6:12; Ezra 6:13; Ezra 6:14; Ezra 6:15
RelatedPeople: Haggai; Zechariah the Prophet; Zerubbabel; Joshua, Son of Jehozadak
LifeLesson: God's work resumed under a foreign king's reign, on God's timetable. No empire — and no delay — is outside the reach of His purposes.

Name: Darkon
Summary: Descendant of Solomon's servants listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Service in God's house spans generations.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Delaiah, Course Head
Summary: Three and twentieth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:18: Three and twentieth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
LifeLesson: The mention of Delaiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Delaiah, of Tel-Melah
Summary: Named among those who returned from Tel-Melah but could not prove their genealogy (Ezra 2:60; Nehemiah 7:62). Not Delaiah son of Mehetabeel, who tried to trap Nehemiah.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Two men, one name, two very different stories.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Delaiah, Son of Mehetabeel
Summary: Father of the prophet Shemaiah who tried to frighten Nehemiah; his house was the meeting place for the plot.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: A house can host either counsel or conspiracy.

Name: Delaiah
Summary: Delaiah, son of Shemaiah, was a prince of Jehoiakim's court who heard Jeremiah's roll and joined the princes pleading with the king not to burn it.
KeyStory: Delaiah sat among the princes who heard the roll and besought the king that he would not burn it, but the king would not hear.
RelatedPeople: Jeremiah; Baruch; Jehoiakim, King of Judah
LifeLesson: A plea refused is still a plea made — God records the dissent, not only the decree.

Name: Demas
Summary: Demas was a fellowlabourer named in Colossians and Philemon, but in 2 Timothy Paul writes that Demas forsook him, having loved this present world, and departed to Thessalonica.
KeyStory: Demas was a fellowlabourer named in Colossians and Philemon, but in 2 Timothy Paul writes that Demas forsook him, having loved this present world, and departed to Thessalonica.
LifeLesson: Love for this present world can undo years of labour beside the gospel; the warning stands.

Name: Demetrius (3 John)
Summary: Demetrius was a believer commended in 3 John as having a good report from all men and from the truth itself. He is treated here as distinct from Demetrius the silversmith, since the letter gives no link between them.
KeyStory: Demetrius was a believer commended in 3 John as having a good report from all men and from the truth itself. He is treated here as distinct from Demetrius the silversmith, since the letter gives no link between them.
LifeLesson: A good report from all and from the truth is the best recommendation a believer can carry.

Name: Demetrius, the Silversmith
Summary: Demetrius was a silversmith at Ephesus who made silver shrines of Diana and stirred up his fellow craftsmen against Paul, fearing their trade and the goddess's honour would fall. The uproar filled the theatre for two hours with cries of Great is Diana. He is distinct from Demetrius of the later epistles.
KeyStory: Demetrius counted his profits in shrines and cried that Paul had turned the city from Diana.
LifeLesson: When the gospel threatens a trade, the trade fights back. Demetrius named his god's honour and meant his income.

Name: Diblaim
Summary: Diblaim is named only as the father of Gomer, Hosea's wife (Hosea 1:3). Nothing else is told of him.
KeyStory: Diblaim's only mention is as the father of Gomer, whom Hosea married at God's command.
LifeLesson: Diblaim's single verse is enough to place him in the story. God remembers fathers whose only recorded act is a daughter He wove into prophecy.

Name: Dionysius the Areopagite
Role: Member of the Council of Athens
Summary: Dionysius was a member of the Areopagus council at Athens who believed after hearing Paul's address on Mars' Hill about the unknown God and the resurrection.
KeyStory: Dionysius, a judge of the Areopagus, heard Paul on the unknown God and believed.
LifeLesson: Philosophy heard the resurrection and one judge believed. Dionysius shows the gospel can reach the council chamber.

Name: Diotrephes
Role: Lover of preeminence who refused John
Summary: Diotrephes loved to have the preeminence among the church, refused to receive John and his messengers, forbade others to do so, and cast objectors out of the church.
KeyStory: Diotrephes loved to have the preeminence among the church, refused to receive John and his messengers, forbade others to do so, and cast objectors out of the church.
LifeLesson: Loving preeminence corrupts a church faster than any outside attack.

Name: Dodai the Ahohite
Summary: Captain over the course of the second month, of whom Mikloth was also ruler.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:4: Captain over the course of the second month, of whom Mikloth was also ruler.
LifeLesson: The mention of Dodai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Dodavah, of Mareshah
Summary: Dodavah of Mareshah was the father of Eliezer the prophet who spoke against Jehoshaphat's alliance with Ahaziah.
KeyStory: Dodavah is named only as the father of Eliezer the son of Dodavah of Mareshah.
LifeLesson: A prophet's home town and father anchor his word in a real place.

Name: Dodo, Father of Eleazar
Summary: Father of Eleazar the Ahohite, one of the three mighties.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:12: Father of Eleazar the Ahohite, one of the three mighties.
LifeLesson: The mention of Dodo in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Dodo, Father of Puah
Summary: Dodo is named in Tola's lineage, as the father of Puah.
KeyStory: Dodo appears in Judges only in Tola's genealogy: Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo.
RelatedPeople: Puah, Father of Tola; Tola, Son of Puah
LifeLesson: A grandfather's name, kept alive in a grandson's introduction.

Name: Doeg the Edomite
Summary: Doeg the Edomite, Saul's chief herdman, saw David receive bread and Goliath's sword from Ahimelech at Nob and reported it to Saul. When Saul's own servants refused to kill the priests, Doeg did it himself, slaughtering eighty-five priests and the whole city of Nob.
KeyStory: Doeg's report turned a loaf of bread into a massacre of eighty-five priests.
RelatedPeople: King Saul; King David; Ahimelech, Son of Ahitub
LifeLesson: A tale carried to a jealous king can become a sword in someone else's hand.

Name: Doeg
Summary: Doeg the Edomite is named in the title of Psalm 52, the psalm David wrote after Doeg told Saul that David had come to the house of Ahimelech.
KeyStory: Doeg's report to Saul set in motion the slaughter of the priests of Nob, and Psalm 52 answers his treachery with a warning about the fate of those who trust in riches and lies.
LifeLesson: Doeg is a warning that words can kill — informing on the innocent for favour is a betrayal God judges.

Name: Drusilla
Summary: Drusilla was a Herodian princess, wife of the governor Felix, who sat beside him while Paul spoke about faith in Christ, righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come.
KeyStory: Felix sent for Paul with Drusilla beside him, and trembled at the sermon about judgment, then sent Paul away.
LifeLesson: Hearing about judgment should tremble us into action, not into postponement. Drusilla and Felix put Paul off until a more convenient season.

Name: Ebed, Father of Gaal
Summary: Ebed is named only as the father of Gaal, who led the revolt at Shechem against Abimelech.
KeyStory: Ebed appears in Judges only as Gaal's father, arriving with him at Shechem.
LifeLesson: A father's name rides on a son's rebellion.

Name: Ebed-Melech
Role: Ethiopian Eunuch in the King's House
Summary: Ebed-melech, an Ethiopian eunuch in Zedekiah's house, heard that Jeremiah had been put in the dungeon, pleaded with the king for him, and drew Jeremiah out with old rags under his arms. God promised him deliverance because he had trusted in the Lord.
KeyStory: Ebed-melech went to the king's gate, obtained thirty men, and let down old cast clouts and rotten rags to lift Jeremiah out of the miry dungeon.
LifeLesson: One outsider's courage at the king's gate can save a prophet — and God remembers it by name.

Name: Ebed, Son of Jonathan
Summary: Son of Jonathan who returned with Ezra from Babylon.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: Returning to God's house is a family decision.

Name: Eber, Son of Elpaal
Summary: Son of Elpaal, named among the sons of Elpaal.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:12: Son of Elpaal, named among the sons of Elpaal.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Eber stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Eber the Priest
Summary: A priest in the days of Joiakim, of the course of Amok; a different Eber from Salah's son in Genesis.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Courses of priests kept their order across generations.

Name: Ebiasaph, Son of Elkanah
Summary: Son of Elkanah and father of Assir in the Kohathite line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:23: Son of Elkanah and father of Assir in the Kohathite line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ebiasaph stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Eden, Priest Distributor
Summary: Eden served with Kore in the cities of the priests, giving portions to his brethren by courses, great and small, under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Eden served with Kore in the cities of the priests, giving portions to his brethren by courses, great and small, under Hezekiah.
RelatedPeople: Kore, Son of Imnah; King Hezekiah
LifeLesson: Fair portions for every priest, great and small, came through faithful distributors.

Name: Eden, Son of Joah
Summary: Eden, son of Joah of the Gershonites, was one of the Levites who arose to cleanse the house of the LORD under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Of the Gershonites, Joah the son of Zimmah and Eden the son of Joah arose to cleanse the house.
RelatedPeople: Joah, Son of Zimmah; King Hezekiah
LifeLesson: Sons followed fathers into the work of restoring worship.

Name: Eder, Son of Mushi
Summary: Son of Mushi, named among the sons of Mushi.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 23:23: Son of Mushi, named among the sons of Mushi.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Eder stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Eglah, Wife of David
Summary: Wife of David and mother of Ithream, born in Hebron.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:3: Wife of David and mother of Ithream, born in Hebron.
LifeLesson: The mention of Eglah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Eglah
Summary: Eglah was one of David's wives at Hebron and the mother of Ithream, his sixth son born there.
KeyStory: Eglah is named once, as the mother of David's sixth son at Hebron.
LifeLesson: The record counts every wife and every son, even those with a single verse.

Name: Eglon, King of Moab
Summary: Eglon, king of Moab, oppressed Israel eighteen years from Jericho until Ehud killed him in his summer parlour.
KeyStory: Eglon, described as a very fat man, received Ehud's 'message from God' alone in his parlour and was killed with a dagger; his servants found him dead after Ehud escaped.
LifeLesson: Power that fattens itself on an oppressed people ends in a locked room.

Name: Ehud, Son of Benjamin's Line
Summary: Head of the fathers of the inhabitants of Geba, whose sons removed them to Manahath.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:6: Head of the fathers of the inhabitants of Geba, whose sons removed them to Manahath.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ehud in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ehud, Son of Bilhan
Summary: Son of Bilhan, named among the sons of Bilhan.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:10: Son of Bilhan, named among the sons of Bilhan.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ehud stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ehud, Son of Gera
Summary: Ehud, a left-handed Benjamite, son of Gera, delivered Israel from Eglon, king of Moab, by killing him with a dagger in his private chamber and leading Israel to retake the fords of Jordan.
KeyStory: Ehud hid a dagger on his right thigh, killed Eglon alone in his summer parlour, escaped, and led Israel to seize the fords of Jordan and strike down Moab.
RelatedPeople: Gera, Father of Ehud; Eglon, King of Moab
LifeLesson: God used an overlooked trait — left-handedness — to undo a king's guard.

Name: Eker
Summary: Son of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:27: Son of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Eker stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Eladah
Summary: Son of Tahath and father of Tahath in Ephraim's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:20: Son of Tahath and father of Tahath in Ephraim's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Eladah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Elah, Father of Hoshea
Summary: Elah was the father of Hoshea, last king of Israel; he is distinct from Elah king of Israel and Elah father of Shimei.
KeyStory: Elah, father of Hoshea.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Elah, Father of Shimei
Summary: Elah was the father of Shimei, Solomon's officer over Benjamin; he is distinct from Elah king of Israel.
KeyStory: Elah, father of Shimei the officer.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Elah, King of Israel
Summary: Elah, son of Baasha, reigned two years in Tirzah and was drinking himself drunk in his steward Arza's house when his chariot captain Zimri conspired and slew him.
KeyStory: Elah slain drunk in Arza's house by Zimri.
RelatedPeople: Baasha, King of Israel; Arza, Steward of Elah; Zimri, King of Israel
LifeLesson: A king found drunk on duty is already dethroned in everything but name.

Name: Elah, Son of Caleb
Summary: Son of Caleb son of Jephunneh and father of Kenaz.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:15: Son of Caleb son of Jephunneh and father of Kenaz.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Elah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Elah, Son of Uzzi
Summary: Son of Uzzi son of Michri, of the sons of Benjamin dwelling in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:8: Son of Uzzi son of Michri, of the sons of Benjamin dwelling in Jerusalem.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Elah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Elam, of the Return
Summary: Head of a family that returned with Zerubbabel; Jeshaiah of his sons returned with Ezra. A different Elam from Shem's son, and from the other Elam of Ezra 2:31.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Faithfulness in returning to rebuild is remembered by name.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Elam, Son of Meshelemiah
Summary: Fifth son of Meshelemiah the porter.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:3: Fifth son of Meshelemiah the porter.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Elam stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Elam, Son of Shashak
Summary: Named among the sons of Shashak in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:24: Named among the sons of Shashak in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Elam stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Elam, the Other Elam
Summary: Head of the 'other Elam' family listed separately among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Faithfulness in returning to rebuild is remembered by name.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Elasah, Son of Pashur
Summary: Son of Pashur named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Elasah
Summary: Elasah, son of Shaphan, was one of the two men Zedekiah sent to Babylon with Jeremiah's letter to the exiles.
KeyStory: Elasah son of Shaphan carried Jeremiah's letter to the captives in Babylon alongside Gemariah son of Hilkiah.
LifeLesson: A messenger's name may be all that survives — and that is enough, if the message was delivered.

Name: Elead, Son of Shuthelah
Summary: Son of Shuthelah, slain by the men of Gath born in the land.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:21: Son of Shuthelah, slain by the men of Gath born in the land.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Elead stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Eleasah, Son of Helez
Summary: Son of Helez and father of Sisamai.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:39: Son of Helez and father of Sisamai.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Eleasah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Eleasah, Son of Rapha
Summary: Son of Rapha and father of Azel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:37; 1 Chronicles 9:43: Son of Rapha and father of Azel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Eleasah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Eleazar, Son of Abinadab
Summary: Eleazar, son of Abinadab of Kirjath-jearim, was sanctified to keep the ark of the Lord while it rested in his father's house.
KeyStory: Eleazar guarded the ark for the twenty years it stayed at Kirjath-jearim.
LifeLesson: Guarding what God has entrusted to you, even in obscurity, is holy work.

Name: Eleazar, Son of Dodo
Summary: Eleazar, son of Dodo the Ahohite, was one of David's three mighty men. When Israel's men retreated at Pas-dammim, he stood alone and struck the Philistines until his hand clave to his sword, and the Lord wrought a great victory.
KeyStory: Eleazar's hand froze to his sword as he stood alone against the Philistines.
RelatedPeople: King David; Shammah, Son of Agee
LifeLesson: Standing alone when everyone retreats is the very definition of might.

Name: Eleazar, Son of Mahli
Summary: Son of Mahli who died with no sons, only daughters.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 23:21: Son of Mahli who died with no sons, only daughters.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Eleazar stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Eleazar, Son of Parosh
Summary: Son of Parosh named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Eleazar, Son of Phinehas
Summary: A priest who with Meremoth weighed the temple vessels on arrival in Jerusalem; a later Eleazar than Aaron's son.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: What is counted carefully is honored.

Name: Elhanan, Son of Dodo
Summary: Elhanan, son of Dodo of Bethlehem, was among David's thirty mighty men. He is distinct from Elhanan son of Jaare-oregim, who slew a giant at Gob.
KeyStory: Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: Two Elhanans, two stories — Bethlehem gave David more than one hero.

Name: Elhanan, Son of Jaare-oregim
Summary: Elhanan, son of Jaare-oregim of Bethlehem, struck down a Philistine giant in the battle at Gob. The Samuel text names his victim as Goliath the Gittite.
KeyStory: Elhanan of Bethlehem struck down a giant at Gob in David's later wars.
LifeLesson: Bethlehem, David's town, produced more than one giant-killer.

Name: Elhanan, Son of Jair
Summary: Son of Jair who slew Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 20:5: Son of Jair who slew Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Elhanan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Eliab, Captain of Gad
Summary: Third captain of the Gadites who separated themselves to David in the wilderness.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:9: Third captain of the Gadites who separated themselves to David in the wilderness.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Eliab stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Eliab, Singer of Second Degree
Summary: Levite of the second degree appointed to sing with psalteries on Alamoth at the bringing up of the ark.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:18; 1 Chronicles 15:20: Levite of the second degree appointed to sing with psalteries on Alamoth at the bringing up of the ark.
LifeLesson: The mention of Eliab in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Eliab, Son of Jesse
Summary: Eliab, Jesse's eldest, was tall and kingly enough that Samuel thought him the Lord's anointed — but God refused him. He served in Saul's army and scorned David when the boy came to the camp at Elah.
KeyStory: Eliab looked like a king and sounded like a king, and God passed him over.
RelatedPeople: Jesse; King David; Abinadab, Son of Jesse; Shammah, Son of Jesse; Abihail, Daughter of Eliab
LifeLesson: God looks on the heart, not on height — and a brother's scorn cannot stop God's choice.

Name: Eliab, Son of Nahath
Summary: Son of Nahath and father of Jeroham in the Samuel line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:27: Son of Nahath and father of Jeroham in the Samuel line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Eliab stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Eliada, Captain of Benjamin
Summary: Eliada, a mighty man of valour of Benjamin, commanded two hundred thousand armed men with bow and shield under Jehoshaphat.
KeyStory: Of Benjamin, Eliada a mighty man of valour, and with him armed men with bow and shield two hundred thousand.
LifeLesson: God's law taught throughout the land, and willing service under a faithful king, strengthened Judah.

Name: Eliada, Son of David
Summary: Son of David born in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:8: Son of David born in Jerusalem.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Eliada stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Eliada
Summary: Eliada was a son of David born at Jerusalem, named last but one among the sons born to him there.
KeyStory: Eliada was born to David at Jerusalem after the city became his capital.
LifeLesson: The last names on a list are still sons of the king.

Name: Eliadah, Father of Rezon
Summary: Eliadah was the father of Rezon, who fled Hadadezer and became king in Damascus.
KeyStory: Eliadah, father of Rezon.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Eliah, Son of Elam
Summary: Son of Elam named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Eliah, Son of Jeroham
Summary: Named among the sons of Jeroham in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:27: Named among the sons of Jeroham in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Eliah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Eliahba the Shaalbonite
Summary: Eliahba the Shaalbonite was among David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Eliahba the Shaalbonite stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: Shaalbon gave David a warrior for the thirty.

Name: Eliakim, Son of Hilkiah
Summary: Eliakim, son of Hilkiah, was over Hezekiah's household and answered Sennacherib's Rabshakeh at the wall, then reported his words to the king with torn clothes.
KeyStory: Eliakim answers the Rabshakeh and reports to Hezekiah.
RelatedPeople: King Hezekiah; Shebna, Scribe; Joah, Son of Asaph; Sennacherib, King of Assyria
LifeLesson: A steward's steady answer at the wall gave his king room to pray.

Name: Eliakim
Summary: Eliakim, son of Hilkiah, was set over Hezekiah's household in Shebna's place and was one of the three officials who met the Assyrian officers at Jerusalem's wall.
KeyStory: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah went out to hear the Rabshakeh at the conduit of the upper pool, then tore their clothes and reported his words to Hezekiah.
LifeLesson: Faithful service means carrying bad news honestly to the king and to God.

Name: Eliam
Summary: Eliam is named as the father of Bathsheba, and again among David's mighty men as Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite. The two mentions are commonly understood to be the same man, making Bathsheba the granddaughter of David's counsellor.
KeyStory: Eliam links Bathsheba's house to Ahithophel's — the counsellor whose granddaughter David wronged.
LifeLesson: One family can hold both the wronged and the avenger — and the reckoning still comes.

Name: Eliashib, Course Head
Summary: Eleventh lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:12: Eleventh lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
LifeLesson: The mention of Eliashib in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Eliashib, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:36).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: A shared name with the high priest did not shield him.

Name: Eliashib, Son of Elioenai
Summary: Son of Elioenai son of Neariah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:24: Son of Elioenai son of Neariah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Eliashib stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Eliashib, Son of Zattu

LifeLesson: Elihu reminds us that youth is no bar to truth, and that suffering may be God's instruction rather than His punishment.

Name: Ethan the Ezrahite
Summary: Ethan the Ezrahite was named among the wise men with whom Solomon's wisdom was compared, and Solomon was wiser than them all.
KeyStory: Ethan named among the wise.
LifeLesson: Even the wisest of men are the measure Solomon surpassed, and still Solomon fell.

Name: Ethan
Summary: Ethan the Ezrahite is named in the title of Psalm 89, a psalm that celebrates God's covenant with David and then wrestles with its apparent failure. Chronicles also names an Ethan son of Zerah, an Ethan son of Zimmah, and an Ethan son of Kushaiah; whether any of these is the same man is not settled, so the profiles are kept separate.
KeyStory: Psalm 89 moves from praise for God's promises to David to a raw question — how long will the covenant seem broken? — and ends still appealing to God's steadfast love.
LifeLesson: Ethan models holding God to His promises honestly: praise and protest can live in the same prayer.

Name: Ethbaal, King of Sidon
Summary: Ethbaal, king of the Zidonians, was the father of Jezebel, whom Ahab married, bringing Baal's worship into Israel's court.
KeyStory: Ethbaal, father of Jezebel.
LifeLesson: A marriage alliance can import a nation's gods with its princess.

Name: Ethnan
Summary: Son of Ashur by Helah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:7: Son of Ashur by Helah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ethnan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ethni, Son of Zerah
Summary: Son of Zerah and father of Malchiah in Asaph's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:41: Son of Zerah and father of Malchiah in Asaph's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ethni stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Eubulus
Summary: Eubulus was one of the believers with Paul in Rome who sends greetings in 2 Timothy, alongside Pudens, Linus, and Claudia.
KeyStory: Eubulus was one of the believers with Paul in Rome who sends greetings in 2 Timothy, alongside Pudens, Linus, and Claudia.
LifeLesson: Greetings from Rome's believers show a church standing with its prisoner.

Name: Eunice
Summary: Eunice was Timothy's mother, whose unfeigned faith Paul says dwelt in her as it had in her mother Lois, and then in Timothy.
KeyStory: Eunice was Timothy's mother, whose unfeigned faith Paul says dwelt in her as it had in her mother Lois, and then in Timothy.
LifeLesson: A mother's sincere faith is often the soil where a child's faith first grows.

Name: Euodias
Summary: Euodias (Euodia) was a Philippian believer whom Paul beseeches, along with Syntyche, to be of the same mind in the Lord.
KeyStory: Euodias (Euodia) was a Philippian believer whom Paul beseeches, along with Syntyche, to be of the same mind in the Lord.
LifeLesson: Unity in the Lord is not uniformity of opinion but agreement in Christ.

Name: Eutychus
Summary: Eutychus was a young man who sat in a window at Troas during Paul's long preaching and, overcome by sleep, fell from the third loft and was taken up dead. Paul embraced him and announced he was alive, and the company broke bread and talked until morning.
KeyStory: Eutychus fell asleep in a window, fell three stories, and was raised in Paul's arms before the bread was broken.
LifeLesson: Long sermons and open windows are a dangerous mix. Eutychus fell, and grace gave him back before dawn.

Name: Evil-Merodach, King of Babylon
Summary: Evil-Merodach, king of Babylon, in the year he began to reign lifted Jehoiachin out of prison, spoke kindly to him, and set his seat above the seats of the other captive kings.
KeyStory: Evil-Merodach releases Jehoiachin.
RelatedPeople: Jehoiachin, King of Judah; King Nebuchadnezzar; Jeconiah
LifeLesson: Mercy can come from the unlikeliest throne, even in Babylon.

Name: Ezbai, Father of Naarai
Summary: Father of Naarai among David's mighty men.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:37: Father of Naarai among David's mighty men.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ezbai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ezbon, Son of Bela
Summary: Son of Bela and head of his father's house, a mighty man of valour.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:7: Son of Bela and head of his father's house, a mighty man of valour.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ezbon stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ezer, Captain of Gad
Summary: First captain of the Gadites who separated themselves to David in the wilderness.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:9: First captain of the Gadites who separated themselves to David in the wilderness.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ezer in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ezer, Father of Hushah
Summary: Son of Hur, called the father of Hushah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:4: Son of Hur, called the father of Hushah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ezer stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ezer, Son of Jeshua
Summary: Son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, who repaired part of the wall; a different Ezer from Seir's son in Genesis.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: God's work is done by many hands, each named.

Name: Ezer, Son of Shuthelah
Summary: Son of Shuthelah, slain by the men of Gath born in the land.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:21: Son of Shuthelah, slain by the men of Gath born in the land.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ezer stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ezra, Father of Jether
Summary: Father of Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:17: Father of Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ezra in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ezra the Priest
Summary: Priest who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:1). Not Ezra the scribe, who came generations later.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Two Ezras served God in different generations.

Name: Ezri, Son of Chelub
Summary: Son of Chelub, over the work of the field for tillage.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:26: Son of Chelub, over the work of the field for tillage.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ezri stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Felix
Summary: Felix was the Roman governor who kept Paul in custody at Caesarea for two years, hearing him often and hoping for a bribe, and who trembled at Paul's preaching on righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, yet left Paul bound to please the Jews.
KeyStory: Felix heard Paul often, trembled at judgment to come, and left him bound when a successor came.
LifeLesson: Felix trembled and postponed, and postponement became his verdict. A convenient season never came.

Name: Festus
Summary: Festus succeeded Felix as governor and heard Paul at Caesarea. When Paul appealed to Caesar, Festus agreed, and, lacking a clear charge to send with him, brought Paul before Agrippa II to help frame the case.
KeyStory: Festus heard Paul, granted his appeal to Caesar, and asked Agrippa to help him write the charge.
LifeLesson: Festus wanted a charge to send and found none. Paul's innocence puzzled every governor who heard him.

Name: Fortunatus
Summary: Fortunatus was one of the Corinthian brethren who came to Paul and supplied what was lacking from the church, refreshing Paul's spirit.
KeyStory: Fortunatus was one of the Corinthian brethren who came to Paul and supplied what was lacking from the church, refreshing Paul's spirit.
LifeLesson: A messenger who carries a church's care refreshes the one who receives it.

Name: Gaal, Son of Ebed
Summary: Gaal, son of Ebed, led a revolt against Abimelech at Shechem, boasting he would remove him, but was defeated and expelled by Zebul.
KeyStory: Gaal came to Shechem with his brethren, won the men's confidence at vintage time, and challenged Abimelech; Zebul warned the king, who routed Gaal at the gate and chased him out.
RelatedPeople: Abimelech, Son of Gideon; Zebul; Ebed, Father of Gaal
LifeLesson: A boast at harvest time withered by the city gate.

Name: Gabbai
Summary: Resident of Jerusalem listed in Nehemiah 11.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Jerusalem was resettled household by household.

Name: Gad, David's Seer
Summary: David's seer through whom the LORD offered David three choices after the numbering.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 21:9; 1 Chronicles 21:11: David's seer through whom the LORD offered David three choices after the numbering.
LifeLesson: The mention of Gad in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Gad the Seer
Summary: Gad the seer was David's prophet. He told the fugitive David to leave the stronghold for Judah, and after the census he gave David God's choice of punishments and told him to build the altar on Araunah's threshingfloor.
KeyStory: Gad guided David as a fugitive and confronted him after the census.
RelatedPeople: King David; Araunah the Jebusite; Nathan; King Solomon
LifeLesson: A true seer speaks when it is welcome and when it is not.

Name: Gadi, Father of Menahem
Summary: Gadi was the father of Menahem, king of Israel.
KeyStory: Gadi, father of Menahem.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Gahar
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Gaius (3 John)
Summary: Gaius was the wellbeloved recipient of John's third letter, commended because he walked in the truth and showed hospitality to travelling brethren. He is treated here as distinct from Gaius of Corinth, since the letters place them in different churches.
KeyStory: Gaius was the wellbeloved recipient of John's third letter, commended because he walked in the truth and showed hospitality to travelling brethren. He is treated here as distinct from Gaius of Corinth, since the letters place them in different churches.
LifeLesson: Hospitality to strangers is truth in action; supporting travellers speeds the gospel.

Name: Gaius of Corinth
Role: Host of Paul and of the whole church
Summary: Gaius was Paul's host at Corinth and host of the whole church there; Paul had baptized him, and he sends greetings in Romans 16. He is distinct from the Gaius addressed in 3 John.
KeyStory: Gaius was Paul's host at Corinth and host of the whole church there; Paul had baptized him, and he sends greetings in Romans 16. He is distinct from the Gaius addressed in 3 John.
LifeLesson: Hospitality opens a home and becomes a church; a host's house can hold a whole congregation.

Name: Gaius of Derbe
Summary: Gaius of Derbe was one of the companions who travelled with Paul from Greece toward Jerusalem, accompanying him through Macedonia and on to Troas. He is distinguished by his home city from Gaius of Macedonia.
KeyStory: Gaius of Derbe travelled with Paul's company toward Jerusalem, one of the bearers of the churches' gift.
LifeLesson: The collection for Jerusalem travelled on faithful feet. Gaius of Derbe walked it toward the holy city.

Name: Gaius of Macedonia
Summary: Gaius of Macedonia was one of Paul's travelling companions seized by the Ephesian mob and dragged into the theatre during the riot of the silversmiths. He is distinguished by his homeland from Gaius of Derbe.
KeyStory: Gaius of Macedonia was seized in the Ephesian riot and dragged with Aristarchus into the theatre.
LifeLesson: Companions share the mob as well as the mission. Gaius of Macedonia was dragged, not just inconvenienced.

Name: Galal, Son of Jeduthun
Summary: Levite dwelling in Jerusalem after the return.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:15: Levite dwelling in Jerusalem after the return.
LifeLesson: The mention of Galal in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Gallio
Summary: Gallio was the proconsul of Achaia before whom the Jews brought Paul at Corinth, accusing him of persuading men to worship contrary to the law. Gallio dismissed the case as a matter of words and names, and cared for none of the beating that followed.
KeyStory: Gallio refused to judge Paul's doctrine, calling it a question of words and names, and the case collapsed.
LifeLesson: Gallio's indifference freed Paul and left Sosthenes beaten. A judge who cares for nothing protects no one.

Name: Gamaliel, the Pharisee
Summary: Gamaliel was a Pharisee and honoured teacher of the law in Jerusalem, and Paul's teacher. Before the Sanhedrin he counselled restraint toward the apostles, arguing that if their work were of men it would fail, but if of God it could not be overthrown. He is distinct from Gamaliel son of Pedahzur of the wilderness generation.
KeyStory: Gamaliel told the council to leave the apostles alone, for if this work were of God, no man could overthrow it.
LifeLesson: Gamaliel's counsel still stands: works of men fail on their own, and works of God cannot be stopped by councils.

Name: Gamul
Summary: Two and twentieth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:17: Two and twentieth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
LifeLesson: The mention of Gamul in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Gareb the Ithrite
Summary: Gareb the Ithrite was among David's thirty mighty men, named beside Ira the Ithrite.
KeyStory: Gareb the Ithrite stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: Two Ithrites stood together in the thirty.

Name: Gazez, Son of Ephah
Summary: Son of Caleb's concubine Ephah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:46: Son of Caleb's concubine Ephah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Gazez stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Gazez, Son of Haran
Summary: Son of Haran son of Ephah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:46: Son of Haran son of Ephah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Gazez stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Gazzam
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Geber, Son of Uri
Summary: Geber, son of Uri, was one of Solomon's twelve officers, over Gilead, the land of Sihon and Og, the only officer in his region.
KeyStory: Geber, officer over Gilead.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Uri, Father of Geber
LifeLesson: One man can hold a whole frontier when he holds it faithfully.

Name: Gedaliah, Son of Ahikam
Summary: Gedaliah, son of Ahikam, was made governor over Judah's remnant by Nebuchadnezzar, gathered the scattered captains at Mizpah, and was murdered by Ishmael son of Nethaniah in the seventh month.
KeyStory: Gedaliah governs the remnant and is murdered.
RelatedPeople: King Nebuchadnezzar; Ahikam, Son of Shaphan; Ishmael, Son of Nethaniah; Johanan, Son of Careah
LifeLesson: A governor who trusted too easily died for the remnant's last hope.
RelatedEvents: Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile

Name: Gedaliah, Son of Amariah
Summary: Gedaliah, son of Amariah, is named only in Zephaniah's genealogy (Zephaniah 1:1), as the grandfather of the prophet. He is not the Gedaliah appointed governor after Jerusalem's fall — that Gedaliah was son of Ahikam, a different man.
KeyStory: Gedaliah appears only in Zephaniah's genealogy, as the prophet's grandfather between Cushi and Amariah.
RelatedPeople: Zephaniah; Cushi, Father of Zephaniah; Amariah, Son of Hezekiah
LifeLesson: Two Gedaliahs, two different men — Scripture's genealogies reward careful reading. Never merge namesakes into one person.

Name: Gedaliah, Son of Jeduthun
Summary: Son of Jeduthun who prophesied with a harp, second lot.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 25:3; 1 Chronicles 25:9: Son of Jeduthun who prophesied with a harp, second lot.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Gedaliah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Gedaliah, Son of Jeshua
Summary: Son of Jeshua named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Gedaliah, Son of Pashur
Summary: Gedaliah, son of Pashur, was one of the princes who demanded Jeremiah's death, charging that his prophecies weakened the hands of the soldiers and the people. He is a different man from Gedaliah the governor.
KeyStory: Gedaliah son of Pashur told Zedekiah that Jeremiah ought to be put to death, and Jeremiah was let down into the dungeon of Malchiah.
RelatedPeople: Zedekiah, King of Judah; Jeremiah; Pashur, Son of Malchiah
LifeLesson: Calling truth treason is the oldest way to silence a prophet.

Name: Gedaliah
Summary: Gedaliah, son of Ahikam, was made governor over the remnant left in Judah after Jerusalem fell. He urged the people to serve Babylon and live, welcomed the scattered captains at Mizpah, and was murdered by Ishmael son of Nethaniah despite Johanan's warning.
KeyStory: Gedaliah told the captains at Mizpah not to fear serving the Chaldeans, but Ishmael came to him at Mizpah and struck him down while eating bread with him.
RelatedPeople: Jeremiah; Ahikam; Ishmael, Son of Nethaniah; Johanan, Son of Kareah; Nebuzaradan
LifeLesson: Trusting a friendly face over a faithful warning can be fatal — discernment is not unkindness.
RelatedEvents: Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile

Name: Gedor, Son of Jehiel
Summary: Son of Jehiel the father of Gibeon.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:31; 1 Chronicles 9:37: Son of Jehiel the father of Gibeon.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Gedor stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Gehazi, Servant of Elisha
Summary: Gehazi, Elisha's servant, ran after Naaman for a gift Elisha had refused, lied about it, and was struck with Naaman's leprosy forever.
KeyStory: Gehazi takes Naaman's gift and is struck with leprosy.
LifeLesson: Greed that trades a prophet's gift for silver inherits the disease it coveted.

Name: Gemariah, Son of Hilkiah
Summary: Gemariah, son of Hilkiah, was one of the two men Zedekiah sent to Babylon carrying Jeremiah's letter to the exiles, telling them to build houses, plant gardens, and seek the city's peace. He is a different man from Gemariah son of Shaphan.
KeyStory: Gemariah son of Hilkiah carried Jeremiah's letter to the captives in Babylon, with its command to seek the peace of the city where God had caused them to be carried captive.
RelatedPeople: Jeremiah; Elasah; Zedekiah, King of Judah
LifeLesson: Carrying an unwelcome letter faithfully is itself an act of obedience.

Name: Gemariah, Son of Shaphan
Summary: Gemariah, son of Shaphan, was a scribe and prince in whose chamber Baruch read Jeremiah's roll to the people; he and other princes pleaded with Jehoiakim not to burn the roll. He is a different man from Gemariah son of Hilkiah.
KeyStory: Baruch read Jeremiah's words in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan in the Lord's house, and Gemariah joined the princes who begged the king not to burn the roll.
LifeLesson: Hearing God's word in a side chamber still demands a public stand when the king reaches for the fire.

Name: Genubath, Son of Hadad
Summary: Genubath was the son of Hadad the Edomite by Pharaoh's sister-in-law, weaned by Queen Tahpenes and raised in Pharaoh's household among Pharaoh's sons.
KeyStory: Genubath raised in Pharaoh's house.
RelatedPeople: Hadad, Prince of Edom; Tahpenes, Queen of Egypt
LifeLesson: A child raised between two kingdoms belongs fully to neither.

Name: Gera, Father of Ehud
Summary: Gera is named only as the father of Ehud, the left-handed deliverer. He is distinct from Gera, son of Benjamin, in Genesis.
KeyStory: Gera appears in Judges only as Ehud's father, a Benjamite.
LifeLesson: Even a one-line mention can anchor a deliverer's story.

Name: Gera, Father of Shimei
Summary: Gera of Bahurim is named as the father of Shimei, the Benjamite who cursed David during Absalom's revolt.
KeyStory: Gera's son became the voice of Benjamin's anger against David.
LifeLesson: A son's curse is remembered long after his father's name is forgotten.

Name: Gera, Son of Bela
Summary: Son of Bela, named among the sons of Bela.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:3: Son of Bela, named among the sons of Bela.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Gera stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Gera, Son of Ehud
Summary: Son of Ehud, named among the sons of Ehud and among those who removed the inhabitants of Geba.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:5; 1 Chronicles 8:7: Son of Ehud, named among the sons of Ehud and among those who removed the inhabitants of Geba.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Gera stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Gershom, of the House of Phinehas
Summary: A priest of the house of Phinehas who returned with Ezra; a different Gershom from the son of Moses.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: Returning to God's house is a family decision.

Name: Gershon, Son of Levi
Summary: Son of Levi, named among the sons of Levi.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:1: Son of Levi, named among the sons of Levi.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Gershon stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Gesham
Summary: Son of Jahdai, named in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:47: Son of Jahdai, named in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Gesham stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Geshem
Summary: Arabian opponent of Nehemiah, named Geshem in most passages and Gashmu in the open letter accusing Nehemiah of rebellion.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: False charges are an old tactic against builders.

Name: Gibbar
Summary: Head of a family listed among those who returned from exile.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: A family's return is recorded household by household.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Giddalti, Son of Heman
Summary: Son of Heman the king's seer, two and twentieth lot for song.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 25:4; 1 Chronicles 25:29: Son of Heman the king's seer, two and twentieth lot for song.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Giddalti stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Giddel
Summary: Named among both the Nethinim (Ezra 2:47) and Solomon's servants (Ezra 2:56); whether one family or two is not stated.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: God's house was served by many families, some named twice.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Gilalai
Summary: Musician at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Music marks the moment a long work is finished.

Name: Gilead, Father of Jephthah
Summary: Gilead is named only as the father of Jephthah the judge, whose other sons drove Jephthah out.
KeyStory: Gilead begat Jephthah, and Gilead's wife's sons thrust Jephthah out, saying he should have no inheritance in their father's house.
LifeLesson: A father's house can cast out its own son — and later beg him back.

Name: Gilead, Son of Michael
Summary: Son of Michael son of Jeshishai son of Jahdo son of Buz in Gad's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:14: Son of Michael son of Jeshishai son of Jahdo son of Buz in Gad's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Gilead stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ginath, Father of Tibni
Summary: Ginath was the father of Tibni, who contended with Omri for Israel's throne.
KeyStory: Ginath, father of Tibni.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Ginnethon
Summary: Priest who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10).
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: A signature on a covenant is a public stand.

Name: Gispa
Summary: Overseer of the Nethinim dwelling in Ophel (Nehemiah 11:21).
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Oversight of God's servants is itself service.

Name: Gog, Son of Shemaiah
Summary: Son of Shemaiah and father of Shimei in Reuben's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:4: Son of Shemaiah and father of Shimei in Reuben's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Gog stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Goliath the Gittite
Summary: Gittite giant whose brother Lahmi was slain by Elhanan son of Jair.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 20:5: Gittite giant whose brother Lahmi was slain by Elhanan son of Jair.
LifeLesson: The mention of Goliath in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Goliath
Summary: Goliath of Gath, nearly ten feet tall and clad in bronze, challenged Israel for forty days until David, a shepherd boy with a sling, struck him down and cut off his head with his own sword.
KeyStory: Goliath's forty-day taunt ended with a single stone from a boy who trusted the Lord of hosts.
LifeLesson: The battle is the Lord's — giants fall to faith, not to armour.

Name: Guni, Father of Abdiel
Summary: Father of Abdiel in Gad's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:15: Father of Abdiel in Gad's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Guni in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Haahashtari
Summary: Son of Ashur by Naarah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:6: Son of Ashur by Naarah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Haahashtari stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Habaiah
Summary: Head of a priestly family among the returnees who could not prove their genealogy (Ezra 2:61; Nehemiah 7:63).
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Even an unproven claim is recorded honestly, not hidden.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Habakkuk
Summary: Habakkuk prophesied in Judah around 609–605 BC, as Babylon rose to power. Unusually, his book is a dialogue: he questioned God about violence and injustice, God answered that He would raise the Chaldeans, Habakkuk questioned again, and God answered with a vision — the just shall live by faith — ending in a psalm of trust even when the fields yield no food.
KeyStory: Habakkuk cried out over violence in Judah, wrestled with God's answer that Babylon would be His instrument, and finished by trusting God even if fig tree and flock should fail.
LifeLesson: Habakkuk teaches that honest questions are not unbelief. Bring them to God, wait for His answer, and trust Him even when the harvest fails.

Name: Hachaliah
Summary: Father of Nehemiah the governor; Nehemiah is introduced as his son.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: A father's name can open a son's story.

Name: Hachmoni
Summary: Father of Jehiel, with the king's sons.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:32: Father of Jehiel, with the king's sons.
LifeLesson: The mention of Hachmoni in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Hadad, Prince of Edom
Summary: Hadad, an Edomite prince of the king's seed, fled to Egypt when Joab smote Edom, was given Pharaoh's sister-in-law to wife, and returned to trouble Solomon after David's death.
KeyStory: Hadad flees to Egypt and returns as Solomon's adversary.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Tahpenes, Queen of Egypt; Genubath, Son of Hadad
LifeLesson: An old enemy spared becomes a new adversary: mercy without repentance repeats itself.

Name: Hadadezer, King of Zobah
Summary: Hadadezer, king of Zobah, was the lord from whom Rezon fled when David's wars broke his power, and whose servant later troubled Solomon from Damascus.
KeyStory: Hadadezer, lord of Rezon.
LifeLesson: Fallen lords leave behind servants who remember the fall.

Name: Hadadezer, Son of Rehob

KeyStory: Hadadezer's Syrian empire broke against David at the Euphrates and again at Helam.
LifeLesson: Empires that march against God's anointed find their border at the river.

Jeremiah answered that Hananiah had made the people trust in a lie, and Hananiah died that same year, as Jeremiah foretold. He is a different man from Hananiah, Daniel's companion, whose Babylonian name was Shadrach.
KeyStory: Hananiah broke Jeremiah's yoke of wood in the temple, and Jeremiah replaced it with a yoke of iron and told Hananiah he would die that year — and he did, in the seventh month.
LifeLesson: A prophecy that only ever promises good news is not a kindness — it is a lie that costs lives.
