Name: Hatipha
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Hatita
Summary: Head of a porter family that returned with Zerubbabel.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Gatekeepers guard the house of God.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Hattil
Summary: Descendant of Solomon's servants listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Service in God's house spans generations.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Hattush the Priest
Summary: Priest who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:4) and returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:2). Not Hattush of David's line who returned with Ezra.
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: Priests and Davidides both returned, and the record keeps them distinct.

Name: Hattush
Summary: Son of Shemaiah son of Shechaniah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:22: Son of Shemaiah son of Shechaniah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Hattush stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Hazael, King of Syria
Summary: Hazael, Elisha's anointed scourge, murdered Ben-Hadad, oppressed Israel through Jehu's and Jehoahaz's days, and died leaving his son Ben-Hadad on the throne.
KeyStory: Hazael murders Ben-Hadad and oppresses Israel.
RelatedPeople: Elisha; Ben-Hadad II, King of Syria; Ben-Hadad III, King of Syria; Jehu, King of Israel; Jehoahaz, King of Israel; Ahaziah, King of Judah; Jehoram, Son of Ahab
LifeLesson: Elisha wept over the cruelty Hazael would do; God uses even cruel kings, and judges them too.

Name: Hazaiah, Son of Adaiah
Summary: Hazaiah son of Adaiah, named in Nehemiah 11:5.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Hazelelponi
Summary: Sister of Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:3: Sister of Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash.
LifeLesson: The mention of Hazelelponi in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Haziel
Summary: Son of Shimei, named with Shelomith and Haran.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 23:9: Son of Shimei, named with Shelomith and Haran.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Haziel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Heber, Father of Socho
Summary: Son of Mered by Jehudijah, called the father of Socho.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:18: Son of Mered by Jehudijah, called the father of Socho.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Heber stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Heber, Son of Beriah
Summary: Son of Beriah and father of Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:31: Son of Beriah and father of Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Heber stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Heber, Son of Elpaal
Summary: Named among the sons of Elpaal in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:17: Named among the sons of Elpaal in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Heber stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Heber, Son of Gad's House
Summary: Named among the brethren of the house of Gad's fathers.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:13: Named among the brethren of the house of Gad's fathers.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Heber stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Heber, Son of Shashak
Summary: Named among the sons of Shashak in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:22: Named among the sons of Shashak in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Heber stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Heber, the Kenite
Summary: Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites and pitched his tent near Kedesh; his wife Jael killed the fleeing Sisera in their tent. He is distinct from Heber, son of Beriah, in Genesis.
KeyStory: Heber, at peace with Jabin, had pitched his tent in the plain of Zaanaim; Sisera fled there trusting that peace, and Jael killed him.
LifeLesson: A household's peace treaty could not protect a tyrant from justice.

Name: Hebron, Son of Mareshah
Summary: Son of Mareshah and father of Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:43: Son of Mareshah and father of Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Hebron stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Hegai
Summary: Keeper of the king's women, named Hege when the maidens were gathered and Hegai when Esther was brought to him; Esther found favour with him and he gave her the best place in the house.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: Favour can be found even in a foreign palace.

Name: Helah
Summary: Wife of Ashur the father of Tekoa and mother of Zereth, Jezoar, and Ethnan.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:5: Wife of Ashur the father of Tekoa and mother of Zereth, Jezoar, and Ethnan.
LifeLesson: The mention of Helah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Heldai the Netophathite
Summary: Captain over the twelfth month's course, of Othniel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:15: Captain over the twelfth month's course, of Othniel.
LifeLesson: The mention of Heldai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Heldai
Summary: Heldai was one of the exiles from Babylon who brought silver and gold to Jerusalem for the crowning of Joshua the high priest (Zechariah 6:10). He appears again in Zechariah 6:14 under the variant name Helem.
KeyStory: Heldai, with Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Josiah son of Zephaniah, brought gifts from Babylon for the crown placed on Joshua's head.
RelatedPeople: Tobijah; Jedaiah; Josiah, Son of Zephaniah
LifeLesson: Heldai carried his wealth home to crown another man. The best use of exile's gains is the glory of the house of God.

Name: Heleb, Son of Baanah
Summary: Heleb, son of Baanah the Netophathite, was among David's thirty mighty men. His father is distinct from Baanah son of Rimmon, Ish-bosheth's murderer.
KeyStory: Heleb son of Baanah the Netophathite stood among David's thirty.
RelatedPeople: King David; Baanah, Father of Heleb
LifeLesson: Two Baanahs, two sons, two opposite stories — the record tells them apart.

Name: Heled, Son of Baanah
Summary: Son of Baanah the Netophathite, one of David's valiant men.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:30: Son of Baanah the Netophathite, one of David's valiant men.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Heled stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Helem
Summary: Brother of Shamer and father of Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:35: Brother of Shamer and father of Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
LifeLesson: The mention of Helem in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Helez, Son of Azariah
Summary: Son of Azariah and father of Eleasah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:39: Son of Azariah and father of Eleasah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Helez stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Helez the Paltite
Summary: Helez the Paltite was among David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Helez the Paltite stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: The thirty are remembered together, and each name counts.

Name: Helez the Pelonite
Summary: Valient man of David's armies and captain of the seventh month's course.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:27; 1 Chronicles 27:10: Valient man of David's armies and captain of the seventh month's course.
LifeLesson: The mention of Helez in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Helkai
Summary: Priest in the days of Joiakim.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Courses of priests kept worship ordered across generations.

Name: Heman, Son of Joel
Summary: Singer, son of Joel son of Shemuel, set by David over the service of song.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:33; 1 Chronicles 15:17: Singer, son of Joel son of Shemuel, set by David over the service of song.
LifeLesson: The mention of Heman in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Heman, Son of Zerah
Summary: Son of Zerah, named among the five sons of Zerah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:6: Son of Zerah, named among the five sons of Zerah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Heman stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Heman
Summary: Heman was named among the wise men with whom Solomon's wisdom was compared. Chronicles also names a Heman son of Zerah and a Heman son of Joel; whether any of these is the same man is not settled, so the profiles are kept separate.
KeyStory: Heman named among the wise.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Ethan the Ezrahite; Chalcol; Darda
LifeLesson: Wisdom's fame is a gift, not a guarantee.

Name: Hemath
Summary: Named as the father of the house of Rechab.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:55: Named as the father of the house of Rechab.
LifeLesson: The mention of Hemath in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Henadad
Summary: Father of Bavai and Binnui, both wall builders (Nehemiah 3:18, 3:24).
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: Two sons building: a father's household at work.

Name: Henoch, Son of Midian
Summary: Son of Midian, named among the sons of Midian and grandsons of Keturah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 1:33: Son of Midian, named among the sons of Midian and grandsons of Keturah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Henoch stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Hepher, Son of Ashur
Summary: Son of Ashur by Naarah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:6: Son of Ashur by Naarah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Hepher stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Hepher the Mecherathite
Summary: Mighty man of David, called the Mecherathite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:36: Mighty man of David, called the Mecherathite.
LifeLesson: The mention of Hepher in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Hephzibah, Mother of Manasseh
Summary: Hephzibah was the mother of Manasseh, Judah's longest-reigning and most idolatrous king.
KeyStory: Hephzibah, mother of Manasseh.
RelatedPeople: Manasseh, King of Judah; King Hezekiah
LifeLesson: A good king's wife can still bear a son who undoes his work.

Name: Heresh
Summary: Levite dwelling in Jerusalem after the return.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:15: Levite dwelling in Jerusalem after the return.
LifeLesson: The mention of Heresh in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Hermas
Summary: Hermas was a Christian in Rome greeted by Paul alongside Asyncritus, Phlegon, Patrobas, and Hermes.
KeyStory: Hermas was a Christian in Rome greeted by Paul alongside Asyncritus, Phlegon, Patrobas, and Hermes.
LifeLesson: Being named among the saints is itself a testimony of belonging.

Name: Hermes
Summary: Hermes was a Christian in Rome greeted by Paul alongside Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, and Patrobas.
KeyStory: Hermes was a Christian in Rome greeted by Paul alongside Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, and Patrobas.
LifeLesson: A name in Paul's greeting shows a life joined to the gospel community.

Name: Hermogenes
Role: One who turned away from Paul in Asia
Summary: Hermogenes was one of those in Asia who turned away from Paul, named with Phygellus in 2 Timothy.
KeyStory: Hermogenes was one of those in Asia who turned away from Paul, named with Phygellus in 2 Timothy.
LifeLesson: When many turn away, the few who stay shine the brighter.

Name: Herod Agrippa I
Summary: Herod Agrippa I, grandson of Herod the Great, ruled Judea in the 40s AD. He killed the apostle James with the sword, imprisoned Peter, and died suddenly after accepting the crowd's cry that his voice was a god's.
KeyStory: Agrippa struck at the church and was himself struck down, eaten by worms, for not giving God glory.
RelatedPeople: James, Son of Zebedee; Simon Peter; Barnabas
LifeLesson: Persecutors rise and fall on God's timetable. Agrippa's crown could not outlast a single sermon of pride.

Name: Herod Agrippa II
Summary: Herod Agrippa II was the last Herodian king, ruling parts of the north-east. Festus brought Paul before him at Caesarea, and Agrippa heard Paul's defence, remarking that Paul almost persuaded him to be a Christian.
KeyStory: Agrippa listened to Paul's whole story and sent him to Rome, judging he had done nothing worthy of death.
LifeLesson: Almost persuaded is still unpersuaded. Agrippa heard the gospel clearly and walked away a king instead of a Christian.

Name: Herod Antipas
Summary: Herod Antipas, son of Herod the Great, ruled Galilee and Perea. He imprisoned and beheaded John the Baptist, heard reports of Jesus and hoped to see a sign, and joined Pilate's mockery of Jesus at the trial.
KeyStory: Antipas beheaded John to keep a rash oath, then met Jesus in silence when the prisoner would not perform.
LifeLesson: Curiosity is not repentance. Antipas wanted a miracle from Jesus and got silence, because he had already silenced the prophet.

Name: Herod the Great
Summary: Herod the Great was the client king ruling Judea when Jesus was born. Hearing from the wise men of a newborn King of the Jews, he ordered the killing of the male children in Bethlehem, and Joseph fled with Mary and Jesus into Egypt.
KeyStory: Herod's soldiers searched Bethlehem for a baby king, while the child escaped to Egypt until Herod was dead.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Mary, Mother of Jesus; Joseph, Husband of Mary
LifeLesson: Earthly power panics at the true King. Herod's rage could not touch the child God was keeping.

Name: Herodias
Summary: Herodias had left Herod Philip to marry his brother Herod Antipas, a union John the Baptist denounced as unlawful. She nursed a grudge against John and used her daughter's dance to demand his head.
KeyStory: Herodias held her grudge until a birthday feast gave her the prophet's head on a charger.
LifeLesson: A grudge kept long enough finds its occasion. Herodias shows how resentment, nursed in private, kills in public.

Name: Herodion
Summary: Herodion was a kinsman of Paul greeted among the Roman Christians.
KeyStory: Herodion was a kinsman of Paul greeted among the Roman Christians.
LifeLesson: Family ties redeemed by the gospel become bonds of ministry.

Name: Hezeki
Summary: Named among the sons of Elpaal in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:17: Named among the sons of Elpaal in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Hezeki stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Hezekiah, Son of Amariah
Summary: Hezekiah, son of Amariah, is the earliest named ancestor in Zephaniah's genealogy (Zephaniah 1:1). He is NOT King Hezekiah of Judah: the genealogy runs Zephaniah–Cushi–Gedaliah–Amariah–Hezekiah, and this Hezekiah lived generations after the king whose name he shared.
KeyStory: Zephaniah traced his line back to a Hezekiah who was his great-great-grandfather — a different man from the reforming king of Judah.
LifeLesson: Names repeat; people don't. Zephaniah's Hezekiah is a warning against assuming every familiar name is the famous one.

Name: Hezekiah, Son of Neariah
Summary: Son of Neariah, named in the post-exilic royal line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:23: Son of Neariah, named in the post-exilic royal line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Hezekiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Hezion, Grandfather of Ben-Hadad I
Summary: Hezion was the grandfather of Ben-Hadad, king of Syria in Asa's days.
KeyStory: Hezion, grandfather of Ben-Hadad.
RelatedPeople: Ben-Hadad I, King of Syria; Tabrimon, Father of Ben-Hadad I
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Hezir
Summary: Seventeenth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:15: Seventeenth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
LifeLesson: The mention of Hezir in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Hezrai the Carmelite
Summary: Hezrai the Carmelite was among David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Hezrai the Carmelite stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: Carmel gave David a warrior for the thirty.

Name: Hezro the Carmelite
Summary: Mighty man of David, called the Carmelite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:37: Mighty man of David, called the Carmelite.
LifeLesson: The mention of Hezro in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Hiddai
Summary: Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash was among David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Hiddai of Gaash stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: A man of the brooks of Gaash stood in the king's thirty.

Name: Hiel the Bethelite
Summary: Hiel the Bethelite rebuilt Jericho in Ahab's days, laying its foundation at the cost of his firstborn Abiram and its gates at the cost of his youngest Segub, according to Joshua's curse.
KeyStory: Hiel rebuilds Jericho at the cost of his sons.
RelatedPeople: King Ahab; Abiram, Son of Hiel; Segub, Son of Hiel
LifeLesson: An old curse is not old news: Hiel paid for Jericho in his own sons.

Name: Hilkiah, Ancestor of Ezra
Summary: Ancestor of Ezra named in his genealogy; a different Hilkiah from the priests of Nehemiah's day.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: A long line of priests ends in a scribe.

Name: Hilkiah, Beside Ezra
Summary: Priest who stood beside Ezra on the platform at the reading of the law (Nehemiah 8:4).
KeyStory: Ezra reads the law
LifeLesson: Priests stood with the people to hear the law.

Name: Hilkiah, Father of Amaziah
Summary: Father of Amaziah in Ethan's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:45: Father of Amaziah in Ethan's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Hilkiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Hilkiah, Father of Azariah
Summary: Father of Azariah the ruler of the house of God, son of Meshullam son of Zadok.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:11: Father of Azariah the ruler of the house of God, son of Meshullam son of Zadok.
LifeLesson: The mention of Hilkiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Hilkiah, High Priest
Summary: Hilkiah the high priest found the book of the law while repairing the temple under Josiah, and sent it to the king, whose heart broke at its words.
KeyStory: Hilkiah finds the book of the law.
RelatedPeople: King Josiah; Shaphan, Scribe; Huldah, Prophetess; Ahikam, Son of Shaphan; Achbor, Son of Michaiah; Asahiah, Servant of Josiah
LifeLesson: Repairing a building found a book, and the book repaired a kingdom.

Name: Hilkiah, Son of Hosah
Summary: Second son of Hosah the porter.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:11: Second son of Hosah the porter.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Hilkiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Hilkiah, Son of Meshullam
Summary: Hilkiah son of Meshullam, named in Nehemiah 11:11.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Hilkiah, Son of Shallum
Summary: Son of Shallum and priest in Aaron's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:13: Son of Shallum and priest in Aaron's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Hilkiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Hilkiah, the High Priest
Summary: Hilkiah the high priest received the temple repair money, found the book of the law of the LORD given by Moses, gave it to Shaphan, and went with the king's men to Huldah the prophetess; he also gave Passover offerings as a ruler of the house of God.
KeyStory: Hilkiah said to Shaphan, 'I have found the book of the law in the house of the LORD,' and the reading of it rent the king's clothes and renewed the covenant.
RelatedPeople: King Josiah; Shaphan, Son of Azaliah; Huldah, the Prophetess
LifeLesson: Finding God's lost book can change a king and a kingdom.

Name: Hillel, Father of Abdon
Summary: Hillel is named only as the father of Abdon the judge, a Pirathonite.
KeyStory: Hillel appears in Judges only as Abdon's father.
LifeLesson: A father known only by his son's judgeship.

Name: Hiram, Craftsman of Tyre
Summary: Hiram, a widow's son of Tyre skilled in bronze, cast the two pillars, the sea, the bases, and all the vessels for Solomon's temple, and finished all the work for the house of the LORD.
KeyStory: Hiram casts the temple's bronze works.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Hiram, King of Tyre
LifeLesson: God-given skill, offered to God's house, becomes part of worship itself.

Name: Hiram, King of Tyre
Summary: Hiram, king of Tyre, sent messengers, cedar trees, carpenters, and masons to David and built him a house at Jerusalem, a sign that David's kingdom was established. Also known as Huram.
KeyStory: Hiram of Tyre built David a cedar house, the first foreign recognition of his kingdom.
KeyVerses: 2 Samuel 5:11; 1 Kings 5:1; 1 Kings 5:10; 1 Chronicles 14:1; 2 Chronicles 2:3; 2 Chronicles 2:11; 2 Chronicles 2:12
RelatedPeople: King David; King Solomon; Hiram, Craftsman of Tyre; Huram, the Craftsman
LifeLesson: Foreign kings honouring God's anointed is itself a testimony.

Name: Hizkijah
Summary: Chief who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:17). Not Hezekiah the king.
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: Sealing a covenant is a chief's public stand.

Name: Hod
Summary: Son of Zophah in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:37: Son of Zophah in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Hod stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Hodaiah
Summary: Son of Elioenai son of Neariah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:24: Son of Elioenai son of Neariah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Hodaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Hodaviah, Father of Meshullam
Summary: Father of Meshullam in the Jerusalem list, son of Hasenuah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:7: Father of Meshullam in the Jerusalem list, son of Hasenuah.
LifeLesson: The mention of Hodaviah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Hodaviah, Head of Manasseh
Summary: Head of the house of Manasseh's fathers, a mighty man of valour.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:24: Head of the house of Manasseh's fathers, a mighty man of valour.
LifeLesson: The mention of Hodaviah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Hodaviah
Summary: A Levite who returned with Zerubbabel; Nehemiah's copy of the list spells the name Hodevah.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Two copies of one list can spell one man's name two ways.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Hodesh
Summary: Wife of Shaharaim, by whom he begat Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcham, Jeuz, Shachia, and Mirma.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:9: Wife of Shaharaim, by whom he begat Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcham, Jeuz, Shachia, and Mirma.
LifeLesson: The mention of Hodesh in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Hodiah
Summary: Wife of Mered, sister of Naham, named in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:19: Wife of Mered, sister of Naham, named in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Hodiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Hodijah
Summary: Levites who taught the law at Ezra's reading.
KeyStory: Ezra reads the law
LifeLesson: Teaching God's word and committing to it go together.

Name: Hophni
Summary: Hophni, son of Eli, served as a priest at Shiloh with his brother Phinehas. The two treated the Lord's offerings with contempt, and both died on the day the ark was captured.
KeyStory: Hophni's corrupt priesthood ended in a single day of judgment at Aphek.
LifeLesson: A sacred office does not protect a corrupt heart; God judges his own house first.

Name: Hophra
Summary: Hophra was Pharaoh of Egypt in the days after Jerusalem's fall; Jeremiah declared that God would give Hophra into the hand of his enemies, just as Zedekiah had been given into Nebuchadnezzar's hand.
KeyStory: Jeremiah gave the Jews who fled to Egypt a sign: Pharaoh-hophra would be delivered to those seeking his life, as surely as Zedekiah had been delivered to Babylon.
LifeLesson: Fleeing to Egypt for safety only moved the judgment to Egypt.

Name: Hosah, Porter
Summary: Porter before the ark, son of Jeduthun's line in chapter 16, and father of Simri in chapter 26.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 16:38; 1 Chronicles 26:10: Porter before the ark, son of Jeduthun's line in chapter 16, and father of Simri in chapter 26.
LifeLesson: The mention of Hosah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Hoshaiah
Summary: Prince of Judah who walked on the wall at its dedication (Nehemiah 12:32).
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Princes walked the wall they had helped restore.

Name: Hoshama
Summary: Son of Jeconiah, named in the post-exilic royal line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:18: Son of Jeconiah, named in the post-exilic royal line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Hoshama stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Hoshea, King of Israel
Summary: Hoshea, son of Elah, slew Pekah, then conspired with So of Egypt and withheld Assyria's tribute; Shalmaneser besieged Samaria three years, and Israel was carried away to Assyria for its sins.
KeyStory: Hoshea's conspiracy and the fall of Samaria.
RelatedPeople: Pekah, King of Israel; So, King of Egypt; Shalmaneser, King of Assyria; Elah, Father of Hoshea
LifeLesson: The last king of Israel shows where a long road of idolatry ends: exile.

Name: Hoshea, Son of Azaziah
Summary: Son of Azaziah, ruler of the children of Ephraim.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:20: Son of Azaziah, ruler of the children of Ephraim.

LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Hothir stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Huldah, Prophetess
Summary: Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum keeper of the wardrobe, told Josiah's messengers that Jerusalem would indeed face the curses of the book, but because Josiah's heart was tender he would be gathered to his grave in peace.
KeyStory: Huldah confirms judgment and promises Josiah peace.
RelatedPeople: King Josiah; Hilkiah, High Priest; Shallum, Husband of Huldah
LifeLesson: A tender heart does not cancel judgment, but it does find mercy within it.

Name: Huldah, the Prophetess
Summary: Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum keeper of the wardrobe, answered Josiah's messengers that evil would come on Jerusalem for forsaking the LORD, but because Josiah's heart was tender and he humbled himself, he would be gathered to his grave in peace and not see the evil.
KeyStory: Huldah declared, 'Because thine heart was tender, and thou didst humble thyself before God... I have even heard thee also, saith the LORD.'
RelatedPeople: King Josiah; Shallum, Son of Tikvath
LifeLesson: A tender, humbled heart can win peace even when judgment is certain.

Name: Huppah

KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:13: Thirteenth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
LifeLesson: The mention of Huppah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Huppim, Son of Ir
Summary: Child of Ir, named with Shuppim among Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:12: Child of Ir, named with Shuppim among Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Huppim stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Hur, Father of Rephaiah
Summary: Father of Rephaiah the wall builder; a different Hur from Moses' helper in Exodus.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: A father's name can open a son's story.

Name: Hur, Father of Uri
Summary: Hur was the father of Uri and grandfather of Bezaleel, the tabernacle craftsman.
KeyStory: Hur is named only in the line of Bezaleel: Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur.
LifeLesson: God's purposes often run through families, one generation preparing the next.

Name: Hurai
Summary: Mighty man of David from the brooks of Gaash.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:32: Mighty man of David from the brooks of Gaash.
LifeLesson: The mention of Hurai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Huram, the Craftsman
Summary: Huram, a cunning man endued with understanding, was sent by the king of Tyre to Solomon; he made the temple's bronze vessels, including the pots, shovels, basins, pillars and sea.
KeyStory: Huram finished the bronze work for the house of God, and made all its instruments of bright brass for King Solomon.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Hiram, King of Tyre
LifeLesson: God-given skill, used for His house, is itself a form of service.

Name: Huram
Summary: Son of Bela, named among the sons of Bela.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:5: Son of Bela, named among the sons of Bela.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Huram stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Huri
Summary: Father of Abihail in Gad's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:14: Father of Abihail in Gad's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Huri in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Hushai, Father of Baanah
Summary: Hushai was the father of Baanah, Solomon's officer over Asher and Aloth.
KeyStory: Hushai, father of Baanah.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Hushai the Archite
Summary: Hushai the Archite, David's friend, stayed in Jerusalem when David fled and pretended to serve Absalom. His counsel — to wait and gather all Israel — overruled Ahithophel's plan for a swift strike and saved David's life and kingdom.
KeyStory: Hushai's slow counsel defeated Ahithophel's swift counsel and saved David.
RelatedPeople: King David; Absalom; Ahithophel the Gilonite; Zadok, Son of Ahitub
LifeLesson: One loyal friend inside the enemy's council can be worth an army.

Name: Hushim, Son of Aher
Summary: Son of Aher, named in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:12: Son of Aher, named in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Hushim stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Hushim, Wife of Shaharaim
Summary: Wife of Shaharaim, by whom he begat Abitub and Elpaal.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:8: Wife of Shaharaim, by whom he begat Abitub and Elpaal.
LifeLesson: The mention of Hushim in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Hymenaeus
Role: Teacher who erred and was delivered to Satan
Summary: Hymenaeus was named by Paul in 1 Timothy among those delivered unto Satan that they might learn not to blaspheme, and in 2 Timothy as one whose teaching, with Philetus, said the resurrection was past already and overthrew the faith of some.
KeyStory: Hymenaeus was named by Paul in 1 Timothy among those delivered unto Satan that they might learn not to blaspheme, and in 2 Timothy as one whose teaching, with Philetus, said the resurrection was past already and overthrew the faith of some.
LifeLesson: Wrong teaching about the resurrection overthrows faith; truth must be guarded, not trimmed.

Name: Ibhar, Son of David
Summary: Son of David born in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:6; 1 Chronicles 14:5: Son of David born in Jerusalem.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ibhar stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ibhar
Summary: Ibhar was a son of David born at Jerusalem, named among the sons born to him there after he took the city.
KeyStory: Ibhar was born to David at Jerusalem after the city became his capital.
LifeLesson: The record keeps even the sons who never take the stage.

Name: Ibneiah, Son of Jeroham
Summary: Son of Jeroham, of the sons of Benjamin dwelling in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:8: Son of Jeroham, of the sons of Benjamin dwelling in Jerusalem.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ibneiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ibnijah

KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:8: Father of Reuel in the Jerusalem list.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ibnijah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ibri

KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:27: Son of Jaaziah, named among the sons of Merari by Jaaziah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ibri stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ibzan, Judge of Israel
Summary: Ibzan of Beth-lehem judged Israel seven years; he had thirty sons and thirty daughters, whom he married outside his family.
KeyStory: Ibzan judged Israel seven years from Bethlehem, sending thirty daughters abroad and bringing thirty daughters in for his thirty sons, and was buried in Bethlehem.
LifeLesson: A judge remembered for marriages, not battles.

Name: Ichabod, Son of Phinehas
Summary: Ichabod was born as his mother lay dying on the day the ark was captured and his father and grandfather died. She named him Ichabod, meaning 'the glory is departed from Israel.'
KeyStory: Ichabod's very name marked the day Israel lost the ark, his father, and his grandfather at once.
LifeLesson: A name can carry a nation's grief — and point to how much God's presence is worth.

Name: Idbash
Summary: Named among the sons of the father of Etam.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:3: Named among the sons of the father of Etam.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Idbash stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Iddo, Chief at Casiphia
Summary: Chief at Casiphia to whom Ezra sent for Levites and Nethinims for the temple service.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: God provides workers when his people ask.

Name: Iddo, Father of Ahinadab
Summary: Iddo was the father of Ahinadab, Solomon's officer over Mahanaim.
KeyStory: Iddo, father of Ahinadab.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Iddo, Grandfather of Zechariah
Summary: Father of the prophet Zechariah (Ezra calls Zechariah 'the son of Iddo'); his grandson prophesied during the temple rebuilding.
KeyStory: Rebuilding of the Temple
LifeLesson: God's work spans generations: a father's faithfulness bears fruit in his children's calling.

Name: Iddo, Son of Joah
Summary: Son of Joah and father of Zerah in Gershom's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:21: Son of Joah and father of Zerah in Gershom's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Iddo stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Iddo, Son of Zechariah
Summary: Son of Zechariah, ruler of the half tribe of Manasseh in Gilead.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:21: Son of Zechariah, ruler of the half tribe of Manasseh in Gilead.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Iddo stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Iddo, the Seer
Summary: Iddo the seer recorded visions against Jeroboam son of Nebat, wrote concerning the genealogies of Rehoboam's days, and wrote the story of Abijah.
KeyStory: Solomon's acts are written in the visions of Iddo the seer, Rehoboam's acts in the book of Iddo concerning genealogies, and Abijah's ways in the story of the prophet Iddo.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Rehoboam; Abijah, King of Judah
LifeLesson: Faithful record-keeping preserves God's dealings for generations who were not there.

Name: Iddo
Summary: Iddo is named as the grandfather of the prophet Zechariah (Zechariah 1:1), and is also called 'Iddo the prophet' among those who encouraged the Temple rebuilding. He stands at the head of Zechariah's line, a prophet himself in the generation of the return.
KeyStory: Iddo, grandfather of Zechariah and himself called a prophet, is named among those whose words spurred the returned exiles to rebuild the Temple.
LifeLesson: Iddo's line runs prophet to prophet, grandfather to grandson. Faith handed down is still the surest inheritance.

Name: Igal, Son of Nathan
Summary: Igal, son of Nathan of Zobah, was among David's thirty mighty men. He is distinct from Igal son of Joseph, the spy of Numbers.
KeyStory: Igal son of Nathan of Zobah stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: Two Igals, two generations — Zobah's son stood in the thirty.

Name: Igeal
Summary: Son of Shemaiah son of Shechaniah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:22: Son of Shemaiah son of Shechaniah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Igeal stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ikkesh, Father of Ira
Summary: Ikkesh the Tekoite is named as the father of Ira, one of David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Ikkesh's son stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: A Tekoite father raised one of the thirty.

Name: Ikkesh
Summary: Father of Ira the Tekoite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:28: Father of Ira the Tekoite.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ikkesh in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ilai the Ahohite

KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:29: Valient man of David's armies, called the Ahohite.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ilai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Imla, Father of Micaiah
Summary: Imla was the father of Micaiah the prophet, consulted before the battle of Ramoth-gilead.
KeyStory: Imla is named only as the father of Micaiah the son of Imla.
LifeLesson: A father's name survives because his son would not bend the truth.

Name: Imlah, Father of Micaiah
Summary: Imlah was the father of Micaiah the prophet, whom Ahab hated.
KeyStory: Imlah, father of Micaiah.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Immer, Course Head

KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:14: Sixteenth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
LifeLesson: The mention of Immer in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

LifeLesson: The mention of Immer in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Immer

KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: A father's name can open a son's story.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Imna

LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Imna stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Imnah, Father of Kore
Summary: Imnah was the father of Kore, the Levite porter toward the east over the freewill offerings.
KeyStory: Imnah is named only as the father of Kore the son of Imnah the Levite.
LifeLesson: A porter's father is named in the distribution list.

Name: Imnah
Summary: Son of Asher, named among the sons of Asher.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:30: Son of Asher, named among the sons of Asher.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Imnah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Imrah
Summary: Son of Zophah in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:36: Son of Zophah in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Imrah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Imri, Father of Omri
Summary: Father of Omri in the Jerusalem list, son of Bani.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:4: Father of Omri in the Jerusalem list, son of Bani.
LifeLesson: The mention of Imri in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Imri
Summary: Father of Zaccur the wall builder (Nehemiah 3:2).
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: A father's name stands behind his son's section of wall.

Name: Iphedeiah
Summary: Named among the sons of Shashak in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:25: Named among the sons of Shashak in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Iphedeiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ir
Summary: Father of Shuppim and Huppim in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:12: Father of Shuppim and Huppim in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ir in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ira, Son of Ikkesh
Summary: Ira, son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, was among David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite stood among David's thirty.
RelatedPeople: King David; Ikkesh, Father of Ira
LifeLesson: Tekoa gave David a warrior as well as a wise woman.

Name: Ira the Ithrite
Summary: Ira the Ithrite was among David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Ira the Ithrite stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: An Ithrite among the thirty — the tribes fought side by side.

Name: Ira the Jairite
Summary: Ira the Jairite was a chief ruler about David, named among his closest officers in the later administration.
KeyStory: Ira stood among David's inner circle at the end of his reign.
LifeLesson: Proximity to the king is itself a calling, even without a battlefield.

Name: Iri
Summary: Son of Bela and head of his father's house, a mighty man of valour.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:7: Son of Bela and head of his father's house, a mighty man of valour.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Iri stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Irijah
Summary: Irijah, son of Shelemiah, was captain of the ward at the gate of Benjamin who arrested Jeremiah as he tried to leave Jerusalem, charging him with falling away to the Chaldeans, and delivered him to the princes who beat him and put him in prison.
KeyStory: As Jeremiah went out toward the land of Benjamin, Irijah the captain laid hold on him, saying he was falling away to the Chaldeans, and would not listen to his denial.
LifeLesson: A guard doing his duty can still become an instrument of injustice when he will not hear the accused.

Name: Iru
Summary: Son of Caleb son of Jephunneh.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:15: Son of Caleb son of Jephunneh.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Iru stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ish-bosheth, Son of Saul
Summary: Ish-bosheth, son of Saul — also called Eshbaal — was made king over Israel by Abner after Saul's death and reigned two years from Mahanaim while David reigned at Hebron. After Abner defected, Ish-bosheth was murdered in his sleep by Rechab and Baanah, and David had the murderers executed.
KeyStory: Ish-bosheth held Saul's throne for two years, then was murdered in his own bed.
RelatedPeople: King Saul; Abner, Son of Ner; Michal; Merab
LifeLesson: A throne held by another man's strength falls when that strength walks away.

Name: Ishbah
Summary: Son borne in Ezra's line, called the father of Eshtemoa.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:17: Son borne in Ezra's line, called the father of Eshtemoa.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ishbah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ishbi-benob
Summary: Ishbi-benob, a descendant of the giant and armed with a new sword and a spear weighing three hundred shekels of brass, thought to slay David when he grew faint in battle. Abishai rescued David and killed him.
KeyStory: Ishbi-benob nearly killed an exhausted David — and Abishai cut him down.
LifeLesson: Even giants fall to the friends who refuse to let a king fight alone.

Name: Ishi, Head of Manasseh
Summary: Head of the house of Manasseh's fathers, a mighty man of valour.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:24: Head of the house of Manasseh's fathers, a mighty man of valour.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ishi in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ishi, Son of Appaim
Summary: Son of Appaim and father of Sheshan.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:31: Son of Appaim and father of Sheshan.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ishi stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ishi, Son of Shimon
Summary: Father of Zoheth and Ben-zoheth in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:20: Father of Zoheth and Ben-zoheth in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ishi stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ishiah, Son of Izrahiah
Summary: Son of Izrahiah, a chief man in Issachar's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:3: Son of Izrahiah, a chief man in Issachar's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ishiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ishijah, Son of Harim
Summary: Son of Harim named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Ishma
Summary: Named among the sons of the father of Etam.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:3: Named among the sons of the father of Etam.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ishma stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ishmael, Father of Zebadiah
Summary: Ishmael was the father of Zebadiah, ruler of the house of Judah under Jehoshaphat.
KeyStory: Ishmael is named only as the father of Zebadiah the son of Ishmael.
LifeLesson: A father's name marks the family behind a public office.

Name: Ishmael, Son of Azel
Summary: Son of Azel, named among the six sons of Azel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:38; 1 Chronicles 9:44: Son of Azel, named among the six sons of Azel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ishmael stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ishmael, Son of Jehohanan
Summary: Ishmael, son of Jehohanan, was one of the captains of hundreds Jehoiada took into covenant to crown Joash.
KeyStory: Jehoiada took Ishmael the son of Jehohanan into covenant with him.
RelatedPeople: Jehoiada, the Priest; Jehohanan, Father of Ishmael
LifeLesson: Faithful officers risked their lives for the LORD's anointed.

Name: Ishmael, Son of Nethaniah
Summary: Ishmael, son of Nethaniah, of the seed royal, came with ten men to Gedaliah at Mizpah, ate with him, and slew him and the Jews and Chaldeans with him, then fled to Ammon.
KeyStory: Ishmael murders Gedaliah at Mizpah.
RelatedPeople: Gedaliah, Son of Ahikam; Nethaniah, Father of Ishmael; Elishama, Grandfather of Ishmael; Gedaliah; Johanan, Son of Kareah; Jeremiah
LifeLesson: Royal blood without loyalty is the most dangerous kind of treason.

Name: Ishmael the Priest
Summary: A priest named among those who had taken foreign wives; a different Ishmael from Abraham's son.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Sin named honestly is the first step back to God.

Name: Ishmaiah, Son of Obadiah
Summary: Son of Obadiah, ruler of Zebulun.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:19: Son of Obadiah, ruler of Zebulun.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ishmaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ishmerai
Summary: Named among the sons of Elpaal in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:18: Named among the sons of Elpaal in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ishmerai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ishod
Summary: Son of Hammoleketh, named in Manasseh's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:18: Son of Hammoleketh, named in Manasseh's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ishod stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ishpan
Summary: Named among the sons of Shashak in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:22: Named among the sons of Shashak in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ishpan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ishuai
Summary: Son of Asher, named among the sons of Asher.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:30: Son of Asher, named among the sons of Asher.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ishuai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ishui, Son of Saul
Summary: Ishui is listed among Saul's sons in 1 Samuel 14 (also rendered Ishvi). Some readers identify him with Ish-bosheth, also called Eshbaal, but the Samuel text names them in different passages and they are kept separate here.
KeyStory: Ishui is named once, among Saul's sons, and then disappears from the record.
LifeLesson: Some lives are recorded in a single verse — and still counted.

Name: Ismachiah, Overseer
Summary: Ismachiah was one of the overseers under Cononiah and Shimei over the offerings and tithes under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Ismachiah was one of the overseers under Cononiah and Shimei over the offerings and tithes under Hezekiah.
RelatedPeople: Cononiah, the Levite; Shimei, Brother of Cononiah; King Hezekiah; Azariah, Chief Priest
LifeLesson: Many overseers together kept one storehouse honest.

Name: Ismaiah the Gibeonite
Summary: Mighty man among the thirty, and over the thirty, who came to David at Ziklag.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:4: Mighty man among the thirty, and over the thirty, who came to David at Ziklag.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ismaiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Ispah
Summary: Named among the sons of Beriah in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:16: Named among the sons of Beriah in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ispah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Issachar, Son of Obed-edom
Summary: Seventh son of Obed-edom the porter.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:5: Seventh son of Obed-edom the porter.
LifeLesson: The mention of Issachar in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Isshiah, Brother of Michah
Summary: Brother of Michah son of Uzziel, father of Zechariah in the rest of the sons of Levi.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:25: Brother of Michah son of Uzziel, father of Zechariah in the rest of the sons of Levi.
LifeLesson: The mention of Isshiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Isuah
Summary: Son of Asher, named among the sons of Asher.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:30: Son of Asher, named among the sons of Asher.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Isuah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ithai, Son of Ribai

LifeLesson: Ithiel's place in Scripture honours the hearer of wisdom, not only its speaker.

KeyStory: Ithra fathered the commander who led a revolt and was murdered for it.
RelatedPeople: Amasa, Son of Ithra; Abigail, Daughter of Nahash
LifeLesson: A father's name rides on a son's divided loyalties.

Name: Ithran, Son of Zophah

Name: Ithream, Son of David

LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ithream stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ithream
Summary: Ithream, David's sixth son by Eglah, was born at Hebron and is named among the six sons born there.
KeyStory: Ithream was born at Hebron to David and Eglah.
LifeLesson: The youngest son of Hebron is still written down.

Name: Ittai, Son of Ribai
Summary: Ittai, son of Ribai of Gibeah of Benjamin, was among David's thirty mighty men. He is distinct from Ittai the Gittite, who stayed loyal to David in Absalom's revolt.
KeyStory: Ittai son of Ribai of Gibeah stood among David's thirty.
RelatedPeople: King David; Ribai, Father of Ittai
LifeLesson: Two Ittais served David — a Benjamite and a Gittite — and both were loyal.

Name: Ittai the Gittite
Summary: Ittai the Gittite, a Philistine from Gath with six hundred men, refused to leave David when he fled from Absalom, saying that where the king was, there would his servant be. He commanded a third of David's army in the battle against Absalom.
KeyStory: Ittai the Gittite, a foreigner with six hundred men, refused to abandon the fleeing king.
LifeLesson: Loyalty from an outsider shames the betrayal of insiders.

Name: Izrahiah
Summary: Son of Uzzi and father of Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Ishiah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:3: Son of Uzzi and father of Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Ishiah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Izrahiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Izri

LifeLesson: Service in God's house spans generations.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Jaanai
Summary: Named among the chiefs of Gad in Bashan.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:12: Named among the chiefs of Gad in Bashan.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jaanai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jaare-oregim
Summary: Jaare-oregim of Bethlehem is named as the father of Elhanan, who struck down a Philistine giant at Gob.
KeyStory: Jaare-oregim's son fought giants in David's later wars.
LifeLesson: A father's name survives in a son's single great blow.

Name: Jaasau, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:37).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Putting away what God forbids is an act of trust.

Name: Jaasiel, Son of Abner
Summary: Son of Abner, ruler of Benjamin.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:21: Son of Abner, ruler of Benjamin.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jaasiel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jaazaniah, Captain
Summary: Jaazaniah, son of the Maachathite, was one of the captains who came to Gedaliah at Mizpah after the fall of Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Jaazaniah comes to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
LifeLesson: After ruin, the remnant's captains still gathered to the governor God left them.

Name: Jaazaniah, Son of Azur
Summary: Jaazaniah, son of Azur, was one of the twenty-five princes at the east gate of the temple whom Ezekiel saw in vision devising mischief and giving wicked counsel in Jerusalem; God told Ezekiel to prophesy against them, and Pelatiah son of Benaiah fell dead as he prophesied. He is a different man from Jaazaniah son of Shaphan and Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah.
KeyStory: Ezekiel saw Jaazaniah son of Azur among the princes at the east gate, and God commanded him to prophesy against the men who devised mischief in the city.
LifeLesson: Wicked counsel at the gate of God's house is judged at the gate of God's house.

Name: Jaazaniah, Son of Jeremiah
Summary: Jaazaniah, son of Jeremiah (a different Jeremiah from the prophet), was a Rechabite whom Jeremiah brought into the temple chamber and tested with wine; Jaazaniah and his brothers refused, holding to Jonadab's command to drink no wine and build no houses. He is a different man from Jaazaniah son of Shaphan and Jaazaniah son of Azur.
KeyStory: Jeremiah set bowls of wine before Jaazaniah and the Rechabites, and they answered that Jonadab their father had commanded them to drink no wine for ever.
LifeLesson: Obedience kept for generations can shame a whole nation that will not obey for a day.

Name: Jaazaniah, Son of Shaphan
Summary: Jaazaniah, son of Shaphan, was one of the seventy elders of Israel whom Ezekiel saw in a vision standing in a dark chamber, each with a censer, burning incense to idols painted on the wall, saying that the Lord did not see them. He is a different man from Jaazaniah son of Azur and Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah.
KeyStory: In vision Ezekiel saw Jaazaniah son of Shaphan among seventy elders worshipping idols in the dark, each man with his censer in his hand.
LifeLesson: Secret idolatry by elders is not hidden from God, even when it is hidden from everyone else.

Name: Jaaziah, Son of Merari
Summary: Son of Merari, father of Beno in the rest of the sons of Levi.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:26: Son of Merari, father of Beno in the rest of the sons of Levi.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jaaziah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jaaziel, Singer

LifeLesson: The mention of Jaaziel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Jabesh, Father of Shallum

KeyStory: Jabesh, father of Shallum.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Jabez
Summary: More honourable than his brethren, who prayed that God would bless him and keep him from evil, and God granted his request.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:9; 1 Chronicles 4:10: More honourable than his brethren, who prayed that God would bless him and keep him from evil, and God granted his request.
LifeLesson: The mention of Jabez in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Jabin, King of Canaan
Summary: Jabin, king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor, oppressed Israel twenty years with nine hundred chariots of iron until Deborah and Barak defeated his captain Sisera at the Kishon. He is distinct from the earlier Jabin of Hazor in Joshua.
KeyStory: Jabin's iron chariots terrorised Israel for twenty years until Deborah sent Barak against Sisera, and God discomfited the whole host at the Kishon.
LifeLesson: Iron chariots look unbeatable until the river rises.

Name: Jachan

LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jachan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jachin, Course Head

LifeLesson: The mention of Jachin in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

LifeLesson: The mention of Jachin in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Jachin the Priest
Summary: A priest who dwelt in Jerusalem after the return; a different Jachin from Simeon's son in Genesis.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Dwelling in the city is itself a commitment.

Name: Jada

KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:28: Son of Onam and brother of Shammai.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jada stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jadau, Son of Nebo

KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Jaddua, Son of Jonathan
Summary: High priest, son of Jonathan, last in the succession listed from Jeshua.
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: A long line ends where faithfulness continues.

Name: Jadon
Summary: Helped rebuild Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: Every section of the wall mattered, and every builder is named.

Name: Jahath, Overseer
Summary: Jahath, a Levite of the sons of Merari, was an overseer of the workmen repairing the house of the LORD under Josiah, and the men did the work faithfully.
KeyStory: The overseers of the repair were Jahath and Obadiah, Levites of the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam of the Kohathites.
LifeLesson: Faithful oversight kept the temple repair honest.

Name: Jahath, Son of Gershom

LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jahath stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jahath, Son of Libni

LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jahath stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jahath, Son of Reaiah
Summary: Son of Reaiah and father of Ahumai and Lahad.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:2: Son of Reaiah and father of Ahumai and Lahad.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jahath stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jahath, Son of Shelomith
Summary: Son of Shelomith of the Izharites in the rest of the sons of Levi.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:22: Son of Shelomith of the Izharites in the rest of the sons of Levi.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jahath stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jahath, Son of Shimei
Summary: Son of Shimei, chief among the sons of Shimei.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 23:10: Son of Shimei, chief among the sons of Shimei.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jahath stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jahaziah, Son of Tikvah
Summary: Son of Tikvah who with Jonathan stood against Ezra's plan to put away the foreign wives.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Even good plans meet honest opposition.

Name: Jahaziel, Priest
Summary: Priest with trumpets continually before the ark of the covenant of God, with Benaiah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 16:6: Priest with trumpets continually before the ark of the covenant of God, with Benaiah.
LifeLesson: The mention of Jahaziel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Jahaziel, Son of Hebron

Name: Jahaziel
Summary: Father of Shechaniah, who returned with Ezra.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: A father's name can open a son's story.

Name: Jahdai
Summary: Named as the father of Regem, Jotham, Gesham, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:47: Named as the father of Regem, Jotham, Gesham, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
LifeLesson: The mention of Jahdai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Jahdiel
Summary: Head of the house of Manasseh's fathers, a mighty man of valour.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:24: Head of the house of Manasseh's fathers, a mighty man of valour.
LifeLesson: The mention of Jahdiel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Jahdo

LifeLesson: The mention of Jahdo in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Jahmai
Summary: Son of Tola and head of his father's house, a valiant man of might.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:2: Son of Tola and head of his father's house, a valiant man of might.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jahmai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jahzerah
Summary: Father of Adiel in the Jerusalem priest list, son of Meshullam.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:12: Father of Adiel in the Jerusalem priest list, son of Meshullam.
LifeLesson: The mention of Jahzerah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Jahziel
Summary: Son of Naphtali, named among the sons of Naphtali by Bilhah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:13: Son of Naphtali, named among the sons of Naphtali by Bilhah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jahziel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jair, Father of Elhanan
Summary: Father of Elhanan who slew Lahmi.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 20:5: Father of Elhanan who slew Lahmi.
LifeLesson: The mention of Jair in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Jair, Father of Mordecai
Summary: Father of Mordecai, son of Shimei, son of Kish, a Benjamite whose family had been carried away with Jeconiah.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: Exile does not erase a family's line.

Name: Jair, the Gileadite
Summary: Jair, a Gileadite, judged Israel twenty-two years; he had thirty sons who rode on thirty ass colts and controlled thirty cities called Havoth-jair. He is distinct from Jair, son of Manasseh, in Numbers.
KeyStory: Jair judged Israel twenty-two years from Gilead, and his thirty sons rode thirty ass colts over thirty cities named Havoth-jair; he died and was buried in Camon.
LifeLesson: Thirty sons and thirty cities — a judge's house looked like a small kingdom.

Name: Jairus
Summary: Jairus was a ruler of the synagogue whose twelve-year-old daughter was dying. He begged Jesus to come, believed through the news of her death, and saw Jesus take her by the hand and raise her.
KeyStory: Jairus heard that his daughter was dead, and Jesus told him, Fear not, believe only, and she shall be made whole.
LifeLesson: Bad news is not the last word when Jesus is on the way. Jairus believed past the point of hope.

Name: Jakeh
Summary: Jakeh was the father of Agur, named in the heading of Proverbs 30 as the author of its sayings is introduced.
KeyStory: Jakeh speaks no words of his own in Scripture; he is known only as Agur's father, preserved in the heading of his son's proverbs.
LifeLesson: A father's name preserved in Scripture is a quiet reminder that wisdom is passed down through generations.

Name: Jakim, Course Head
Summary: Twelfth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:12: Twelfth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
LifeLesson: The mention of Jakim in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Jakim, Son of Shimhi
Summary: Named among the sons of Shimhi in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:19: Named among the sons of Shimhi in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jakim stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jalon
Summary: Son of Ezra in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:17: Son of Ezra in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jalon stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jambres
Summary: Jambres is named in 2 Timothy with Jannes as one who withstood Moses, an example of men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith. Jewish tradition identifies Jambres and Jannes as magicians in Pharaoh's court, though Exodus itself does not name them.
KeyStory: Jambres is named in 2 Timothy with Jannes as one who withstood Moses, an example of men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith. Jewish tradition identifies Jambres and Jannes as magicians in Pharaoh's court, though Exodus itself does not name them.
LifeLesson: Truth withstands its opponents; their folly is made plain in time.

Name: James, Brother of Jesus
Summary: James, the brother of Jesus, did not believe during Jesus' ministry but became a pillar of the Jerusalem church after the resurrection. He presided at the Jerusalem Council and received Paul's report of his journeys.
KeyStory: James, once unbelieving, stood in Jerusalem and judged that Gentiles need not be circumcised to be saved.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Simon Peter; Paul; Mary, Mother of Jesus
LifeLesson: The brother who doubted became the brother who led. The resurrection changes families first.

Name: James, Brother of the Lord
Summary: James, the brother of the Lord, is named by Paul as one who saw the risen Christ and as a pillar of the Jerusalem church alongside Peter and John. He is traditionally identified as the author of the Epistle of James, and is distinct from James son of Zebedee and James son of Alphaeus.
KeyStory: James, the brother of the Lord, is named by Paul as one who saw the risen Christ and as a pillar of the Jerusalem church alongside Peter and John. He is traditionally identified as the author of the Epistle of James, and is distinct from James son of Zebedee and James son of Alphaeus.
RelatedPeople: Simon Peter; John the Apostle; Paul; Jude, Brother of James
LifeLesson: The brother who once doubted became a pillar; grace can turn family scepticism into steadfast faith.

Name: Jamin, Son of Ram
Summary: Son of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:27: Son of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jamin stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jamin, Son of Simeon
Summary: Son of Simeon, named among the sons of Simeon.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:24: Son of Simeon, named among the sons of Simeon.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jamin stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jamin the Levite
Summary: A Levite who taught the Law when Ezra read it; a different Jamin from Simeon's son in Genesis.
KeyStory: Ezra reads the law
LifeLesson: Understanding God's word is itself a ministry.

Name: Jamlech
Summary: Prince of Simeon named among those whose families increased greatly.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:34: Prince of Simeon named among those whose families increased greatly.
LifeLesson: The mention of Jamlech in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Jannes
Summary: Jannes is named in 2 Timothy with Jambres as one who withstood Moses, an example of men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith. Jewish tradition identifies Jannes and Jambres as magicians in Pharaoh's court, though Exodus itself does not name them.
KeyStory: Jannes is named in 2 Timothy with Jambres as one who withstood Moses, an example of men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith. Jewish tradition identifies Jannes and Jambres as magicians in Pharaoh's court, though Exodus itself does not name them.
LifeLesson: Resisting the truth, however learned, ends in folly made manifest to all.

Name: Japhia, Son of David
Summary: Japhia, son of David, was born at Jerusalem and named among the sons born to him there. He is distinct from Japhia, king of Lachish.
KeyStory: Japhia son of David was born at Jerusalem, sharing a name with a Canaanite king.
LifeLesson: A prince and a foreign king can share a name and nothing else.

Name: Japhlet
Summary: Son of Heber and father of Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:32: Son of Heber and father of Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Japhlet stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jaresiah
Summary: Named among the sons of Jeroham in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:27: Named among the sons of Jeroham in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jaresiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jarha
Summary: Egyptian servant of Sheshan who married Sheshan's daughter.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:34: Egyptian servant of Sheshan who married Sheshan's daughter.
LifeLesson: The mention of Jarha in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Jarib, Chief Man
Summary: A chief man sent by Ezra to Iddo at Casiphia to bring ministers for the house of God.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: Leaders are sent to find servants, not only to be served.

Name: Jarib, Son of Jeshua
Summary: Son of Jeshua named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Jarib
Summary: Son of Simeon, named among the sons of Simeon.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:24: Son of Simeon, named among the sons of Simeon.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jarib stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jaroah
Summary: Father of Huri in Gad's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:14: Father of Huri in Gad's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Jaroah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Jashub, Son of Issachar

LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jashub stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jashubi-lehem
