KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:4: Father of Shemaiah in Reuben's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Joel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Joel, Prince of Simeon
Summary: Prince of Simeon named among those whose families increased greatly.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:35: Prince of Simeon named among those whose families increased greatly.
LifeLesson: The mention of Joel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Joel, Son of Azariah
Summary: Joel, son of Azariah of the Kohathites, was one of the Levites who arose to cleanse the house of the LORD under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: The Levites arose, Mahath the son of Amasai and Joel the son of Azariah, of the sons of the Kohathites.
RelatedPeople: Azariah, Father of Joel; King Hezekiah
LifeLesson: Two Levites named together began eight days of cleansing.

Name: Joel, Son of Izrahiah
Summary: Son of Izrahiah, a chief man in Issachar's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:3: Son of Izrahiah, a chief man in Issachar's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Joel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Joel, Son of Jehiel
Summary: Brother of Zetham, over the treasures of the house of the LORD.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:22: Brother of Zetham, over the treasures of the house of the LORD.
LifeLesson: The mention of Joel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Joel, Son of Laadan
Summary: Son of Laadan, named with Jehiel and Zetham.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 23:8: Son of Laadan, named with Jehiel and Zetham.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Joel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Joel, Son of Nebo
Summary: Son of Nebo named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Joel, Son of Pedaiah
Summary: Son of Pedaiah, ruler of the half tribe of Manasseh.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:20: Son of Pedaiah, ruler of the half tribe of Manasseh.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Joel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Joel, Son of Samuel
Summary: Joel, Samuel's firstborn, was made a judge at Beersheba with his brother Abiah. Both turned aside after money, took bribes, and perverted judgment, and their corruption became Israel's excuse for demanding a king.
KeyStory: Joel's corrupt judgeship helped push Israel to ask for a king like the nations.
LifeLesson: A godly parent's children must choose faithfulness for themselves; a famous name is no substitute.

Name: Joel, Son of Zichri
Summary: Joel son of Zichri, named in Nehemiah 11:9.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Joel
Summary: Joel, son of Pethuel, prophesied to Judah, likely in the divided-monarchy period (his exact date is debated). Using a devastating locust plague as his picture, he called the people to repent and promised that God would pour out His Spirit on all flesh.
KeyStory: Joel saw locusts strip the land bare and called priests and people to a solemn fast and repentance, promising restoration and the outpouring of God's Spirit.
LifeLesson: When disaster strips everything bare, Joel's answer is not despair but return — rend your heart, not your garments, and God restores.

Name: Joelah
Summary: Son of Jeroham of Gedor who came to David at Ziklag.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:7: Son of Jeroham of Gedor who came to David at Ziklag.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Joelah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Joezer
Summary: One of those who came to David at Ziklag, of the Korhites.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:6: One of those who came to David at Ziklag, of the Korhites.
LifeLesson: The mention of Joezer in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Joha, Brother of Jediael
Summary: Brother of Jediael, son of Shimri the Tizite, one of David's mighty men.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:45: Brother of Jediael, son of Shimri the Tizite, one of David's mighty men.
LifeLesson: The mention of Joha in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Joha, Son of Beriah
Summary: Named among the sons of Beriah in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:16: Named among the sons of Beriah in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Joha stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Johanan, Captain of Gad
Summary: Eighth captain of the Gadites who separated themselves to David in the wilderness.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:12: Eighth captain of the Gadites who separated themselves to David in the wilderness.
LifeLesson: The mention of Johanan in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Johanan, Father of Azariah
Summary: Johanan was the father of Azariah, a head of Ephraim who opposed keeping Judah's captives.
KeyStory: Johanan is named only as the father of Azariah the son of Johanan.
LifeLesson: A head of Ephraim is traced to his father in a single line.

Name: Johanan, High Priest
Summary: Named in the succession of high priests from Jeshua to Jaddua.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: A long line ends where faithfulness continues.

Name: Johanan, Son of Azariah
Summary: Son of Azariah and priest in Aaron's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:9: Son of Azariah and priest in Aaron's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Johanan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Johanan, Son of Careah
Summary: Johanan, son of Careah, was one of the captains who came to Gedaliah at Mizpah and warned him against Ishmael's plot.
KeyStory: Johanan warns Gedaliah against Ishmael.
RelatedPeople: Gedaliah, Son of Ahikam; Careah, Father of Johanan; Ishmael, Son of Nethaniah
LifeLesson: A warning ignored is still a warning given: Johanan did his duty.

Name: Johanan, Son of Eliashib
Summary: A priest in whose chamber Ezra lodged while mourning the people's unfaithfulness; the chronicles of the Levites run to his days.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Mourning over sin sometimes needs a borrowed room.

Name: Johanan, Son of Elioenai
Summary: Son of Elioenai son of Neariah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:24: Son of Elioenai son of Neariah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Johanan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Johanan, Son of Hakkatan
Summary: Son of Hakkatan who returned with Ezra from Babylon.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: Returning to God's house is a family decision.

Name: Johanan, Son of Josiah
Summary: Firstborn son of Josiah, named among the sons of Josiah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:15: Firstborn son of Josiah, named among the sons of Josiah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Johanan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Johanan, Son of Kareah
Summary: Johanan, son of Kareah, was a captain who warned Gedaliah of Ishmael's plot, pursued Ishmael and recovered the captives after the murder, and then led the remnant to Egypt against Jeremiah's counsel, carrying Jeremiah and Baruch with them.
KeyStory: Johanan warned Gedaliah in secret, recovered the captives at Gibeon, then asked Jeremiah to pray — and when the answer was 'stay,' he led the people to Egypt anyway.
RelatedPeople: Gedaliah; Ishmael, Son of Nethaniah; Jeremiah; Azariah, Son of Hoshaiah; Baruch
LifeLesson: Asking God for guidance and then doing the opposite is worse than never asking.

Name: Johanan, Son of Tobiah
Summary: Son of Tobiah the Ammonite who married the daughter of Meshullam, binding Tobiah's house to Jerusalem's builders.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
RelatedPeople: Tobiah the Ammonite; Meshullam, Son of Berechiah
LifeLesson: Marriages can ally a household with either side of a wall.

Name: Johanan, Son of Ziklag Band
Summary: One of those who came to David at Ziklag.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:4: One of those who came to David at Ziklag.
LifeLesson: The mention of Johanan in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: John Mark
Summary: John Mark, surnamed Mark, was the son of Mary of Jerusalem, at whose house the church prayed for Peter. He travelled with Paul and Barnabas, left them at Perga, and later became the occasion of their sharp parting, before Paul again called him profitable for the ministry. Tradition identifies him as the author of Mark's Gospel. Also known as Mark, Cousin of Barnabas.
KeyStory: Mark left the first journey at Perga, split two apostles over his return, and was restored to usefulness in the end.
KeyVerses: Acts 12:12; Acts 15:37; Colossians 4:10; Philemon 1:24; 1 Peter 5:13; 2 Timothy 4:11
LifeLesson: A failed first journey is not a final verdict. Mark's restoration is hope for every quitter who returns.

Name: Joiada, Son of Eliashib
Summary: Son of Eliashib the high priest, named in the succession of high priests down to Jaddua.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
RelatedPeople: Eliashib the High Priest; Jonathan, Son of Joiada
LifeLesson: Priesthood passes from father to son, but faithfulness must be chosen anew.

Name: Joiakim, Son of Jeshua
Summary: High priest, son of Jeshua, in whose days the priests and Levites of Nehemiah 12 are listed.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Records keep a priesthood honest across generations.

Name: Joiarib, Chief Man
Summary: A chief man sent by Ezra to Iddo at Casiphia to bring ministers for the house of God.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: Leaders are sent to find servants, not only to be served.

Name: Joiarib, Father of Jedaiah
Summary: Father of Jedaiah the priest, and himself a priest in Zerubbabel's days.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: A father's name can open a son's story.

Name: Joiarib, Son of Zechariah
Summary: Joiarib son of Zechariah, named in Nehemiah 11:5.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Jokim
Summary: Named among the ancient men of Shelah's line who had dominion in Moab.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:22: Named among the ancient men of Shelah's line who had dominion in Moab.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jokim stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jonadab, Son of Shimeah
Summary: Jonadab, son of Shimeah, David's brother, was a very subtil man and Amnon's friend. He devised the trick by which Amnon lured Tamar into his chamber, and later assured David that only Amnon, not all his sons, had been slain.
KeyStory: Jonadab's clever plan put Tamar in Amnon's chamber — and his counsel was the crime's first step.
LifeLesson: Clever friends who plan another's sin share the guilt of it.

Name: Jonadab
Summary: Jonadab, son of Rechab, commanded his descendants to drink no wine, build no houses, sow no seed, and live in tents; generations later his sons still obeyed him, and Jeremiah held their obedience up against Judah's refusal to obey God.
KeyStory: Jonadab's command outlived him by centuries: his sons refused Jeremiah's wine in the temple because their father had forbidden it.
LifeLesson: A father's faithful command can echo for generations — and God notices when children keep it better than his own people keep his.

Name: Jonathan, Father of Ebed
Summary: Father of Ebed, who returned with Ezra; a different Jonathan from Saul's son.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: A father's name can open a son's story.

Name: Jonathan, of Melicu's Course
Summary: Head of Melicu's priestly course in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:14).
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Every course had a head, and every head is named.

Name: Jonathan, Son of Abiathar
Summary: Jonathan, son of Abiathar, served as a secret messenger for David during Absalom's revolt, carrying word from Jerusalem with Ahimaaz and hiding from Absalom's men.
KeyStory: Jonathan risked his life as a boy-messenger between Jerusalem and David's camp.
RelatedPeople: Abiathar, Son of Ahimelech; Ahimaaz, Son of Zadok; King David; Abiathar, Priest; Adonijah, Son of Haggith; King Solomon
LifeLesson: Young messengers in a civil war carry the kingdom on their feet.

Name: Jonathan, Son of Asahel
Summary: Son of Asahel who with Jahaziah stood against Ezra's plan to put away the foreign wives.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Even good plans meet honest opposition.

Name: Jonathan, Son of Gershom
Summary: Jonathan, son of Gershom, was the young Levite from Bethlehemjudah who became Micah's priest and then priest to the tribe of Dan, serving until the captivity. Judges 18:30 gives his line as 'son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh' in the KJV reading.
KeyStory: A young Levite wandering from Bethlehemjudah was hired by Micah for ten shekels a year, then went with the Danites to Laish, where he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the captivity.
LifeLesson: A priest for hire will serve whoever carries him off.

Name: Jonathan, Son of Jada
Summary: Son of Jada and father of Peleth and Zaza.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:32: Son of Jada and father of Peleth and Zaza.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jonathan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jonathan, Son of Joiada
Summary: Son of Joiada the high priest and father of Jaddua, named in the priestly succession.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
RelatedPeople: Joiada, Son of Eliashib; Jaddua, Son of Jonathan
LifeLesson: A long line ends where faithfulness continues.

Name: Jonathan, Son of Saul
Summary: Son of Saul, named among Saul's sons.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:33; 1 Chronicles 9:39; 1 Chronicles 10:2: Son of Saul, named among Saul's sons.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jonathan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jonathan, Son of Shage
Summary: Son of Shage the Hararite, one of David's mighty men.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:34: Son of Shage the Hararite, one of David's mighty men.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jonathan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jonathan, Son of Shammah
Summary: Jonathan, son of Shammah the Hararite, was among David's thirty mighty men. He is distinct from Jonathan son of Shimea, David's nephew, who slew the six-fingered giant.
KeyStory: Jonathan son of Shammah the Hararite stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: Two Jonathans fought for David — a mighty man and a giant-killer.

Name: Jonathan, Son of Shimea
Summary: Jonathan, son of Shimea, David's brother, slew a Philistine of great stature with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, who had defied Israel in the battle at Gath.
KeyStory: Jonathan, David's nephew, slew the six-fingered giant who defied Israel at Gath.
RelatedPeople: King David; Shimea, Son of Jesse
LifeLesson: Defiance answered by a nephew's sword — giants keep falling to David's house.

Name: Jonathan the Scribe
Summary: Jonathan the scribe owned the house that was made into a prison where Jeremiah was beaten and held for many days; Zedekiah later had Jeremiah brought from Jonathan's house and kept him in the prison court instead. He is a different man from Jonathan, son of Saul.
KeyStory: The princes put Jeremiah in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe, where he remained many days until the king moved him to the court of the prison.
LifeLesson: A scribe's house turned into a prison is a picture of what happens when law serves power instead of truth.

Name: Jonathan, Uncle of David
Summary: David's uncle, a counsellor, a wise man, and a scribe.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:32: David's uncle, a counsellor, a wise man, and a scribe.
LifeLesson: The mention of Jonathan in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Jorah
Summary: Head of a family listed among those who returned from exile.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: A family's return is recorded household by household.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Jorai
Summary: Named among the brethren of the house of Gad's fathers.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:13: Named among the brethren of the house of Gad's fathers.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jorai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Joram, Son of Jehoshaphat
Summary: Son of Jehoshaphat in the kingly line of Judah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:11: Son of Jehoshaphat in the kingly line of Judah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Joram stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Joram, Son of Jeshaiah
Summary: Son of Jeshaiah in the treasurers' line by Eliezer.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:25: Son of Jeshaiah in the treasurers' line by Eliezer.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Joram stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Joram, Son of Toi
Summary: Joram, son of Toi king of Hamath, was sent to David with vessels of silver, gold, and brass to salute him for defeating Hadadezer.
KeyStory: Joram carried his father's thank-offering to the king who had broken their common enemy.
RelatedPeople: Toi, King of Hamath; King David
LifeLesson: Gratitude carried by a son honours both fathers and kings.

Name: Josabad the Gederathite
Summary: One of those who came to David at Ziklag, called the Gederathite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:4: One of those who came to David at Ziklag, called the Gederathite.
LifeLesson: The mention of Josabad in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Joseph, of Shebaniah's Course
Summary: A priest of Shebaniah's course in the days of Joiakim.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Courses of priests kept their order across generations.

Name: Joseph, Son of Asaph
Summary: Son of Asaph who prophesied under the hands of Asaph, first lot for Asaph.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 25:2; 1 Chronicles 25:9: Son of Asaph who prophesied under the hands of Asaph, first lot for Asaph.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Joseph stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Joseph, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Sin named honestly is the first step back to God.

Name: Joses, Brother of Jesus
Summary: Joses was one of the brothers of Jesus named by the people of Nazareth, alongside James, Simon, and Judas. The Gospels record nothing further of him by name.
KeyStory: The people of Nazareth named Joses among Jesus' brothers and stumbled that the carpenter's family held no prophet.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; James, Brother of Jesus; Mary, Mother of Jesus
LifeLesson: Familiarity can blind us to glory. Nazareth knew Jesus' brothers and missed its Saviour.

Name: Joshah, Son of Amaziah
Summary: Son of Amaziah, prince of Simeon named among those whose families increased.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:34: Son of Amaziah, prince of Simeon named among those whose families increased.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Joshah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Joshaphat the Mithnite
Summary: Mighty man of David, called the Mithnite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:43: Mighty man of David, called the Mithnite.
LifeLesson: The mention of Joshaphat in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Joshaviah, Son of Elnaam
Summary: Son of Elnaam, one of David's mighty men.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:46: Son of Elnaam, one of David's mighty men.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Joshaviah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Joshbekashah, Son of Heman
Summary: Son of Heman the king's seer, seventeenth lot for song.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 25:4; 1 Chronicles 25:24: Son of Heman the king's seer, seventeenth lot for song.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Joshbekashah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Joshua, Governor of Jerusalem
Summary: Joshua, governor of the city, had a gate in Jerusalem where Josiah broke down the high places, from Geba to Beer-sheba.
KeyStory: Joshua's gate broken down by Josiah.
LifeLesson: Even a governor's gate could not shelter idolatry from Josiah's purge.

Name: Joshua of Beth-shemesh
Summary: Joshua of Beth-shemesh owned the field where the Philistines' cart stopped when the ark was returned. The ark was set down on a great stone in his field, and the men of Beth-shemesh offered sacrifices there.
KeyStory: The ark's return journey ended in Joshua's field, where Israel worshipped before the tragedy that followed.
LifeLesson: God's return to his people is cause for worship — and for reverence.

Name: Joshua, Son of Jehozadak
Summary: Joshua, son of Jehozadak, was the high priest of the returned exiles, working alongside Zerubbabel the governor and the prophets Haggai and Zechariah. Zechariah's visions show him standing before the LORD in filthy garments, cleansed and clothed anew — a picture of Israel's own restoration. He is a different man from Joshua son of Nun.
KeyStory: Joshua the high priest stood before the LORD in filthy garments, was cleansed and given a clean turban, and crowned with the hopes of the returning nation.
RelatedPeople: Haggai; Zechariah the Prophet; Zerubbabel; Jehozadak
LifeLesson: Joshua's filthy garments became clean ones — not by his scrubbing, but by God's word. Restoration is a gift, not an achievement.

Name: Josiah, Son of Zephaniah
Summary: Josiah, son of Zephaniah, was one of the exiles from Babylon who brought silver and gold to Jerusalem for the crowning of Joshua the high priest (Zechariah 6:10). He is NOT King Josiah of Judah, who lived two centuries earlier. Zechariah 6:14 names 'Hen the son of Zephaniah' in the same list, which may be the same man under a variant reading or the word for 'grace' — the entry keeps to the clear 6:10 identification.
KeyStory: Josiah son of Zephaniah, with Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, brought gifts from Babylon for the crown placed on Joshua's head.
LifeLesson: Josiah son of Zephaniah is a namesake warning: the famous king and this quiet exile share nothing but a name. Read the genealogy, not just the name.

Name: Josibiah
Summary: Father of Jehu, son of Seraiah son of Asiel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:35: Father of Jehu, son of Seraiah son of Asiel.
LifeLesson: The mention of Josibiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Josiphiah
Summary: Father of Shelomith, who returned with Ezra.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: A father's name can open a son's story.

Name: Jotham, King of Judah
Summary: Jotham governed Judah while his father Azariah lived apart as a leper, and reigned sixteen years doing right, though the high places were not removed.
KeyStory: Jotham governs for his leprous father and reigns in his stead.
KeyVerses: 2 Kings 15:32; 2 Kings 15:38; 2 Chronicles 27:1; 2 Chronicles 27:6; Isaiah 1:1; Isaiah 7:1; Hosea 1:1; Micah 1:1
RelatedPeople: Uzziah, King of Judah; Jerusha, Mother of Jotham; Ahaz, King of Judah; Jerushah, Daughter of Zadok; Isaiah
LifeLesson: Faithfulness in a supporting role is still faithfulness: Jotham served well before he ever wore the crown.

Name: Jotham, Son of Azariah
Summary: Son of Azariah in the kingly line of Judah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:12: Son of Azariah in the kingly line of Judah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jotham stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jotham, Son of Gideon
Summary: Jotham, Gideon's youngest son and the only brother to escape Abimelech's massacre, stood on Mount Gerizim and told the parable of the trees choosing a king, then fled to Beer.
KeyStory: Jotham alone hid from the slaughter at Ophrah, climbed Gerizim, and cried out the fable of the trees anointing the bramble — a warning Shechem ignored — then fled and dwelt in Beer.
LifeLesson: One survivor's parable outlived the king it warned against.

Name: Jotham, Son of Jahdai
Summary: Son of Jahdai, named in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:47: Son of Jahdai, named in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jotham stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Jozabad, Captain of Manasseh
Summary: Captain of the thousands of Manasseh who fell to David at Ziklag.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:20: Captain of the thousands of Manasseh who fell to David at Ziklag.
LifeLesson: The mention of Jozabad in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Jozabad, Chief of the Levites
Summary: Jozabad, a chief of the Levites, gave with Cononiah and the other chiefs five thousand small cattle and five hundred oxen for Josiah's Passover.
KeyStory: Hashabiah and Jeiel and Jozabad, chief of the Levites, gave unto the Levites for passover offerings.
RelatedPeople: Cononiah, Chief of the Levites; King Josiah
LifeLesson: Generosity among leaders fed a national feast.

Name: Jozabad, Overseer
Summary: Jozabad was one of the overseers under Cononiah and Shimei over the offerings and tithes under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Jozabad was one of the overseers under Cononiah and Shimei over the offerings and tithes under Hezekiah.
RelatedPeople: Cononiah, the Levite; Shimei, Brother of Cononiah; King Hezekiah; Azariah, Chief Priest
LifeLesson: Many overseers together kept one storehouse honest.

Name: Jozabad the Levite
Summary: A Levite who weighed the temple vessels, taught the Law, and oversaw the outward business of the house of God.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: Understanding God's word is itself a ministry.

Name: Jozabad the Priest
Summary: A priest named among those who had taken foreign wives.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Sin named honestly is the first step back to God.

Name: Jozachar, Son of Shimeath
Summary: Jozachar, son of Shimeath, with Jehozabad, conspired and slew King Joash in the house of Millo.
KeyStory: Jozachar slays Joash.
RelatedPeople: Joash, King of Judah; Shimeath, Mother of Jozachar; Jehozabad, Son of Shomer
LifeLesson: A king who turned from God was slain by the servants he had trusted.

Name: Jozadak
Role: Father of Jeshua the High Priest
Summary: Father of Jeshua the high priest, named in the return and temple-building accounts.
KeyStory: Rebuilding of the Temple
LifeLesson: Faithfulness in one generation prepares leaders in the next.
RelatedEvents: Rebuilding of the Temple; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Judah, Son of Senuah
Summary: Son of Senuah, second over the city of Jerusalem after the return; a different Judah from Jacob's son.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Oversight of the city is a trust, not a title.

Name: Judah the Levite
Summary: Levite named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:23), among the Levites who returned with Zerubbabel (Nehemiah 12:8), and among the musicians at the dedication of the wall (Nehemiah 12:33, 12:34, 12:36).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: A Levite who fell, returned, and sang: repentance restores service.

Name: Judas Barsabbas
Role: Prophet; Messenger of the Jerusalem Church
Summary: Judas Barsabbas was a leading man among the Jerusalem brethren and a prophet, sent with Silas to Antioch to confirm the Council's letter by word of mouth, exhorting and confirming the brethren. He is distinct from Judas Iscariot, Judas son of James, Judas brother of Jesus, and Judas of Galilee.
KeyStory: Judas Barsabbas carried the Council's letter to Antioch and stayed to exhort the brethren with many words.
LifeLesson: Letters need living voices. Judas Barsabbas carried a decision and a confirmation in the same journey.

Name: Judas, Brother of Jesus
Summary: Judas was one of the brothers of Jesus named by the people of Nazareth. He is distinct from Judas Iscariot, Judas son of James, Judas Barsabbas, and Judas of Galilee, and is traditionally identified with Jude, the author of the letter of Jude.
KeyStory: Nazareth named Judas among Jesus' brothers, one more familiar name that could not see the Messiah at home.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; James, Brother of Jesus; Mary, Mother of Jesus
LifeLesson: The family that grew up with Jesus had to learn to worship Him. Blood ties do not save; belief does.

Name: Judas of Galilee
Summary: Judas of Galilee rose in the days of the taxing and drew away many people after him, but he perished and his followers were dispersed. Gamaliel cited him alongside Theudas to counsel restraint toward the apostles.
KeyStory: Judas of Galilee rose at the taxing, drew many after him, and perished, and his followers scattered.
LifeLesson: Tax revolts and messianic claims both scatter in the end. Judas of Galilee is the caution beside Theudas.

Name: Judas, Son of James
Summary: Judas son of James was one of the twelve apostles, listed by Luke and in Acts. Matthew and Mark call him Thaddaeus, and Matthew adds the name Lebbaeus. At the Last Supper he asked Jesus why He would manifest Himself to the disciples and not to the world.
KeyStory: Thaddaeus asked the question every disciple wonders: Lord, why do You show Yourself to us and not to the world?
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Simon Peter; James, Son of Alphaeus
LifeLesson: A quiet apostle asked one honest question at the table. Jesus answered that love keeps His word, and the Father comes to dwell.

Name: Jude, Brother of James
Role: Servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James
Summary: Jude describes himself as the servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, and wrote his short letter urging believers to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints.
KeyStory: Jude describes himself as the servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, and wrote his short letter urging believers to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints.
LifeLesson: Contending for the faith is done as a servant, not as a master of it.

Name: Julia
Summary: Julia was a Christian woman in Rome greeted by Paul alongside Philologus, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas.
KeyStory: Julia was a Christian woman in Rome greeted by Paul alongside Philologus, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas.
LifeLesson: Women named in the greetings stood as full members of the early church.

Name: Junia
Summary: Junia was a kinswoman of Paul and a fellowprisoner, described as of note among the apostles and in Christ before Paul himself.
KeyStory: Junia was a kinswoman of Paul and a fellowprisoner, described as of note among the apostles and in Christ before Paul himself.
LifeLesson: Suffering for Christ alongside others, even in prison, is a mark of honour in the gospel.

Name: Jushab-hesed
Summary: Named among the sons of Zerubbabel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:20: Named among the sons of Zerubbabel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Jushab-hesed stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Justus of Corinth
Summary: Justus was a man at Corinth who worshipped God, whose house joined hard to the synagogue. Paul left the synagogue and preached next door at Justus' house after the Jews opposed him. He is distinct from Joseph Barsabbas, also called Justus.
KeyStory: Paul moved next door to the synagogue, into the house of Justus, and the church met at the wall between.
LifeLesson: When one door closes, the house next door opens. Justus' wall adjoined the synagogue and held the gospel.

Name: Kadmiel
Summary: A Levite who oversaw the temple work, taught the Law, and sealed the covenant.
KeyStory: Return from exile
KeyVerses: Ezra 2:40; Ezra 3:9; Nehemiah 7:43; Nehemiah 9:4; Nehemiah 10:9; Nehemiah 12:8
LifeLesson: Steady service in worship and in teaching holds a community together.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile; Rebuilding of the Temple; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Kallai
Summary: Priest in the days of Joiakim.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Courses of priests kept worship ordered across generations.

Name: Keilah
Summary: Named as the father of Keilah the Garmite in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:19: Named as the father of Keilah the Garmite in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Keilah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Kelita
Summary: Son of Levites named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Kemuel, Father of Hashabiah
Summary: Father of Hashabiah the ruler of the Levites.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:17: Father of Hashabiah the ruler of the Levites.
LifeLesson: The mention of Kemuel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Kenaz, Father of Othniel
Summary: Kenaz is named only as the father of Othniel, Israel's first judge, and as the brother of Caleb. He is distinct from Kenaz, son of Eliphaz, in Genesis.
KeyStory: Kenaz appears as Othniel's father when Othniel takes Kirjath-sepher and marries Achsah, and again when Othniel becomes judge.
LifeLesson: The first judge's father is remembered in two verses.

Name: Kenaz, Son of Elah
Summary: Son of Elah son of Caleb.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:15: Son of Elah son of Caleb.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Kenaz stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Keren-happuch
Summary: Keren-happuch was Job's youngest daughter after his restoration, named in Job 42 among the three daughters born when God restored Job's fortunes.
KeyStory: With her sisters, Keren-happuch was counted among the fairest women in the land, and Job gave her an inheritance among her brothers.
LifeLesson: Keren-happuch's story closes Job's book with beauty after ashes — suffering was not the end of Job's story.

Name: Keros
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Kezia
Summary: Kezia was Job's second daughter after his restoration, named in Job 42 among the three daughters born when God restored Job's fortunes.
KeyStory: With her sisters Jemima and Keren-happuch, Kezia received an inheritance from her father alongside her brothers — an unusual honour in that time.
LifeLesson: Kezia's inheritance shows that restoration in God's hands can include dignity and honour beyond mere replacement.

Name: Kish, Ancestor of Mordecai
Summary: Benjamite ancestor of Mordecai, named in his genealogy; a different Kish from Saul's father.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: Exile does not erase a family's line.

Name: Kish, Son of Abdi
Summary: Kish, son of Abdi of the sons of Merari, was one of the Levites who arose to cleanse the house of the LORD under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Of the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi and Azariah the son of Jehalelel arose to cleanse the house.
RelatedPeople: Abdi, Father of Kish; King Hezekiah
LifeLesson: Merarites as well as Kohathites shared the cleansing work.

Name: Kish, Son of Abiel
Summary: Kish, son of Abiel, was a mighty man of power from Benjamin. His lost donkeys sent Saul searching, and that search led Saul to Samuel and to the throne.
KeyStory: Kish's lost donkeys set in motion the day his son was anointed king.
RelatedPeople: King Saul; Ner, Son of Abiel; Abiel
LifeLesson: God often steers a life through the most ordinary errand.

Name: Kish, Son of Jehiel
Summary: Son of Jehiel the father of Gibeon.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:30; 1 Chronicles 9:36: Son of Jehiel the father of Gibeon.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Kish stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Kish, Son of Mahli
Summary: Son of Mahli, whose sons took the daughters of Eleazar.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 23:21: Son of Mahli, whose sons took the daughters of Eleazar.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Kish stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Kish, Son of Ner
Summary: Son of Ner and father of Saul.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:33; 1 Chronicles 9:39: Son of Ner and father of Saul.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Kish stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Kishi
Summary: Father of Ethan the Merarite singer, also called Kushaiah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:44: Father of Ethan the Merarite singer, also called Kushaiah.
LifeLesson: The mention of Kishi in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Kolaiah, Son of Maaseiah
Summary: Kolaiah son of Maaseiah, named in Nehemiah 11:7.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Korah, Son of Hebron
Summary: Son of Hebron son of Mareshah, named in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:43: Son of Hebron son of Mareshah, named in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Korah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Kore, Father of Shallum
Summary: Father of Shallum the porter, son of Ebiasaph son of Korah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:19: Father of Shallum the porter, son of Ebiasaph son of Korah.
LifeLesson: The mention of Kore in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Kore, Son of Asaph
Summary: Father of Meshelemiah the porter, of the sons of Asaph.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:1: Father of Meshelemiah the porter, of the sons of Asaph.
LifeLesson: The mention of Kore in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Kore, Son of Imnah
Summary: Kore, son of Imnah the Levite and porter toward the east, was over the freewill offerings of God, distributing the oblations of the LORD and the most holy things.
KeyStory: Kore the son of Imnah the Levite, porter toward the east, was over the freewill offerings to distribute them.
RelatedPeople: Imnah, Father of Kore; King Hezekiah
LifeLesson: A gatekeeper's faithfulness extended to distributing God's gifts.

Name: Koz
Summary: Head of a priestly family that could not prove its genealogy on returning, and ancestor of the Koz (Hakkoz) line to which Meremoth's father Urijah belonged.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Even an unproven genealogy is still recorded.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Laadah
Summary: Son of Shelah son of Judah, called the father of Mareshah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:21: Son of Shelah son of Judah, called the father of Mareshah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Laadah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Laadan, Son of Gershon
Summary: Gershonite named among the sons of Levi in David's divisions.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 23:7: Gershonite named among the sons of Levi in David's divisions.
LifeLesson: The mention of Laadan in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Laadan, Son of Tahan
Summary: Son of Tahan and father of Ammihud in Ephraim's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:26: Son of Tahan and father of Ammihud in Ephraim's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Laadan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Lahad
Summary: Son of Jahath, named among the families of the Zorathites.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:2: Son of Jahath, named among the families of the Zorathites.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Lahad stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Lahmi
Summary: Brother of Goliath the Gittite, slain by Elhanan son of Jair.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 20:5: Brother of Goliath the Gittite, slain by Elhanan son of Jair.
LifeLesson: The mention of Lahmi in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Laish, Father of Palti
Summary: Laish of Gallim is named as the father of Phalti, to whom Saul gave Michal (called Phaltiel in 2 Samuel 3:15) after taking her from David.
KeyStory: Laish's son became a pawn in Saul's struggle against David.
LifeLesson: A father's name survives in his son's story, even a sorrowful one.

Name: Lapidoth, Husband of Deborah
Summary: Lapidoth is named only as the husband of Deborah, the prophetess and judge.
KeyStory: Lapidoth appears in Judges only as the husband of Deborah, who judged Israel under the palm tree between Ramah and Bethel.
LifeLesson: Standing beside a great calling is itself a place in the story.

Name: Lebanah
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Lemuel
Summary: Lemuel was a king whose words make up Proverbs 31, recording the teaching his mother gave him — including the famous portrait of the virtuous woman.
KeyStory: King Lemuel's oracle warns kings against wine and injustice, and praises the woman who fears the Lord, whose worth is far above rubies.
LifeLesson: Lemuel shows that the best royal wisdom is often learned at home — a mother's teaching, kept and passed on.

Name: Libni, Son of Gershom
Summary: Son of Gershom, named among the sons of Gershom.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:17: Son of Gershom, named among the sons of Gershom.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Libni stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Libni, Son of Mahli
Summary: Son of Mahli and father of Shimei in Merari's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:29: Son of Mahli and father of Shimei in Merari's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Libni stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Likhi
Summary: Son of Shemidah, named among the sons of Shemidah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:19: Son of Shemidah, named among the sons of Shemidah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Likhi stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Linus
Summary: Linus was one of the believers with Paul in Rome who sends greetings in 2 Timothy, alongside Eubulus, Pudens, and Claudia.
KeyStory: Linus was one of the believers with Paul in Rome who sends greetings in 2 Timothy, alongside Eubulus, Pudens, and Claudia.
LifeLesson: Standing by in the last days of a ministry is faithfulness to the end.

Name: Lo-Ammi
Summary: Lo-Ammi (KJV 'Lo-ammi'), son of Hosea and Gomer, was named by God as a sign: his name means 'not my people,' declaring that Israel had broken covenant so deeply that God would disown them as His people — a judgment later reversed in the promise that they would be called sons of the living God.
KeyStory: God named Hosea's son Lo-Ammi — 'not my people' — the hardest of the three sign-names, announcing the breaking of the covenant bond.
LifeLesson: Lo-Ammi's name is the darkest sentence in Hosea — and the reason the book's ending shines: the God who says 'not my people' also promises to say 'my people' again.

Name: Lo-Ruhamah
Summary: Lo-Ruhamah (KJV 'Lo-ruhamah'), daughter of Hosea and Gomer, was named by God as a sign: her name means 'not pitied' or 'no mercy,' declaring that God would no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, though He would still have mercy on Judah.
KeyStory: God named Hosea's daughter Lo-Ruhamah — 'not pitied' — as a living sign that His patience with Israel's idolatry had run out.
LifeLesson: Mercy refused long enough becomes judgment pronounced. Lo-Ruhamah's name is a sobering reminder that God's patience, though long, is not endless.

Name: Lois
Summary: Lois was Timothy's grandmother, whose unfeigned faith Paul says dwelt first in her, then in Eunice, and then in Timothy.
KeyStory: Lois was Timothy's grandmother, whose unfeigned faith Paul says dwelt first in her, then in Eunice, and then in Timothy.
LifeLesson: Faith passed from grandmother to mother to child is a chain of grace across generations.

Name: Lucius, Kinsman of Paul
Summary: Lucius was a kinsman of Paul who sends greetings in Romans 16. He is listed separately from Lucius of Cyrene, since the letter does not identify them as the same man.
KeyStory: Lucius was a kinsman of Paul who sends greetings in Romans 16. He is listed separately from Lucius of Cyrene, since the letter does not identify them as the same man.
LifeLesson: Kinship in Christ turns family into fellow workers.

Name: Lucius of Cyrene
Summary: Lucius of Cyrene was among the prophets and teachers at Antioch who, as they ministered and fasted, heard the Spirit set apart Barnabas and Saul for the work of the Gentile mission.
KeyStory: Lucius stood among the Antioch teachers when the Spirit said, Separate Barnabas and Saul for the work.
LifeLesson: Mission begins in worship, not in planning. Lucius fasted with the church that sent the first missionaries.

Name: Luke
Summary: Luke, called the beloved physician, travelled and laboured with Paul, is named in Colossians and Philemon, and was the only companion still with Paul near the end of 2 Timothy. Tradition identifies him as the author of the Gospel of Luke and Acts.
KeyStory: Luke, called the beloved physician, travelled and laboured with Paul, is named in Colossians and Philemon, and was the only companion still with Paul near the end of 2 Timothy. Tradition identifies him as the author of the Gospel of Luke and Acts.
LifeLesson: Staying with a servant of God to the end is a quiet, costly faithfulness.

Name: Lysanias
Summary: Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene when John the Baptist began his ministry. Luke names him alongside the other rulers of that year to date the coming of God's word to John.
KeyStory: Luke lists Lysanias among the rulers of the year John began preaching in the wilderness.
LifeLesson: Even a ruler known only from one verse has his place in God's dated story. No detail of Luke's history is filler.

Name: Maacah, Daughter of Talmai
Summary: Maacah, daughter of Talmai king of Geshur, was David's wife and the mother of Absalom and Tamar.
KeyStory: Maacah's marriage joined David's house to Geshur — and her son nearly tore it apart.
RelatedPeople: King David; Absalom; Tamar, Daughter of David; Talmai, King of Geshur
LifeLesson: A royal marriage can plant both alliance and rebellion in one house.

Name: Maachah, Concubine of Caleb
Summary: Concubine of Caleb who bore Sheber, Tirhanah, and Shaaph.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:48: Concubine of Caleb who bore Sheber, Tirhanah, and Shaaph.
LifeLesson: The mention of Maachah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Maachah, Daughter of Absalom
Summary: Maachah, daughter of Absalom, was Rehoboam's favoured wife and mother of Abijah; Asa later removed her from being queen because she had made an idol in a grove. Also known as Maachah, Queen Mother.
KeyStory: Rehoboam loved Maachah above all his wives, made her son Abijah chief among his brethren, and years later Asa cut down and burnt her idol at the brook Kidron.
RelatedPeople: Rehoboam; Absalom; Abijah, King of Judah; King Asa; Abijam, King of Judah
LifeLesson: Favour in a palace is no shelter from God's judgment on idolatry, even for a queen mother.

Name: Maachah, Wife of Jehiel
Summary: Wife of Jehiel the father of Gibeon.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:29; 1 Chronicles 9:35: Wife of Jehiel the father of Gibeon.
LifeLesson: The mention of Maachah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Maachah, Wife of Machir
Summary: Wife of Machir who bore Peresh, and sister of Huppim and Shuppim.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:15; 1 Chronicles 7:16: Wife of Machir who bore Peresh, and sister of Huppim and Shuppim.
LifeLesson: The mention of Maachah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Maadai, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:34).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Reform begins with named obedience.

Name: Maadiah
Summary: Priest who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Priests restored worship before walls were rebuilt.

Name: Maai
Summary: Musician at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Music marks the moment a long work is finished.

Name: Maaseiah, Governor of the City
Summary: Maaseiah, governor of the city, was sent by Josiah with Shaphan and Joah to repair the house of the LORD.
KeyStory: Josiah sent Shaphan, Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah the recorder, to repair the house of the LORD.
RelatedPeople: King Josiah; Shaphan, Son of Azaliah
LifeLesson: City government joined the work of repairing God's house.

Name: Maaseiah, Singer
Summary: Levite of the second degree appointed to sing with psalteries on Alamoth at the bringing up of the ark.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:18; 1 Chronicles 15:20: Levite of the second degree appointed to sing with psalteries on Alamoth at the bringing up of the ark.
LifeLesson: The mention of Maaseiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Maaseiah, Son of Adaiah
Summary: Maaseiah, son of Adaiah, was one of the captains of hundreds Jehoiada took into covenant to crown Joash.
KeyStory: Jehoiada took Maaseiah the son of Adaiah into covenant with him.
RelatedPeople: Jehoiada, the Priest; Adaiah, Father of Maaseiah
LifeLesson: A covenant kept in secret became a coronation in public.

Name: Maaseiah, Son of Ahaz
Summary: Maaseiah, the king's son, was slain by Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, in Pekah's invasion of Judah.
KeyStory: Zichri slew Maaseiah the king's son, and Azrikam the governor of the house, and Elkanah next to the king.
RelatedPeople: Ahaz, King of Judah; Zichri, Man of Ephraim
LifeLesson: A king's idolatry cost even his own son's life.

Name: Maaseiah, Son of Ananiah
Summary: Father of Azariah the wall builder, son of Ananiah (Nehemiah 3:23).
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: A father's name stands behind his son's section of wall.

Name: Maaseiah, Son of Baruch
Summary: Maaseiah son of Baruch, named in Nehemiah 11:5.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Maaseiah, Son of Harim
Summary: Son of Harim named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Maaseiah, Son of Ithiel
Summary: Maaseiah son of Ithiel, named in Nehemiah 11:7.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Maaseiah, Son of Jeshua
Summary: Son of Jeshua named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Maaseiah, Son of Pahath-moab
Summary: Son of Pahath-moab named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Maaseiah, Son of Pashur
Summary: Son of Pashur named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Maaseiah, Son of Shallum
Summary: Maaseiah, son of Shallum, was keeper of the door of the temple; the chamber of the sons of Hanan was by the chamber of the princes above his chamber, where Jeremiah tested the Rechabites.
KeyStory: Jeremiah brought the Rechabites into the chamber of the sons of Hanan, above the chamber of Maaseiah the keeper of the door, and set wine before them.
RelatedPeople: Zephaniah, Son of Maaseiah; Hanan, Son of Igdaliah
LifeLesson: Even a doorkeeper's chamber can become the room where faithfulness is tested.

Name: Maaseiah, the Ruler
Summary: Maaseiah the ruler, with Jeiel the scribe under Hananiah, numbered Uzziah's army for war.
KeyStory: The host went out by bands by the hand of Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the ruler, under Hananiah.
RelatedPeople: Uzziah, King of Judah; Jeiel, the Scribe
LifeLesson: Order in an army begins with faithful record-keepers.

Name: Maaseiah
Summary: Priest who stood beside Ezra at the reading of the law, taught the people, and sang and played at the dedication of the wall (Nehemiah 8:4, 8:7, 12:41, 12:42).
KeyStory: Ezra reads the law
LifeLesson: From hearing the law to teaching it to celebrating it.
RelatedEvents: Ezra Reads the Law; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Maasiai, Son of Adiel
Summary: Son of Adiel son of Jahzerah son of Meshullam son of Meshillemith son of Immer, priest dwelling in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:12: Son of Adiel son of Jahzerah son of Meshullam son of Meshillemith son of Immer, priest dwelling in Jerusalem.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Maasiai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Maaz
Summary: Son of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:27: Son of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Maaz stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Maaziah
Summary: Four and twentieth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:18: Four and twentieth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
LifeLesson: The mention of Maaziah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Machbanai
Summary: Eleventh captain of the Gadites who separated themselves to David in the wilderness.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:13: Eleventh captain of the Gadites who separated themselves to David in the wilderness.
LifeLesson: The mention of Machbanai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Machir, Son of Ammiel
Summary: Machir, son of Ammiel of Lo-debar, had sheltered Mephibosheth, Jonathan's lame son, in his house. He later brought provisions to David at Mahanaim during Absalom's revolt.
KeyStory: Machir sheltered Jonathan's son in Lo-debar, then fed David at Mahanaim.
RelatedPeople: Mephibosheth, Son of Jonathan; King David; Ammiel, Father of Machir
LifeLesson: The man who shelters the forgotten is ready to feed the king.

Name: Machnadebai, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:40).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Every name on the list was a person who had to choose.

Name: Magpiash
Summary: Chief who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10).
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: A signature on a covenant is a public stand.

Name: Mahalah, Daughter of Hammoleketh
Summary: Daughter of Hammoleketh, named in Manasseh's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:18: Daughter of Hammoleketh, named in Manasseh's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mahalah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mahalath, Daughter of Jerimoth
Summary: Mahalath, daughter of Jerimoth son of David, was a wife of Rehoboam and bore him Jeush, Shamariah and Zaham.
KeyStory: Mahalath bore Rehoboam three children: Jeush, Shamariah and Zaham.
RelatedPeople: Rehoboam; Jerimoth, Son of David; Jeush, Son of Rehoboam
LifeLesson: Royal marriages wove David's house together, for better and for worse.

Name: Maharai the Netophathite
Summary: Maharai the Netophathite was among David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Maharai the Netophathite stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: Netophah's son stood in the king's thirty.

Name: Mahath, Overseer
Summary: Mahath was one of the overseers under Cononiah and Shimei over the offerings and tithes under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Mahath was one of the overseers under Cononiah and Shimei over the offerings and tithes under Hezekiah.
RelatedPeople: Cononiah, the Levite; Shimei, Brother of Cononiah; King Hezekiah; Azariah, Chief Priest
LifeLesson: Many overseers together kept one storehouse honest.

Name: Mahath, Son of Amasai
Summary: Mahath, son of Amasai of the Kohathites, was one of the Levites who arose to cleanse the house of the LORD under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: The Levites arose, Mahath the son of Amasai and Joel the son of Azariah, of the sons of the Kohathites, to cleanse the house.
RelatedPeople: Amasai, Father of Mahath; King Hezekiah
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mahath stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mahazioth, Son of Heman
Summary: Son of Heman the king's seer, three and twentieth lot for song.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 25:4; 1 Chronicles 25:30: Son of Heman the king's seer, three and twentieth lot for song.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mahazioth stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Maher-shalal-hash-baz
Summary: Maher-shalal-hash-baz, whose name means 'swift to the spoil, hasty to the prey,' was Isaiah's son, named by God's command as a sign that Assyria would soon plunder Damascus and Samaria.
KeyStory: Before the child could cry 'my father' or 'my mother,' the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria would be taken away before the king of Assyria.
LifeLesson: God's signs can be uncomfortable — this child's name announced judgment, not comfort.

Name: Mahli, Son of Levi
Summary: Mahli son of Levi, named in Ezra 8:18.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Mahli, Son of Merari
Summary: Son of Merari, named among the sons of Merari.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:19: Son of Merari, named among the sons of Merari.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mahli stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mahli, Son of Mushi
Summary: Son of Mushi, named among the sons of Mushi.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 23:23: Son of Mushi, named among the sons of Mushi.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mahli stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mahli
Summary: Ancestor of the Levites brought from Casiphia, named as the house of Mahli, son of Levi, from which Sherebiah came.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: God provides workers when his people ask.

Name: Mahlon, Son of Elimelech
Summary: Mahlon, son of Elimelech and Naomi, died in Moab after marrying Ruth; his widow's marriage to Boaz restored his family's name and land.
KeyStory: Mahlon went with his family to Moab in the famine, married Ruth, and died there, leaving his mother a widow and his name to be raised up by Boaz.
RelatedPeople: Elimelech; Naomi; Ruth; Chilion, Son of Elimelech
LifeLesson: A man who died young in a foreign field lived on through the kinsman who married his widow.

Name: Mahol, Father of Chalcol and Darda
Summary: Mahol was the father of Chalcol and Darda, named among the wise men compared with Solomon.
KeyStory: Mahol, father of Chalcol and Darda.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Malachi
Summary: Malachi, whose name means 'my messenger,' was the last of the Old Testament prophets, ministering to post-exile Judah around 460–430 BC (the exact date is debated). He confronted a weary, half-hearted people — corrupt priests, broken covenants, withheld tithes — and promised the coming messenger and the Sun of Righteousness, closing the Old Testament with a call to remember Moses and expect Elijah.
KeyStory: Malachi charged Judah's priests and people with robbing God and dishonouring His name, then promised a refining messenger and Elijah before the great day of the LORD.
LifeLesson: Half-hearted worship wearies God more than honest struggle does. Bring Him your best, not your leftovers — and watch for the Messenger He promised.

Name: Malcham
Summary: Son of Shaharaim by Hodesh.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:9: Son of Shaharaim by Hodesh.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Malcham stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Malchi-shua, Son of Saul
Summary: Malchi-shua, spelled Melchi-shua in 1 Samuel 14, was a son of Saul who died with his father and brothers on Mount Gilboa.
KeyStory: Malchi-shua died beside his father on the day Israel's first kingdom fell.
RelatedPeople: King Saul; Jonathan; Abinadab, Son of Saul
LifeLesson: A dynasty's fall sweeps up sons who never chose the throne.

Name: Malchiah, Father of Pashur
Summary: Father of Pashur, in the Jerusalem priestly line (Nehemiah 11:12).
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Priestly lines in Jerusalem ran father to son.

Name: Malchiah, Son of Ethni
Summary: Son of Ethni and father of Baaseiah in Asaph's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:40: Son of Ethni and father of Baaseiah in Asaph's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Malchiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Malchiah, Son of Harim
Summary: Son of Harim named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Malchiah, Son of Parosh
Summary: Son of Parosh named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Malchiah, Son of Rechab
Summary: Son of Rechab, ruler of Beth-haccerem, who repaired the dung gate and its wall (Nehemiah 3:14).
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: No part of the work is beneath a ruler's hands.

Name: Malchiah the Goldsmith's Son
Summary: Son of a goldsmith who repaired a section of the wall to the house of the Nethinim (Nehemiah 3:31).
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: A craftsman's skill serves God's city too.

Name: Malchiah
Summary: Malchiah, son of Hammelech, owned the dungeon in the prison court into which Jeremiah was let down with cords until he sank in the mire.
KeyStory: Jeremiah was let down with cords into the dungeon of Malchiah the king's son, where there was no water but mire, and he sank in the mire.
LifeLesson: A dungeon with an owner's name attached to it reminds us that cruelty is always somebody's property.
RelatedEvents: Ezra Reads the Law; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Malchiel, Son of Beriah
Summary: Son of Beriah and father of Birzavith.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:31: Son of Beriah and father of Birzavith.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Malchiel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Malchijah, Course Head
Summary: Fifth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:9: Fifth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Malchijah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Malchijah, Father of Pashur
Summary: Father of Pashur in the Jerusalem priest list.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:12: Father of Pashur in the Jerusalem priest list.
LifeLesson: The mention of Malchijah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Malchijah, Son of Harim
Summary: Son of Harim who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3:11).
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: A repaired wall is a repaired community.

Name: Malchijah, Son of Parosh
Summary: Son of Parosh named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Malchijah
Summary: Priest who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah 10 (Nehemiah 10:3).
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: A priest's signature binds him to the people's promise.

Name: Malchiram
Summary: Son of Jeconiah, named in the post-exilic royal line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:18: Son of Jeconiah, named in the post-exilic royal line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Malchiram stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Malchus
Summary: Malchus was the high priest's servant whose right ear Peter cut off with a sword in Gethsemane. Jesus healed the wound, rebuking the sword and the arrest.
KeyStory: Malchus came to arrest Jesus and left healed by Him, the last miracle before the cross.
LifeLesson: Jesus healed the man who came to arrest Him. His mercy reaches the very hands raised against Him.

Name: Mallothi, Son of Heman
Summary: Son of Heman the king's seer, nineteenth lot for song.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 25:4; 1 Chronicles 25:26: Son of Heman the king's seer, nineteenth lot for song.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mallothi stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Malluch, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:29).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Two men named Malluch made two separate choices.

Name: Malluch, Son of Harim
Summary: Son of Harim named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:32).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: A shared name is not a shared record.

Name: Malluch the Chief
Summary: Chief who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:27). Not Malluch the priest.
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: Sealing a covenant is a chief's public stand.

Name: Malluch
Summary: Father of Abdi in Ethan's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:44: Father of Abdi in Ethan's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Malluch in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Manaen
Summary: Manaen was among the prophets and teachers at Antioch, and had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch. He shared in the worship from which Barnabas and Saul were sent to the Gentiles.
KeyStory: Manaen grew up with Herod and ended up sending missionaries to the nations Herod's family feared.
LifeLesson: Upbringing does not fix a destiny. Manaen left Herod's court for the church's sending.

Name: Manasseh, King of Judah
Summary: Manasseh reigned fifty-five years, rebuilt the high places his father had removed, set idols in the temple, and shed innocent blood, filling Jerusalem with evil that hastened Judah's judgment.
KeyStory: Manasseh's long idolatrous reign.
KeyVerses: 2 Kings 21:1; 2 Kings 21:18; Jeremiah 15:4; 1 Chronicles 3:13; 2 Chronicles 33:1; 2 Chronicles 33:12; 2 Chronicles 33:15
RelatedPeople: King Hezekiah; Hephzibah, Mother of Manasseh; Amon, King of Judah; King Josiah
LifeLesson: A father's faith is not inherited: Hezekiah's son undid his father's reforms in a single reign.

Name: Manasseh, Son of Hashum
Summary: Son of Hashum named among those who had taken foreign wives; a different Manasseh from Joseph's son.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Sin named honestly is the first step back to God.

Name: Manasseh, Son of Pahath-moab
Summary: Son of Pahath-moab named among those who had taken foreign wives; a different Manasseh from Joseph's son.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Sin named honestly is the first step back to God.

Name: Manoah, Father of Samson
Summary: Manoah of Zorah, a Danite, was Samson's father; he and his wife received the angel's announcement of Samson's birth and offered a sacrifice, and Manoah later went with Samson to Timnath.
KeyStory: Manoah prayed to see the man of God again, offered a kid and an offering on the rock, watched the angel ascend in the flame, and afterwards accompanied Samson to Timnath.
LifeLesson: Manoah feared he would die for seeing God — and learned that God's message was life, not death.

Name: Maoch
Role: King of Gath; Father of Achish
Summary: Maoch was king of Gath before his son Achish, in whose reign David twice sought refuge among the Philistines.
KeyStory: Maoch's son inherited a throne that would shelter Israel's future king.
RelatedPeople: Achish, Son of Maoch; King David
LifeLesson: A father's throne can become, unknowingly, a refuge for God's purposes.

Name: Maon, Son of Shammai
Summary: Son of Shammai, called the father of Beth-zur.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:45: Son of Shammai, called the father of Beth-zur.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Maon stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mareshah, Father of Hebron
Summary: Named as the father of Hebron in the Caleb line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:42: Named as the father of Hebron in the Caleb line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Mareshah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Marsena
Summary: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media who saw the king's face.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: Counsel near the throne carries weight for a kingdom.

Name: Mary, Mother of James and Joses
Role: Disciple; Witness of the Crucifixion and Resurrection
Summary: Mary, the mother of James and Joses, followed Jesus and watched His crucifixion and burial. She came to the tomb on the first day of the week. She is traditionally identified with Mary the wife of Clopas named in John's Gospel, though the texts give the two descriptions separately.
KeyStory: This Mary stood at the cross, watched where He was laid, and returned to anoint a body that was already risen.
LifeLesson: She watched the burial and still came to serve. Love does not wait for proof before it shows up.

Name: Mary of Rome
Summary: Mary was a Christian woman in Rome whom Paul greets in Romans 16:6 for bestowing much labour on the apostles. She is distinct from Mary, the mother of Jesus.
KeyStory: Mary was a Christian woman in Rome whom Paul greets in Romans 16:6 for bestowing much labour on the apostles. She is distinct from Mary, the mother of Jesus.
LifeLesson: Quiet, hard labour for the Lord is seen and remembered, even when history records only a name.

Name: Mattan, Priest of Baal
Summary: Mattan, priest of Baal, was slain before the altars when Jehoiada's purge broke down Baal's house and altars in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Mattan slain in Jehoiada's purge.
RelatedPeople: Jehoiada, High Priest; Athaliah; Joash, King of Judah; Jehoiada, the Priest
LifeLesson: Baal's priest fell with Baal's house the day the true king was crowned.

Name: Mattaniah, Ancestor of Jahaziel
Role: Levite of the Sons of Asaph
Summary: Mattaniah was the ancestor in Jahaziel's line: Jahaziel son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph.
KeyStory: Mattaniah is named only at the head of the line given when the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel.
RelatedPeople: Jahaziel, Son of Zechariah; Jeiel, Son of Mattaniah
LifeLesson: God's Spirit came to a man rooted in a long line of singers.

Name: Mattaniah, Son of Asaph
Summary: Mattaniah, of the sons of Asaph, was one of the Levites who arose to cleanse the house of the LORD under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Of the sons of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah arose to cleanse the house.
RelatedPeople: Zechariah, Son of Asaph; King Hezekiah; Asaph
LifeLesson: Singers and cleansers were the same Levites.

Name: Mattaniah, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:37).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: The reform named names because repentance is personal.

Name: Mattaniah, Son of Elam
Summary: Son of Elam named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Mattaniah, Son of Heman
Summary: Son of Heman the king's seer, ninth lot for song.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 25:4; 1 Chronicles 25:16: Son of Heman the king's seer, ninth lot for song.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mattaniah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mattaniah, Son of Micah
Summary: Son of Micah son of Zichri son of Asaph, Levite dwelling in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:15: Son of Micah son of Zichri son of Asaph, Levite dwelling in Jerusalem.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mattaniah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mattaniah, Son of Micha
Summary: Mattaniah son of Micha, named in Nehemiah 11:17.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Mattaniah, Son of Michaiah
Summary: Mattaniah son of Michaiah, named in Nehemiah 12:35.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Mattaniah, Son of Pahath-moab
Summary: Son of Pahath-moab named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Mattaniah, Son of Zattu
Summary: Son of Zattu named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Mattaniah
Summary: Levite who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua and served as a porter at the dedication of the wall (Nehemiah 12:8, 12:25).
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Returning Levites became the wall's gatekeepers.

Name: Mattathah, Son of Hashum
Summary: Son of Hashum named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Mattenai, of Joiarib's Course
Summary: Head of Joiarib's priestly course in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:19).
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Faithful courses of priests kept the temple served.

Name: Mattenai, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:37).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Each man on the list faced the same choice.

Name: Mattenai, Son of Hashum
Summary: Son of Hashum named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Mattithiah, Singer
Summary: Levite appointed to sing with harps on the Sheminith at the bringing up of the ark.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:18; 1 Chronicles 15:21: Levite appointed to sing with harps on the Sheminith at the bringing up of the ark.
LifeLesson: The mention of Mattithiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Mattithiah, Son of Jeduthun
Summary: Son of Jeduthun who prophesied with a harp, fourteenth lot.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 25:3; 1 Chronicles 25:21: Son of Jeduthun who prophesied with a harp, fourteenth lot.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mattithiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mattithiah, Son of Nebo
Summary: Son of Nebo named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Mattithiah, Son of Shallum
Summary: Firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, who had the set office over the things made in the pans.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:31: Firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, who had the set office over the things made in the pans.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mattithiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mattithiah
Summary: Stood beside Ezra on the platform at the reading of the law (Nehemiah 8:4). Not Mattithiah son of Nebo.
KeyStory: Ezra reads the law
LifeLesson: Standing beside the reader is itself a testimony.

Name: Mebunnai the Hushathite
Summary: Mebunnai the Hushathite was among David's thirty mighty men, and slew Saph the Philistine giant at Gob. He is also called Sibbechai (rendered Sibbecai in many modern versions).
KeyStory: Mebunnai the Hushathite slew the giant Saph at Gob.
LifeLesson: The man who slew a giant is named twice — once for the deed, once for the list.

Name: Mehetabeel
