Summary: Father of Delaiah, grandfather of the prophet Shemaiah in Nehemiah's day.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: Names in a plot are still part of the record.

Name: Mehida
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Mehir
Summary: Son of Chelub and father of Eshton.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:11: Son of Chelub and father of Eshton.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mehir stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mehuman
Summary: One of the seven chamberlains who served Ahasuerus at his feast.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: Even attendants at a feast are part of the story.

Name: Mehunim
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Melatiah
Summary: Helped rebuild Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: Every section of the wall mattered, and every builder is named.

Name: Melech, Son of Micah
Summary: Son of Micah, named among the sons of Micah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:35; 1 Chronicles 9:41: Son of Micah, named among the sons of Micah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Melech stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Melicu
Summary: Priest in the days of Joiakim.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Courses of priests kept worship ordered across generations.

Name: Melzar
Summary: Melzar was the steward whom the prince of the eunuchs had set over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah; Daniel asked him to prove the youths with pulse and water for ten days, and Melzar agreed and took away their portion of the king's meat.
KeyStory: Daniel asked Melzar to test them ten days on pulse and water, and at the end of ten days their countenances appeared fairer and fatter than all the children who ate the king's meat.
LifeLesson: A small steward's willingness to run a ten-day test made room for God's vindication.

Name: Memucan
Summary: The prince who advised deposing Vashti and publishing the decree throughout the empire.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: Advice given to protect a throne can open the way for deliverance.

Name: Menahem, King of Israel
Summary: Menahem, son of Gadi, slew Shallum, cruelly smote Tiphsah, and bought off Pul king of Assyria with a thousand talents exacted from Israel's wealthy men.
KeyStory: Menahem buys off Assyria with Israel's silver.
RelatedPeople: Shallum, King of Israel; Tiglath-Pileser, King of Assyria; Gadi, Father of Menahem; Pekahiah, King of Israel
LifeLesson: Buying peace with tribute only rents the peace and mortgages the people.

Name: Meonothai
Summary: Father of Ophrah in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:14: Father of Ophrah in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Meonothai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mephibosheth, Son of Jonathan
Summary: Mephibosheth, son of Jonathan, was lame in both feet from a fall when he was five, on the day Saul and Jonathan died. David sought him out for Jonathan's sake, restored Saul's land to him, and set him to eat at the king's table continually. He is also called Merib-baal.
KeyStory: Mephibosheth, lame since childhood, ate at David's table for Jonathan's sake.
RelatedPeople: Jonathan; King David; Ziba; Micha, Son of Mephibosheth
LifeLesson: Covenant kindness seeks out the lame and forgotten and seats them at the table.

Name: Mephibosheth, Son of Saul
Summary: Mephibosheth, son of Saul by Rizpah — distinct from Mephibosheth son of Jonathan — was handed to the Gibeonites with his brother Armoni in atonement for Saul's bloodguilt and was hanged at the beginning of barley harvest.
KeyStory: Mephibosheth son of Saul, Rizpah's son, was hanged beside his brother for Saul's broken oath.
RelatedPeople: King Saul; Rizpah, Daughter of Aiah; Armoni, Son of Saul
LifeLesson: Two men can share a name, a father, and a fate — and still be different men.

Name: Merab
Summary: Merab, Saul's elder daughter, was promised to David as a reward for fighting the Lord's battles, but Saul gave her instead to Adriel the Meholathite.
KeyStory: Merab was used as a bargaining piece in Saul's jealous war against David.
RelatedPeople: King Saul; Michal; Adriel the Meholathite
LifeLesson: Being treated as a token in someone else's jealousy is a real wound, and God sees it.

Name: Meraiah
Summary: Priest in the days of Joiakim.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Courses of priests kept worship ordered across generations.

Name: Meraioth, Ancestor of Ezra
Summary: Ancestor of Ezra named in his genealogy.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: A long line of priests ends in a scribe.

Name: Meraioth, Son of Ahitub
Summary: Meraioth son of Ahitub, named in Nehemiah 11:11.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Meraioth, Son of Zerahiah
Summary: Son of Zerahiah and priest in Aaron's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:6; 1 Chronicles 6:52: Son of Zerahiah and priest in Aaron's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Meraioth stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mered
Summary: Son of Ezra, who took Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:17: Son of Ezra, who took Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mered stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Meremoth, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives; a different Meremoth from Uriah's son.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Sin named honestly is the first step back to God.

Name: Meremoth, Son of Uriah
Summary: Priest who weighed the temple vessels on arrival in Jerusalem and repaired two sections of the wall.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: What is counted carefully is also built carefully.

Name: Meres
Summary: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media who saw the king's face.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: Counsel near the throne carries weight for a kingdom.

Name: Merib-baal, Son of Jonathan
Summary: Son of Jonathan and father of Micah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:34; 1 Chronicles 9:40: Son of Jonathan and father of Micah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Merib-baal stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Merodach-baladan
Summary: Merodach-baladan, son of Baladan, was king of Babylon who sent letters and a present to Hezekiah after hearing of his sickness and recovery; Hezekiah showed the envoys all his treasures, and Isaiah foretold that Babylon would one day carry them away.
KeyStory: Babylon's envoys came to Hezekiah, who showed them his silver, gold, spices, and armoury — and Isaiah announced that everything in the palace would be carried to Babylon.
LifeLesson: Showing off what God gave you to impress a foreign power invites the very loss you boast about.

Name: Mesha, King of Moab
Summary: Mesha, king of Moab, a sheepmaster who paid Israel a hundred thousand lambs and as many rams, rebelled after Ahab's death, and in desperation offered his firstborn son on the wall of Kir-hareseth.
KeyStory: Mesha rebels and offers his son on the wall.
RelatedPeople: King Ahab; Jehoram, King of Israel; King Jehoshaphat; Elisha
LifeLesson: Desperation that sacrifices a child shows how far rebellion runs.

Name: Mesha, Son of Caleb
Summary: Firstborn son of Caleb brother of Jerahmeel, called the father of Ziph.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:42: Firstborn son of Caleb brother of Jerahmeel, called the father of Ziph.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mesha stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mesha, Son of Shaharaim
Summary: Son of Shaharaim by Hodesh.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:9: Son of Shaharaim by Hodesh.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mesha stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Meshach
Summary: Meshach was the Babylonian name given to Mishael, one of Daniel's three companions; he was set over the affairs of the province of Babylon and, with Shadrach and Abednego, refused the golden image and survived the fiery furnace. ONE profile covers both names; he is a different man from Mishael, son of Uzziel, who already has a profile.
KeyStory: Meshach stood with Shadrach and Abednego before the furnace and answered the king: our God is able to deliver us, but if not, we will not worship your image.
LifeLesson: 'But if not' is the deepest confession of faith — obedience that does not bargain for rescue.
RelatedEvents: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the Fiery Furnace

Name: Meshech, Son of Shem
Summary: Son of Shem, named among the sons of Shem in the table of nations.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 1:17: Son of Shem, named among the sons of Shem in the table of nations.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Meshech stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Meshelemiah, Son of Kore
Summary: Son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph, head of the divisions of the porters.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:1; 1 Chronicles 26:14: Son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph, head of the divisions of the porters.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Meshelemiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Meshezabeel
Summary: Named as Meshullam's grandfather in the wall-building account (Nehemiah 3:4), as a covenant sealer (Nehemiah 10:21), and as father of Pethahiah (Nehemiah 11:24).
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: One man's name can span building, sealing, and fatherhood.

Name: Meshillemith
Summary: Father of Meshullam in the Jerusalem priest list, son of Immer.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:12: Father of Meshullam in the Jerusalem priest list, son of Immer.
LifeLesson: The mention of Meshillemith in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Meshillemoth, Father of Berechiah
Summary: Meshillemoth was the father of Berechiah, a head of Ephraim who opposed keeping Judah's captives.
KeyStory: Meshillemoth is named only as the father of Berechiah the son of Meshillemoth.
LifeLesson: A father's name stands behind a son's stand for mercy.

Name: Meshillemoth, Son of Immer
Summary: Meshillemoth son of Immer, named in Nehemiah 11:13.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Meshobab
Summary: Prince of Simeon named among those whose families increased greatly.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:34: Prince of Simeon named among those whose families increased greatly.
LifeLesson: The mention of Meshobab in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Meshullam, Chief Man
Summary: A chief man sent by Ezra to bring Levites for the temple service; a Meshullam is also named among those who stood against the plan to put away foreign wives.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: The same name can serve well in one place and object in another.

Name: Meshullam, Father of Hilkiah
Summary: Father of Hilkiah in the Jerusalem priest list, son of Zadok son of Meraioth.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:11: Father of Hilkiah in the Jerusalem priest list, son of Zadok son of Meraioth.
LifeLesson: The mention of Meshullam in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Meshullam, Father of Jahzerah
Summary: Father of Jahzerah in the Jerusalem priest list, son of Meshillemith.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:12: Father of Jahzerah in the Jerusalem priest list, son of Meshillemith.
LifeLesson: The mention of Meshullam in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Meshullam, Father of Sallu
Summary: Father of Sallu in the Jerusalem list, son of Hodaviah son of Hasenuah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:7: Father of Sallu in the Jerusalem list, son of Hodaviah son of Hasenuah.
LifeLesson: The mention of Meshullam in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Meshullam, Grandfather of Shaphan
Summary: Meshullam was the father of Azaliah and grandfather of Shaphan the scribe.
KeyStory: Meshullam, grandfather of Shaphan.
RelatedPeople: Shaphan, Scribe; Azaliah, Father of Shaphan
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Meshullam, Overseer
Summary: Meshullam, a Levite of the sons of the Kohathites, was an overseer of the workmen repairing the house of the LORD under Josiah.
KeyStory: The overseers included Zechariah and Meshullam, of the sons of the Kohathites.
LifeLesson: Repairing God's house needed overseers from every Levite clan.

Name: Meshullam, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Sin named honestly is the first step back to God.

Name: Meshullam, Son of Berechiah
Summary: Son of Berechiah who repaired two sections of the wall and whose daughter married Tobiah's son; he also sealed the covenant.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: Building the wall and keeping the covenant belong together.

Name: Meshullam, Son of Besodeiah
Summary: Son of Besodeiah who with Joiada repaired the old gate of Jerusalem's wall.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: Old gates are repaired by new hands.

Name: Meshullam, Son of Elpaal
Summary: Named among the sons of Elpaal in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:17: Named among the sons of Elpaal in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Meshullam stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Meshullam, Son of Gad's House
Summary: Named among the brethren of the house of Gad's fathers.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:13: Named among the brethren of the house of Gad's fathers.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Meshullam stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Meshullam, Son of Joed
Summary: Meshullam son of Joed, named in Nehemiah 11:7.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Meshullam, Son of Shephathiah
Summary: Son of Shephathiah son of Reuel son of Ibnijah, of the sons of Benjamin dwelling in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:8: Son of Shephathiah son of Reuel son of Ibnijah, of the sons of Benjamin dwelling in Jerusalem.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Meshullam stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Meshullam, Son of Zadok
Summary: Meshullam son of Zadok, named in Nehemiah 11:11.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Meshullam, Son of Zerubbabel
Summary: Son of Zerubbabel, named in the post-exilic royal line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:19: Son of Zerubbabel, named in the post-exilic royal line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Meshullam stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Meshullemeth, Mother of Amon
Summary: Meshullemeth, daughter of Haruz of Jotbah, was the mother of Amon king of Judah.
KeyStory: Meshullemeth, mother of Amon.
RelatedPeople: Amon, King of Judah; Haruz, Father of Meshullemeth
LifeLesson: Two years of a son's reign are all that remember her name.

Name: Miamin, Son of Parosh
Summary: Son of Parosh named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Miamin
Summary: Priest who returned with Zerubbabel (Nehemiah 12:5); the course of Miniamin in Joiakim's days bears his name (Nehemiah 12:17, spelled Miniamin).
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: A priest's name can outlive him in the course that bears it.

Name: Mibhar, Son of Haggeri
Summary: Son of Haggeri, one of David's mighty men.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:38: Son of Haggeri, one of David's mighty men.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mibhar stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mibsam, Son of Shallum
Summary: Son of Shallum and father of Mishma.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:25: Son of Shallum and father of Mishma.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mibsam stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Micah, Father of Abdon
Summary: Micah was the father of Abdon, sent by Josiah to enquire of the LORD concerning the found book.
KeyStory: Micah is named only as the father of Abdon the son of Micah.
LifeLesson: A messenger's father is named in Josiah's enquiry.

Name: Micah, Father of Mattaniah
Summary: Father of Mattaniah the Levite, son of Zichri son of Asaph.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:15: Father of Mattaniah the Levite, son of Zichri son of Asaph.
LifeLesson: The mention of Micah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Micah, Son of Merib-baal
Summary: Son of Merib-baal and father of Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:34; 1 Chronicles 9:40: Son of Merib-baal and father of Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Micah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Micah, Son of Shimei
Summary: Son of Shimei and father of Reaia in Reuben's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:5: Son of Shimei and father of Reaia in Reuben's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Micah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Micah, the Ephraimite
Summary: Micah, a man of Mount Ephraim, set up a shrine with a graven image and hired a Levite as his priest; the Danites later took his idols and his priest when they moved north. He is distinct from Micah the prophet.
KeyStory: Micah restored his mother's silver, made a graven and a molten image with an ephod and teraphim, consecrated one of his sons and then a Levite as priest, and lost gods and priest alike when the Danites passed through to Laish.
LifeLesson: A religion a man can make, carry off, and lose is no religion at all.

Name: Micaiah, Son of Imla
Summary: Micaiah, son of Imla, was the prophet Jehoshaphat insisted on consulting before Ramoth-gilead; he foretold Israel scattered as sheep without a shepherd and Ahab's fall, and was imprisoned for it.
KeyStory: Micaiah saw the LORD on His throne and a lying spirit sent to entice Ahab, and declared that if Ahab returned in peace, the LORD had not spoken by him.
LifeLesson: A true prophet speaks what God says, even when four hundred others say the opposite.

Name: Micaiah, Son of Imlah
Summary: Micaiah, son of Imlah, was the one prophet Ahab hated because he never prophesied good of him; he saw the LORD send a lying spirit to Ahab's prophets and foretold Ahab's death at Ramoth-gilead, and was imprisoned on bread and water.
KeyStory: Micaiah alone foretells Ahab's death at Ramoth-gilead.
RelatedPeople: King Ahab; King Jehoshaphat; Zedekiah, Son of Chenaanah; Imlah, Father of Micaiah
LifeLesson: One true voice against four hundred is still the majority when God has spoken.

Name: Micha, Son of Mephibosheth
Summary: Micha was the young son of Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, living in Jerusalem when David restored his father's inheritance and set him at the king's table.
KeyStory: Micha grew up in Jerusalem under the shadow of his father's restored place at David's table.
RelatedPeople: Mephibosheth, Son of Jonathan; King David
LifeLesson: A restored father's table feeds his children too.

Name: Micha, Son of Zabdi
Summary: Micha son of Zabdi, named in Nehemiah 11:17.
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Michael, Captain of Manasseh
Summary: Captain of the thousands of Manasseh who fell to David at Ziklag.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:20: Captain of the thousands of Manasseh who fell to David at Ziklag.
LifeLesson: The mention of Michael in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Michael, Father of Zebadiah
Summary: Father of Zebadiah, who returned with Ezra.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: A father's name can open a son's story.

Name: Michael, Son of Baaseiah
Summary: Son of Baaseiah and father of Shimea in Asaph's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:40: Son of Baaseiah and father of Shimea in Asaph's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Michael stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Michael, Son of Beriah
Summary: Named among the sons of Beriah in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:16: Named among the sons of Beriah in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Michael stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Michael, Son of Gad's House
Summary: Named among the brethren of the house of Gad's fathers.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:13: Named among the brethren of the house of Gad's fathers.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Michael stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Michael, Son of Izrahiah
Summary: Son of Izrahiah, a chief man in Issachar's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:3: Son of Izrahiah, a chief man in Issachar's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Michael stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Michael, Son of Jehoshaphat
Summary: Michael was a son of Jehoshaphat who received great gifts from his father and was slain by his brother Jehoram.
KeyStory: Jehoshaphat's sons, including Michael, received gifts and fenced cities, but Jehoram slew all his brethren.
RelatedPeople: King Jehoshaphat; Jehoram, King of Judah
LifeLesson: Inheritance without justice is a fragile gift.

Name: Michael, Son of Jeshishai
Summary: Son of Jeshishai son of Jahdo son of Buz in Gad's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:14: Son of Jeshishai son of Jahdo son of Buz in Gad's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Michael stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Michah, Son of Uzziel
Summary: First son of Uzziel in David's divisions.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 23:20; 1 Chronicles 24:24: First son of Uzziel in David's divisions.
LifeLesson: The mention of Michah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Michaiah, Daughter of Uriel
Summary: Michaiah, daughter of Uriel of Gibeah, was the mother of Abijah, king of Judah.
KeyStory: Abijah reigned three years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Michaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah.
RelatedPeople: Abijah, King of Judah; Uriel, of Gibeah
LifeLesson: Mothers of kings are named because their sons' reigns are part of God's record.

Name: Michaiah, Father of Achbor
Summary: Michaiah was the father of Achbor, one of Josiah's messengers to Huldah; he is distinct from Micaiah the prophet.
KeyStory: Michaiah, father of Achbor.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Michaiah, Prince of Judah
Summary: Michaiah was one of the princes Jehoshaphat sent in his third year to teach in the cities of Judah, distinct from Michaiah daughter of Uriel.
KeyStory: Jehoshaphat sent his princes, including Michaiah, to teach in the cities of Judah.
LifeLesson: God's law taught throughout the land, and willing service under a faithful king, strengthened Judah.

Name: Michaiah, Son of Zaccur
Summary: Michaiah son of Zaccur, named in Nehemiah 12:35.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Michaiah
Summary: Michaiah, son of Gemariah, heard Baruch read Jeremiah's roll in his father's chamber and reported all the words to the princes, who then sent for Baruch and heard the roll themselves.
KeyStory: Michaiah heard the words Baruch read and declared them to the princes in the scribe's chamber, setting in motion the reading before the king.
RelatedPeople: Gemariah, Son of Shaphan; Jeremiah; Baruch
LifeLesson: Repeating what you heard faithfully can be the first link in a chain that reaches the king.

Name: Michal, Daughter of Saul
Summary: Daughter of Saul who saw David dancing before the ark and despised him in her heart.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:29: Daughter of Saul who saw David dancing before the ark and despised him in her heart.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Michal stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Michal
Role: Daughter of Saul; Wife of David
Summary: Michal, Saul's younger daughter, loved David and married him, then saved his life by letting him down through a window when Saul sent men to kill him. Saul later gave her to Palti, and David took her back when he became king. She despised David's dancing before the ark and remained childless.
KeyStory: Michal loved David, saved him from her father's assassins, and later scorned his worship before the ark.
KeyVerses: 1 Samuel 14:49; 1 Samuel 18:20; 1 Samuel 19:11; 1 Samuel 19:12; 2 Samuel 3:13; 2 Samuel 6:16; 2 Samuel 6:23
RelatedPeople: King Saul; King David; Merab; Phalti, Son of Laish
LifeLesson: Love, loyalty, and later contempt can live in one heart — and worship scorned has its own cost.

Name: Michri
Summary: Father of Uzzi in the Jerusalem list.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:8: Father of Uzzi in the Jerusalem list.
LifeLesson: The mention of Michri in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Mijamin
Summary: Sixth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:9: Sixth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mijamin stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mikloth, Ruler of Second Course
Summary: Ruler of the second month's course, with Dodai the Ahohite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:4: Ruler of the second month's course, with Dodai the Ahohite.
LifeLesson: The mention of Mikloth in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Mikloth, Son of Jehiel
Summary: Son of Jehiel the father of Gibeon, father of Shimeah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:32; 1 Chronicles 9:37: Son of Jehiel the father of Gibeon, father of Shimeah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mikloth stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mikneiah, Singer
Summary: Levite appointed to sing with harps on the Sheminith at the bringing up of the ark.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:18; 1 Chronicles 15:21: Levite appointed to sing with harps on the Sheminith at the bringing up of the ark.
LifeLesson: The mention of Mikneiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Milalai
Summary: Musician at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Music marks the moment a long work is finished.

Name: Miniamin, Priest Distributor
Summary: Miniamin served with Kore in the cities of the priests, giving portions to his brethren by courses under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Miniamin served with Kore in the cities of the priests, giving portions to his brethren by courses under Hezekiah.
RelatedPeople: Kore, Son of Imnah; King Hezekiah
LifeLesson: Fair portions for every priest, great and small, came through faithful distributors.

Name: Miriam, Daughter of Ezra
Summary: Daughter borne to Ezra's line, named beside Shammai and Ishbah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:17: Daughter borne to Ezra's line, named beside Shammai and Ishbah.
LifeLesson: The mention of Miriam in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Mirma
Summary: Son of Shaharaim by Hodesh, head of his father's house.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:10: Son of Shaharaim by Hodesh, head of his father's house.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mirma stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mishael, Companion of Ezra
Summary: One who stood beside Ezra on the pulpit at the reading of the Law; a different Mishael from Uzziel's son in Exodus.
KeyStory: Ezra reads the law
LifeLesson: Standing beside the word is itself a service.

Name: Misham
Summary: Son of Elpaal, named among the sons of Elpaal.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:12: Son of Elpaal, named among the sons of Elpaal.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Misham stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mishma, Son of Mibsam
Summary: Son of Mibsam and father of Hamuel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:25: Son of Mibsam and father of Hamuel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mishma stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mishmannah
Summary: Fourth captain of the Gadites who separated themselves to David in the wilderness.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:10: Fourth captain of the Gadites who separated themselves to David in the wilderness.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mishmannah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mispar
Summary: A leader who returned with Zerubbabel; Nehemiah's copy of the list spells the name Mispereth.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Two copies of one list can spell one man's name two ways.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Mithredath
Summary: Treasurer of Cyrus who counted out the temple vessels to Sheshbazzar; a Mithredath is also named among those who later wrote against Jerusalem's rebuilding.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Even officials of a foreign king can serve God's purposes for his people.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile; Rebuilding of the Temple

Name: Mnason
Summary: Mnason was an old disciple of Cyprus with whom Paul's company lodged on reaching Jerusalem, his house providing their first lodging in the city.
KeyStory: Mnason, an old disciple, opened his house at Jerusalem to Paul's company at the end of the road.
LifeLesson: Old disciples open houses. Mnason's hospitality received the mission at Jerusalem's gate.

Name: Molid
Summary: Son of Abishur by Abihail.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:29: Son of Abishur by Abihail.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Molid stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mordecai, Companion of Zerubbabel
Summary: A leader who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel, named in both return lists; a different man from Mordecai of Esther, whose genealogy is given separately.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Two men can share a name and both serve the same return.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Moza, Son of Ephah
Summary: Son of Caleb's concubine Ephah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:46: Son of Caleb's concubine Ephah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Moza stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Moza, Son of Zimri
Summary: Son of Zimri and father of Binea.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:36; 1 Chronicles 9:42: Son of Zimri and father of Binea.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Moza stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Mushi, Son of Merari
Summary: Son of Merari, named among the sons of Merari.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:19: Son of Merari, named among the sons of Merari.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Mushi stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Naam
Summary: Son of Caleb son of Jephunneh.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:15: Son of Caleb son of Jephunneh.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Naam stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Naamah, Mother of Rehoboam
Summary: Naamah, an Ammonitess, was the mother of Rehoboam, under whom the kingdom divided.
KeyStory: Naamah, mother of Rehoboam.
LifeLesson: A foreign mother's son still sat on David's throne, and lost most of it.

Name: Naamah, the Ammonitess
Summary: Naamah, an Ammonitess, was the mother of Rehoboam, who was forty-one when he began to reign seventeen years in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Naamah is named only as Rehoboam's mother in the record of his reign.
LifeLesson: A mother's identity is part of a king's story, even in a single line.

Name: Naaman, Son of Bela
Summary: Son of Bela, named among the sons of Bela.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:4: Son of Bela, named among the sons of Bela.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Naaman stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Naaman, Son of Ehud
Summary: Son of Ehud who removed the inhabitants of Geba and begat Uzza and Ahihud.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:7: Son of Ehud who removed the inhabitants of Geba and begat Uzza and Ahihud.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Naaman stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Naarah
Summary: Wife of Ashur the father of Tekoa and mother of Ahuzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:5: Wife of Ashur the father of Tekoa and mother of Ahuzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari.
LifeLesson: The mention of Naarah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Naarai, Son of Ezbai
Summary: Son of Ezbai, one of David's mighty men.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:37: Son of Ezbai, one of David's mighty men.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Naarai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Naboth the Jezreelite
Summary: Naboth the Jezreelite refused to sell his ancestral vineyard to Ahab, and Jezebel had him falsely accused and stoned so Ahab could take it; Elijah met Ahab there with judgment.
KeyStory: Naboth refuses, is stoned, and Ahab takes his vineyard.
LifeLesson: An inheritance kept by faith is worth more than a king's price, even at the cost of life.

Name: Nadab, King of Israel
Summary: Nadab, son of Jeroboam, reigned two years and walked in his father's sin, and was slain by Baasha at Gibbethon while Israel besieged the Philistines.
KeyStory: Nadab follows Jeroboam's sin and is slain by Baasha.
LifeLesson: A son who inherits only his father's sins inherits his father's judgment too.

Name: Nadab, Son of Jehiel
Summary: Son of Jehiel the father of Gibeon.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:30; 1 Chronicles 9:36: Son of Jehiel the father of Gibeon.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Nadab stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Nadab, Son of Shammai
Summary: Son of Shammai and father of Seled and Appaim.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:28: Son of Shammai and father of Seled and Appaim.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Nadab stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Naham
Summary: Brother of Hodiah, named in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:19: Brother of Hodiah, named in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Naham stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Nahamani
Summary: A leader named in Nehemiah's copy of the return list.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Faithfulness in returning to rebuild is remembered by name.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Naharai the Beerothite
Summary: Naharai the Beerothite, Joab's armourbearer, was among David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Naharai the Beerothite, Joab's armourbearer, stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: The commander's armourbearer earned his own place in the thirty.

Name: Naharai the Berothite
Summary: Armourbearer of Joab son of Zeruiah, one of David's mighty men.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:39: Armourbearer of Joab son of Zeruiah, one of David's mighty men.
LifeLesson: The mention of Naharai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Nahash, King of Ammon
Summary: Nahash, king of Ammon, besieged Jabesh-gilead and demanded every man's right eye as terms of surrender. Saul's rescue of the city launched his kingship. Nahash later died, and David showed kindness to his son Hanun for Nahash's earlier kindness to him.
KeyStory: Nahash's cruel terms at Jabesh-gilead gave Saul his first victory — and David later repaid an old kindness to his son.
KeyVerses: 1 Samuel 11:1; 1 Samuel 11:2; 1 Samuel 12:12; 2 Samuel 10:1; 2 Samuel 10:2; 1 Chronicles 19:1
RelatedPeople: King Saul; King David; Hanun, Son of Nahash
LifeLesson: Cruelty invites judgment, but an old kindness is still remembered and repaid.

Name: Nahath, Overseer
Summary: Nahath was one of the overseers under Cononiah and Shimei over the offerings and tithes under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Nahath was one of the overseers under Cononiah and Shimei over the offerings and tithes under Hezekiah.
RelatedPeople: Cononiah, the Levite; Shimei, Brother of Cononiah; King Hezekiah; Azariah, Chief Priest
LifeLesson: Many overseers together kept one storehouse honest.

Name: Nahath, Son of Zophai
Summary: Son of Zophai and father of Eliab in the Samuel line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:26: Son of Zophai and father of Eliab in the Samuel line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Nahath stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Nahshon, Son of Amminadab
Summary: Nahshon appears in Ruth's genealogy as the son of Amminadab and father of Salmon, in the line from Pharez to David.
KeyStory: Nahshon stands in the closing genealogy between Amminadab and Salmon, in the line that runs from Pharez to David.
RelatedPeople: Amminadab; Salmon, Son of Nahshon; Pharez
LifeLesson: A name in a list is a link in a chain that ends at Bethlehem's king.

Name: Nahum
Summary: Nahum the Elkoshite prophesied against Nineveh, capital of Assyria, around 660–630 BC, about a century after Jonah's visit. Where Jonah preached mercy to a repenting city, Nahum announced its coming fall: a jealous, avenging God would not acquit the wicked, though He is a stronghold for those who trust Him.
KeyStory: Nahum pictured Nineveh's chariots, flooded river gates, and plundered palaces, and declared that the city that once terrorized nations would itself be laid waste.
LifeLesson: God is both a stronghold for the trusting and an avenger of the cruel. Mercy refused hardens into judgment — but those who run to Him are never turned away.

Name: Narcissus
Role: Head of a household in Rome
Summary: Narcissus is named only as the head of a household in Rome, and Paul greets those of his household who are in the Lord.
KeyStory: Narcissus is named only as the head of a household in Rome, and Paul greets those of his household who are in the Lord.
LifeLesson: The Lord knows his own even inside households that do not wholly believe.

Name: Nathan, Chief Man
Summary: A chief man sent by Ezra to Iddo at Casiphia to bring ministers for the house of God.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: Leaders are sent to find servants, not only to be served.

Name: Nathan, Prophet
Summary: Prophet to whom the word of God came concerning David's house, telling David he would not build the house.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 17:1; 1 Chronicles 17:3: Prophet to whom the word of God came concerning David's house, telling David he would not build the house.
LifeLesson: The mention of Nathan in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Nathan, Son of Attai
Summary: Son of Attai and father of Zabad.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:36: Son of Attai and father of Zabad.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Nathan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Nathan, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives; a different Nathan from the prophet.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Sin named honestly is the first step back to God.

Name: Nathan, Son of David
Summary: Nathan, son of David, was born at Jerusalem and named among the sons born to him there. He is distinct from Nathan the prophet who confronted David.
KeyStory: Nathan son of David was born at Jerusalem, sharing a name with the prophet who rebuked his father.
LifeLesson: Sharing a prophet's name does not make a prince a prophet.

Name: Neariah, Son of Ishi
Summary: Son of Ishi and captain of the five hundred Simeonites who went to Mount Seir.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:42: Son of Ishi and captain of the five hundred Simeonites who went to Mount Seir.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Neariah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Neariah, Son of Shemaiah
Summary: Son of Shemaiah son of Shechaniah and father of Elioenai, Hezekiah, and Azrikam.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:22: Son of Shemaiah son of Shechaniah and father of Elioenai, Hezekiah, and Azrikam.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Neariah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Nebai
Summary: Chief who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10).
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: A signature on a covenant is a public stand.

Name: Nebat, Father of Jeroboam
Summary: Nebat, an Ephrathite of Zereda, was the father of Jeroboam, first king of Israel.
KeyStory: Nebat, father of Jeroboam.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Nebushasban
Summary: Nebushasban, titled Rab-saris (chief eunuch), was one of the Babylonian officers sent to take Jeremiah out of the prison court after Jerusalem fell.
KeyStory: Nebushasban joined Nebuzaradan's party in sending for Jeremiah and bringing him out of the court of the prison.
LifeLesson: Small acts of obedience by minor officials can be the hinge of a prophet's survival.

Name: Nebuzaradan, Captain of the Guard
Summary: Nebuzaradan, captain of Nebuchadnezzar's guard, burned the temple and the king's house, broke Jerusalem's walls, carried the people away, and slew the chief priests at Riblah.
KeyStory: Nebuzaradan burns Jerusalem and carries Judah away.
RelatedPeople: King Nebuchadnezzar; Seraiah, Chief Priest; Zephaniah, Second Priest; Gedaliah, Son of Ahikam
LifeLesson: The man who burned the temple was also the instrument of God's long-promised judgment.
RelatedEvents: Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile

Name: Nebuzaradan
Role: Captain of the Guard of Babylon
Summary: Nebuzaradan (KJV: Nebuzar-adan) was Nebuchadnezzar's captain of the guard who burned the temple and the king's house, broke down Jerusalem's walls, carried the people to Babylon, and — on his king's orders — protected Jeremiah and gave him the choice of going to Babylon or staying in the land.
KeyStory: Nebuzaradan burned the house of the Lord and all the houses of Jerusalem, then took Jeremiah out of the prison court, loosed his chains, and told him to go wherever seemed good to him.
LifeLesson: Even the officer sent to destroy a city can be the one God uses to spare his prophet.
RelatedEvents: Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile

Name: Necho, King of Egypt
Summary: Necho, king of Egypt, came up to fight against Carchemish by Euphrates; he warned Josiah that God had commanded him to make haste and not to meddle, but Josiah disguised himself, fought at Megiddo, was wounded by archers, and died at Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Necho sent ambassadors saying, 'What have I to do with thee, thou king of Judah? forbear thee from meddling with God, who is with me,' but Josiah hearkened not.
RelatedPeople: King Josiah; Jehoahaz, Son of Josiah
LifeLesson: Ignoring a warning, even from an enemy king, can end a righteous reign.

Name: Nedabiah
Summary: Son of Jeconiah, named in the post-exilic royal line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:18: Son of Jeconiah, named in the post-exilic royal line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Nedabiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Nehemiah, Companion of Zerubbabel
Summary: A leader who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel, named first among the companions in the return lists; a different man from Nehemiah the governor, who came some ninety years later.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Two men can share a name and both serve the same return.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Nehemiah, Son of Azbuk
Summary: Ruler of half of Beth-zur who repaired part of Jerusalem's wall; a different Nehemiah from the governor.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: Two men can share a name and both serve the same wall.

Name: Nehushta, Mother of Jehoiachin
Summary: Nehushta, daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem, was the mother of Jehoiachin, and was carried to Babylon with him.
KeyStory: Nehushta, mother of Jehoiachin, carried to Babylon.
RelatedPeople: Jehoiachin, King of Judah; Elnathan, Father of Nehushta
LifeLesson: A queen mother went into exile with the son she had raised to the throne.

Name: Nekoda
Summary: Head of a Nethinim family (Ezra 2:48) and named among those who could not prove their genealogy (Ezra 2:60); whether one family or two is not stated.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Honest records admit what cannot be proved.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Nemuel, Son of Simeon
Summary: Son of Simeon, named among the sons of Simeon.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:24: Son of Simeon, named among the sons of Simeon.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Nemuel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Nepheg, Son of David
Summary: Nepheg, son of David, was born at Jerusalem and named among the sons born to him there. He is distinct from Nepheg son of Izhar of the Exodus generation.
KeyStory: Nepheg son of David was born at Jerusalem, sharing a name with an older Nepheg.
LifeLesson: Old names return in new generations, and the record keeps them straight.

Name: Nephusim
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Ner, Father of Abner
Summary: Ner was the father of Abner, captain of Saul's army.
KeyStory: Ner, father of Abner.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Ner, Son of Abiel
Summary: Ner, son of Abiel and brother of Kish, was the father of Abner, commander of Saul's army.
KeyStory: Ner fathered the man who would hold Saul's kingdom together after Saul's death.
RelatedPeople: Abner, Son of Ner; Kish, Son of Abiel
LifeLesson: Behind every commander stands a father whose name is barely remembered.

Name: Ner, Son of Jehiel
Summary: Son of Jehiel the father of Gibeon, father of Kish.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:36: Son of Jehiel the father of Gibeon, father of Kish.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ner stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Nereus
Summary: Nereus was a Christian in Rome greeted by Paul alongside his sister, Philologus, Julia, and Olympas.
KeyStory: Nereus was a Christian in Rome greeted by Paul alongside his sister, Philologus, Julia, and Olympas.
LifeLesson: Brothers and sisters in the faith are greeted together, as family.

Name: Nergal-sharezer
Summary: Nergal-sharezer was a prince of the king of Babylon who sat in the middle gate of Jerusalem when the city fell, and later — called Rab-mag — was among those sent to release Jeremiah from prison.
KeyStory: When Jerusalem was taken, the princes of Babylon, including Nergal-sharezer, sat in the middle gate, and Nergal-sharezer later helped send for Jeremiah's release.
LifeLesson: The fall of a city is carried out by named men, not by faceless forces.
RelatedEvents: Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile

Name: Nethaneel, Chief of the Levites
Summary: Nethaneel, a chief of the Levites and brother of Cononiah, gave with the other chiefs five thousand small cattle and five hundred oxen for Josiah's Passover.
KeyStory: Conaniah, Shemaiah and Nethaneel, his brethren, gave unto the Levites for passover offerings.
RelatedPeople: Cononiah, Chief of the Levites; Shemaiah, Chief of the Levites; King Josiah
LifeLesson: A family of chiefs served one Passover together.

Name: Nethaneel, Father of Shemaiah
Summary: Father of Shemaiah the scribe.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:6: Father of Shemaiah the scribe.
LifeLesson: The mention of Nethaneel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Nethaneel, Priest of the Ark
Summary: Priest who blew with the trumpet before the ark of God.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:24: Priest who blew with the trumpet before the ark of God.
LifeLesson: The mention of Nethaneel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Nethaneel, Prince of Judah
Summary: Nethaneel was one of the princes Jehoshaphat sent in his third year to teach in the cities of Judah.
KeyStory: Jehoshaphat sent his princes, including Nethaneel, to teach in the cities of Judah.
LifeLesson: God's law taught throughout the land, and willing service under a faithful king, strengthened Judah.

Name: Nethaneel, Son of Jesse
Summary: Fourth son of Jesse and brother of David.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:14: Fourth son of Jesse and brother of David.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Nethaneel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Nethaneel, Son of Obed-edom
Summary: Fifth son of Obed-edom the porter.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:4: Fifth son of Obed-edom the porter.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Nethaneel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Nethaneel, Son of Pashur
Summary: Son of Pashur named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Nethaneel
Summary: Priest in Joiakim's days (Nehemiah 12:21) and musician at the dedication of the wall (Nehemiah 12:36).
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Priests both kept the courses and sounded the praise.

Name: Nethaniah, Father of Ishmael
Summary: Nethaniah was the father of Ishmael, who murdered Gedaliah at Mizpah.
KeyStory: Nethaniah, father of Ishmael.
RelatedPeople: Ishmael, Son of Nethaniah; Elishama, Grandfather of Ishmael
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Nethaniah, Son of Asaph
Summary: Son of Asaph who prophesied under the hands of Asaph.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 25:2; 1 Chronicles 25:12: Son of Asaph who prophesied under the hands of Asaph.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Nethaniah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Nethaniah, the Levite
Summary: Nethaniah was one of the Levites sent with Jehoshaphat's princes to teach the book of the law throughout Judah.
KeyStory: With the princes went Levites, including Nethaniah, teaching the people from the book of the law.
LifeLesson: God's law taught throughout the land, and willing service under a faithful king, strengthened Judah.

Name: Neziah
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Nicanor
Summary: Nicanor was one of the seven men chosen to serve tables in the Jerusalem church. Acts names him among the seven and records nothing further of him by name.
KeyStory: Nicanor was chosen with the seven to see that no widow was neglected in the daily ministration.
LifeLesson: Faithful service needs no further story. Nicanor's one verse holds a whole ministry of fairness.

Name: Nicolas
Summary: Nicolas was one of the seven men chosen to serve tables in the Jerusalem church, and the only one Acts describes as a proselyte, a Gentile convert to Judaism from Antioch.
KeyStory: Nicolas, a proselyte of Antioch, was chosen among the seven, a Gentile convert serving a Jewish church's widows.
LifeLesson: The gospel's first officers already crossed the Jew-Gentile line. Nicolas served widows not his own by birth.

Name: Nimshi, Father of Jehu
Summary: Nimshi was the father of Jehu, whom the LORD anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
KeyStory: Nimshi is named only as the father of Jehu the son of Nimshi.
LifeLesson: An anointed judge came from an otherwise unnamed family.

Name: Nimshi, Grandfather of Jehu
Summary: Nimshi was the father of Jehoshaphat and grandfather of Jehu, king of Israel.
KeyStory: Nimshi, grandfather of Jehu.
RelatedPeople: Jehu, King of Israel; Jehoshaphat, Son of Nimshi
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Noadiah, Son of Binnui
Summary: A Levite who with Meremoth weighed the temple vessels on arrival in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: What is counted carefully is honored.

Name: Noadiah the Prophetess
Summary: A prophetess named among those hired to frighten Nehemiah and stop the wall.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: Not every voice claiming God speaks for him.

Name: Nogah, Son of David
Summary: Son of David born in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:7; 1 Chronicles 14:6: Son of David born in Jerusalem.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Nogah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Nohah
Summary: Fourth son of Benjamin, named among the sons of Benjamin.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:2: Fourth son of Benjamin, named among the sons of Benjamin.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Nohah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Non
Summary: Son of Elishama and father of Jehoshua in Ephraim's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:27: Son of Elishama and father of Jehoshua in Ephraim's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Non stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Nun
Summary: Father of Joshua (Jeshua son of Nun), named in Nehemiah 8:17.
KeyStory: Ezra reads the law
LifeLesson: A father's name stands behind a great son.

Name: Nymphas
Summary: Nymphas was a believer in whose house a church met, greeted by Paul in Colossians alongside the brethren in Laodicea.
KeyStory: Nymphas was a believer in whose house a church met, greeted by Paul in Colossians alongside the brethren in Laodicea.
LifeLesson: A house opened for the church becomes a church itself.

Name: Obadiah, Captain of Gad
Summary: Second captain of the Gadites who separated themselves to David in the wilderness.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:9: Second captain of the Gadites who separated themselves to David in the wilderness.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Obadiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Obadiah, Overseer
Summary: Obadiah, a Levite of the sons of Merari, was an overseer of the workmen repairing the house of the LORD under Josiah.
KeyStory: The overseers were Jahath and Obadiah, Levites of the sons of Merari, to set the work forward.
LifeLesson: Merarite overseers shared the repair with Kohathites.

Name: Obadiah, Prince of Judah
Summary: Obadiah was one of the princes Jehoshaphat sent in his third year to teach in the cities of Judah.
KeyStory: Jehoshaphat sent his princes, including Obadiah, to teach in the cities of Judah.
LifeLesson: God's law taught throughout the land, and willing service under a faithful king, strengthened Judah.

Name: Obadiah, Son of Arnan
Summary: Named in the chain of sons after Hananiah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:21: Named in the chain of sons after Hananiah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Obadiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Obadiah, Son of Azel
Summary: Son of Azel, named among the six sons of Azel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:38; 1 Chronicles 9:44: Son of Azel, named among the six sons of Azel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Obadiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Obadiah, Son of Izrahiah
Summary: Son of Izrahiah, a chief man in Issachar's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:3: Son of Izrahiah, a chief man in Issachar's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Obadiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Obadiah, Son of Jehiel
Summary: Son of Jehiel who returned with Ezra from Babylon.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: Returning to God's house is a family decision.

Name: Obadiah, Son of Shemaiah
Summary: Son of Shemaiah son of Galal son of Jeduthun, Levite dwelling in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:16: Son of Shemaiah son of Galal son of Jeduthun, Levite dwelling in Jerusalem.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Obadiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Obadiah, Steward of Ahab
Summary: Obadiah, who was over Ahab's house, feared the LORD greatly and hid a hundred prophets in caves and fed them when Jezebel slew the LORD's prophets; he is distinct from Obadiah the prophet.
KeyStory: Obadiah hides a hundred prophets from Jezebel.
LifeLesson: Quiet courage feeds prophets in caves while the court serves Baal.

Name: Obadiah the Porter
Summary: Porter at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 12:25).
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Gatekeepers kept the dedication ordered.

Name: Obadiah
Summary: Obadiah is the shortest book of the Old Testament: a single-chapter prophecy against Edom, probably delivered around or after Jerusalem's fall in 586 BC (the exact date is debated). He condemned Edom for standing by — and joining in — when Babylon plundered Judah, and promised that the kingdom shall be the LORD's.
KeyStory: Obadiah pronounced judgment on Edom for its pride and its violence against brother Jacob in the day of Jerusalem's calamity.
LifeLesson: Pride falls hardest when it feeds on a brother's suffering. Do not rejoice over another's calamity — the day of the LORD comes to all nations alike.

Name: Obed-edom, Porter
Summary: Levite porter appointed at the bringing up of the ark, and later porter before the ark.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:18; 1 Chronicles 15:21; 1 Chronicles 16:38: Levite porter appointed at the bringing up of the ark, and later porter before the ark.
LifeLesson: The mention of Obed-edom in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Obed-edom the Gittite
Summary: Obed-edom the Gittite kept the ark in his house for three months after Uzzah's death, and the Lord blessed him and all his household. David then brought the ark up from his house to Jerusalem with gladness.
KeyStory: Obed-edom housed the ark for three months and was blessed for it.
KeyVerses: 2 Samuel 6:10; 2 Samuel 6:11; 2 Samuel 6:12; 1 Chronicles 13:13; 1 Chronicles 13:14; 1 Chronicles 15:18
LifeLesson: Housing God's presence in fear and reverence brings blessing to a whole household.

Name: Obed-edom
Summary: Obed-edom is named in 2 Chronicles only as the man with whom the vessels of the house of God were found when Joash of Israel took them; the book does not state whether he is the Obed-edom of David's day.
KeyStory: Joash of Israel took all the vessels found in the house of God with Obed-edom, and the treasures of the king's house, and returned to Samaria.
LifeLesson: Temple treasures entrusted to one man can be carried off in a single defeat.

Name: Obed, Father of Azariah
Summary: Obed was the father of Azariah, a captain of hundreds in Jehoiada's covenant.
KeyStory: Obed is named only as the father of Azariah the son of Obed.
LifeLesson: Obed's son stood for the king when it mattered.

Name: Obed, Son of Boaz
Summary: Obed, son of Boaz and Ruth, was born in Bethlehem and became the father of Jesse and grandfather of David, carrying the line named in Ruth's genealogy.
KeyStory: When Ruth bore a son, the women of Bethlehem named him Obed and told Naomi he would be a restorer of her life; Obed became the father of Jesse, the father of David.
RelatedPeople: Boaz; Ruth; Jesse, Son of Obed; Naomi
LifeLesson: A child born to a foreign widow became the hinge of a king's line.

Name: Obed, Son of Ephlal
Summary: Son of Ephlal and father of Jehu.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:37: Son of Ephlal and father of Jehu.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Obed stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Obed, Son of Shemaiah
Summary: Son of Shemaiah son of Obed-edom, mighty man of valour.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:7: Son of Shemaiah son of Obed-edom, mighty man of valour.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Obed stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Obed the Mesobaite
Summary: Mighty man of David, named among the Mesobaites.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:47: Mighty man of David, named among the Mesobaites.
LifeLesson: The mention of Obed in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Obil the Ishmaelite
Summary: Ishmaelite over the camels of the king.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:30: Ishmaelite over the camels of the king.
LifeLesson: The mention of Obil in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Oded, Father of Azariah
Summary: Oded was the father of Azariah the prophet; the record also speaks of 'the prophecy of Oded the prophet' which Asa heard, though 2 Chronicles does not state plainly whether father or son spoke it.
KeyStory: When Asa heard the words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage and put away the abominable idols.
RelatedPeople: Azariah, Son of Oded; King Asa
LifeLesson: God's word, whether through father or son, bears the same call: seek Him while He may be found.

Name: Oded, Prophet of Samaria
Summary: Oded, a prophet of the LORD at Samaria, met Israel's returning host and warned that they had slain Judah in a rage reaching to heaven, and that keeping the captives would add to their own sin; the captives were then returned.
KeyStory: Oded told the host to deliver the captives again, for the fierce wrath of the LORD was upon them, and the men expressed by name clothed and fed the captives and carried the feeble to Jericho.
RelatedPeople: Ahaz, King of Judah; Pekah, Son of Remaliah
LifeLesson: A prophet's rebuke can turn plunder into mercy.

Name: Ohel
Summary: Named among the sons of Zerubbabel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:20: Named among the sons of Zerubbabel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ohel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Olympas
Summary: Olympas was a Christian in Rome greeted by Paul alongside Philologus, Julia, and Nereus and his sister.
KeyStory: Olympas was a Christian in Rome greeted by Paul alongside Philologus, Julia, and Nereus and his sister.
LifeLesson: Even the briefest mention in Scripture marks a life known to God.

Name: Omri, Father of Ammihud
Summary: Father of Ammihud in the Jerusalem list, son of Imri son of Bani.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:4: Father of Ammihud in the Jerusalem list, son of Imri son of Bani.
LifeLesson: The mention of Omri in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Omri, King of Israel
Summary: Omri, commander of Israel's army, was made king after Zimri's death, prevailed over the rival Tibni, built Samaria on Shemer's hill, and did worse than all before him, establishing the dynasty of Ahab.
KeyStory: Omri prevails over Tibni and builds Samaria.
RelatedPeople: Zimri, King of Israel; Tibni, King of Israel; Shemer, Owner of Samaria's Hill; King Ahab; Athaliah; Ahaziah, King of Judah
LifeLesson: Political skill without godliness only builds a stronger platform for sin.

Name: Omri, Son of Becher
Summary: Son of Becher, named among the sons of Becher.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:8: Son of Becher, named among the sons of Becher.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Omri stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Omri, Son of Michael
Summary: Son of Michael, ruler of Issachar.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:18: Son of Michael, ruler of Issachar.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Omri stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Onesimus
Role: Runaway servant received as a brother
Summary: Onesimus was Philemon's servant who ran away, met Paul in his bonds, and became Paul's son in the faith; Paul sent him back to Philemon no longer as a servant but above a servant, a brother beloved, and names him to the Colossians as one of their own.
KeyStory: Onesimus was Philemon's servant who ran away, met Paul in his bonds, and became Paul's son in the faith; Paul sent him back to Philemon no longer as a servant but above a servant, a brother beloved, and names him to the Colossians as one of their own.
LifeLesson: The gospel makes the unprofitable profitable; no past bars a person from brotherhood.

Name: Onesiphorus
Role: Refresher of Paul, not ashamed of his chain
Summary: Onesiphorus often refreshed Paul and was not ashamed of his chain, seeking Paul out diligently at Rome; Paul also greets his household and prays the Lord grant him mercy.
KeyStory: Onesiphorus often refreshed Paul and was not ashamed of his chain, seeking Paul out diligently at Rome; Paul also greets his household and prays the Lord grant him mercy.
LifeLesson: Seeking out a prisoner instead of shrinking from his chain is mercy in action.

Name: Ophrah
Summary: Son of Meonothai in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:14: Son of Meonothai in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ophrah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Oreb, Prince of Midian
Summary: Oreb, a prince of Midian, was captured and killed by Ephraim at the rock Oreb during Gideon's victory.
KeyStory: After Gideon's night attack, Ephraim took the waters and slew Oreb at the rock Oreb and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb.
RelatedPeople: Gideon; Zeeb, Prince of Midian; Zebah, King of Midian; Zalmunna, King of Midian
LifeLesson: Princes fall where the battle turns, and the rock keeps their name.

Name: Oren
Summary: Son of Jerahmeel, named among the sons of Jerahmeel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:25: Son of Jerahmeel, named among the sons of Jerahmeel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Oren stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ornan the Jebusite
Summary: Jebusite whose threshing floor at Mount Moriah David bought for six hundred shekels of gold to build an altar to the LORD, and where Solomon later built the house of the LORD.
KeyStory: David bought Ornan’s threshing floor to build an altar to the LORD (1 Chronicles 21); Solomon built the temple at Jerusalem in Mount Moriah, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, in the place David had prepared (2 Chronicles 3:1).
LifeLesson: The place of sacrifice and worship often begins in an ordinary person’s field.

Name: Orpah
Summary: Orpah, a Moabitess, married Chilion, son of Naomi; after her husband's death she kissed Naomi farewell and returned to her own people, unlike Ruth.
KeyStory: Orpah, Naomi's daughter-in-law, wept with Ruth at the parting, but when Naomi urged her to return, Orpah kissed her mother-in-law and went back to Moab.
RelatedPeople: Naomi; Ruth; Chilion, Son of Elimelech
LifeLesson: Orpah's farewell was not faithlessness — she did what Naomi herself urged.

Name: Othni, Son of Shemaiah
Summary: Son of Shemaiah son of Obed-edom, mighty man of valour.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:7: Son of Shemaiah son of Obed-edom, mighty man of valour.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Othni stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ozem, Son of Jerahmeel
Summary: Son of Jerahmeel, named among the sons of Jerahmeel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:25: Son of Jerahmeel, named among the sons of Jerahmeel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ozem stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ozem, Son of Jesse
Summary: Sixth son of Jesse and brother of David.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:15: Sixth son of Jesse and brother of David.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ozem stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Paarai the Arbite
Summary: Paarai the Arbite was among David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Paarai the Arbite stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: An Arbite among the thirty — the tribes fought side by side.

Name: Padon
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Pahath-moab
Summary: Head of a large returning family (2,812 in Ezra 2:6); his sons returned with Ezra, built the wall, and sealed the covenant (Ezra 2:6, 8:4, 10:30; Nehemiah 3:11, 7:11, 10:14).
KeyStory: Return from exile
KeyVerses: Ezra 2:6; Ezra 8:4; Ezra 10:30; Nehemiah 3:11; Nehemiah 7:11; Nehemiah 10:14
LifeLesson: A family's faithfulness can span the return, the building, and the renewal.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Palal, Son of Uzai
Summary: Palal son of Uzai, named in Nehemiah 3:25.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Pallu, Son of Reuben
Summary: Son of Reuben the firstborn of Israel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:3: Son of Reuben the firstborn of Israel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Pallu stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Parmashta
Summary: One of the ten sons of Haman, slain by the Jews in Shushan and afterwards hanged on the gallows.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: A house built on hatred falls with its builder.

Name: Parmenas
Summary: Parmenas was one of the seven men chosen to serve tables in the Jerusalem church. Acts names him among the seven and records nothing further of him by name.
KeyStory: Parmenas was chosen with the seven, men of honest report, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom.
LifeLesson: A church that feeds its widows fairly needs honest hands. Parmenas was one of them.

Name: Parosh
Summary: Head of a family listed among those who returned from exile.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: A family's return is recorded household by household.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Parshandatha
Summary: One of the ten sons of Haman, slain by the Jews in Shushan and afterwards hanged on the gallows.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: A house built on hatred falls with its builder.

Name: Paruah, Father of Jehoshaphat the Officer
Summary: Paruah was the father of Jehoshaphat, Solomon's officer over Issachar.
KeyStory: Paruah, father of the officer.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Pasach
Summary: Son of Japhlet, named among the children of Japhlet.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:33: Son of Japhlet, named among the children of Japhlet.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Pasach stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Paseah
Summary: Son of Eshton, named in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:12: Son of Eshton, named in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Paseah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Pashur, Father of Jeroham
Summary: Father of Jeroham in the Jerusalem priest list, son of Malchijah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:12: Father of Jeroham in the Jerusalem priest list, son of Malchijah.
LifeLesson: The mention of Pashur in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Pashur, Son of Immer
Role: Priest; Chief Governor of the Temple
Summary: Pashur, son of Immer the priest, was chief governor in the house of the Lord. When Jeremiah prophesied in the temple court, Pashur struck him and put him in the stocks overnight. Jeremiah renamed him Magor-missabib — terror on every side — and foretold his captivity in Babylon.
KeyStory: Pashur smote Jeremiah and put him in the stocks at the high gate of Benjamin, and in the morning Jeremiah told him his name would be Terror on every side.
LifeLesson: Using temple authority to punish a prophet turns the punisher into the prophecy's example.

Name: Pashur, Son of Malchiah
Summary: Pashur, son of Malchiah, was sent by Zedekiah to ask Jeremiah whether God would deal with Babylon, and later joined the princes who demanded Jeremiah's death and had him cast into Malchiah's dungeon. He is a different man from Pashur son of Immer.
KeyStory: Zedekiah sent Pashur son of Malchiah to enquire of the Lord about Nebuchadnezzar's war, and Jeremiah answered that the city would be given into Babylon's hand.
RelatedPeople: Zedekiah, King of Judah; Jeremiah; Gedaliah, Son of Pashur
LifeLesson: Asking God's counsel while planning to kill his messenger shows the question was never honest.

Name: Pashur
Summary: Head of a priestly family that returned with Zerubbabel; his sons are named among those who took foreign wives, and a Pashur sealed the covenant.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: One family's story can hold both return and repentance.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Patrobas
Summary: Patrobas was a Christian in Rome greeted by Paul alongside Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, and Hermes.
KeyStory: Patrobas was a Christian in Rome greeted by Paul alongside Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, and Hermes.
LifeLesson: The church is built of named individuals, not anonymous crowds.

Name: Pedaiah, Father of Zebudah
Summary: Pedaiah of Rumah was the father of Zebudah, mother of Jehoiakim.
KeyStory: Pedaiah, father of Zebudah.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Pedaiah, Son of Jeconiah
Summary: Son of Jeconiah and father of Zerubbabel and Shimei.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:18: Son of Jeconiah and father of Zerubbabel and Shimei.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Pedaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Pedaiah, Son of Kolaiah
Summary: Pedaiah son of Kolaiah, named in Nehemiah 11:7.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Pedaiah
Summary: Stood beside Ezra at the reading of the law (Nehemiah 8:4), repaired a section of the wall as son of Parosh (Nehemiah 3:25), and served as a treasurer over the storehouses (Nehemiah 13:13).
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: One Levite could stand, build, and keep the storehouses.
RelatedEvents: Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall; Ezra Reads the Law

Name: Pekah, King of Israel
Summary: Pekah, son of Remaliah, seized the throne by murder, allied with Rezin of Syria against Ahaz, and lost Israel's northern cities to Tiglath-pileser before Hoshea slew him.
KeyStory: Pekah allies with Rezin and loses the north to Assyria.
RelatedPeople: Pekahiah, King of Israel; Rezin, King of Syria; Ahaz, King of Judah; Tiglath-Pileser, King of Assyria; Remaliah, Father of Pekah; Hoshea, King of Israel; Isaiah
LifeLesson: An alliance against God's people invites the very empire it fears.

Name: Pekah, Son of Remaliah
Summary: Pekah, son of Remaliah, slew a hundred and twenty thousand valiant men of Judah in one day because they had forsaken the LORD, and carried away two hundred thousand captives to Samaria.
KeyStory: Pekah's slaughter of Judah was answered by Oded's rebuke, and the captives were clothed, fed and returned to Jericho.
RelatedPeople: Ahaz, King of Judah; Oded, Prophet of Samaria
LifeLesson: Victory won in rage against brethren invites God's rebuke, not His blessing.

Name: Pekahiah, King of Israel
Summary: Pekahiah, son of Menahem, reigned two years and did evil, and was slain in the palace at Samaria by his captain Pekah, with Argob and Arieh.
KeyStory: Pekahiah slain by his captain Pekah.
