RelatedPeople: Menahem, King of Israel; Pekah, King of Israel; Argob, Officer of Pekahiah; Arieh, Officer of Pekahiah
LifeLesson: The palace guard that crowns a king can unmake him just as fast.

Name: Pelaiah
Summary: Son of Elioenai son of Neariah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:24: Son of Elioenai son of Neariah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Pelaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Pelaliah, Son of Amzi
Summary: Pelaliah son of Amzi, named in Nehemiah 11:12.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Pelatiah, Son of Hananiah
Summary: Son of Hananiah son of Zerubbabel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:21: Son of Hananiah son of Zerubbabel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Pelatiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Pelatiah, Son of Ishi
Summary: Son of Ishi and captain of the five hundred Simeonites who went to Mount Seir.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:42: Son of Ishi and captain of the five hundred Simeonites who went to Mount Seir.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Pelatiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Pelatiah
Summary: Pelatiah, son of Benaiah, was one of the twenty-five princes at the east gate of the temple; as Ezekiel prophesied against them in vision, Pelatiah fell down dead, and Ezekiel cried out at the judgment.
KeyStory: While Ezekiel prophesied against the princes at the east gate, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died, and Ezekiel fell on his face and cried out to the Lord.
LifeLesson: Judgment can fall in the very moment the word is spoken — the prophecy is not a warning about someday, but about now.

Name: Pelet, Son of Azmaveth
Summary: Son of Azmaveth who came to David at Ziklag.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:3: Son of Azmaveth who came to David at Ziklag.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Pelet stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Pelet, Son of Jahdai
Summary: Son of Jahdai, named in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:47: Son of Jahdai, named in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Pelet stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Peleth, Son of Jonathan
Summary: Son of Jonathan son of Jada.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:33: Son of Jonathan son of Jada.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Peleth stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Peninnah
Role: Wife of Elkanah; Rival of Hannah
Summary: Peninnah was Elkanah's other wife. She had children and provoked Hannah bitterly because Hannah had none, year after year at Shiloh.
KeyStory: Peninnah's provoking drove Hannah to pray the prayer that gave Israel Samuel.
LifeLesson: Words used to wound can become the pressure that drives someone to God — and a warning about how we use our own.

Name: Penuel, Father of Gedor
Summary: Son of Hur, called the father of Gedor.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:4: Son of Hur, called the father of Gedor.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Penuel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Penuel, Son of Shashak
Summary: Named among the sons of Shashak in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:25: Named among the sons of Shashak in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Penuel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Peresh
Summary: Son of Machir by Maachah, and brother of Sheresh.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:16: Son of Machir by Maachah, and brother of Sheresh.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Peresh stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Persis
Summary: Persis was a beloved woman in the Roman church who laboured much in the Lord.
KeyStory: Persis was a beloved woman in the Roman church who laboured much in the Lord.
LifeLesson: Much labour in the Lord is remembered with love, not measured by visibility.

Name: Peruda
Summary: Descendant of Solomon's servants listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Service in God's house spans generations.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Pethahiah, Son of Meshezabeel
Summary: Pethahiah son of Meshezabeel, named in Nehemiah 11:24.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Pethahiah
Summary: Nineteenth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:16: Nineteenth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
LifeLesson: The mention of Pethahiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Pethuel
Summary: Pethuel is named only as the father of the prophet Joel (Joel 1:1). Nothing else is told of him.
KeyStory: Pethuel's only mention is as Joel's father, in the opening line of his son's prophecy.
LifeLesson: Like Beeri, Pethuel is remembered for a son God used. Faithful obscurity is still faithfulness.

Name: Peulthai
Summary: Eighth son of Obed-edom the porter.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:5: Eighth son of Obed-edom the porter.
LifeLesson: The mention of Peulthai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Phalti, Son of Laish
Summary: Phalti, son of Laish of Gallim, was given Michal as wife after Saul took her from David. When David demanded her back, Phalti followed weeping behind her until Abner sent him home.
KeyStory: Palti wept as he followed Michal back to David, a husband caught in a king's bargain.
LifeLesson: Even a weeping walk home is part of the record; God notices the collateral damage of power.

Name: Pharaoh Necho
Summary: Pharaoh-necho was king of Egypt whose army was defeated by Nebuchadnezzar at Carchemish by the Euphrates; Jeremiah's oracle against Egypt is dated to that battle, and Necho had earlier carried Shallum son of Josiah away to Egypt.
KeyStory: At Carchemish, Nebuchadnezzar smote the army of Pharaoh-necho, and Jeremiah declared that Egypt's day of the Lord's vengeance had come.
RelatedPeople: Shallum, Son of Josiah; King Nebuchadnezzar
LifeLesson: Egypt's power, like every empire's, had a Carchemish waiting for it.

Name: Pharosh
Summary: Head of a father's house who returned with Ezra.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: Heads of houses led their families home.

Name: Philemon
Role: Master of Onesimus and host of a house church
Summary: Philemon was Paul's dearly beloved fellowlabourer, in whose house a church met; Paul wrote to him asking him to receive back his runaway servant Onesimus no longer as a servant but as a brother beloved.
KeyStory: Philemon was Paul's dearly beloved fellowlabourer, in whose house a church met; Paul wrote to him asking him to receive back his runaway servant Onesimus no longer as a servant but as a brother beloved.
LifeLesson: The gospel turns a master and a runaway into brothers; forgiveness remakes relationships.

Name: Philetus
Summary: Philetus is named in 2 Timothy with Hymenaeus as one whose word ate as a canker, teaching that the resurrection was past already and overthrowing the faith of some.
KeyStory: Philetus is named in 2 Timothy with Hymenaeus as one whose word ate as a canker, teaching that the resurrection was past already and overthrowing the faith of some.
LifeLesson: Error spreads quietly; naming it plainly protects the faith of others.

Name: Philip the Tetrarch
Summary: Philip the Tetrarch, a son of Herod the Great, ruled the north-eastern territories when John the Baptist began preaching. He is distinct from the apostle Philip and from Philip the Evangelist.
KeyStory: Luke names Philip among the rulers of the year the word of God came to John in the wilderness.
LifeLesson: God's story runs on a dated calendar of real rulers. Luke anchors the gospel in history, not myth.

Name: Philologus
Summary: Philologus was a Christian in Rome greeted by Paul alongside Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas.
KeyStory: Philologus was a Christian in Rome greeted by Paul alongside Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas.
LifeLesson: Greetings in Scripture remind us that fellowship is personal.

Name: Phinehas, Son of Eli
Summary: Phinehas, son of Eli, served as a priest at Shiloh with his brother Hophni. Both men abused the offerings, and both died when the Philistines captured the ark. His wife died naming her son Ichabod, 'the glory is departed.'
KeyStory: Phinehas died on the day the ark was taken, and his son was named for the glory that had left Israel.
RelatedPeople: Eli; Hophni; Ichabod, Son of Phinehas; Ahitub, Son of Phinehas
LifeLesson: Sin in a priest's house does not stay private; it costs a whole nation its sense of God's presence.

Name: Phlegon
Summary: Phlegon was a Christian in Rome greeted by Paul alongside Asyncritus, Hermas, Patrobas, and Hermes.
KeyStory: Phlegon was a Christian in Rome greeted by Paul alongside Asyncritus, Hermas, Patrobas, and Hermes.
LifeLesson: Faithfulness in an ordinary congregation is the ordinary stuff of the kingdom.

Name: Phurah, Servant of Gideon
Summary: Phurah was Gideon's servant, who went with him by night to the edge of the Midianite camp, where they overheard the dream that strengthened Gideon.
KeyStory: When Gideon feared to go down to the host, God told him to take Phurah his servant; together they heard a Midianite tell his dream of a barley cake overturning a tent, and Gideon worshipped.
LifeLesson: Courage sometimes needs one companion in the dark.

Name: Phygellus
Role: One who turned away from Paul in Asia
Summary: Phygellus was one of those in Asia who turned away from Paul, named with Hermogenes in 2 Timothy.
KeyStory: Phygellus was one of those in Asia who turned away from Paul, named with Hermogenes in 2 Timothy.
LifeLesson: Turning away in hard times is recorded soberly, as a warning to the rest.

Name: Pileha
Summary: Chief who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10).
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: A signature on a covenant is a public stand.

Name: Piltai
Summary: Priest in the days of Joiakim.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Courses of priests kept worship ordered across generations.

Name: Pispah
Summary: Son of Jether in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:38: Son of Jether in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Pispah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Pithon
Summary: Son of Micah, named among the sons of Micah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:35; 1 Chronicles 9:41: Son of Micah, named among the sons of Micah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Pithon stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Pochereth
Summary: Descendant of Solomon's servants listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Service in God's house spans generations.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Pontius Pilate
Summary: Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor who tried Jesus. He repeatedly declared he found no fault in Him, yet handed Him over to be crucified to satisfy the crowd, washing his hands of the verdict.
KeyStory: Pilate asked, What is truth?, then gave the order he did not believe in.
LifeLesson: Knowing the right verdict is not the same as giving it. Pilate warns us against trading conscience for quiet.

Name: Poratha
Summary: One of the ten sons of Haman, slain by the Jews in Shushan and afterwards hanged on the gallows.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: A house built on hatred falls with its builder.

Name: Prochorus
Summary: Prochorus was one of the seven men chosen to serve tables in the Jerusalem church, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom. Tradition later links him with John, though Acts says nothing further of him.
KeyStory: Prochorus was chosen with six others to carry the daily distribution, freeing the apostles for prayer and the word.
LifeLesson: The church's first officers were chosen for character, not for show. Prochorus served tables and is remembered.

Name: Puah, Father of Tola
Summary: Puah is named only as the father of Tola the judge, in the line of Dodo. He is distinct from Puah the midwife in Exodus.
KeyStory: Puah appears in Judges only as Tola's father.
RelatedPeople: Tola, Son of Puah; Dodo, Father of Puah
LifeLesson: Two people can share a name and nothing else — the line, not the name, tells them apart.

Name: Publius
Summary: Publius was the chief man of Malta who courteously lodged Paul's shipwrecked company for three days, and whose father Paul healed of fever and dysentery, after which others on the island came and were healed.
KeyStory: Publius lodged the shipwrecked company three days, and his father's healing opened the island to Paul.
LifeLesson: Hospitality to strangers became healing for an island. Publius lodged Paul and found his father whole.

Name: Pudens
Summary: Pudens was one of the believers with Paul in Rome who sends greetings in 2 Timothy, alongside Eubulus, Linus, and Claudia.
KeyStory: Pudens was one of the believers with Paul in Rome who sends greetings in 2 Timothy, alongside Eubulus, Linus, and Claudia.
LifeLesson: A name in a final greeting marks presence at the hardest hour.

Name: Pul, King of Assyria
Summary: King of Assyria stirred up by God to carry away the Reubenites, Gadites, and half tribe of Manasseh.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:26: King of Assyria stirred up by God to carry away the Reubenites, Gadites, and half tribe of Manasseh.
LifeLesson: The mention of Pul in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Quartus
Summary: Quartus is named in Romans 16:23 simply as a brother, sending greetings with Paul's letter.
KeyStory: Quartus is named in Romans 16:23 simply as a brother, sending greetings with Paul's letter.
LifeLesson: To be called simply a brother is a complete identity in Christ.

Name: Queen of Sheba
Summary: The queen of Sheba, hearing of Solomon's fame, came to Jerusalem with hard questions and great gifts, and declared that the half of his wisdom had not been told her, before returning to her own land.
KeyStory: The queen of Sheba tests Solomon with hard questions.
LifeLesson: True wisdom invites hard questions; it does not fear them.

Name: Quirinius
Summary: Quirinius (spelled Cyrenius in the King James Version) was governor of Syria at the time of the census that brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem for Jesus' birth.
KeyStory: Luke ties the census of Jesus' birth to the governorship of Cyrenius in Syria.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Mary, Mother of Jesus; Joseph, Husband of Mary; Caesar Augustus
LifeLesson: Luke names names and offices because the birth he reports is history. The details invite checking, not blind trust.

Name: Raddai
Summary: Fifth son of Jesse and brother of David.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:14: Fifth son of Jesse and brother of David.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Raddai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Raham
Summary: Son of Shema, called the father of Jorkoam.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:44: Son of Shema, called the father of Jorkoam.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Raham stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Rakem
Summary: Son of Peresh, named beside Ulam.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:16: Son of Peresh, named beside Ulam.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Rakem stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ram, Son of Hezron
Summary: Ram appears in Ruth's genealogy as the son of Hezron and father of Amminadab, in the line from Pharez to David.
KeyStory: Ram stands in the closing genealogy between Hezron and Amminadab, in the line that runs from Pharez to David.
LifeLesson: One generation's whole record can be a single line — and still matter.

Name: Ram, Son of Jerahmeel
Summary: Firstborn son of Jerahmeel and father of Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:25: Firstborn son of Jerahmeel and father of Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ram stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ramiah, Son of Parosh
Summary: Son of Parosh named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Ramoth, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:29).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Returning from exile meant returning to the covenant.

Name: Rapha, Son of Benjamin
Summary: Fifth son of Benjamin, named among the sons of Benjamin.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:2: Fifth son of Benjamin, named among the sons of Benjamin.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Rapha stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Rapha, Son of Binea
Summary: Son of Binea and father of Eleasah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:37; 1 Chronicles 9:43: Son of Binea and father of Eleasah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Rapha stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Reaia, Son of Micah
Summary: Son of Micah and father of Baal in Reuben's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:5: Son of Micah and father of Baal in Reuben's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Reaia stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Reaiah, Son of Shobal
Summary: Son of Shobal and father of Jahath.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:2: Son of Shobal and father of Jahath.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Reaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Reaiah
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Rechab, Father of Jehonadab
Summary: Rechab was the father of Jehonadab, who rode with Jehu against Baal.
KeyStory: Rechab, father of Jehonadab.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Rechab, Son of Rimmon
Summary: Rechab, son of Rimmon the Beerothite and a captain of Ish-bosheth's bands, murdered Ish-bosheth in his bed at noon and carried his head to David, expecting reward. David had him and his brother executed for killing a righteous man in his own house.
KeyStory: Rechab murdered his own king for a reward and was executed for it the same day.
RelatedPeople: Ish-bosheth, Son of Saul; Baanah, Son of Rimmon; King David
LifeLesson: Murder offered as a gift is still murder, and a just king refuses the price.

Name: Rechab
Summary: Ancestor of the house of Rechab, named among the scribes' families at Jabez.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:55: Ancestor of the house of Rechab, named among the scribes' families at Jabez.
LifeLesson: The mention of Rechab in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Reelaiah
Summary: A leader who returned with Zerubbabel; Nehemiah's copy of the list spells the name Raamiah.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Two copies of one list can spell one man's name two ways.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Regem
Summary: Son of Jahdai, named in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:47: Son of Jahdai, named in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Regem stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Regemmelech
Summary: Regemmelech (KJV 'Regem-melech') was sent with Sherezer from Bethel to Jerusalem to pray before the LORD and ask about the fasts of the exile (Zechariah 7:2).
KeyStory: Regemmelech, sent with Sherezer from Bethel, asked whether the fasts of the exile should continue — and heard God's answer about justice over ritual.
LifeLesson: Regemmelech's question got an answer bigger than fasting: God wanted mercy, not mourning. Ask God about your habits; expect Him to examine your heart.

Name: Rehabiah, Son of Eliezer, Treasurer
Summary: Son of Eliezer, in the treasurers' line by Eliezer.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:25: Son of Eliezer, in the treasurers' line by Eliezer.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Rehabiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Rehabiah, Son of Eliezer
Summary: Chief of the sons of Eliezer son of Moses, whose sons were very many.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 23:17: Chief of the sons of Eliezer son of Moses, whose sons were very many.
LifeLesson: The mention of Rehabiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Rehob
Summary: Rehob is named as the father of Hadadezer, king of Zobah, David's Syrian enemy.
KeyStory: Rehob's son built the Syrian power David broke.
LifeLesson: A father's name rides on his son's wars, for good or ill.

Name: Rehum, Chancellor
Summary: Chancellor under the Persian administration who, with Shimshai the scribe, wrote to Artaxerxes against Jerusalem's rebuilding and succeeded in halting it for a time.
KeyStory: Rebuilding of the Temple
LifeLesson: Opposition to God's work often arrives in official dress.

Name: Rehum, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani who repaired part of Jerusalem's wall.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: God's work is done by many hands, each named.

Name: Rehum
Role: Leader of the Return; Covenant Sealer
Summary: A leader who returned with Zerubbabel — Nehemiah's copy of the list reads Nehum — and later sealed the covenant. A different Rehum from the Persian chancellor.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Two men can share a name and serve on opposite sides of a wall.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Rei, Officer of David
Summary: Rei was one of David's men who, with Zadok, Benaiah, Nathan, and Shimei, refused to join Adonijah's bid for the throne.
KeyStory: Rei refuses Adonijah.
RelatedPeople: King David; Zadok, High Priest; Benaiah, Son of Jehoiada; Nathan
LifeLesson: Standing aside from a coup is itself a stand.

Name: Rekem, Son of Hebron
Summary: Son of Hebron son of Mareshah and father of Shammai.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:43: Son of Hebron son of Mareshah and father of Shammai.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Rekem stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Remaliah, Father of Pekah
Summary: Remaliah was the father of Pekah, king of Israel.
KeyStory: Remaliah, father of Pekah.
RelatedPeople: Pekah, King of Israel; Pekah, Son of Remaliah
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Rephael, Son of Shemaiah
Summary: Son of Shemaiah son of Obed-edom, mighty man of valour.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:7: Son of Shemaiah son of Obed-edom, mighty man of valour.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Rephael stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Rephah
Summary: Son of Ephraim, named in Ephraim's line after Beriah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:25: Son of Ephraim, named in Ephraim's line after Beriah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Rephah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Rephaiah, Son of Hur
Summary: Son of Hur, ruler of half of Jerusalem, who repaired a section of the wall (Nehemiah 3:9).
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: Leaders lead by building, not only by ruling.

Name: Rephaiah, Son of Ishi
Summary: Son of Ishi and captain of the five hundred Simeonites who went to Mount Seir.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:42: Son of Ishi and captain of the five hundred Simeonites who went to Mount Seir.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Rephaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Rephaiah, Son of Jesaiah
Summary: Named in the chain of sons after Hananiah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:21: Named in the chain of sons after Hananiah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Rephaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Rephaiah, Son of Tola
Summary: Son of Tola and head of his father's house, a valiant man of might.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:2: Son of Tola and head of his father's house, a valiant man of might.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Rephaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Resheph
Summary: Son of Rephah and father of Telah in Ephraim's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:25: Son of Rephah and father of Telah in Ephraim's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Resheph stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Reuel, Father of Shephathiah
Summary: Father of Shephathiah in the Jerusalem list, son of Ibnijah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:8: Father of Shephathiah in the Jerusalem list, son of Ibnijah.
LifeLesson: The mention of Reuel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Rezia
Summary: Son of Ulla in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:39: Son of Ulla in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Rezia stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Rezin, King of Syria
Summary: Rezin, king of Syria, allied with Pekah against Ahaz, besieged Jerusalem without taking it, took Elath for Syria, and was slain when Tiglath-Pileser took Damascus.
KeyStory: Rezin besieges Jerusalem and is slain at Damascus.
RelatedPeople: Pekah, King of Israel; Ahaz, King of Judah; Tiglath-Pileser, King of Assyria; Isaiah
LifeLesson: A siege that fails still leaves its mark, and its maker still falls.

Name: Rezin
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Rezon, King of Damascus
Summary: Rezon, son of Eliadah, fled from his lord Hadadezer of Zobah, gathered men, became captain, and reigned in Damascus as an adversary to Solomon all his days.
KeyStory: Rezon becomes Solomon's adversary in Damascus.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Hadadezer, King of Zobah; Eliadah, Father of Rezon
LifeLesson: A runaway servant can become a king, and a king an adversary.

Name: Rhoda
Summary: Rhoda was the servant girl who answered Peter's knock at Mary's house in Jerusalem on the night of his escape from prison. Recognising his voice, she ran back in joy without opening the gate, leaving Peter knocking outside.
KeyStory: Rhoda heard Peter's voice at the gate and ran to tell the praying church, forgetting to let him in.
LifeLesson: Joy can make us forget the door. Rhoda's church prayed for Peter's release and could hardly believe it came.

Name: Ribai, Father of Ittai
Summary: Ribai of Gibeah is named as the father of Ittai, one of David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Ribai's son stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: Gibeah, Saul's own town, gave David a mighty man.

Name: Ribai
Summary: Father of Ithai of Gibeah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:31: Father of Ithai of Gibeah.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ribai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Rimmon the Beerothite
Summary: Rimmon the Beerothite was the father of Rechab and Baanah, the captains who murdered Ish-bosheth and were executed by David.
KeyStory: Rimmon's sons became the assassins whose crime ended Saul's house.
RelatedPeople: Rechab, Son of Rimmon; Baanah, Son of Rimmon
LifeLesson: Sons can turn a father's name into a byword for treachery.

Name: Rinnah
Summary: Son of Shimon in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:20: Son of Shimon in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Rinnah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Rizpah, Daughter of Aiah
Summary: Rizpah, daughter of Aiah and concubine of Saul, was the mother of Armoni and Mephibosheth. After her sons were hanged, she spread sackcloth on a rock and guarded their bodies from birds and beasts from harvest until rain fell, shaming David into burying Saul's house properly.
KeyStory: Rizpah guarded her hanged sons' bodies for months on a rock, until the king buried them.
RelatedPeople: King Saul; Armoni, Son of Saul; Mephibosheth, Son of Saul; Abner, Son of Ner
LifeLesson: A mother's vigil on a rock can move a king to do the just thing at last.

Name: Rohgah
Summary: Son of Shamer in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:34: Son of Shamer in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Rohgah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Romamti-ezer, Son of Heman
Summary: Son of Heman the king's seer, four and twentieth lot for song.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 25:4; 1 Chronicles 25:31: Son of Heman the king's seer, four and twentieth lot for song.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Romamti-ezer stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Rufus of Rome
Summary: Rufus was a Roman Christian described by Paul as chosen in the Lord, and Paul also greets Rufus's mother, who had been like a mother to Paul himself.
KeyStory: Rufus was a Roman Christian described by Paul as chosen in the Lord, and Paul also greets Rufus's mother, who had been like a mother to Paul himself.
LifeLesson: A mother's care for God's servants is itself a ministry, honoured in Scripture.

Name: Rufus, Son of Simon of Cyrene
Summary: Rufus was a son of Simon of Cyrene, named by Mark alongside his brother Alexander. Paul later greets a Rufus, chosen in the Lord, in Rome, who may be the same man, though the text does not say so.
KeyStory: Mark names Rufus only as the son of the man who carried Jesus' cross.
RelatedPeople: Simon of Cyrene; Alexander, Son of Simon of Cyrene
LifeLesson: A name in one verse can outlive an empire. Rufus is remembered because his father carried a cross.

Name: Sacar, Son of Obed-edom
Summary: Fourth son of Obed-edom the porter.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:4: Fourth son of Obed-edom the porter.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Sacar stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Sacar
Summary: Father of Ahiam the Hararite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:35: Father of Ahiam the Hararite.
LifeLesson: The mention of Sacar in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Salathiel, Son of Jeconiah
Summary: Son of Jeconiah in the post-exilic royal line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:17: Son of Jeconiah in the post-exilic royal line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Salathiel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Sallai the Benjaminite
Summary: Benjaminite resident of Jerusalem, counted with 928 men of Benjamin (Nehemiah 11:8).
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Jerusalem was resettled household by household.

Name: Sallai the Priest
Summary: Head of Sallai's priestly course in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:20).
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: A priestly course bore its head's name.

Name: Sallu, Son of Meshullam
Summary: Son of Meshullam son of Hodaviah son of Hasenuah, of the sons of Benjamin dwelling in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:7: Son of Meshullam son of Hodaviah son of Hasenuah, of the sons of Benjamin dwelling in Jerusalem.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Sallu stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Sallu
Summary: Priest who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Nehemiah 12:7).
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Returning priests restored worship before walls were rebuilt.

Name: Salma, Son of Caleb
Summary: Son of Caleb son of Hur, called the father of Beth-lehem.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:51: Son of Caleb son of Hur, called the father of Beth-lehem.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Salma stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Salma, Son of Nahshon
Summary: Son of Nahshon and father of Boaz in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:11: Son of Nahshon and father of Boaz in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Salma stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Salmon, Son of Nahshon
Summary: Salmon appears in Ruth's genealogy as the son of Nahshon and father of Boaz, in the line from Pharez to David.
KeyStory: Salmon stands in the closing genealogy between Nahshon and Boaz, in the line that runs from Pharez to David.
LifeLesson: Salmon fathered Boaz, who married Ruth — the genealogy's quiet hinge.

Name: Salome
Role: Disciple; Witness of the Crucifixion and Resurrection
Summary: Salome was one of the women who followed Jesus in Galilee, watched the crucifixion from afar, and came to the tomb on the first day of the week. Tradition identifies her as the mother of James and John, the sons of Zebedee.
KeyStory: Salome stood at a distance at the cross and came early to the tomb, and heard that He was risen.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Mary Magdalene; Mary, Mother of James and Joses; James, Son of Zebedee; John the Apostle
LifeLesson: Salome stayed when staying cost everything, and came early when hope was gone. Faithful presence is its own witness.

Name: Sanballat
Summary: Horonite governor of Samaria who mocked, threatened, and plotted against Nehemiah's wall at every stage.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
KeyVerses: Nehemiah 2:10; Nehemiah 2:19; Nehemiah 4:1; Nehemiah 4:7; Nehemiah 6:1; Nehemiah 6:2; Nehemiah 6:5; Nehemiah 6:12; Nehemiah 6:14; Nehemiah 13:28
LifeLesson: Mockery is often the first weapon against God's work.

Name: Saph
Summary: Saph, a descendant of the giant, was slain by Sibbechai the Hushathite in the battle at Gob during David's later wars with the Philistines.
KeyStory: Saph fell to Sibbecai at Gob in David's later Philistine wars.
LifeLesson: The giants' sons fall like their fathers before them.

Name: Sapphira
Summary: Sapphira conspired with her husband Ananias to keep back part of their land's price while claiming the whole. When Peter questioned her three hours after her husband's death, she repeated the lie and fell dead as well.
KeyStory: Sapphira agreed with her husband's lie and, questioned alone, told it again and fell at Peter's feet.
RelatedPeople: Ananias, Husband of Sapphira; Simon Peter
LifeLesson: A lie agreed together is still a lie each one tells. Sapphira had three hours to repent and used them to repeat.

Name: Saraph
Summary: Named among the ancient men of Shelah's line who had dominion in Moab.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:22: Named among the ancient men of Shelah's line who had dominion in Moab.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Saraph stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Sargon
Summary: Sargon was king of Assyria who sent his commander against Ashdod and captured it; Isaiah used the event as a sign of Assyria's coming captivity of Egypt and Ethiopia.
KeyStory: In the year Tartan came to Ashdod, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, Isaiah walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign against Egypt and Ethiopia.
LifeLesson: God sometimes makes his prophets a living picture of a message people would rather not hear.

Name: Sceva
Summary: Sceva was a Jewish chief priest whose seven sons attempted to cast out an evil spirit using the name of Jesus whom Paul preached. The possessed man overpowered them, and they fled naked and wounded, so that the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified at Ephesus.
KeyStory: Sceva's seven sons borrowed Paul's Jesus and were beaten naked by the spirit they could not command.
LifeLesson: The name of Jesus is not a charm to borrow. Sceva's sons learned that authority comes from knowing Him, not naming Him.

Name: Secundus
Summary: Secundus was a Thessalonian who accompanied Paul on his journey toward Jerusalem with the collection for the saints, travelling with the company as far as Troas.
KeyStory: Secundus of Thessalonica walked with Paul's company toward Jerusalem, bearing the churches' gift.
LifeLesson: Secundus is named once, on a road to Jerusalem with a gift. The road remembers its walkers.

Name: Segub, Son of Hiel
Summary: Segub was Hiel's youngest son, in whom Hiel set up Jericho's gates, according to the word of Joshua.
KeyStory: Segub, in whom Jericho's gates were set up.
RelatedPeople: Hiel the Bethelite; Abiram, Son of Hiel
LifeLesson: The curse finished what it started, firstborn to youngest.

Name: Segub
Summary: Son of Hezron by the daughter of Machir, and father of Jair.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:21: Son of Hezron by the daughter of Machir, and father of Jair.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Segub stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Seled
Summary: Son of Nadab who died without children.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:30: Son of Nadab who died without children.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Seled stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Semachiah
Summary: Brother of Elzabad, strong man among the sons of Shemaiah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:7: Brother of Elzabad, strong man among the sons of Shemaiah.
LifeLesson: The mention of Semachiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Sennacherib, King of Assyria
Summary: Sennacherib, king of Assyria, took Judah's fenced cities, demanded Hezekiah's surrender, mocked the living God through the Rabshakeh, and lost a hundred and fourscore and five thousand men in one night to the angel of the LORD.
KeyStory: Sennacherib mocks God and loses his army in a night.
KeyVerses: 2 Kings 18:13; 2 Kings 19:35; 2 Chronicles 32:1; 2 Chronicles 32:9; 2 Chronicles 32:21; Isaiah 36:1; Isaiah 37:21-29; Isaiah 37:36-38
RelatedPeople: King Hezekiah; Isaiah; Eliakim, Son of Hilkiah; Adrammelech, Son of Sennacherib; Sharezer, Son of Sennacherib; Adrammelech; Sharezer
LifeLesson: Mocking the living God is the last boast an empire makes before morning.

Name: Senuah
Summary: Father of Judah, second over Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:9).
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: A father's name stands behind his son's office.

Name: Seorim
Summary: Fourth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:8: Fourth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Seorim stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Serah, Daughter of Asher
Summary: Daughter of Asher, named as sister of Imnah, Isuah, Ishuai, and Beriah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:30: Daughter of Asher, named as sister of Imnah, Isuah, Ishuai, and Beriah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Serah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Seraiah, Chief Priest
Summary: Seraiah the chief priest was taken by Nebuzaradan after Jerusalem's fall and slain at Riblah by the king of Babylon.
KeyStory: Seraiah slain at Riblah.
RelatedPeople: Nebuzaradan, Captain of the Guard; Zephaniah, Second Priest
LifeLesson: The chief priest's death at Riblah marked the end of temple service as Judah knew it.

Name: Seraiah, Father of Ezra
Summary: Father of Ezra the scribe; son of Azariah, in the priestly line from Aaron (Ezra 7:1).
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: Faithful lineage matters: Ezra's ministry stood on generations of priestly service.

Name: Seraiah, Son of Asiel
Summary: Son of Asiel and father of Josibiah in Simeon's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:35: Son of Asiel and father of Josibiah in Simeon's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Seraiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Seraiah, Son of Azariah
Summary: Son of Azariah and priest in Aaron's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:14: Son of Azariah and priest in Aaron's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Seraiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Seraiah, Son of Azriel
Summary: Seraiah, son of Azriel, was one of the officers Jehoiakim sent to seize Jeremiah and Baruch after the scroll was burned, but the Lord hid them. He is a different man from Seraiah son of Neriah, Seraiah the chief priest, and Seraiah son of Tanhumeth.
KeyStory: The king commanded Seraiah son of Azriel to take Jeremiah and Baruch, but the Lord hid them.
RelatedPeople: Jehoiakim, King of Judah; Jeremiah; Baruch
LifeLesson: A shared name does not mean a shared story — four Seraiahs walk through Jeremiah, and each must be told apart.

Name: Seraiah, Son of Hilkiah
Role: Ruler of the House of God
Summary: Priest dwelling in Jerusalem, son of Hilkiah, in the line of Zadok, Meraioth, and Ahitub, and ruler of the house of God (Nehemiah 11:11). Not Seraiah the father of Ezra.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Two men named Seraiah served God in different generations; the record tells them apart by their fathers.

Name: Seraiah, Son of Kenaz
Summary: Son of Kenaz and father of Joab, the father of the valley of Charashim.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:13: Son of Kenaz and father of Joab, the father of the valley of Charashim.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Seraiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Seraiah, Son of Neriah
Summary: Seraiah, son of Neriah and brother of Baruch, went with Zedekiah to Babylon and carried Jeremiah's written prophecy against Babylon; at Jeremiah's command he read it aloud and threw the book, tied to a stone, into the Euphrates as a sign that Babylon would sink and never rise.
KeyStory: Seraiah read the words against Babylon in Babylon itself, tied the book to a stone, and cast it into the Euphrates, saying: thus shall Babylon sink.
RelatedPeople: Baruch; Jeremiah; Zedekiah, King of Judah
LifeLesson: Proclaiming judgment in the heart of the empire takes the same courage as proclaiming it at home.

Name: Seraiah, Son of Tanhumeth
Summary: Seraiah, son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, was one of the captains who came to Gedaliah at Mizpah after the fall of Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Seraiah comes to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
RelatedPeople: Gedaliah, Son of Ahikam; Tanhumeth, Father of Seraiah; Gedaliah; Johanan, Son of Kareah
LifeLesson: Small names in a remnant list are still lives God kept.

Name: Seraiah the Chief Priest
Summary: Seraiah the chief priest was taken with Zephaniah the second priest to Riblah after Jerusalem fell, where the king of Babylon slew them. He is a different man from Seraiah son of Neriah, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Seraiah son of Tanhumeth.
KeyStory: Nebuzaradan took Seraiah the chief priest and Zephaniah the second priest to Riblah, and the king of Babylon smote them and put them to death.
LifeLesson: The highest religious office offers no shelter when the city it served has fallen.
RelatedEvents: Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile

Name: Seraiah
Summary: Seraiah was the scribe in David's administration, recording the kingdom's affairs beside Joab, Jehoshaphat, Zadok, and Abiathar.
KeyStory: Seraiah kept the records of David's kingdom at its height.
KeyVerses: 2 Samuel 8:17; Ezra 2:2; Nehemiah 7:7; Nehemiah 10:2; Nehemiah 12:1; Nehemiah 12:12
RelatedPeople: King David; Joab; Zadok, Son of Ahitub; Zerubbabel
LifeLesson: Kingdoms run on scribes whose names survive in a single verse.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Sergius Paulus
Summary: Sergius Paulus was the Roman proconsul of Cyprus, a prudent man who called for Barnabas and Saul to hear the word of God. When Elymas opposed them and was struck blind, the proconsul believed, astonished at the doctrine of the Lord.
KeyStory: Sergius Paulus sent for the word of God, watched his sorcerer go blind, and believed the doctrine of the Lord.
LifeLesson: A prudent ruler can still be astonished by the gospel. Sergius Paulus listened, watched, and believed.

Name: Shaaph, Son of Jahdai
Summary: Son of Jahdai, named in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:47: Son of Jahdai, named in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shaaph stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shaaph, Son of Maachah
Summary: Son of Caleb's concubine Maachah, called the father of Madmannah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:49: Son of Caleb's concubine Maachah, called the father of Madmannah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shaaph stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shaashgaz
Summary: Keeper of the king's second house, the house of the concubines, to which Esther would have returned had she not been chosen queen.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: God's purposes move through palace routines.

Name: Shabbethai
Summary: A Levite who stood against Ezra's plan, later taught the Law and oversaw the outward business of the house of God.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Opposition and service can live in one man's story.

Name: Shachia
Summary: Son of Shaharaim by Hodesh, head of his father's house.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:10: Son of Shaharaim by Hodesh, head of his father's house.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shachia stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shadrach
Summary: Shadrach was the Babylonian name given to Hananiah, one of the four Judean youths taken to Babylon; he was set over the affairs of the province of Babylon and, with Meshach and Abednego, refused to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image and was thrown into the burning fiery furnace, from which all three walked out unharmed. ONE profile covers both names; Hananiah is his Hebrew name, not a separate person.
KeyStory: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego told the king they would not serve his gods nor worship the golden image, and the fire that killed the men who threw them in did not even singe their clothes.
LifeLesson: Faith that will not bow does not need to know whether God will deliver — it obeys either way.
RelatedEvents: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the Fiery Furnace

Name: Shage
Summary: Father of Jonathan the Hararite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:34: Father of Jonathan the Hararite.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shage in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shaharaim
Summary: Begat children in the country of Moab after sending away his wives Hushim and Baara.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:8: Begat children in the country of Moab after sending away his wives Hushim and Baara.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shaharaim in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shallum, Ancestor of Ezra
Summary: Ancestor of Ezra named in his genealogy, son of Zadok.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: A long line of priests ends in a scribe.

Name: Shallum, Father of Jehizkiah
Summary: Shallum was the father of Jehizkiah, a head of Ephraim who opposed keeping Judah's captives.
KeyStory: Shallum is named only as the father of Jehizkiah the son of Shallum.
LifeLesson: A brief patronymic ties a merciful leader to his family.

Name: Shallum, Husband of Huldah
Summary: Shallum, son of Tikvah, keeper of the wardrobe, was the husband of Huldah the prophetess, to whom Josiah's messengers went.
KeyStory: Shallum, husband of Huldah.
RelatedPeople: Huldah, Prophetess; Tikvah, Father of Shallum
LifeLesson: A prophetess's husband kept the wardrobe; great and small serve side by side.

Name: Shallum, King of Israel
Summary: Shallum, son of Jabesh, conspired against Zachariah, smote him before the people, and reigned one month in Samaria before Menahem slew him.
KeyStory: Shallum's one-month reign.
RelatedPeople: Zachariah, King of Israel; Menahem, King of Israel; Jabesh, Father of Shallum
LifeLesson: A throne taken by murder is seldom kept longer than a month.

Name: Shallum, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Sin named honestly is the first step back to God.

Name: Shallum, Son of Halohesh
Summary: Son of Halohesh, ruler of half of Jerusalem, who repaired the wall with his daughters.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: Whole households, daughters included, build God's city.

Name: Shallum, Son of Josiah
Summary: Shallum, son of Josiah, also called Jehoahaz, reigned three months in Jerusalem before Pharaoh-necho carried him to Egypt, where he died. Jeremiah told his people not to weep for dead Josiah but for Shallum, who would never return.
KeyStory: Shallum reigned in his father Josiah's place, was taken to Egypt, and never saw his native land again.
RelatedPeople: King Josiah; Jehoiakim, King of Judah; Pharaoh Necho
LifeLesson: A three-month reign can still end in a permanent exile — length of rule is no measure of its weight.

Name: Shallum, Son of Kore
Summary: Chief porter, son of Kore son of Ebiasaph son of Korah, keeper of the gates of the tabernacle.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:17; 1 Chronicles 9:19: Chief porter, son of Kore son of Ebiasaph son of Korah, keeper of the gates of the tabernacle.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shallum in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shallum, Son of Naphtali
Summary: Son of Naphtali, named among the sons of Naphtali by Bilhah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:13: Son of Naphtali, named among the sons of Naphtali by Bilhah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shallum stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shallum, Son of Shaul
Summary: Son of Shaul son of Simeon and father of Mibsam.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:25: Son of Shaul son of Simeon and father of Mibsam.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shallum stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shallum, Son of Sisamai
Summary: Son of Sisamai and father of Jekamiah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:40: Son of Sisamai and father of Jekamiah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shallum stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shallum, Son of Tikvath
Summary: Shallum, son of Tikvath son of Hasrah and keeper of the wardrobe, was the husband of Huldah the prophetess, who dwelt in Jerusalem in the college.
KeyStory: Huldah was the wife of Shallum the son of Tikvath, the son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe.
RelatedPeople: Huldah, the Prophetess; Tikvath, Father of Shallum
LifeLesson: A prophetess's husband kept the wardrobe; God speaks through ordinary households.

Name: Shallum, Son of Zadok
Summary: Son of Zadok and priest in Aaron's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:12: Son of Zadok and priest in Aaron's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shallum stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shallum the Porter
Summary: Head of a porter family that returned with Zerubbabel and served again after the return.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Gatekeepers guard the house of God.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Shallun, Son of Col-hozeh
Summary: Son of Col-hozeh, ruler of Mizpah, who repaired the fountain gate and the wall of the pool of Siloah.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: God's work is done by many hands, each named.

Name: Shalmai
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Shalmaneser, King of Assyria
Summary: Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, came up against Hoshea, made him his servant, then besieged Samaria three years and carried Israel away to Assyria.
KeyStory: Shalmaneser besieges Samaria and carries Israel away.
RelatedPeople: Hoshea, King of Israel; So, King of Egypt
LifeLesson: The empire that Israel trusted instead of God became its captor.

Name: Shama, Son of Hothan
Summary: Son of Hothan the Aroerite, one of David's mighty men.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:44: Son of Hothan the Aroerite, one of David's mighty men.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shama stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shamariah, Son of Rehoboam
Summary: Shamariah was a son of Rehoboam by Mahalath, daughter of Jerimoth.
KeyStory: Mahalath bore Rehoboam children: Jeush, Shamariah and Zaham.
LifeLesson: God keeps His covenant through ordinary, briefly named lives.

Name: Shamed
Summary: Son of Elpaal, who built Ono and Lod with their towns.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:12: Son of Elpaal, who built Ono and Lod with their towns.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shamed stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shamer, Son of Asher
Summary: Father of Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:34: Father of Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shamer in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shamer, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani and father of Mahli in Ethan's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:46: Son of Bani and father of Mahli in Ethan's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shamer stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shamgar, Son of Anath
Summary: Shamgar, son of Anath, killed six hundred Philistines with an ox goad and also delivered Israel.
KeyStory: Shamgar, named between Ehud and Deborah, slew six hundred Philistines with an ox goad and also delivered Israel.
LifeLesson: Deliverance does not always come with an army — sometimes with a farmer's tool.

Name: Shamhuth the Izrahite
Summary: Captain over the fifth month's course, called the Izrahite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:8: Captain over the fifth month's course, called the Izrahite.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shamhuth in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shamir, Son of Michah
Summary: Son of Michah son of Uzziel in the rest of the sons of Levi.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:24: Son of Michah son of Uzziel in the rest of the sons of Levi.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shamir stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shamma, Son of Zophah
Summary: Son of Zophah in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:37: Son of Zophah in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shamma stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shammah, Son of Agee
Summary: Shammah, son of Agee the Hararite, was one of David's three mighty men. When the Philistines gathered at a field of lentiles and Israel fled, he stood in the middle of the field, defended it, and the Lord wrought a great victory.
KeyStory: Shammah held a lentil field alone against the Philistines — and God gave the victory.
RelatedPeople: King David; Eleazar, Son of Dodo; Agee, Father of Shammah
LifeLesson: Defending an ordinary field can be the greatest victory of a life.

Name: Shammah, Son of Jesse
Summary: Shammah, Jesse's third son, was passed over by Samuel at the anointing and served in Saul's army at Elah. He is also called Shimea and Shimeah in the record of David's family.
KeyStory: Shammah was the third son presented to Samuel and passed over, then stood with his brothers against Goliath's army.
RelatedPeople: Jesse; King David; Eliab, Son of Jesse; Abinadab, Son of Jesse
LifeLesson: The same man can be remembered under more than one name — God knows each one.

Name: Shammah the Hararite
Summary: Shammah the Hararite is named as the father of Jonathan, one of David's thirty mighty men. He is distinct from Shammah the Harodite and from Shammah son of Agee.
KeyStory: Shammah the Hararite fathered one of David's thirty.
LifeLesson: A Hararite father raised one of the thirty.

Name: Shammah the Harodite
Summary: Shammah the Harodite was among David's thirty mighty men. He is distinct from Shammah son of Agee the Hararite and from Shammah son of Jesse.
KeyStory: Shammah the Harodite stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: Three Shammahs served David — the record keeps each one's place.

Name: Shammai, Son of Ezra
Summary: Son borne in Ezra's line, named beside Miriam and Ishbah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:17: Son borne in Ezra's line, named beside Miriam and Ishbah.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shammai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shammai, Son of Onam
Summary: Son of Onam and father of Nadab and Abishur.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:28: Son of Onam and father of Nadab and Abishur.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shammai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shammai, Son of Rekem
Summary: Son of Rekem and father of Maon.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:44: Son of Rekem and father of Maon.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shammai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shammoth the Harorite
Summary: Valient man of David's armies, called the Harorite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:27: Valient man of David's armies, called the Harorite.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shammoth in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shammua, of Bilgah's Course
Summary: Head of Bilgah's priestly course in the days of Joiakim (Nehemiah 12:18).
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Every course had a head, and every head is named.

Name: Shammua, Son of David
Summary: Shammua was a son of David born at Jerusalem, named among the sons born to him there after he took the city.
KeyStory: Shammua was born to David at Jerusalem after the city became his capital.
LifeLesson: Children born in the capital inherit both its glory and its troubles.

Name: Shammua, Son of Galal
Summary: Shammua son of Galal, named in Nehemiah 11:17.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Shamsherai
Summary: Named among the sons of Jeroham in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:26: Named among the sons of Jeroham in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shamsherai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shapham
Summary: Next to Joel among the chiefs of Gad in Bashan.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:12: Next to Joel among the chiefs of Gad in Bashan.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shapham in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shaphan, Scribe
Summary: Shaphan the scribe read the found book of the law before Josiah, and went with the king's messengers to inquire of Huldah.
KeyStory: Shaphan reads the book before Josiah.
RelatedPeople: King Josiah; Hilkiah, High Priest; Ahikam, Son of Shaphan; Azaliah, Father of Shaphan
LifeLesson: The scribe who reads God's word aloud becomes its first hearer.

Name: Shaphan, Son of Azaliah
Summary: Shaphan, son of Azaliah and scribe, was sent by Josiah with Maaseiah and Joah to repair the house of the LORD; he carried the found book of the law to the king, reported the work, and read the book before Josiah, who rent his clothes.
KeyStory: Hilkiah gave Shaphan the book of the law, and Shaphan read it before the king, whose heart was tender and humbled.
RelatedPeople: King Josiah; Hilkiah, the High Priest; Ahikam, Son of Shaphan
LifeLesson: A scribe who carries God's book faithfully can start a nation's reformation.

Name: Shaphat, Chief of Gad
Summary: Named among the chiefs of Gad in Bashan.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:12: Named among the chiefs of Gad in Bashan.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shaphat stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shaphat, Father of Elisha
Summary: Shaphat of Abel-meholah was the father of Elisha the prophet.
KeyStory: Shaphat, father of Elisha.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Shaphat, Son of Adlai
Summary: Son of Adlai, over the herds in the valleys.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:29: Son of Adlai, over the herds in the valleys.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shaphat stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shaphat, Son of Shemaiah
Summary: Son of Shemaiah son of Shechaniah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:22: Son of Shemaiah son of Shechaniah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shaphat stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Sharai, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:40).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: The reform reached into ordinary families.

Name: Sharar, Father of Ahiam
Summary: Sharar the Hararite is named as the father of Ahiam, one of David's thirty mighty men.
KeyStory: Sharar's son stood among David's thirty.
LifeLesson: A father's name rides on a son's place in the thirty.

Name: Sharezer, Son of Sennacherib
Summary: Sharezer, with his brother Adrammelech, slew their father Sennacherib as he worshipped in the house of Nisroch, and escaped to Armenia.
KeyStory: Sharezer slays Sennacherib and flees.
RelatedPeople: Sennacherib, King of Assyria; Adrammelech, Son of Sennacherib
LifeLesson: An empire built on terror ends in terror at home.

Name: Sharezer
Summary: Sharezer was a son of Sennacherib who, with his brother Adrammelech, murdered his father in the house of Nisroch and fled to Ararat.
KeyStory: Sharezer and Adrammelech killed Sennacherib as he worshipped, and Esar-haddon his son reigned in his place.
LifeLesson: Violence sown by an empire is often reaped inside its own house.

Name: Shashai, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:40).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Choosing God's law over a marriage was costly and public.

Name: Shashak
Summary: Named among the sons of Beriah in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:14: Named among the sons of Beriah in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shashak stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shaul, Son of Simeon
Summary: Son of Simeon, named among the sons of Simeon.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:24: Son of Simeon, named among the sons of Simeon.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shaul stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shaul, Son of Uzziah
Summary: Son of Uzziah in the Kohathite line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:24: Son of Uzziah in the Kohathite line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shaul stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shavsha
Summary: Scribe under David.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 18:16: Scribe under David.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shavsha in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Sheal, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:29).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: God's law reached every branch of the family.

Name: Shealtiel
Summary: Shealtiel, father of Zerubbabel, is named in Haggai as the father of the governor who led the returned exiles. Through Zerubbabel, Shealtiel stands in the royal line that Matthew's genealogy traces to Christ.
KeyStory: Shealtiel's son Zerubbabel governed the returned exiles and, with Joshua the high priest, led the rebuilding of the Temple.
KeyVerses: Haggai 1:1; Haggai 2:2; Ezra 3:2; Ezra 3:8; Ezra 5:2; Nehemiah 12:1
LifeLesson: Shealtiel never held office himself, but his son did — and through that son, the royal line ran on to Christ. God builds His purposes through fathers, not only through kings.
RelatedEvents: Rebuilding of the Temple; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Shear-jashub
Summary: Shear-jashub, whose name means 'a remnant shall return,' was Isaiah's son who stood with his father when Isaiah met Ahaz at the conduit of the upper pool.
KeyStory: Isaiah met Ahaz at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, with his son Shear-jashub beside him, and told the king not to fear Rezin and Pekah.
LifeLesson: God sometimes puts the promise in a child's name before the child can understand it.

Name: Sheariah
Summary: Son of Azel, named among the six sons of Azel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:38; 1 Chronicles 9:44: Son of Azel, named among the six sons of Azel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Sheariah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Sheba, Son of Bichri
Summary: Sheba, son of Bichri, a Benjamite, blew a trumpet after Absalom's fall and cried that Israel had no part in David, drawing the northern tribes into revolt. Joab besieged him at Abel, and a wise woman of the city had his head thrown over the wall to end the siege.
KeyStory: Sheba's trumpet called Israel away from David — and a wise woman's bargain ended him at Abel.
LifeLesson: A trumpet blown in bitterness can summon a rebellion — and a city can buy peace with one head.

Name: Sheba, Son of Gad's House
Summary: Named among the brethren of the house of Gad's fathers.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:13: Named among the brethren of the house of Gad's fathers.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Sheba stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shebaniah, Priest

KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:24: Priest who blew with the trumpet before the ark of God.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shebaniah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shebaniah
Summary: Levite who led prayer at the covenant renewal.

LifeLesson: Prayer and confession renew a covenant people.

Name: Sheber
Summary: Son of Caleb's concubine Maachah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:48: Son of Caleb's concubine Maachah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Sheber stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shebna, Scribe
Summary: Shebna the scribe stood with Eliakim and Joah before the Rabshakeh's threats and carried his words to Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Shebna hears the Rabshakeh and reports to Hezekiah.
RelatedPeople: King Hezekiah; Eliakim, Son of Hilkiah; Joah, Son of Asaph; Isaiah
LifeLesson: Hearing threats and carrying them to prayer is itself faithful service.

Name: Shebna
Summary: Shebna was the steward over Hezekiah's household and a scribe; Isaiah rebuked him for carving himself a grand tomb in the rock, and foretold that he would be thrust from office and replaced by Eliakim.
KeyStory: Isaiah confronted Shebna the treasurer, who was hewing out a sepulchre on high, and announced that God would drive him from his station.
LifeLesson: Office used for self-glory is taken away; God gives it to another.

Name: Shebuel, Son of Gershom, Treasurer
Summary: Son of Gershom son of Moses, ruler of the treasures.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:24: Son of Gershom son of Moses, ruler of the treasures.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shebuel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shebuel, Son of Gershom
Summary: Chief of the sons of Gershom son of Moses in David's divisions.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 23:16: Chief of the sons of Gershom son of Moses in David's divisions.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shebuel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shebuel, Son of Heman
Summary: Son of Heman the king's seer, thirteenth lot for song.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 25:4; 1 Chronicles 25:20: Son of Heman the king's seer, thirteenth lot for song.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shebuel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shecaniah, Course Head
