KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:11: Tenth lot among the divisions of the sons of Aaron.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shecaniah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shecaniah, Priest Distributor
Summary: Shecaniah served with Kore in the cities of the priests, giving portions to his brethren by courses under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Shecaniah served with Kore in the cities of the priests, giving portions to his brethren by courses under Hezekiah.
RelatedPeople: Kore, Son of Imnah; King Hezekiah
LifeLesson: Fair portions for every priest, great and small, came through faithful distributors.

Name: Shechaniah, Father of Shemaiah
Summary: Father of Shemaiah the wall builder in Nehemiah 3.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: A father's name can open a son's story.

Name: Shechaniah, Son of Arah
Summary: Son of Arah whose daughter married Johanan, son of Tobiah, binding his house to Tobiah's.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: Marriages can ally a household with either side of a wall.

Name: Shechaniah, Son of Jahaziel
Summary: Son of Jahaziel who returned with Ezra from Babylon.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: Returning to God's house is a family decision.

Name: Shechaniah, Son of Jehiel
Summary: Son of Jehiel who proposed to Ezra that the people covenant to put away their foreign wives, and the people agreed.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Confession that proposes a remedy is better than confession alone.

Name: Shechaniah, Son of Obadiah
Summary: Named in the chain of sons after Hananiah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:21: Named in the chain of sons after Hananiah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shechaniah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shechem, Son of Shemidah
Summary: Son of Shemidah, named among the sons of Shemidah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:19: Son of Shemidah, named among the sons of Shemidah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shechem stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shehariah
Summary: Named among the sons of Jeroham in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:26: Named among the sons of Jeroham in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shehariah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shelemiah, Father of Hananiah
Summary: Father of Hananiah the wall builder (Nehemiah 3:30). Not Shelemiah son of Bani.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: A father's name stands behind his son's section of wall.

Name: Shelemiah, Son of Abdeel
Summary: Shelemiah, son of Abdeel, was one of the officers Jehoiakim sent to seize Jeremiah and Baruch after the scroll was burned, but the Lord hid them.
KeyStory: The king commanded Shelemiah son of Abdeel to take Jeremiah and Baruch, but the Lord hid them.
RelatedPeople: Jehoiakim, King of Judah; Jeremiah; Baruch
LifeLesson: Orders to arrest God's messengers fail when God himself is the hiding place.

Name: Shelemiah, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:39, 10:41).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is recorded by name, not in general terms.

Name: Shelesh
Summary: Son of Helem in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:35: Son of Helem in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shelesh stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shelomith, Daughter of Rehoboam
Summary: Shelomith was a daughter of Rehoboam by Maachah, daughter of Absalom.
KeyStory: Maachah bore Rehoboam Abijah, Attai, Ziza and Shelomith.
LifeLesson: Daughters as well as sons carried the royal line's story.

Name: Shelomith, Daughter of Zerubbabel
Summary: Daughter of Zerubbabel, named as sister of Meshullam and Hananiah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:19: Daughter of Zerubbabel, named as sister of Meshullam and Hananiah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shelomith stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shelomith, Son of Izhar
Summary: Chief of the sons of Izhar in David's divisions.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 23:18; 1 Chronicles 24:22: Chief of the sons of Izhar in David's divisions.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shelomith in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shelomith, Son of Josiphiah
Summary: Son of Josiphiah who returned with Ezra from Babylon; a different Shelomith from Dibri's daughter in Leviticus.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: Returning to God's house is a family decision.

Name: Shelomith, Son of Shimei
Summary: Son of Shimei, named with Haziel and Haran as chief of the fathers of Laadan.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 23:9: Son of Shimei, named with Haziel and Haran as chief of the fathers of Laadan.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shelomith stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shelomith, Son of Zichri
Summary: Son of Zichri, over all the treasures of the dedicated things with his brethren.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:25: Son of Zichri, over all the treasures of the dedicated things with his brethren.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shelomith stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shema, Son of Elpaal
Summary: Son of Elpaal and head of the fathers of the inhabitants of Aijalon, who drove away the inhabitants of Gath.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:13: Son of Elpaal and head of the fathers of the inhabitants of Aijalon, who drove away the inhabitants of Gath.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shema stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shema, Son of Hebron
Summary: Son of Hebron son of Mareshah and father of Raham.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:43: Son of Hebron son of Mareshah and father of Raham.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shema stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shema, Son of Joel
Summary: Son of Joel and father of Azaz in Reuben's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:8: Son of Joel and father of Azaz in Reuben's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shema stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shema
Summary: Stood beside Ezra on the platform at the reading of the law.
KeyStory: Ezra reads the law
LifeLesson: Standing to hear God's word is an act of reverence.

Name: Shemaah the Gibeathite
Summary: Father of Ahiezer and Joash who came to David at Ziklag.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:3: Father of Ahiezer and Joash who came to David at Ziklag.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shemaah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shemaiah, Chief of Elizaphan
Summary: Chief of the sons of Elizaphan who brought up the ark, with his brethren two hundred.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:8; 1 Chronicles 15:11: Chief of the sons of Elizaphan who brought up the ark, with his brethren two hundred.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shemaiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shemaiah, Chief of the Levites
Summary: Shemaiah, a chief of the Levites and brother of Cononiah, gave with the other chiefs five thousand small cattle and five hundred oxen for Josiah's Passover.
KeyStory: Conaniah, Shemaiah and Nethaneel, his brethren, gave unto the Levites for passover offerings.
RelatedPeople: Cononiah, Chief of the Levites; Nethaneel, Chief of the Levites; King Josiah
LifeLesson: Brothers leading together supplied the Passover for all.

Name: Shemaiah, Father of Shimri
Summary: Father of Shimri in Simeon's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:37: Father of Shimri in Simeon's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shemaiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shemaiah, Man of God
Summary: Shemaiah the man of God came to Rehoboam as Judah marched to fight Israel and said, You shall not go up nor fight your brethren, for this thing is from me; and the army turned back.
KeyStory: Shemaiah stops Rehoboam's war against Israel.
LifeLesson: Sometimes the bravest word a prophet speaks is 'do not fight your brothers.'

Name: Shemaiah, of the Sons of Jeduthun
Summary: Shemaiah, of the sons of Jeduthun, was one of the Levites who arose to cleanse the house of the LORD under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Of the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel arose to cleanse the house.
RelatedPeople: Uzziel, of the Sons of Jeduthun; King Hezekiah; Jeduthun
LifeLesson: Jeduthun's line kept serving the house in every generation.

Name: Shemaiah, Priest Distributor
Summary: Shemaiah served with Kore in the cities of the priests, giving portions to his brethren by courses under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Shemaiah served with Kore in the cities of the priests, giving portions to his brethren by courses under Hezekiah.
RelatedPeople: Kore, Son of Imnah; King Hezekiah
LifeLesson: Fair portions for every priest, great and small, came through faithful distributors.

Name: Shemaiah, Son of Delaiah
Summary: A prophet hired to lure Nehemiah into the temple for safety, which would have discredited him; Nehemiah refused.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
LifeLesson: Not every voice claiming God speaks for him.

Name: Shemaiah, Son of Galal
Summary: Son of Galal son of Jeduthun, father of Obadiah the Levite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:16: Son of Galal son of Jeduthun, father of Obadiah the Levite.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shemaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shemaiah, Son of Harim
Summary: Son of Harim named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Shemaiah, Son of Hashub
Summary: Shemaiah son of Hashub, named in Nehemiah 11:15.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Shemaiah, Son of Hasshub
Summary: Son of Hasshub son of Azrikam son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari, dwelling in Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:14: Son of Hasshub son of Azrikam son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari, dwelling in Jerusalem.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shemaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shemaiah, Son of Joel
Summary: Son of Joel and father of Gog in Reuben's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:4: Son of Joel and father of Gog in Reuben's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shemaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shemaiah, Son of Mattaniah
Summary: Shemaiah son of Mattaniah, named in Nehemiah 12:35.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Shemaiah, Son of Nethaneel
Summary: Son of Nethaneel the scribe, one of the Levites, who wrote the divisions before the king.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:6: Son of Nethaneel the scribe, one of the Levites, who wrote the divisions before the king.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shemaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shemaiah, Son of Obed-edom
Summary: Firstborn son of Obed-edom the porter.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:4: Firstborn son of Obed-edom the porter.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shemaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shemaiah, Son of Shechaniah
Summary: Son of Shechaniah and father of Hattush, Igeal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:22: Son of Shechaniah and father of Hattush, Igeal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shemaiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shemaiah, the Levite
Summary: Shemaiah was one of the Levites sent with Jehoshaphat's princes to teach the book of the law throughout Judah.
KeyStory: With the princes went Levites, including Shemaiah, and they taught in Judah with the book of the law of the LORD.
LifeLesson: God's law taught throughout the land, and willing service under a faithful king, strengthened Judah.

Name: Shemaiah the Nehelamite
Summary: Shemaiah the Nehelamite was a false prophet among the exiles who wrote letters from Babylon ordering the priest Zephaniah to imprison Jeremiah as a madman, and who wrote to the exiles telling them to settle in for a long captivity. Jeremiah answered that Shemaiah would be punished and none of his seed would see the good God would do.
KeyStory: Shemaiah's letters demanded Jeremiah's imprisonment, and Jeremiah replied with a prophecy that Shemaiah's line would not dwell among the people to see their return.
LifeLesson: Writing letters to silence a prophet is still an attempt to silence God.

Name: Shemaiah, the Prophet
Summary: Shemaiah the man of God told Rehoboam not to fight his brethren, for the division was from the LORD, and later told him that because Judah had forsaken the LORD they were left in Shishak's hand.
KeyStory: Shemaiah's word stopped Rehoboam's army of 180,000, and when king and princes humbled themselves, the LORD granted some deliverance from Shishak.
LifeLesson: Listening to God's word can stop a war; humbling ourselves can lessen a judgment.

Name: Shemaiah
Summary: Named among Adonikam's sons returning with Ezra, among the chief men sent to bring Levites, and among the covenant sealers and dedication musicians (Ezra 8:13, 8:16; Nehemiah 10:8, 12:36).
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: Steady service across decades: present at the return, the reading, and the renewal.

Name: Shemariah, Son of Harim
Summary: Son of Harim named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:32).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Harim's sons appear twice in the record, and both times by name.

Name: Shemariah, Son of Ziklag Band
Summary: One of those who came to David at Ziklag.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:5: One of those who came to David at Ziklag.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shemariah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shemer, Owner of Samaria's Hill
Summary: Shemer owned the hill which Omri bought for two talents of silver and built Samaria upon, naming it for Shemer.
KeyStory: Shemer sells Omri the hill of Samaria.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Shemidah
Summary: Son of Gilead, father of Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:19: Son of Gilead, father of Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shemidah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shemiramoth, Singer
Summary: Levite of the second degree appointed to sing with psalteries on Alamoth at the bringing up of the ark.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:18; 1 Chronicles 15:20: Levite of the second degree appointed to sing with psalteries on Alamoth at the bringing up of the ark.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shemiramoth in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shemiramoth, the Levite
Summary: Shemiramoth was one of the Levites sent with Jehoshaphat's princes to teach the book of the law throughout Judah.
KeyStory: With the princes went Levites, including Shemiramoth, and they taught in Judah.
LifeLesson: God's law taught throughout the land, and willing service under a faithful king, strengthened Judah.

Name: Shemuel, Son of Tola
Summary: Son of Tola and head of his father's house, a valiant man of might.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:2: Son of Tola and head of his father's house, a valiant man of might.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shemuel stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shenazar
Summary: Son of Jeconiah, named in the post-exilic royal line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:18: Son of Jeconiah, named in the post-exilic royal line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shenazar stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shephathiah, Father of Meshullam
Summary: Father of Meshullam in the Jerusalem list, son of Reuel son of Ibnijah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:8: Father of Meshullam in the Jerusalem list, son of Reuel son of Ibnijah.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shephathiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shephatiah, Son of David
Summary: Shephatiah, David's fifth son by Abital, was born at Hebron and is named among the six sons born there.
KeyStory: Shephatiah was born at Hebron to David and Abital.
LifeLesson: A single verse can hold a whole life's dignity.

Name: Shephatiah, Son of Jehoshaphat
Summary: Shephatiah was a son of Jehoshaphat who received great gifts from his father and was slain by his brother Jehoram.
KeyStory: Jehoshaphat's sons, including Shephatiah, were slain by Jehoram with the sword.
RelatedPeople: King Jehoshaphat; Jehoram, King of Judah
LifeLesson: The house of a faithful king was not spared a violent succession.

Name: Shephatiah, Son of Maachah
Summary: Son of Maachah, ruler of the Simeonites.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:16: Son of Maachah, ruler of the Simeonites.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shephatiah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shephatiah, Son of Mahalaleel
Summary: Shephatiah son of Mahalaleel, named in Nehemiah 11:4.
KeyStory: Resettling Jerusalem
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Shephatiah, Son of Mattan
Summary: Shephatiah, son of Mattan, was one of the princes who demanded Jeremiah's death, charging that his words weakened the hands of the men of war and all the people.
KeyStory: Shephatiah joined Gedaliah son of Pashur and others in telling Zedekiah that Jeremiah ought to die for weakening the city's hands.
RelatedPeople: Zedekiah, King of Judah; Jeremiah; Gedaliah, Son of Pashur
LifeLesson: Calling a prophet a traitor for telling the truth is a charge that outlives the siege.

Name: Shephatiah the Haruphite
Summary: One of those who came to David at Ziklag, called the Haruphite.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 12:5: One of those who came to David at Ziklag, called the Haruphite.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shephatiah in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shephatiah
Summary: Head of a family listed among those who returned from exile (Ezra 2:4; Nehemiah 7:9).
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: A family's return is recorded household by household.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Shephuphan
Summary: Son of Bela, named among the sons of Bela.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:5: Son of Bela, named among the sons of Bela.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shephuphan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Sherah
Summary: Daughter of Ephraim who built Beth-horon the nether and the upper, and Uzzen-sherah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:24: Daughter of Ephraim who built Beth-horon the nether and the upper, and Uzzen-sherah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Sherah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Sherebiah
Summary: A Levite of understanding whom Ezra brought from Casiphia; he guarded the temple treasure on the journey and later taught the Law and sealed the covenant.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
KeyVerses: Ezra 8:18; Ezra 8:24; Nehemiah 8:7; Nehemiah 9:4; Nehemiah 9:5; Nehemiah 10:12; Nehemiah 12:8; Nehemiah 12:24
LifeLesson: Understanding and trustworthiness go together in God's service.
RelatedEvents: Ezra Reads the Law; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Sheresh
Summary: Son of Machir by Maachah, and brother of Peresh.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:16: Son of Machir by Maachah, and brother of Peresh.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Sheresh stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Sherezer
Summary: Sherezer was sent with Regemmelech from Bethel to Jerusalem to pray before the LORD and ask the priests whether the fasts of the exile should continue (Zechariah 7:2). The question he carried drew from Zechariah a searching answer about empty fasting and true justice.
KeyStory: Sherezer, sent from Bethel to ask whether the exile's fasts should go on, carried a question that exposed the difference between ritual and repentance.
LifeLesson: Sherezer asked the right question in the wrong spirit — and God answered deeper than he asked. Bring God your rituals; He will ask for your heart.

Name: Sheshan
Summary: Son of Ishi, who had daughters but no sons.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:31: Son of Ishi, who had daughters but no sons.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Sheshan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Sheshbazzar
Summary: Prince of Judah to whom Cyrus entrusted the temple vessels; he brought them from Babylon to Jerusalem and laid the foundation of the house of God.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: God restores what was carried away, and entrusts the work to known hands.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile; Rebuilding of the Temple

Name: Shethar-boznai
Summary: Companion of Tatnai who questioned the temple rebuilding and carried the inquiry to Darius.
KeyStory: Rebuilding of the Temple
LifeLesson: Even scrutiny can become part of God's provision.

Name: Shethar, Prince of Persia
Summary: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media who saw the king's face; a different Shethar from Shethar-boznai of Ezra.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: Counsel near the throne carries weight for a kingdom.

Name: Sheva
Summary: Sheva was scribe in David's later administration, serving beside Zadok, Abiathar, and Ira the Jairite at the time of Sheba's revolt.
KeyStory: Sheva kept the king's records through David's last wars.
RelatedPeople: King David; Zadok, Son of Ahitub; Ira the Jairite
LifeLesson: Late in a reign, the scribes still write it all down.

Name: Shilhi, Father of Azubah
Summary: Shilhi was the father of Azubah, mother of Jehoshaphat.
KeyStory: Shilhi, father of Azubah.
RelatedPeople: Azubah, Mother of Jehoshaphat; Azubah, Daughter of Shilhi
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Shilshah
Summary: Son of Zophah in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:37: Son of Zophah in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shilshah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shimea, Father of Berachiah
Summary: Father of Berachiah in Asaph's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:39: Father of Berachiah in Asaph's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shimea in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shimea, Son of David
Summary: Son of David born in Jerusalem to Bath-shua.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:5; 1 Chronicles 14:4: Son of David born in Jerusalem to Bath-shua.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shimea stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shimea, Son of Jesse
Summary: Third son of Jesse and brother of David.

Name: Shimea, Son of Uzza

Name: Shimeah, Son of Mikloth

LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shimeah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shimeath, Mother of Jozachar
Summary: Shimeath was the mother of Jozachar, who with Jehozabad slew King Joash.
KeyStory: Shimeath, mother of Jozachar.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Shimeath, the Ammonitess
Summary: Shimeath, an Ammonitess, was the mother of Zabad, who conspired against King Joash.
KeyStory: Shimeath is named only as the mother of Zabad the son of Shimeath.
LifeLesson: A conspirator's parentage is recorded, not hidden.

Name: Shimei, Brother of Cononiah
Summary: Shimei, brother of Cononiah, was next to him over the offerings, tithes and dedicated things under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Over the offerings Cononiah the Levite was ruler, and Shimei his brother was the next.
LifeLesson: Brothers serving side by side kept the storehouses faithful.

Name: Shimei, Daughter of Kish
Summary: Shimei son of Kish, named in Esther 2:5.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Shimei, Singer of the Tenth Lot
Summary: Tenth lot for song.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 25:17: Tenth lot for song.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shimei in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shimei, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:38).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: A common name, a personal decision.

Name: Shimei, Son of Elah
Summary: Shimei, son of Elah, was one of Solomon's twelve officers, over Benjamin.
KeyStory: Shimei, officer over Benjamin.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Elah, Father of Shimei
LifeLesson: Not every Shimei is the one who cursed David: names repeat, men do not.

Name: Shimei, Son of Gera
Summary: Shimei, son of Gera of Bahurim, cursed David as he fled from Absalom, throwing stones and dust and calling him a bloody man. David forbade revenge, and on his return spared Shimei, who came first among Benjamin to meet him.
KeyStory: Shimei cursed the fleeing king with stones and dust — and the returning king spared him.
KeyVerses: 2 Samuel 16:5; 2 Samuel 16:13; 2 Samuel 19:16; 2 Samuel 19:23; 1 Kings 2:8; 1 Kings 2:46
RelatedPeople: King David; Gera, Father of Shimei; Abishai; King Solomon; Benaiah, Son of Jehoiada
LifeLesson: A king who refuses revenge on his way down shows mercy on his way back up.

Name: Shimei, Son of Gershom
Summary: Son of Gershom, named among the sons of Gershom.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:17: Son of Gershom, named among the sons of Gershom.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shimei stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shimei, Son of Gershon
Summary: Gershonite named among the sons of Levi in David's divisions.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 23:7: Gershonite named among the sons of Levi in David's divisions.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shimei in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shimei, Son of Gog
Summary: Son of Gog and father of Micah in Reuben's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 5:4: Son of Gog and father of Micah in Reuben's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shimei stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shimei, Son of Hashum
Summary: Son of Hashum named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Shimei, Son of Heman
Summary: Shimei, of the sons of Heman, was one of the Levites who arose to cleanse the house of the LORD under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Of the sons of Heman, Jehiel and Shimei arose to cleanse the house.
RelatedPeople: Jehiel, Son of Heman; King Hezekiah; Heman, Son of Joel
LifeLesson: Worship and cleansing belong together.

Name: Shimei, Son of Kish
Summary: Son of Kish and father of Jair in Mordecai's genealogy; a different Shimei from David's Shimei.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
RelatedPeople: Jair, Father of Mordecai; Kish, Ancestor of Mordecai
LifeLesson: Exile does not erase a family's line.

Name: Shimei, Son of Libni
Summary: Son of Libni and father of Uzza in Merari's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:29: Son of Libni and father of Uzza in Merari's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shimei stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shimei, Son of Pedaiah
Summary: Son of Pedaiah and brother of Zerubbabel.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:19: Son of Pedaiah and brother of Zerubbabel.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shimei stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shimei, Son of Zacchur
Summary: Son of Zacchur in Simeon's line, who had sixteen sons and six daughters.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:26: Son of Zacchur in Simeon's line, who had sixteen sons and six daughters.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shimei stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shimei the Levite
Summary: Levite named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:23).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Even Levites were not exempt from the call to repent.

Name: Shimei the Ramathite
Summary: Ramathite over the vineyards of the king.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:27: Ramathite over the vineyards of the king.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shimei in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shimeon, Son of Harim
Summary: Son of Harim named among those who had taken foreign wives and were called to put them away (Ezra 10).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Repentance is specific: naming the sin is the first step to putting it away.

Name: Shimhi, Father of Jakim
Summary: Father of Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi, Elienai, Zilthai, Eliel, Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:21: Father of Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi, Elienai, Zilthai, Eliel, Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shimhi in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shimon
Summary: Father of Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan, and Tilon.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:20: Father of Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan, and Tilon.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shimon in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shimrath
Summary: Named among the sons of Shimhi in Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:21: Named among the sons of Shimhi in Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shimrath stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shimri, Father of Jediael
Summary: Father of Jediael and Joha the Tizites.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:45: Father of Jediael and Joha the Tizites.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shimri in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shimri, of the Sons of Elizaphan
Summary: Shimri, of the sons of Elizaphan, was one of the Levites who arose to cleanse the house of the LORD under Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Of the sons of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeiel arose to cleanse the house.
RelatedPeople: Jeiel, of the Sons of Elizaphan; King Hezekiah
LifeLesson: Every Levite family had men ready for the cleansing.

Name: Shimri, Son of Shemaiah
Summary: Son of Shemaiah in Simeon's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:37: Son of Shemaiah in Simeon's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shimri stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shimrith, the Moabitess
Summary: Shimrith, a Moabitess, was the mother of Jehozabad, who conspired against King Joash.
KeyStory: Shimrith is named only as the mother of Jehozabad the son of Shimrith.
LifeLesson: Even conspirators are traced to real mothers.

Name: Shimshai
Summary: Scribe who joined Rehum the chancellor in writing against Jerusalem's rebuilding.
KeyStory: Rebuilding of the Temple
LifeLesson: Words written against God's people do not have the last word.

Name: Shiphi
Summary: Father of Ziza in Simeon's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:37: Father of Ziza in Simeon's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shiphi in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shisha, Father of Elihoreph and Ahiah
Summary: Shisha was the father of Elihoreph and Ahiah, Solomon's scribes.
KeyStory: Shisha, father of the scribes.
RelatedPeople: Elihoreph, Scribe of Solomon; Ahiah, Scribe of Solomon
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Shishak, King of Egypt
Summary: Shishak, king of Egypt, came up against Jerusalem in Rehoboam's fifth year with 1,200 chariots and 60,000 horsemen, and carried away the treasures of the house of the LORD and the king's house.
KeyStory: Because Judah had forsaken the LORD, Shishak took the fenced cities of Judah and stripped Jerusalem of Solomon's shields of gold.
LifeLesson: Forsaking the LORD leaves even a fortified kingdom open to its enemies.

Name: Shishak, Pharaoh of Egypt
Summary: Shishak, king of Egypt, sheltered Jeroboam from Solomon, then in Rehoboam's fifth year came up against Jerusalem and took the temple treasures and Solomon's gold shields.
KeyStory: Shishak plunders Jerusalem in Rehoboam's fifth year.
LifeLesson: A refuge for a rebel becomes a robber of his son's temple.

Name: Shitrai the Sharonite
Summary: Sharonite over the herds that fed in Sharon.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 27:29: Sharonite over the herds that fed in Sharon.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shitrai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shiza
Summary: Father of Adina the Reubenite captain.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:42: Father of Adina the Reubenite captain.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shiza in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shobab, Son of Caleb
Summary: Son of Caleb son of Hezron by Azubah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:18: Son of Caleb son of Hezron by Azubah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shobab stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shobab, Son of David
Summary: Son of David born in Jerusalem to Bath-shua.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:5: Son of David born in Jerusalem to Bath-shua.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shobab stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shobab
Summary: Shobab was a son of David born at Jerusalem, named among the sons born to him there after he took the city.
KeyStory: Shobab was born to David at Jerusalem after the city became his capital.
LifeLesson: A name in a list is still a life God counted.

Name: Shobach
Summary: Shobach was captain of the host of Hadadezer, king of Zobah. He led the Syrian confederacy against David at Helam and was slain there with the flower of the Syrian army.
KeyStory: Shobach led Syria's last great army against David and fell at Helam.
RelatedPeople: Hadadezer, Son of Rehob; King David
LifeLesson: The captain of a doomed confederacy still dies at his post.

Name: Shobai
Summary: Head of a porter family that returned with Zerubbabel.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Gatekeepers guard the house of God.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Shobal, Son of Caleb
Summary: Son of Caleb son of Hur, called the father of Kirjath-jearim.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:50: Son of Caleb son of Hur, called the father of Kirjath-jearim.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shobal stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shobek
Summary: Chief who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10).
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: A signature on a covenant is a public stand.

Name: Shobi, Son of Nahash
Summary: Shobi, son of Nahash of Rabbah, was among those who brought beds, basins, and food to David and his people at Mahanaim during Absalom's revolt.
KeyStory: Shobi of Rabbah fed David's exhausted people at Mahanaim.
RelatedPeople: King David; Barzillai the Gileadite; Machir, Son of Ammiel
LifeLesson: An Ammonite's son fed Israel's king — kindness crosses old borders.

Name: Shoham
Summary: Son of Jaaziah, named among the sons of Merari by Jaaziah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:27: Son of Jaaziah, named among the sons of Merari by Jaaziah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shoham stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shomer, Mother of Jehozabad
Summary: Shomer was the mother of Jehozabad, who with Jozachar slew King Joash.
KeyStory: Shomer, mother of Jehozabad.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Shomer, Son of Heber
Summary: Son of Heber, named beside Japhlet and Hotham.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:32: Son of Heber, named beside Japhlet and Hotham.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shomer stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shophach
Summary: Captain of the host of Hadarezer, slain by David's army.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 19:16; 1 Chronicles 19:18: Captain of the host of Hadarezer, slain by David's army.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shophach in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shua, Sister of Japhlet
Summary: Sister of Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:32: Sister of Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shua in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shuah
Summary: Brother of Chelub, named in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:11: Brother of Chelub, named in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shuah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shual
Summary: Son of Zophah in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:36: Son of Zophah in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shual stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shubael, Son of Amram
Summary: Son of Amram in the rest of the sons of Levi, father of Jehdeiah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 24:20: Son of Amram in the rest of the sons of Levi, father of Jehdeiah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shubael stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shuppim, Porter
Summary: Porter to whom the lot westward fell, with Hosah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:16: Porter to whom the lot westward fell, with Hosah.
LifeLesson: The mention of Shuppim in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Shuppim
Summary: Child of Ir, named with Huppim among Benjamin's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:12: Child of Ir, named with Huppim among Benjamin's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shuppim stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shuthelah, Son of Ephraim
Summary: Son of Ephraim, named first among the sons of Ephraim.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:20: Son of Ephraim, named first among the sons of Ephraim.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shuthelah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Shuthelah, Son of Zabad
Summary: Son of Zabad and father of Ezer and Elead in Ephraim's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:21: Son of Zabad and father of Ezer and Elead in Ephraim's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Shuthelah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Siaha
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Sibbecai the Hushathite
Summary: Valient man of David's armies, who slew Sippai of the children of the giant, and captain of the eighth month's course.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:29; 1 Chronicles 27:11: Valient man of David's armies, who slew Sippai of the children of the giant, and captain of the eighth month's course.
LifeLesson: The mention of Sibbecai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Sibbechai the Hushathite
Summary: Hushathite who slew Sippai of the children of the giant at Gezer.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 20:4: Hushathite who slew Sippai of the children of the giant at Gezer.
LifeLesson: The mention of Sibbechai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Silas
Summary: Silas, also called Silvanus, was a prophet and leading man among the Jerusalem brethren, sent with Judas Barsabbas to confirm the Council's letter. He became Paul's companion on the second missionary journey, was beaten and imprisoned with him at Philippi, and sang hymns at midnight before the earthquake.
KeyStory: Silas sang in a Philippian prison at midnight, and the earthquake opened every door.
KeyVerses: Acts 15:22; Acts 15:32; 2 Corinthians 1:19; 1 Thessalonians 1:1; 2 Thessalonians 1:1; 1 Peter 5:12
LifeLesson: Silas sang where most would curse. Worship at midnight is the missionary's loudest sermon.

Name: Simeon Niger
Summary: Simeon called Niger was among the prophets and teachers at Antioch who sent Barnabas and Saul to the Gentiles. His Latin nickname, meaning black, suggests he was of African origin, and he is distinct from Simeon of Jerusalem and from Simon Peter.
KeyStory: Simeon Niger worshipped at Antioch when the Spirit separated Barnabas and Saul for the Gentile mission.
RelatedPeople: Barnabas; Paul; Lucius of Cyrene; Manaen
LifeLesson: The church that sent the first missionaries already spanned continents. Simeon Niger stood in that company.

Name: Simon, Brother of Jesus
Summary: Simon was one of the brothers of Jesus named by the people of Nazareth, alongside James, Joses, and Judas. He is distinct from Simon Peter, Simon the Zealot, and every other Simon in the Gospels.
KeyStory: Nazareth named Simon among Jesus' brothers, and took offence at the carpenter's son in their midst.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; James, Brother of Jesus; Mary, Mother of Jesus
LifeLesson: Jesus' own town could name His family and still not know Him. Nearness to Jesus is not the same as faith in Him.

Name: Simon of Cyrene
Summary: Simon of Cyrene was a passer-by coming in from the country whom the soldiers compelled to carry Jesus' cross to Golgotha. Mark names his sons Alexander and Rufus, suggesting his family later joined the church.
KeyStory: Simon did not volunteer; he was pressed into service, and carried the cross behind Jesus to the place of the skull.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Alexander, Son of Simon of Cyrene; Rufus, Son of Simon of Cyrene
LifeLesson: Sometimes the cross finds us on an ordinary errand. Simon's forced steps became his family's doorway into faith.

Name: Simon the Leper
Summary: Simon the Leper lived at Bethany, where Jesus dined at his house shortly before the crucifixion. During that meal a woman anointed Jesus' head with costly ointment, which He received as preparation for His burial.
KeyStory: At Simon's table in Bethany, a woman poured ointment on Jesus' head, and He called it anointing for His burial.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Martha; Mary of Bethany; Lazarus
LifeLesson: A former leper hosted the Healer at his own table. Grace turns outcasts into hosts.

Name: Simon the Pharisee
Summary: Simon the Pharisee invited Jesus to eat at his house, where a sinful woman washed Jesus' feet with tears and anointed them. Jesus answered Simon's silent judgment with the parable of the two debtors.
KeyStory: Simon gave Jesus a meal but no water for His feet, and watched a weeping woman love much because she was forgiven much.
LifeLesson: Simon kept the rules of hospitality and missed its heart. Forgiveness, not formality, teaches love.

Name: Simon the Sorcerer
Summary: Simon the Sorcerer, also called Simon Magus, amazed Samaria with sorcery and claimed to be someone great. He believed and was baptised under Philip's preaching, then tried to buy the gift of the Holy Spirit from Peter and was sharply rebuked.
KeyStory: Simon offered money for the power of the Spirit and heard Peter say, Your money perish with you.
LifeLesson: Faith cannot be bought, and power is not a product. Simon's error still tempts every ministry that trades in gifts.

Name: Simon the Tanner
Summary: Simon the Tanner lived at Joppa by the sea, and Peter lodged at his house while the Lord prepared him to receive Cornelius, the Gentile centurion.
KeyStory: Peter stayed with Simon the Tanner while a sheet from heaven taught him to call no man unclean.
LifeLesson: God prepared Peter for the Gentiles in a tanner's house, a trade the law counted unclean. The lesson began before the vision.

Name: Simri, Son of Hosah
Summary: Son of Hosah of Merari, made chief by his father though not the firstborn.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:10: Son of Hosah of Merari, made chief by his father though not the firstborn.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Simri stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Sippai
Summary: Of the children of the giant, slain by Sibbechai the Hushathite at Gezer.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 20:4: Of the children of the giant, slain by Sibbechai the Hushathite at Gezer.
LifeLesson: The mention of Sippai in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Sisamai
Summary: Son of Eleasah and father of Shallum.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:40: Son of Eleasah and father of Shallum.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Sisamai stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Sisera, of the Nethinim
Summary: Head of a Nethinim family listed among the returnees (Ezra 2:53; Nehemiah 7:55). Not Sisera, the Canaanite general of Judges.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: A shared name does not make a shared life.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Sisera
Summary: Sisera commanded Jabin's army with nine hundred chariots of iron; defeated at the Kishon, he fled to Jael's tent, where she killed him with a tent peg.
KeyStory: Sisera's host was routed at the Kishon, and he fled on foot to the tent of Jael, wife of Heber, who gave him milk, covered him, and drove a nail through his temples as he slept.
RelatedPeople: Deborah; Barak; Jael; Jabin, King of Canaan
LifeLesson: The general who trusted in iron found his end in a housewife's tent.

Name: So, King of Egypt
Summary: So, king of Egypt, was the ruler to whom Hoshea sent messengers and withheld Assyria's tribute, a conspiracy Shalmaneser discovered before Samaria fell.
KeyStory: So, Hoshea's Egyptian ally.
RelatedPeople: Hoshea, King of Israel; Shalmaneser, King of Assyria
LifeLesson: Egypt's help has always been a broken reed for kings who will not trust God.

Name: Sopater
Summary: Sopater of Berea accompanied Paul toward Jerusalem with the collection for the saints. He is traditionally identified with Sosipater, greeted in the later epistles, though Acts names him Sopater.
KeyStory: Sopater of Berea travelled with Paul's company toward Jerusalem, carrying the gift of the churches.
LifeLesson: Berea's nobility bore fruit in a travelling companion. Sopater carried more than luggage to Jerusalem.

Name: Sophereth
Summary: Descendant of Solomon's servants listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Service in God's house spans generations.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Sosipater, Kinsman of Paul
Summary: Sosipater was a kinsman of Paul who sends greetings in Romans 16. He is listed separately from Sopater of Berea, since the letter does not identify them as the same man.
KeyStory: Sosipater was a kinsman of Paul who sends greetings in Romans 16. He is listed separately from Sopater of Berea, since the letter does not identify them as the same man.
LifeLesson: Faithful kinsmen stood with Paul to the end of his letters.

Name: Sosthenes
Summary: Sosthenes was a ruler of the synagogue at Corinth who was beaten by the Greeks before Gallio's judgment seat after Gallio dismissed the Jews' case against Paul. He is traditionally identified with the Sosthenes who later greets the Corinthians with Paul, though Acts does not say so.
KeyStory: Sosthenes was beaten before the judgment seat while Gallio cared for none of these things.
LifeLesson: Gallio's indifference left Sosthenes bleeding at the tribunal. The world often shrugs at the church's wounds.

Name: Sotai
Summary: Descendant of Solomon's servants listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Service in God's house spans generations.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Stachys
Summary: Stachys was a Roman Christian whom Paul greets as his beloved.
KeyStory: Stachys was a Roman Christian whom Paul greets as his beloved.
LifeLesson: Personal affection between believers is part of the gospel's fruit, not an extra.

Name: Stephanas
Summary: Stephanas was one of the few Paul baptized at Corinth, the firstfruits of Achaia, whose household devoted itself to the ministry of the saints and who, with Fortunatus and Achaicus, refreshed Paul's spirit.
KeyStory: Stephanas was one of the few Paul baptized at Corinth, the firstfruits of Achaia, whose household devoted itself to the ministry of the saints and who, with Fortunatus and Achaicus, refreshed Paul's spirit.
LifeLesson: A household devoted to serving the saints refreshes the whole church.

Name: Suah
Summary: Son of Zophah in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:36: Son of Zophah in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Suah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Susanna
Summary: Susanna was one of the women who had been healed by Jesus and who travelled with Him through Galilee, ministering to Him from their substance.
KeyStory: Susanna is named once, among the women who kept Jesus' travelling ministry going from their own means.
LifeLesson: A single verse can hold a whole faithfulness. Susanna gave quietly and is remembered for it.

Name: Syntyche
Summary: Syntyche was a Philippian believer whom Paul beseeches, along with Euodias, to be of the same mind in the Lord.
KeyStory: Syntyche was a Philippian believer whom Paul beseeches, along with Euodias, to be of the same mind in the Lord.
LifeLesson: Disagreement between two faithful people is settled in the Lord, not by taking sides.

Name: Tabbaoth
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Tabeel
Summary: Named among those who wrote to Artaxerxes against Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Rebuilding of the Temple
LifeLesson: Opposition to rebuilding is an old story.

Name: Tabitha
Role: Disciple at Joppa, also called Dorcas
Summary: Tabitha, called Dorcas in Greek, was a disciple at Joppa full of good works and almsdeeds. When she died, the widows showed Peter the coats she had made, and Peter prayed and raised her, saying, Tabitha, arise.
KeyStory: Tabitha died, and the widows wept over her coats; Peter prayed, and she opened her eyes and sat up.
LifeLesson: A life of coats and kindness is a sermon the widows preached at her bedside. Tabitha's works outlived her death.

Name: Tabrimon, Father of Ben-Hadad I
Summary: Tabrimon, son of Hezion, was the father of Ben-Hadad, king of Syria in Asa's days.
KeyStory: Tabrimon, father of Ben-Hadad.
RelatedPeople: Ben-Hadad I, King of Syria; Hezion, Grandfather of Ben-Hadad I
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Tahan, Son of Telah
Summary: Son of Telah and father of Laadan in Ephraim's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:25: Son of Telah and father of Laadan in Ephraim's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Tahan stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Tahath, Son of Assir
Summary: Son of Assir and father of Uriel in the Kohathite line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:24: Son of Assir and father of Uriel in the Kohathite line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Tahath stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Tahath, Son of Bered
Summary: Son of Bered and father of Eladah in Ephraim's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:20: Son of Bered and father of Eladah in Ephraim's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Tahath stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Tahath, Son of Eladah
Summary: Son of Eladah and father of Zabad in Ephraim's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:20: Son of Eladah and father of Zabad in Ephraim's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Tahath stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Tahpenes, Queen of Egypt
Summary: Tahpenes, queen of Egypt, was Pharaoh's wife, whose sister was given to Hadad the Edomite, and who weaned Hadad's son Genubath in Pharaoh's house.
KeyStory: Tahpenes, queen of Egypt, and Genubath.
RelatedPeople: Hadad, Prince of Edom; Genubath, Son of Hadad
LifeLesson: A queen's household sheltered the very child who would trouble Israel.

Name: Tahrea
Summary: Son of Micah, named among the sons of Micah in the chapter 9 list.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:41: Son of Micah, named among the sons of Micah in the chapter 9 list.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Tahrea stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Talmai, King of Geshur
Summary: Talmai, king of Geshur, was the father of Maacah, David's wife, and the grandfather of Absalom. Absalom fled to him for three years after murdering Amnon.
KeyStory: Talmai sheltered his grandson Absalom for three years after the murder of Amnon.
RelatedPeople: Maacah, Daughter of Talmai; Absalom; King David
LifeLesson: A grandfather's refuge can shelter a fugitive — and delay a reckoning.

Name: Talmon
Summary: Porter in the companies of the children of Levi.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 9:17: Porter in the companies of the children of Levi.
LifeLesson: The mention of Talmon in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile; Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall

Name: Tamar, Daughter of Absalom
Summary: Tamar, daughter of Absalom, is named as his only daughter, a beautiful woman, at the end of the account of Absalom's return to Jerusalem.
KeyStory: Absalom's daughter Tamar, named for his wronged sister, closes the account of his return.
LifeLesson: A daughter named for a wronged aunt carries a family's grief forward.

Name: Tamar, Daughter of David
Summary: Tamar, daughter of David and sister of Absalom, was assaulted by her half-brother Amnon, who then cast her out. She lived desolate in Absalom's house, and her brother's vengeance for her began the road to civil war.
KeyStory: Tamar's desolation after Amnon's crime set Absalom on the path to rebellion.
RelatedPeople: King David; Absalom; Amnon; Maacah, Daughter of Talmai
LifeLesson: A wronged sister's grief, left unjudged by her father, can burn down a kingdom.

Name: Tamar, Sister of David's Sons
Summary: Sister of David's sons, named after the list of David's sons.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 3:9: Sister of David's sons, named after the list of David's sons.
LifeLesson: The mention of Tamar in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Tanhumeth, Father of Seraiah
Summary: Tanhumeth the Netophathite was the father of Seraiah, captain under Gedaliah.
KeyStory: Tanhumeth, father of Seraiah.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Taphath, Daughter of Solomon
Summary: Taphath, a daughter of Solomon, was given as wife to Ben-Abinadab, one of Solomon's officers over Dor.
KeyStory: Taphath, wife of Ben-Abinadab.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Ben-Abinadab, Officer of Solomon
LifeLesson: Royal daughters married the men who fed the kingdom.

Name: Tappuah
Summary: Son of Hebron son of Mareshah, named in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:43: Son of Hebron son of Mareshah, named in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Tappuah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Tarea
Summary: Son of Micah, named among the sons of Micah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:35; 1 Chronicles 9:41: Son of Micah, named among the sons of Micah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Tarea stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Tarshish, Prince of Persia
Summary: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media who saw the king's face; a different Tarshish from Javan's son in Genesis.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: Counsel near the throne carries weight for a kingdom.

Name: Tatnai
Summary: Persian governor beyond the river who questioned the Jews' authority to rebuild the temple, then, on Darius's order, let the work proceed and funded it.
KeyStory: Rebuilding of the Temple
LifeLesson: Honest inquiry can end in unexpected help.

Name: Tebaliah
Summary: Third son of Hosah the porter.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 26:11: Third son of Hosah the porter.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Tebaliah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Tehinnah
Summary: Son of Eshton, called the father of Ir-nahash.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:12: Son of Eshton, called the father of Ir-nahash.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Tehinnah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Telah
Summary: Son of Resheph and father of Tahan in Ephraim's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:25: Son of Resheph and father of Tahan in Ephraim's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Telah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Telem the Porter
Summary: Porter named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:24).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Gatekeepers guard their own households first.

Name: Temeni
Summary: Son of Ashur by Naarah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:6: Son of Ashur by Naarah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Temeni stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Teresh
Summary: Chamberlain and doorkeeper who with Bigthan conspired against Ahasuerus; Mordecai exposed the plot and both were hanged.
KeyStory: Esther's deliverance
LifeLesson: A plot exposed in time saves a king and a people.

Name: Tertius
Role: Amanuensis of the Epistle to the Romans
Summary: Tertius was the scribe who wrote down Paul's Epistle to the Romans at Paul's dictation, adding his own greeting in the Lord.
KeyStory: Tertius was the scribe who wrote down Paul's Epistle to the Romans at Paul's dictation, adding his own greeting in the Lord.
LifeLesson: Those who serve behind the scenes, pen in hand, share in the work they help deliver.

Name: Tertullus
Summary: Tertullus was the orator hired by the high priest Ananias to present the Jews' case against Paul before Felix at Caesarea, accusing Paul of sedition, of being a ringleader of the Nazarenes, and of profaning the temple.
KeyStory: Tertullus flattered Felix and accused Paul of sedition, calling him a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes.
RelatedPeople: Paul; Felix; Ananias, the High Priest
LifeLesson: Hired eloquence can dress up any charge. Tertullus flattered the judge and slandered the prisoner.

Name: Thamah
Summary: Nethinim (temple servant) listed among the returnees.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Temple service is honourable work, even when it is lowly.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Tharshish, Son of Bilhan
Summary: Son of Bilhan, named among the sons of Bilhan.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:10: Son of Bilhan, named among the sons of Bilhan.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Tharshish stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Theophilus
Summary: Theophilus was the most excellent recipient to whom Luke addressed both his Gospel and the book of Acts, so that he might know the certainty of the things he had been taught.
KeyStory: Luke wrote to Theophilus in order, that he might know the certainty of the things he had been taught.
LifeLesson: Luke wrote for certainty, not for feeling. Theophilus reminds us that faith loves an orderly account.

Name: Theudas
Summary: Theudas was a rebel leader who rose before the days of the census, claiming to be somebody, and gathered about four hundred men before he was slain and his followers scattered. Gamaliel cited him to counsel restraint toward the apostles.
KeyStory: Theudas rose, boasting himself to be somebody, and was slain, and all who obeyed him were scattered.
RelatedPeople: Gamaliel, the Pharisee; Judas of Galilee
LifeLesson: Movements built on somebody scatter when somebody falls. Theudas warns every cause that rests on a man.

Name: Tiberius Caesar
Summary: Tiberius Caesar was emperor when John the Baptist began preaching and when Jesus was crucified under Pontius Pilate. Luke dates the Baptist's ministry to the fifteenth year of his reign.
KeyStory: Luke dates the gospel to the fifteenth year of Tiberius, tying John's preaching to a real emperor's reign.
LifeLesson: The gospel happened under a named emperor in a numbered year. Faith here rests on history, not legend.

Name: Tibni, King of Israel
Summary: Tibni, son of Ginath, was set up by half of Israel against Omri after Zimri's death, and after a divided struggle he died and Omri prevailed.
KeyStory: Tibni's rival claim against Omri.
RelatedPeople: Omri, King of Israel; Ginath, Father of Tibni
LifeLesson: A divided people cannot stand, and a rival crown is no crown at all.

Name: Tiglath-Pileser, King of Assyria
Summary: Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria, also called Pul, took tribute from Menahem, stripped Israel's northern cities under Pekah, took Damascus and slew Rezin, and received Ahaz's appeal and temple treasure.
KeyStory: Tiglath-Pileser, called Pul, strips Israel's north and takes Damascus.
RelatedPeople: Menahem, King of Israel; Pekah, King of Israel; Rezin, King of Syria; Ahaz, King of Judah
LifeLesson: The king Ahaz bought became the king who owned him.

Name: Tikvah, Father of Shallum
Summary: Tikvah was the father of Shallum, keeper of the wardrobe and husband of Huldah.
KeyStory: Tikvah, father of Shallum.
RelatedPeople: Shallum, Husband of Huldah; Harhas, Grandfather of Shallum
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Tikvah
Summary: Father of Jahaziah, who opposed Ezra's plan.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: A father's name can open a son's story.

Name: Tikvath, Father of Shallum
Summary: Tikvath, son of Hasrah, was the father of Shallum, keeper of the wardrobe and husband of Huldah the prophetess.
KeyStory: Tikvath is named only as the father of Shallum the son of Tikvath.
RelatedPeople: Shallum, Son of Tikvath; Hasrah, Father of Tikvath
LifeLesson: A wardrobe-keeper's line is traced two generations.

Name: Tilgath-pilneser, King of Assyria
Summary: Tilgath-pilneser, king of Assyria, came to Ahaz when Ahaz sent for help, and distressed him but strengthened him not, though Ahaz had stripped the LORD's house and the king's house to pay him.
KeyStory: Ahaz gave the king of Assyria a portion out of the house of the LORD and the king's house, but he helped him not.
LifeLesson: The mention of Tilgath-pilneser in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Tilon
Summary: Son of Shimon in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:20: Son of Shimon in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Tilon stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Timon
Summary: Timon was one of the seven men chosen to serve tables in the Jerusalem church. Acts names him among the seven and records nothing further of him by name.
KeyStory: Timon was chosen with the seven to carry the daily distribution to the widows of the church.
LifeLesson: The church grows on unseen service. Timon is named once, and that naming is honour enough.

Name: Tirhakah, King of Ethiopia
Summary: Tirhakah, king of Ethiopia, marched out to fight Sennacherib while the Assyrian threatened Jerusalem, prompting Sennacherib's renewed threats to Hezekiah.
KeyStory: Tirhakah marches against Sennacherib.
RelatedPeople: King Hezekiah; Sennacherib, King of Assyria
LifeLesson: Help from afar still could not save Jerusalem; only the angel of the LORD did.

Name: Tirhanah
Summary: Son of Caleb's concubine Maachah.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 2:48: Son of Caleb's concubine Maachah.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Tirhanah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Tiria
Summary: Son of Jehaleleel in Judah's genealogy.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 4:16: Son of Jehaleleel in Judah's genealogy.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Tiria stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Tirshatha, Son of Hachaliah
Summary: Tirshatha son of Hachaliah, named in Nehemiah 10:1.
KeyStory: Covenant renewal
LifeLesson: Every person in the record, however briefly named, belongs to God's story.

Name: Titus
Role: Fellow worker and messenger to Corinth
Summary: Titus was Paul's fellow worker who carried letters to Corinth, reported the church's repentance, and was later left by Paul in Crete to set in order the things that were wanting and ordain elders.
KeyStory: Titus was Paul's fellow worker who carried letters to Corinth, reported the church's repentance, and was later left by Paul in Crete to set in order the things that were wanting and ordain elders.
KeyVerses: 2 Corinthians 2:13; 2 Corinthians 7:6; 2 Corinthians 8:23; Galatians 2:1; 2 Timothy 4:10; Titus 1:4
LifeLesson: A trusted messenger who brings both hard words and comfort is a gift to the church.

Name: Toah
Summary: Son of Zuph and father of Eliel in Heman's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 6:34: Son of Zuph and father of Eliel in Heman's line.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Toah stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Tobadonijah, the Levite
Summary: Tobadonijah was one of the Levites sent with Jehoshaphat's princes to teach the book of the law throughout Judah.
KeyStory: With the princes went Levites, including Tobadonijah, and they taught the people.
LifeLesson: God's law taught throughout the land, and willing service under a faithful king, strengthened Judah.

Name: Tobiah, of Tel-Melah
Summary: Named among those who returned from Tel-Melah but could not prove their genealogy (Ezra 2:60; Nehemiah 7:62). Not Tobiah the Ammonite, Nehemiah's opponent.
KeyStory: Return from exile
LifeLesson: Honest records distinguish namesakes; a shared name is not a shared story.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile

Name: Tobiah the Ammonite
Summary: Ammonite servant-official who joined Sanballat against the wall, later occupied a temple chamber through Eliashib, and was expelled by Nehemiah.
KeyStory: Rebuilding the wall
KeyVerses: Nehemiah 2:10; Nehemiah 2:19; Nehemiah 4:3; Nehemiah 4:7; Nehemiah 6:1; Nehemiah 6:12; Nehemiah 6:14; Nehemiah 6:17; Nehemiah 6:19; Nehemiah 13:4; Nehemiah 13:7; Nehemiah 13:8
LifeLesson: An enemy inside the house is more dangerous than one outside the wall.

Name: Tobijah, the Levite
Summary: Tobijah was one of the Levites sent with Jehoshaphat's princes to teach the book of the law throughout Judah.
KeyStory: With the princes went Levites, including Tobijah, teaching throughout all the cities of Judah.
LifeLesson: God's law taught throughout the land, and willing service under a faithful king, strengthened Judah.

Name: Tobijah
Summary: Tobijah (KJV 'Tobiah' in Zechariah 6:14) was one of the exiles from Babylon who brought silver and gold to Jerusalem for the crowning of Joshua the high priest (Zechariah 6:10). He is not Tobiah the Ammonite opponent of Nehemiah — a different man in a different generation.
KeyStory: Tobijah, with Heldai, Jedaiah, and Josiah son of Zephaniah, brought gifts from Babylon for the crown placed on Joshua's head.
RelatedPeople: Heldai; Jedaiah; Josiah, Son of Zephaniah
LifeLesson: Two Tobiahs, opposite stories: one brought gifts to crown the priest, the other opposed the wall. The name is the same; the choice is everything.

Name: Tohu, Son of Zuph
Summary: Tohu, son of Zuph, is named in Elkanah's genealogy as the grandfather of Elihu.
KeyStory: Tohu links Zuph's line to Elihu and Elkanah, Samuel's father.
LifeLesson: A faithful family line is itself part of God's preparation.

Name: Toi, King of Hamath
Summary: Toi, king of Hamath, had been at war with Hadadezer all his days. When David defeated Hadadezer, Toi sent his son Joram with vessels of silver, gold, and brass to bless David, and David dedicated them to the Lord.
KeyStory: Toi turned an enemy's defeat into an offering, sending silver, gold, and brass to David.
RelatedPeople: King David; Hadadezer, Son of Rehob; Joram, Son of Toi
LifeLesson: Wisdom knows when a rival's fall is a gift to dedicate, not to hoard.

Name: Tola, Son of Puah
Summary: Tola, son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, judged Israel twenty-three years and dwelt in Shamir in Mount Ephraim. He is distinct from Tola, son of Issachar, in Genesis.
KeyStory: After Abimelech, Tola arose to defend Israel, judged twenty-three years from Shamir in Mount Ephraim, and died and was buried there.
LifeLesson: A quiet twenty-three years of defending Israel left barely a paragraph — and that is enough.

Name: Tou, King of Hamath
Summary: King of Hamath who sent his son Hadoram to David to congratulate him.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 18:9: King of Hamath who sent his son Hadoram to David to congratulate him.
LifeLesson: The mention of Tou in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Trophimus
Summary: Trophimus was an Ephesian companion of Paul who travelled with him to Jerusalem. Jews who saw him with Paul in the city supposed Paul had brought a Greek into the temple, which sparked the riot that led to Paul's arrest.
KeyStory: Trophimus walked with Paul in Jerusalem, and a false supposition about him filled the temple courts with uproar.
LifeLesson: A rumour about Trophimus chained Paul. False suppositions still start riots around innocent men.

Name: Tryphena
Summary: Tryphena was a woman in the Roman church who laboured in the Lord, greeted alongside Tryphosa.
KeyStory: Tryphena was a woman in the Roman church who laboured in the Lord, greeted alongside Tryphosa.
LifeLesson: Labour in the Lord is never wasted, even when it is shared and unsung.

Name: Tryphosa
Summary: Tryphosa was a woman in the Roman church who laboured in the Lord, greeted alongside Tryphena.
KeyStory: Tryphosa was a woman in the Roman church who laboured in the Lord, greeted alongside Tryphena.
LifeLesson: Two labouring side by side show that the work of the Lord is shared work.

Name: Tychicus
Summary: Tychicus was an Asian companion of Paul who travelled with him toward Jerusalem, and later carried Paul's letters to the churches, a beloved brother and faithful minister.
KeyStory: Tychicus travelled with Paul toward Jerusalem and later carried his letters to the churches he loved.
LifeLesson: Messengers carry more than paper. Tychicus carried Paul's heart to churches he could not visit.

Name: Ucal
Summary: Ucal was one of the two men to whom Agur addressed his words in Proverbs 30, named alongside Ithiel in its opening verse.
KeyStory: Agur's oracle was spoken to Ithiel and Ucal; nothing more is told of Ucal, but his name is preserved as a hearer of wisdom.
LifeLesson: Ucal's place in Scripture honours the hearer of wisdom, not only its speaker.

Name: Uel, Son of Bani
Summary: Son of Bani named among those who had taken foreign wives (Ezra 10:34).
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: No family was exempt from the covenant's demands.

Name: Ulam, Son of Eshek
Summary: Firstborn son of Eshek, a mighty man of valour whose sons were archers.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 8:39: Firstborn son of Eshek, a mighty man of valour whose sons were archers.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ulam stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ulam, Son of Peresh
Summary: Son of Peresh and father of Bedan.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:16: Son of Peresh and father of Bedan.
LifeLesson: Named in the covenant line, Ulam stands among the individuals God placed within His people's story in 1 Chronicles.

Name: Ulla
Summary: Father of Arah, Haniel, and Rezia in Asher's line.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 7:39: Father of Arah, Haniel, and Rezia in Asher's line.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ulla in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Unni, Singer
Summary: Levite of the second degree appointed to sing with psalteries on Alamoth at the bringing up of the ark.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:18; 1 Chronicles 15:20: Levite of the second degree appointed to sing with psalteries on Alamoth at the bringing up of the ark.
LifeLesson: The mention of Unni in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Unni
Summary: Levite who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua.
KeyStory: Dedication of the wall
LifeLesson: Levites served the house of God in every generation.

Name: Ur, Father of Eliphal
Summary: Father of Eliphal among David's mighty men.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 11:35: Father of Eliphal among David's mighty men.
LifeLesson: The mention of Ur in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Urbane
Summary: Urbane (also rendered Urbanus) was a helper in Christ greeted by Paul among the Roman Christians.
KeyStory: Urbane (also rendered Urbanus) was a helper in Christ greeted by Paul among the Roman Christians.
LifeLesson: Helpers in the gospel share in the work even when their part is only a greeting in a letter.

Name: Uri, Father of Bezaleel
Summary: Uri, son of Hur, was the father of Bezaleel, the craftsman who made the bronze altar.
KeyStory: Uri is named only as the father of Bezaleel, son of Hur, maker of the bronze altar set before the tabernacle.
LifeLesson: A faithful line can be remembered through the work God gives the next generation.

Name: Uri, Father of Geber
Summary: Uri was the father of Geber, Solomon's officer over Gilead.
KeyStory: Uri, father of Geber.
LifeLesson: A name on a list is still a life God knew.

Name: Uri the Porter
Summary: A porter named among the temple servants after the return; a different Uri from Bezaleel's father in Exodus.
KeyStory: Ezra's reform
LifeLesson: Gatekeepers guard the house of God.

Name: Uriah the Hittite
Summary: Uriah the Hittite was one of David's mighty men and the husband of Bathsheba. While Uriah fought at Rabbah, David took Bathsheba, then had Joab place Uriah where the fighting was fiercest so that he was killed. He is named last among the thirty-seven, as if the list itself remembers him.
KeyStory: Uriah refused comfort at home while the ark and Israel camped in the open — and was murdered for his loyalty.
KeyVerses: 2 Samuel 11:3; 2 Samuel 11:6; 2 Samuel 11:17; 2 Samuel 23:39; 1 Kings 15:5; 1 Chronicles 11:41
LifeLesson: Loyalty that refuses privilege shames the king who abused it — and God did not forget.

Name: Uriah the Priest
Summary: Uriah the priest was one of the two faithful witnesses Isaiah took when he wrote the prophecy of Maher-shalal-hash-baz on a great roll. He is a different man from Urijah the prophet of Jeremiah's day.
KeyStory: Isaiah took Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah as faithful witnesses to the written prophecy.
LifeLesson: God's word is given with witnesses, so that no one can later say it was never spoken.

Name: Uriah
Summary: Priest, father of Meremoth; named Uriah in Ezra and Urijah in Nehemiah, where he stood beside Ezra at the reading of the Law.
KeyStory: Ezra's return
LifeLesson: One man can be spelled two ways and still be the same servant.
RelatedEvents: Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall; Ezra Reads the Law

Name: Uriel, Chief of Kohath
Summary: Chief of the sons of Kohath who brought up the ark, with his brethren an hundred and twenty.
KeyStory: Named in 1 Chronicles at 1 Chronicles 15:5; 1 Chronicles 15:11: Chief of the sons of Kohath who brought up the ark, with his brethren an hundred and twenty.
LifeLesson: The mention of Uriel in 1 Chronicles places this person within the story of God's people under David and his kingdom.

Name: Uriel, of Gibeah
Summary: Uriel of Gibeah was the father of Michaiah, mother of King Abijah.
KeyStory: Uriel is named only as the father of Michaiah, Abijah's mother.
LifeLesson: A grandfather's name can be the only trace of a faithful family.
